even those who have fallen from grace or are sinful— attain liberation by taking refuge in her.
Merely by being remembered, these of great power lead one to the world of Brahmā;
all the virtuous Upaniṣads should be resorted to by those seeking liberation. 14.
By bestowing the knowledge of the Self, by imparting the Brahma-mantra, and by granting refuge, they constantly deliver others from [saṃsāra]. 15.
By means of the method for the destruction of craving, through the dissolution of latent impressions,
and by bestowing self-satisfaction, they constantly deliver themselves.
By destroying the accumulation of karma, by burning away its causes,
and by utterly dispelling ignorance, they constantly enable themselves to cross over.
By attaining direct realization of their own self, by uniting the self with Brahman,
and by bringing about the state of being Brahman itself, they constantly deliver themselves.
By means of the bestowal of eternal bliss and through the attainment of perpetual satisfaction,
they indeed constantly bring happiness to themselves by attaining the fullness of all aesthetic flavors.
By bestowing omniscience, by fulfilling all desires,
and by manifesting their nature as the self of all, they delight themselves incessantly.
By granting residence in the same world as Hari, by bestowing his own creation,
and by the attainment of his very form, they constantly bring joy to their own souls.
By means of the attainment of union alone, and also by the bringing about of oneness.
They constantly relish their own self through the attainment of the nectar of Brahman.
Until the realization of the Self as Brahman, through the arrival of the vision of Brahman and through direct experience, they incessantly liberate the Self.
These virtuous women, whose nature is to assist others and who bestow liberation, should be served by me and by you as well, in every way and again and again. (24)
Indeed, those liberated ones who abide in all abodes are lords created by the Lord;
they are living beings situated within the cosmic egg of living beings, resting upon the Upaniṣads.
Likewise, there were female attendants born of the Vedas (Upaniṣads), daughters of Brahmā, the various Śrutis in diverse forms—virtuous and divine maidens beyond counting. (26)

They are hymns of praise to the Supreme Brahman, descriptions of the Supreme Brahman, the entire essence of the meaning of the Supreme Brahman, and the traditional means for attaining the Supreme Brahman. || 27 ||
All were divine and beautiful, possessing a radiance equal to that of the Upaniṣads;
all were twelve years of age and moved gracefully through every creation.
The infinite goddesses who are the Śrutis have emerged from each individual limb of the divine form of Śrī Hari; they are considered to bestow liberation through their retention.
They have neither a single purpose nor a single form; they are devoid of both shape and formlessness;
golden-hued, tawny, with the luster of refined gold and bright metal.
White, pale, and red, as soft as lotus petals, they are exquisite and destroyers of sin through taking refuge in them or merely hearing them. (31)
Likewise, the Gītās, the Upaniṣads, and the Śrutis always abide in their own form as liberated beings within the supreme, imperishable abode.
Moreover, those who were indeed requested by the Creator according to their merit have arrived here and dwell eternally in the supreme reality, the world of truth.
Their creation is indeed infinite and beyond counting, including their celestial abodes; their riches are priceless, and they possess heads like those of the Supreme Lord (Brahmā).
These goddesses are always divine, always maidens, and always virgins;
they are to be meditated upon, worshipped, contemplated, and served daily. (35)

Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, titled "The Narration of the Greatness of the Virtuous Woman Consisting of the Upanishadic Śrutis," in the first section, the Kṛtayuga-santāna, of the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī, to other supreme sciences that grant excellent liberation;
they are innumerable, truly great, virtuous, and twelve years in duration. || 1 ||
The supreme sciences that bestow nirvāṇa, by which Brahman is realized—
those sciences were revealed by Hari through his two eyes.
Divine, embodied, brilliantly radiant, and resplendent, these virtuous women are delicate, filled with the bliss of knowledge, and bring about the attainment of Brahman. (3)
They were fortunate, of radiant complexion, and possessed of great beauty;
they were filled with a fullness of limbs that transcended the mere onset of youth.
They were wonder-inspiring, gentle, peaceful, and embodiments of the quality of goodness (sattva);
they possessed beauty in accordance with their forms, and wore matted hair and golden nails.
With their breasts concealed, they were gentle and moderate; their bodies were filled with fragrance;
they were unblinking, possessed of soft smiles, tranquil and peaceful, and free from agitation.
They have attained eternal omniscience, possess minds of true resolve,
are destroyers of ignorance, and are endowed with the power of attraction.
Awakening all people and destroying internal darkness, they lead them to the imperishable abode; bestowing immortality, they are ever victorious.
Truly, they gladden the principle of life, behold the form of the Supreme Self,
and wed those who have come for refuge.
They repeatedly bring about liberation and victory. || 9 ||
Proclaiming their own nature as bliss,
manifesting their vast essential form,
and causing one to well-drink the desired, excellent nectar of Hari.
They bring about the state of being absorbed into the form of Hari.
Causing [the senses] to enter, manifesting the forms of Hari and Kṛṣṇa,
they illuminate the lamps of internal wisdom and sweep away the webs of subtle dust.
They lead one easily to the state of the world of the imperishable realm. || 11 ||
Stilling [the senses] with the splendor of the imperishable, fully satisfying them with the true essences of Hari and Kṛṣṇa,
and bringing about true delight in Hari and Kṛṣṇa.
Causing [others] to ascend to the supreme goal of the Blessed One.
The knowledge of the eyes, the knowledge of honey, the five-fire ritual, the Dahara-vidyā and others—all those great vidyās beginning with the Udgītha that reside in Hari; || 13 ||
All those maidens, having become virtuous, wander through millions of universes and swiftly lead men and women to liberation.
They are to be worshipped like Brahman and always to be served like Brahman;
they are to be meditated upon constantly like Brahman, and they, who are dear to Brahman, are to be attained like Brahman. || 15 ||
There are indeed millions of attendants to those Brahma-vidyās;
they are called the beloveds of Brahman, for they abide in the Imperishable Brahman.
All [the goddesses] are dear to Brahman, possess the form of Brahman, and have Brahman as their body;
they consist of Brahman, are the subtle essence of Brahman, and are united with the identity of Brahman.
For the sake of liberation, virtuous women of noble character indeed wander throughout the worlds of the Lord and the worlds of living beings, as far as the Great Abode (Mahālaya).
Their maidservants, female friends, and other female slaves, as well as their attendants—
all of them intact and numbering in the tens of millions— are bestowers of liberation.
Through service, these bestow prosperity; through reliance, they grant the highest good.
Therefore, virtuous women who observe celibacy should certainly be served from within one's own heart.
At the request of Brahmā, from the eye of the divine Śrī Hari at Naimiṣa,
there appeared hundreds of millions of billions of female companions who are dear to Brahmā.
All those female attendants are said to be the nurturers of the Great Vidyā;
for the sake of liberation, they should be worshipped, honored, and served by women. ||22||

Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, titled "The Narration of the Greatness of the Chaste Women Consisting of Supreme Knowledge and Their Maidens Consisting of the Beloveds of Brahmā," in the first section, the Kṛta-yuga lineage, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*. ||22||
Śrī Lakṣmī said:
O God of gods, Lord of the world, Beloved of my life, Great Master!
O Nārāyaṇa, salutations be unto you; I have certainly been delivered by you.
But I see, O Brahmin, that the Blessed One is victorious;
whose mantra is being recited by the Blessed One, the Supreme Self? (2)
Devotees always chant your name; indeed, there is no other worthy object for chanting.
You are the God to be chanted by all; who else could possibly be chanted? Thus I ask you.
"Upon seeing him, anxiety arises; therefore, O beloved, compose yourself.
Having heard this from his own wife, Nārāyaṇa spoke to her exactly as it was.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Goddess, to my secret which brings about all auspiciousness;
I alone am the true vessel for all auspiciousness, of this there is no doubt.
I myself am indeed the one to be recited by all; there is no doubt that I exist even therein.
Nevertheless, for the sake of instructing the world, I recite my own mantra.
From Vāsudeva, Mahāviṣṇu, Brahmā, and the other progenitors, as many emanations as were duly produced by me, so many were likewise produced by them in turn.
Therefore, having been requested by me for the sake of reciting the mantra,
the power consisting of my own form was manifested from my body.
She is not inferior to me, she is my very nature, my sovereignty, and my self;
she is divine, attracting [all] through meditation, and bestowing peace through recitation.
A beautiful maiden of twelve years, composed of the splendor of form, lovely with every auspicious grace, and endowed with the power for liberation.
Upon seeing her, they were all bewildered—the liberated ones, the lords, and others alike;
indeed, at that moment, they became utterly confused as to what ought to be done.
I myself chanted that Gāyatrī for the sake of protection; she is known as Kanyā, and the lords of the gods have also chanted her.
But those who chant the Gāyatrī as my own form and worship it, having burned away the mine of their own karma, attain my state. || 12 ||
O Lord, do not forget me, who was entreated by Gāyatrī;
may I always be protected by you and thereby become strong.
O Hari, if you do not grant me this power, how can you be capable of burning away the evil deeds of the wicked? (15)
Then I granted a boon: "I shall indeed always remember you.
Thereafter, by my command, the goddess Gāyatrī departed everywhere.
Furthermore, in the worlds of the lords and throughout the entire universe of living beings,
the maiden Gāyatrī is my own bodily radiance— weighty, virtuous, and noble.
Visible indeed to those with divine eyes, yet invisible to those with dull eyes, she exists as the means of deliverance for those who recite the mantra. (18)
Manifest as a maiden, having the form of knowledge, and residing in the heart;
consisting of sound and suitable for recitation—such is her threefold establishment. (19)
When the Vedas were restored by Brahmā from my presence,
I then brought them forth through Gāyatrī and returned them to him.
Therefore, she has attained the status of being reckoned as the Mother of the Vedas;
and many other Gāyatrīs exist for the sake of serving her. (21)
Indeed, by means of a mere fraction of my power, they have been manifested through my body;
yet in the worlds and sub-worlds, they appear under various distinct names.
These are considered to possess various distinct successions and diverse forms;
all of them exist as crores of handmaidens to the primary Gāyatrī. (23)
Greatly virtuous women who have not yet reached the onset of youth, being delicate and with unblemished inner selves, wander about; do they perhaps grant liberation to those who recite prayers? (24)
Endowed with Brahman-splendor, being the very forms of Brahman and bestowers of Brahman-yoga,
they— whose nature is Brahman— dwell indeed in the supreme truth, the auspicious world.
Those who are omniscient and all-knowing, whom the worlds remember— having swiftly approached there, they purify their own reciters.

Whether they be living beings, lords, gods, yakṣas, or even other rākṣasas; whether they be sinful, addicted to sin, or those characterized by the qualities of darkness (tamas) and passion (rajas). ||27||
These women attend upon those men and liberate them from evil;
traveling together with them, they protect them and lead them to nirvāṇa. || 28 ||
Thus, O Goddess, the reason for my recitation has been declared to you:
I always recite your name, O Lakṣmī, so that you might likewise recite mine. (29)
"O Goddess, I, the Blessed One, constantly recite my mantra for my devotees;
my devotees constantly recite their mantra for me—thus we recite for one another. (1.23.30)
Indeed, I perform their recitation for the sake of their protection;
but they, O Goddess, perform my recitation for the sake of attaining liberation. (3.1)
Now, there can be no recitation whatsoever without speech;
therefore, speech must be employed, and how could that exist without phonemes? (32)
And those who were born as lords were indeed unable to speak;
they remained in the silence of knowledge, equanimous and devoid of verbal discourse. ||33||
Even Brahmā and the other gods remained silent and praised the imperishable Śrī Hari;
knowing this silent praise, Hari himself became the leader of speech.
From the region of the tip of his own tongue, he indeed created a divine maiden; having been born, she herself asked the god, "What shall be my task? (35)
To that Goddess who was desiring to know, the Lord, having bestowed upon her his own power consisting of his own self—the power called Prasāra which is directed toward expansion—[said]: 36.
Having made her the very embodiment of speech, she indeed became Sarasvatī;
taking up a divine lute, she played it again and again. ||37||
In every world, whether belonging to Īśa or to Jīva, she went throughout the universe; in each manifestation, she assumed infinite forms for the sake of entering.
Infinite millions of those female forms of Śaradā, consisting of speech, were born—countless maidens and young girls produced from the very form of Hari. 39.
For all of them became female slaves, attendants to the Gāyatrīs;
they were sweet, pleasant, resonant with Ṛks, and clear in their sounds.
The wrathful, the loathsome, the compassionate, the humorous, the base, and the terrifying;
the divine, the non-divine, the subtle, and the gross—these are endowed with manifold meanings. ||41||
All of them, having reached the age of twelve, possessed various beautiful forms;
they were uninjured, unblemished, fortunate, and endowed with wealth.
These [energies] are threefold: embodied, consisting of knowledge, and consisting of speech;
they are virtuous women endowed with good character and vows, and they are to be worshipped for the sake of liberation.
Without me, there can be no liberation; the Sarasvatīs are identical with me, as are my tongues, which possess my own sovereignty—they are my very bodies. (44)

They should always be worshipped, always served, and always meditated upon for the sake of liberation, as long as the traditional collection of phonemes exists, being composed of the essence of Sarasvatī. (45)
Just as I am all-pervasive, so too is that Speech all-pervasive;
one who is proficient in the Śabdabrahman attains the Supreme Brahman. ||46||
From my Brahman there arises reflection (vimarśa), and from reflection the point (bindu) exists;
from the point nāda is produced, and from nāda indeed the sounds (dhvanis) are said to arise. ||47||
Indeed, the arrangements of syllables arising from sound, which are endowed with the Brahman of Sphoṭa, become those Sarasvatīs—the Great Goddesses of Speech—among people. (48)
Endowed with the dharma of the virtuous, they indeed liberate those who have taken refuge in them;
when served according to the lineage of Brahmā, they lead one to the supreme abode.
In the supreme truth of the Brahma-world, there are divine realms and celestial abodes,
as well as forests filled with objects of enjoyment and indeed infinite treasures.
For their sake, he indeed ordained inconceivable cities,
as well as inexhaustible means of transport, vehicles, musical instruments, objects of enjoyment, and drinks.
"O Sundarī, nothing at all will come of that in this world; therefore, O beloved, you must be persuaded by me to dwell in the midst of the Sarasvatī. (52)
Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, titled "The Description of Gāyatrī and Sarasvatī," in the first section, the Kṛtayuga-santāna, of the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā. || 23 ||
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Now, formerly, in the great creation within the cosmic egg of the Supreme Lord, while the Lord Nārāyaṇa was reclining upon the Ocean of Milk; (1)
The maiden who destroys the Dānavas, who emerged from the eleven sense-faculties—that great virtuous lady is Ekādaśī in the Mahālaya. (2)
And then she attained dissolution into the form of Nārāyaṇa.
As far as the powers of the senses extend, so far do the splendors of that All-pervading Lord.
Nārāyaṇa himself always resides within those forms;
at the commencement of the great creation, he does so out of a desire for the vows of the lords.
Those maidens were twelve years of age, divine, and richly endowed with a golden complexion.
They were complete in all their limbs and forms, and endowed with the splendor of asceticism.
He revealed them to the lords for the sake of the vow;
they were offered by the Blessed One, being solely devoted to Nārāyaṇa.
In granting liberation, those of great power are not inferior to Nārāyaṇa.
Adorned with liberation, they abide in the supreme abode, the imperishable syllable of Brahman.
Having performed that vow, the lords attain liberation in the imperishable state;
possessing bodies of Brahman, having the form of Brahman, they are endowed with the sovereignty of Brahman.
All these are bestowers of Brahman and liberation, they are the Brahmāṇīs who grant the knowledge of Brahman;
for when the Creator [desired] to come into his own creation, [he sent them].
And then, at the mere glance of Nārāyaṇa who had been thus entreated, I became prepared for the destruction of the great enemy named Mura.
"O Dānava, as long as I am sleeping there in the Ocean of Milk, a most terrible and powerful one named Mura has arrived. (11)
For the purpose of battle and for his destruction, the Śakti has been manifested by me.
And that [power] is accumulated through the capacity of the eleven sense-faculties. (12)
This enchanting and beautiful maiden has been empowered by me with radiant energy.
Svarṇasundarī was sent forth for the destruction of the Dānava.
As long as he goes toward destruction, so long does the Dānava remain an Asura.
Upon seeing her, he fell into a state of delusion; he chose her and desired her again and again. ||14||
Then, urged by the maiden, [he fought] both Nārāyaṇa and me in battle.
"O wicked one, win back your wife; otherwise, your desire shall not be fulfilled. (15)
Having heard that, the Dānava was bewildered and continued to fight.
But at that moment, his head was previously severed by the maiden with her sword. ||16||
He fell there upon the earth and died; he did not rise again.
Since then, O Lakṣmī, I have bestowed a great boon upon the maiden.
Those who perform your vow, O Datta, shall go to the supreme goal.
Those who perform your worship shall attain the imperishable Brahman.
Those who perform its concluding rite shall attain heaven, which grants all desired objects.
O sinner, those who practice generosity toward you shall attain liberation.
Those people who have come to you for refuge— whether they possess desires or are free from them— will, through your grace, obtain an abundance of enjoyments as the givers of their own merit.
Whether they be men, women, or others—be they gods, Daityas, or the like.
They will surely attain their own desired goal—Heaven, which bestows liberation. ||21||
She is the destroyer of great sins and even greater evils, and the bringer of happiness.
O maiden, become the purifier of people and the bestower of liberation. ||22||
Thus, by the attainment of this boon, she exists as one who destroys all sins, bestows the state of great liberation, and is superior to all else. (23)
Then that goddess said to me: "O Lord, I have been made by you to be alone;
there are many people and many worlds—how then can my pervasiveness be [established]? (24)
Therefore, may I become manifold in form; act in such a way that it may be so.
Then I bestowed upon her a most great power.
From that, the twenty-four principal forms of excellent nature arose, and from them, forms of infinite bodies were born;
indeed, as they pervaded the vastness of the universe on the eleventh day, they became of immeasurable nature.
Then, through my own resolve, I have likewise manifested from my own form millions and even infinite Ekādaśīs again and again. (27)
Likewise, their principal and secondary forms, as well as infinite maidservants created by me, exist everywhere throughout all the universes, bestowing liberation upon human beings. (28)
But here, in the world of Satya, that abode was created by the Creator;
for there dwell virtuous women who are practitioners of austerity.
Always possessing unimpaired good fortune and devoted to Nārāyaṇa,
these divine maidens were twelve years of age and possessed the full power of unbroken grains.

Because they lead one to that single, perfectly prosperous state which consists of liberation, these days are considered by name to be "Ekādaśīs"—the destroyers of worldly existence and the washers away of sin. (31)
Possessing divine forms and natures, they constantly accept worship.
"You must always worship and serve virtuous women together with me every day. (32)
And [the same applies] to the lords of the gods, the ṛṣis, and the beasts and birds.
And of humans and Daityas dwelling in water and on land. ||33||
Whenever my manifestation occurs within the assemblies, at that very time...
Their victory is a complete victory, along with mine.
The auspicious Jayā, the bestower of victory, my own daughter and handmaid, named Prākaṭyā and possessed of great power, has arrived, inseparable from me. (35)
In every way, she exists as divine, auspicious, and the bestower of victory upon her devotees;
that delicate maiden is certainly the giver of liberation to her devotees.
She is celebrated as Nārāyaṇī and Jayantī, and she is my very self.
My form is of the nature of Brahman, yet it is always identical with my own essential nature.
"Without me she does not dwell anywhere; existing together with me, she is the giver of liberation, Jayantī, the bringer of victory. (38)
And for her as well, I [bestowed] powers to assume many forms.
And then she too was bestowed [upon him], assuming the form of many tens of millions.
"Having assumed these forms known as the Jayantīs, which are infinite in number, I indeed manifest myself wherever Śrī Hari is present. (1.24.40)
The virtuous Jayantī is born together with it, bestowing liberation.
And even the secondary Jayantīs, which were previously uncounted, have been renewed by me. ||41||
Those maidservants were always accompanied by the principal Jayantīs;
through their service, worship, and the cultivation of the practice of their vows, [they attained success]. ||42||
They liberate all people who are well-established in the creation of the Lord of Life;
their dwelling is with me, and wherever I am, they abide there.

In the world of Brahmā, in the world of Īśa, in the world of living beings, and likewise in the world of the Creator, as well as in the world of truth—the divine worlds of the Jayantīs have been made stable. (44)
Jayantīs dwell there in every way by the millions;
wherever there is a festival of Hari, they come there in their true forms.
They are virtuous in form, beautiful in form, and likewise festive in form;
they are formless and the very embodiment of vows, and are considered in every way to be bestowers of liberation. (46)
Therefore, those who desire their own liberation should always serve the victorious ones.
Likewise, through great devotion, liberation shall always reside in the hands of both men and women. ||47||
Thus, being worshipped on my birthdays, these victorious ones, who are equal to my own worship, nourish their devotees who are absorbed in me. 48.
Whether pure or even impure, whoever is a devotee who observes the vow, having propitiated me through that, goes to my imperishable state. 49.
Having heard various delightful stories and having given abundant gifts, he departed.
Having performed each respective pure vow and having worshipped them thereafter, ||1.24.50||
Through the grace of Śrī Hari, they all attain the supreme goal.
The Jayantīs triumph here by means of bestowing the gift of liberation. ||51||
The Gāyatrī chants eternally, Sarasvatī chants, the Ekādaśīs chant, and the Gītā chants for that long. (52)
As long as the victorious ones do not indeed roar throughout the three worlds.
Even the roar of other [beings] that grant liberation is not so great as this. ||53||
Whatever thunder there may be, it serves as the head of Kṛṣṇa-jayantī.
Therefore, the Jayantī of Hari is indeed the most excellent for the bestowing of liberation.

Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, titled "The Narration of the Greatness of the Ekādaśīs and Jayantīs," in the first section on the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga of the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā. ||24||
Śrī Lakṣmī said:
O Nārāyaṇa, O Lord of the universe, O Sustainer of all, O Great Sovereign!
All your forms, beginning with Gītā, are bestowers of liberation. || 1 ||
What has been stated exists exactly so; however, it consists primarily of effort.
That which is easily accomplished and simple will bear fruit quickly as if it were already done.
For there can exist no other means that is more supreme or excellent than this, which does not depend on anything else.
Tell me that, O Great King, so that it may be for the benefit of all. || 3 ||

Whether by children, the elderly, or the young; by a woman, a man, a fool, or a great scholar; by one who is wealthy or one deeply distressed by poverty—by whomever it may have been commissioned. || 4 ||
Through this means of accomplishment, the supreme deity, the Blessed One, the Puruṣottama, [is attained].
That which is attained by women in such a manner—let that be explained. || 5 ||
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: I shall now describe that Goddess, by taking refuge in whom even the Gītā and other [scriptures], though they themselves are virtuous, swiftly attain supreme liberation.
Among all virtuous women, she who is the beloved of Hari is indeed the embodiment of the head [the most honored], for she is easily attained without effort.
Devotion, which bestows the bliss of liberation upon its commencement, is the mother most highly esteemed by me.
Indeed, at the commencement of the creation by Īśa, Vāsudeva and the others [honored] me.
The younger brothers made their request with hearts overflowing with love.
O Nārāyaṇa, sustainer of the world, ordainer of the world's welfare!
You are Śrī Hari, our primordial form, who shines resplendent in the divine abode.
From that form, through divine power, there manifest auspicious female energies of infinite virtuous potency for the welfare of embodied beings.
For them, as well as for us, the practice of attaining oneness with Śrī Hara would be most excellent;
yet there may be nothing superior to it. (11)
Thus questioned, I said nothing at that time; rather, it flashed clearly in my heart: "Let us go into the presence of Hari. (12)
Vāsudeva and all others are likewise Blessed Lords and Sovereigns.
They went to where Hari himself, the Supreme Brahman, shines resplendent. ||13||
In that supreme imperishable world, having approached it as if to test its purity,
they bowed, offered praise, prostrated like a staff, and sat down upon the ground.
"Welcome," he said, and with joy he offered him hospitality;
we inquired after his welfare and showed him the highest compassion. (15)
But our father, having understood that heartfelt desire, has made it known [to you].
Indeed, this is for that very purpose for which all of you have come. ||16||
I contemplate my own supreme, virtuous form,
which consists of the births of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, Vāsudeva, Nārāyaṇa, and the Supreme Self.
Likewise, I create for their wives worshipful bodies composed of my own essence.
For she is both embodied and unembodied; indeed, her embodied form is my own auspicious body.

Having thus personally conceived a manifestation of birth suitable for his own dwelling within those respective forms—though he himself is formless—Śrī Hari, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), [appeared]. 19.
Having revealed his own male form, he became the embodiment of devotion;
and that auspicious goddess, the great divine one, was composed of the Supreme Brahman.
Gentle, beautiful, and fair of form, adorned with all excellent qualities, she is endowed with every sovereignty and accompanied by all happiness—such is the Mother. (21)
The Supreme Brahman himself also manifested in the form of devotion.
In that case, what deficiency could there be, or what could not possibly exist from that? ||22||
As long as it is filled with that nectar, as long as it possesses auspicious fortune, and as long as it is replete with all sovereignty, this body is composed of the Supreme Brahman. (23)
The form of service preceded by love was assumed by Śrī Hari himself.
Everything is deposited therein; there is not even an atom's worth of deficiency in it. ||24||
And that devotion is considered the mother of the incarnations, as well as of the Blessed Ones; it is the sovereign and eternal mother that brings about liberation. (25)
Devotion, however, exists everywhere as something easily accomplished; it consists of mental contemplation in general, but takes the form of love toward a conscious being. (26)
In the body, she is known as the divine form of action, consisting of affection;
she is manifold, of various forms, and the binder of diverse purposes. (27)
Devotion is the virtuous Great Goddess, situated everywhere in manifold ways; for the Blessed Incarnations, the Lords, and their consorts are all her manifestations. (28)
Sages, ancestors, gods, humans, yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, kūṣmāṇḍas, and vināyakas—[all these have come]. (29)
Vetālas, as well as Ḍākinīs, Śākinīs, and Yoginīs.
And the charioteers, the Magadha bards, the heralds, and the professional panegyrists—||1.25.30||
The Vidyādharas, the Sādhyas, the Viśvedevas, and the Mārutas.
The Nāgas, Sarpas, as well as the Daityas, Dānavas, and those who are Uragas; ||31||
Furthermore, those that are stationary, those that are moving, and even those that are animals;
Some are subtle and some are gross; some are embodied and some are formless; and some are divine. ||32||
In the creation, those living beings who are born in the world are either embodied or bodiless.
And likewise, he dwells in the world of Āloka and in the southern city of Dharma. ||33||
Whether in heaven or in hell, in divine realms or in the worlds of truth, whatever living beings exist within creation—whether sinful or meritorious—[all are subject to this]. (34)
They are both defiled and undefiled, and they consist of various types of worthy and unworthy recipients.
Whether possessing knowledge or devoid of it, they are all freed from the burden of the knowable and the unknowable. ||35||
Devotion toward them is a great saintly woman that bestows liberation; of this there is no doubt.
In Śrī Hari, she is of the nature of divine love (prema) and is the immediate bestower of liberation. ||36||
She should always be worshipped, honored, served, and held dear in the hearts of all.
It should always be worn and beheld; it bestows liberation and should be made into an object of devotion. ||37||
A supreme goddess such as this has never been born anywhere, nor will she ever be born.
Indeed, no other devotion shall ever arise; she alone is considered the supreme mother.
For all [beings], exclusive devotion alone brings about union with Brahman.
Having thus resolved, the Lord of All created her in the form of Satī. 39.
The embodiment of supreme bliss and consciousness, the beautiful beloved of Kṛṣṇa.
The queen of the gods, with palms joined in reverence, asked Hari, "What shall I do? (1.25.40)
Then the Lord commanded, "Nourish my devotees."
She indeed accepted that, and at that time Hari became pleased.
He gave her Liberation as a maidservant, and two sons, Knowledge and Dispassion;
and Devotion [he gave] in the abodes of Goloka, Vaikuṇṭha, the Imperishable (Akṣara), and the Unmanifest (Avyākṛta). ||42||
Nourished by the attendants in the forms of the Blessed One, it has been made eternal.
But among the worlds of the lords, there are ten million lords who have been nourished. ||43||
In heaven, on earth, and in the netherworld, they were nourished by Nārada and others.
Where they are united together, accompanied by liberation, knowledge, and dispassion. ||44||
In all those places— whether in time consisting of truth and untruth, or in an age consisting of righteousness and unrighteousness— that devotion remains established with great bliss.
Devotion, however, is considered in every way divine, powerful, and the bestower of liberation.
In this creation, it increases among the virtuous in every house and among every person.
Having taken hold of liberation, he indeed bestows liberation upon his own people;
for those living beings who are endowed with devotion will exist in age after age. (47)
Even sinners shall go to that fearless abode of Hari, in whose hearts devotion in the form of love always resides. (48)
Those of pure form do not behold the plowman even in a dream.
Neither a preta, nor a piśāca, nor a rākṣasa, nor even an asura [is able to harm him]. ||49||
He becomes manifest even upon being seen to those whose minds are endowed with devotion;
neither by austerities, nor by the Vedas, nor by knowledge, nor by ritual action [is He so attained]. (1.25.50)
Hari is attained through devotion, for Hari is the very form of devotion;
through the power of the virtuous deeds of living beings, love for devotion increases. (51)
May Hari grant devotion; through devotion, Hari is devotion; by devotion, Kṛṣṇa stands before one.
Those who commit acts of treachery against devotion perish within the three worlds.
Enough with vows, enough with sacred fords, enough with yogas, and enough with sacrifices;
enough with discourses on knowledge—devotion alone is the giver of liberation. (53)
Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Greatness of Devotion," in the first section on the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga of the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
In brief, devotion (bhakti) should be understood as service preceded by love.

That service is always declared to be for Hari, the Lord of the abode of Brahman. [It may arise] from desire, from affection, from fear, from greed, from pride, from self-interest, or likewise from other causes.
Devotion offered by living beings certainly bestows liberation. || 2 ||
Devotion to one's wife, devotion to one's husband, devotion to the family, as well as devotion to the country, devotion to the gods, and devotion to the Self—these are the forms of devotion. (3)
Indeed, devotion to Hari excels all other forms of devotion;
for the various types of devotion are but infinite handmaidens of devotion. (4)
There are millions of various forms of devotion that take refuge in devotion to Hari: devotion to one's ancestors, devotion to one's teacher, and devotion to the divine beings.
Devotion to the Lord, devotion to the world, and likewise devotion to cows;
But all forms of devotion are indeed service (dāsya) to Hari; such is the established principle of devotion.
Because the cosmic eggs are infinite, due to the diversity of their respective channels.
The forms of devotion are diverse, and they differ according to the distinctions in what is revered. ||7||
Just as liberation is always attained through devotion,
so too is service a form of worship, and even the act of serving is considered an act of adoration.
The waving of the light is a maidservant, and circumambulation is also a maidservant;
praise is a maidservant, and meditative absorption is a servant, as is salutation—a maidservant. (9)
Meditative concentration (dhāraṇā) is considered a maidservant, and prayer is another;
the handful of flowers is considered a maidservant, and all supernatural powers (siddhis) are her maidservants. ||1.26.10||
All these women are indeed maidservants who manifest the form of Hari;
they are all identical in essence to the form of Hari, arising with a power equal to that of devotion. ||11||
Having made their dwelling in the abode of Brahmā, they were all twelve years of age.
These others, such as Divya and Muktānī, are indeed those very forms of Hari.
They should always be served, honored, and respected with joy; that is how it should be.
Whatever forms of devotion exist among the lords in the worlds, they are indeed those [which lead to liberation]. ||13||
But those residing in each respective abode exist in innumerable forms.
But those [goddesses] dwell here in this world, while the others reside in the supreme truth of the Creator.
The various modes of worship, the services, and the commands that are prescribed—even those remain well-established with the Mistress in their respective abodes. (15)
In the case of female slaves, service is for the purpose of propitiation; now, [the following applies] to the means of accomplishment.
Therefore, worship is considered to be of various kinds, consisting of honor and excellent renown. ||16||
The *nīrājanā* (lustration with lights) is known as the *ārātrika*, which always provides protection;
for the devotee, circumambulation (*pradakṣiṇā*) consists of moving clockwise around Hari.
Praise (stuti) is said to consist of singing the multitude of [the Lord's] qualities; hymn (stavana) is described as being of the nature of that same praise.
Samādhi is his state of abiding as if dissolved in identity with His very essence. (18)
Veneration is an internal state of one's own being that is manifested outwardly through speech.
Dhāraṇā is the one-pointed concentration of the functions of knowledge upon Śrī Hari. (19)
Prayer is considered the choosing of one's desired objects; likewise, the handful of flowers (puṣpāñjali) manifests the love of the heart through the medium of flowers. ||1.26.20||
The supernatural powers (siddhis) are indeed aṇimā, mahimā, and likewise garimā.
Minuteness, attainment, irresistible will, lordship, and likewise mastery; ||21||
Reasoning, verbal instruction, and likewise practice—these three are the destroyers of suffering.
The acquisition of friends, generosity, and the spiritual accomplishments are also highly esteemed. ||22||
Tārā, Sutārā, and then Tāratārā; Ramyā, Pramodā, and then Modamānā; Sudā as well as Muditā and Salīlā—indeed, many varieties of Siddhi are recognized. (23)
Worship before Hari is pure conduct for the sake of dwelling [in His presence];
therein, command is the protection resulting from following the will of Hari. (24)
O Blessed One, all these forms have indeed been manifested by the Blessed Hari himself; they are considered to be identical with his own self and bestowers of liberation. (25)
These maidens are virgins, auspicious, and the source of all blessings.
They are remembered as bestowing divine vision upon those who have taken refuge in them as soon as they are called to mind. ||26||
As soon as they were born, they all practiced divine austerity, with the aim that their Lord Hari might always remain pleased with them. (27)
But the Lord Hari, the sovereign of the divine abode, became exceedingly well-pleased by their love and austerity, and He urged them toward the granting of a boon.
By means of them, auspicious boons were obtained from the presence of Śrī Hari.
The fulfillment of the devotees' desires and likewise eternal imperishability [are His qualities]. ||29||
The nature of both the formed and the formless, and the virtuous practice of the dharma of faithful women.
The state of being the inexhaustible nature of the maiden, and the functioning in the form of Hari’s will.
Always maintaining the state of being twelve years old, protecting the status of a servant through devotion, and being intent on residing wherever the residence of Hari’s devotee is found. (31)
Constant residence in the form of Hari, the possession of Hari’s own power, and the ability to travel at will as far as the imperishable abode (akṣaradhāma). ||32||
The nature of possessing the form of a divine woman, being stainless, as well as being free from the bond of *māyā*, and being eternally liberated—this is the meaning. ||33||
They possess the bestowal of great prosperity and perpetual purity;
thus, through the attainment of such boons, they rejoice and cause others to rejoice. (34)

Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter, titled "The Enumeration of the Attainment of the Devotion of the Female Servants through Worship and Other Means," in the first section, the Kṛtayuga-santāna, of the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā. || 26 ||
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Furthermore, O Lakṣmī, hear now of those eternal forms of mine.
They are eternally non-different from my eternal nature and are identical with my own self. || 1 ||
Mahālakṣmī, Lakṣmī, Ramā, Rādhā, and Satī, as well as Vṛndā, the Mothers, and the maidens beginning with Gaṅgā. || 2 ||
Having separated them from my own body, I myself held them fast.
All these are non-different from me; like me, they are considered to be bestowers of liberation. || 3 ||
All supernatural powers reside in Śrī Hari, who is my own form and whose abode is the Imperishable.
They are the very embodiments of Mahālakṣmī, manifested by me alone.
Likewise, those supreme prosperities that exist within my very form are present right there.
Indeed, those forms of Lakṣmī have been revealed by me in their entirety.
Likewise, whatever beauty exists there in my very form,
that I have set apart and manifested as those various goddesses of fortune (Ramās).
Furthermore, whatever desires for perfection I had regarding that form of mine,
those very desires were manifested by me as Rādhās, who are my own forms.
And likewise, the omnipresent existence that resides there within my own form—
All these women, who possess the form of Satī, have been manifested by me alone.
Likewise, in that regard, I possess the power to grant boons through my physical form.
Having separated their respective powers, all the Vṛndās were manifested.
Likewise, those nourishing powers that reside within my form there have all been separated and manifested as the Mothers. (1.27.10)
Likewise, in that image of mine, you should perceive [the deities] as being composed of the essence of the rasa of love.
Having separated them all, Gaṅgā and the other rivers were indeed made manifest.
All of them were free from passion, and all of them had their virginity intact.
All possess eternal bodies; all are remembered as my own forms. ||12||
In my supreme, imperishable abode, those [energies] exist as truly liberated entities.
And in all the creations of Īśa, those [women] are indeed Īśvarīs. 13.
In the world of the living and in the supreme truth, those women are indeed goddesses.
Likewise, those whose nature is that of effects reside layer upon layer. (14)
Mahālakṣmī is the embodiment of prosperity; Lakṣmī is the form of gold and other riches;
Ramā is the very nature of wealth; Rādhā is the perfection born of action. 15.
Likewise, Tulasī, in her embodied form, brought fulfillment to the blessings bestowed by Vṛndā.
The virtuous woman is the power of goodness; the mothers are the powers of nourishment. ||16||
The Gaṅgā is renowned for its flowing water and is considered by Hari to be the bestower of liberation;
the lakes such as Puṣkara and others are but drops of the essence of love for Him. (17)
Furthermore, sacred fields such as Haridvāra and the Naimiṣa forest indeed originate from portions of Hari’s imperishable abode. 18.
Indeed, virtuous celestial women dwell in those meritorious fields.
For they are considered to be born from a portion of the Brahman-city situated in the abode of the Imperishable (Akṣara). ||19||
In all those places, maidens such as Lakṣmī and others indeed reside;
they are perceived through divine vision, and they bestow divine liberation.
Having taken birth as women, Mahālakṣmī and others are born in some places as auspicious maidens among householders.
From their youth, these maidens remain virtuous with their virginity intact;
once initiated, they become yoginīs who accomplish yoga.
Some indeed become female renunciants by adopting renunciation, while others become free from passion through the destruction of desire. (23)
Some indeed, through the investigation of Sāṃkhya and through the yoga of Brahman, become Sāṃkhyayoginīs, ever devoted to celibacy. ||24||
Those who are lifelong celibates (naiṣṭhika-brahmacāriṇyaḥ) become givers of liberation in this creation;
pure and having the nature of fire, those Brahmāṇīs deliver men. 25.
They were virtuous, upholders of moral conduct and vows, possessing the splendor and beauty of the sun.
May those [rays] consisting of lunar peace descend upon her, destroying the threefold suffering. ||26||
By seeing them, they destroy suffering; by serving them, they bring about happiness;
by venerating them, they remove poison; and by hearing them, they bestow purity. ||27||
Through chanting, they grant desired fruits; through remembrance, they take away the god of love.
Through worship, they lead one indeed upon the radiant path and bestow liberation. ||28||
From servitude, they grant the state of being a servant; from friendship, they bestow the attainment of friendship.
By the offering of oneself, they cause the devotee to be established within the Self of Hari. ||29||
Worshipped with an abundance of food, clothing, garments, and articles,
they reach the imperishable abode of Śrī Hari by the power of Hari.
By massaging his limbs, feet, and so forth, they cause him to traverse the path of Hari.
Indeed, by performing those various desired rites, the devotee shall surely obtain his own cherished goal. ||31||
Wearing saffron-colored robes, they were bound by ties of affection for the sake of Hari.
For the sake of Brahman, the lifelong celibate women [attain their goal] through devotion to Hari.
He is Muktānya because he is liberated from death; Brahmāṇya because he originates from Brahman;
Mokṣāṇya because his very form is liberation; and Brāhma because he is dedicated to Brahman. ||33||

They are true because of their continuous succession of chastity; they are virtuous because they are the refuge of the qualities of the righteous; they are goddesses because they have attained a divine state; and they are venerable because of their instruction in knowledge. (34)

The female servants (dāsyaḥ) are considered to be "servants of Brahman" (brahmadāsyaḥ) because they always follow the conduct of servants; however, those who take refuge in the Supreme Lord (parameśvara) should be understood as "mistresses" (īśvarāṇyaḥ). //35//
These wives of Hari, the Protector, should be understood as devoted wives (pativratā) because of their attainment of him;
they are called "wives" (patnyaḥ) also because they lead the fallen one to the supreme abode.
Women are to be understood as "saviors" because they lead men to the state of Nṛhari;
they are "universal sovereigns" because they enter the vehicle of the King of Kings, the Lord of the Gods. (37)
They are called *tyāginīs* because they renounce [all else], and *svāminīs* because of their offering of themselves.
They are called *muṇḍinī* because they shaved their hair, which was like that of Brahmā, for the sake of Hari. ||38||
And they are called *ācāryāṇīs* because they promote proper conduct (*ācāra*).
And they are called *āravālyas* because of their filling with the sound of Hari. (39)
They are also called *liṅginīs* because they move toward Hari, whose nature is dissolution;
and they are called *avadhūtīs* because of their shaking off of *māyā*. (1.27.40)
And they are called "Bhagavatis" because of their attainment of the sixfold sovereign powers (ṣaḍbhaga-aiśvarya).
And they are also called "mothers" (mātaraḥ), because they bestow the measure of liberation.
And they are called "initiated" (dīkṣitāṇya) because of the destruction of sins through the granting of knowledge.
Even those who are weak should be understood as strong by virtue of their reliance on the power of this Viṣṇu.
But those [mantras] originating from the ṛṣis are always to be understood as such, because they rely upon the ṛṣis, the Vedas, and so forth.
But the eight noble ones are superior because they lead to awakening and because they bring one near to Hari. ||43||

And those [energies] should be understood as *nārāyaṇī*, because they lead men (*narān*) to Nārāyaṇa; and they should also be understood as *hariṇī*, for they lead those who have taken refuge in them to Hari. 44.
And likewise, the glories of Śrī Hara shall also be attained through taking refuge in Śrī Hari.
But those divine [mantras] that have been properly mastered always bestow divinity through their application. ||45||
Their supreme and divine form arises from dwelling within Nārāyaṇa.
Having received initiation from Hari, the Niṣādas became bearers of the emblem of Hari. ||46||
Waiting for Hari, they go to the abode of Hari;
they lead those who endure all things, who are dependent on life, and who walk the path of devotion. 47.
These virtuous women should always be served by lords of men, gods, and others;
indeed, they should always be served, honored, and saluted with devotion by women. 48.
The Blessed Lord Śrī Hari shines eternally as one with that [reality].
There, in that assembly of virtuous women, I always appear in a divine form. ||49||
The virtuous woman’s beauty, disposition, righteousness, and very form—
O King, I myself have always personally assumed the form of virtuous women.
These virtuous women are indeed not different from me, nor are they inferior to me, nor are they born of material elements;
for they are to be known as rubies, being my very own forms.
Not even an atom's worth of their bodies is considered illusory.
Their bodies are indeed my body; they are simply my own forms.
Form, charm, beauty, attractiveness, nectar-like sweetness, desirability, sweetness of appearance, gentleness, consoling nature, coolness, and so forth; ||53||
Humility, dependence, service, modesty, contentment, wretchedness, steadfastness, goodness, affection, gentleness, and so forth. ||54||
Affection for the grove, skillfulness, endurance, compliance, faith, trust, truthfulness, purposefulness, non-possessiveness, protection, and so forth. ||55||
Giving, nourishing, offering one's entire being, and treating [others] as friends; providing support through fortitude, acting as a true friend, and equanimity toward pleasure and pain. ||56||
Endurance, lack of fickleness, devotion, service, constancy, renown, praise, secrecy, profundity, magnanimity, modesty, and so forth are the qualities. (57)
All my [qualities] have been surrendered by me to them within my own form;
for, having bestowed all virtues upon them, I dwell only within those virtuous women.
The clarity attained by them is considered to be mine;
they are indeed the Yoginīs of Sāṃkhya, virtuous women who are the abode of all noble qualities. (59)
They destroy the sins of ignorance and bestow immortality.
O beloved, these authorized women of Śrī Hari are to be honored by you just as I am.

Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Various Etymologies and Attributes of Mahālakṣmī and Other Virtuous Women Embodied as the Forms of Nārāyaṇa," in the first section, the Kṛtayuga-santāna, of the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā. ||27||
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
My divine qualities always reside within them.
I shall describe those meaningful qualities to you; listen, O beloved.
A disposition that is beneficial to all beings is proclaimed therein as truth.
However, purity (śauca) is proclaimed therein as being the state of being an adversary to that which is to be abandoned. || 2 ||
Compassion is proclaimed therein as the removal of the suffering of others;
forbearance is proclaimed therein as the capacity to endure offenses. ||3||
Disregard even for one's own interests is renunciation; contentment is the state of having all desires fulfilled.
Straightforwardness toward all beings is proclaimed as sincerity. || 4 ||
Tranquility is the non-subjugation of the afflictions; self-restraint is the control of the senses.
Austerity is the cessation of desire; equanimity is the state of being undifferentiated toward all things. || 5 ||
Forbearance, endurance, sovereignty, and learning, which is the knowledge of the meaning of the scriptures.
Cessation, however, is proclaimed to be the non-arising of effort. (6)
Knowledge is traditionally defined as the thorough acquaintance with reality exactly as it is;
dispassion is proclaimed to be the state of being entirely devoid of attachment. (7)
Sovereignty is the state of being a controller, the nature of being the lord of all; valor is victory by one's own nature, and splendor is considered to be invincibility. (8)
Strength is the capacity of the body and self; memory, however, is eternal manifestation.
And sovereignty is said to be non-dependent on others and independent of anything else. (9)
Skill in all undertakings is proclaimed as proficiency.
Lustre is considered to be an innate beauty that captivates the minds of all. (1.28.10)
Fortitude is highly esteemed as the absence of confusion when success is swiftly attained;
gentleness, however, is considered in every respect to be the lack of harshness in one's natural disposition. (11)
Boldness is proclaimed as the emergence of quick-wittedness; humility is to be understood as modesty; and character is the purity of one's conduct. (12)
May there be, in every way, the ripening [of beings] through their restoration;
may there be vigor in the undertaking of tasks, and the kindling of energy through their successful completion. (13)
Bhaga is considered to be the excellence of the illumination of knowledge and other such qualities at all times.
Its profundity is proclaimed as the unfathomability even regarding its underlying intention. ||14||
Fame is that which is sung by the people of the world; renown is said to be the state of being a worthy vessel for glory.
Silence is the absence of idle chatter, and steadfastness is the state of being free from fickleness. ||15||
Faith (āstikya) is proclaimed as confidence in the meaning of the words of a reliable authority;
freedom from pride (agarva) is indeed considered to be the absence of conceit regarding one's own virtues. (16)
The absence of pride and the state of being empty of egoism are indeed considered non-conceit.
Freedom from hypocrisy is conduct that is free from deceit and not obstructed by the desire for rewards. ||17||
Moderate eating is defined as taking only what is necessary to achieve satisfaction;
skillfulness is said to be the ability to see through to the completion of tasks that have been interrupted. (18)
Loving-kindness toward all living beings is considered the foundation of trust.
Benefiting others consists in providing assistance without regard for personal gain. ||19||
Non-malice is indeed the avoidance of harming others by any means whatsoever;
it consists of bestowing honor as is appropriate and performing every act of hospitality.
The conquest of the six waves is proclaimed as the complete victory over the six;
hunger, thirst, sorrow, delusion, old age, and death are the six waves. (21)
The state of being a protector of those who have come for refuge is proclaimed as "refuge-ness" (śaraṇyatva);
while the state of being free from the thread of craving is proclaimed as "effortlessness" (anīhatva). ||22||
Just as the grasping of superior objects according to one's expectations is called non-grasping.
Indeed, there is service in every way and the nourishment of living beings. ||23||
For these qualities always reside in Śrī Hari, and they are the bestowers of liberation.
They may be accepted as devotees through the force of their worship of Hari. ||24||
Endowed with those very same six virtues, I dwell among virtuous women.
Therefore, virtuous women are always worthy of worship; they are pure and sanctifiers of the assembly. ||25||
The daughters of Māpu are practitioners of Sāṃkhya and Yoga; they are truthful and the refuge of virtuous qualities.
The maidens whose resolve is true, and those women who have sought refuge in me. ||26||
They lead one to the supreme abode and likewise grant happiness;
they gladden me and offer themselves to the embodied form of Hari.
Because they have performed my work, because they have served me virtuously, and because they have worn a portion of my garment, they are not considered inferior to me. (28)
In the supreme, imperishable abode, whatever powers of yoga belong to me—
Having distinguished them individually, I have revealed these yoginīs. ||29||
Indeed, those infinite female servants always become identical with my own nature.
By my command, those divine ones roam throughout all the worlds.
Divine, possessing divine wonders, they are always twelve years of age.
Not born from a womb, they always dwell in the true Brahma-world. ||31||
These deities are proclaimed to be the *ātivāhika* (conveying) ones;
they alone lead the one destined for liberation along the path to liberation. ||3||
However, the capacities regarding place, time, and suitability are to be understood as being innumerable.
In whatever manner a task may be, they perform it in that very manner. ||33||
Whatever quality is entirely renounced within my own self becomes [liberation].
Having separated that quality, they were then made into female renunciants (sannyāsinīs). ||34||
They too, possessing divine forms, constantly move about within the creation.
The divine twelve-year [observances] lead embodied beings to liberation. ||35||
He who, through detachment, has separated the quality from my form—by my will, those free from passion have been made manifest because of him. (36)
These twelve-year-old girls bestow divine liberation.
Just as I exist eternally, so too do they exist eternally. //37//
Likewise, in that imperishable abode, which is my own form, there exists the knowledge of Sāṃkhya;
similarly, the capacity for Yoga is also present—indeed, both of these exist therein. (38)
Then, having separated [the essence], twelve divine maidens were produced—gentle, beautiful, and endowed with a form resembling my own, though they were twelve years of age. (39)
Filled with the essence of all selves, overflowing with all bliss,
they were women whose fullness of every limb was such that their youth had not yet reached its bloom.
These, however, are the female practitioners of Sāṃkhya-yoga, who in every way contemplate upon Brahman.
They are always the bodies of Brahman, because they consist entirely of Brahman. ||41||
They move through all creations in a divine form,
constantly liberating living beings or lords from within the darkness.
But when they manifest from the womb of certain women, then signs appear upon their hands and feet. (43)
They are to be recognized by seekers of liberation through divine signs and by their virtuous conduct.
I shall describe those signs; listen before me, O Lakṣmī. ||44||
But those whose breasts are indeed in the heart of Nārāyaṇa in the center;
Indeed, there appeared a line of dots known as *tilaka* above his feet. ||45||
Below the navel, in the region of the hips, there should be a line as golden and deep orange as a tawny bee;
on the forehead, it should have the form of an arrow, and at the crown of the head, the shape of a diadem.
Furthermore, on the right cheek and then on the forehead in the middle region,
there shall also be a red spot, which is equal to the Sudarśana [cakra].
On whose chest there appears a line of Viṣṇu extending across four cubits, and on the left side of her arm-band there appears the mark of a mace; ||48||
If there should be the mark of a sandal upon her left thigh, and if there is a golden line on the chest of the Vaijayantī [necklace], [she is a woman of noble lineage]. 49.
Holding a lotus in her hand, she whose hand [is adorned] with an elephant.
But this maiden in human form should be known as Lakṣmī herself. ||1.28.50||
Now I shall describe other natural marks by which those women whose feet or hands bear them are to be known as the consorts of Nārāyaṇa. (51)

Thus ends the twenty-eighth chapter, titled "The Display of Divine Marks on the Holy Women Whose Nature is the Qualities of the Lord," in the first section, the lineage of the Kṛta Yuga, of the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā. ||28||
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī, I shall describe the marks upon your feet; by these, people may recognize you when your birth occurs in the world.
On the right foot, however, beneath the base of the big toe, there is a hooded serpent (phaṇaka) bearing a boon-granting gesture (vara).
The mark of the conch (śaṅkha) should be understood as being at the base of the two fingers.
The sign of a celestial chariot (vimāna) is on the ring finger near its base;
likewise, there is the sign of a boat and the sign of a mace below a conch shell.
And below that, there should be a mark in the shape of a crocodile, and from there, a pinnacle at the heel; in the middle, there should be a line of fish and a betel vine.
There, at the base of the left thumb, the mark of a barley grain is proclaimed.
But beneath that, it is proclaimed, there is a great palace.
Below that, there should be an umbrella, while the upward line is eternal;
there, at the base of the two fingers, a lotus is considered to be on the hood.
Below that is the line of the banner, and at its side the goad is said to be located.
Below that, on the side, are the kumuda, the śrīphala, and likewise the pitcher.
Below that is the earth-lotus, and on the heel is the second moon.
There are ten full wheels upon the hood, marked with golden lines.
O Lakṣmī, whenever these syllables of mine are seen, then that which is called Śrī-Lakṣmī should be known as the Supreme Brahman; of this there is no doubt.
O Goddess, when two, three, four, or even five [marks] are seen on your feet, she is considered a human being who possesses a portion of you.
On the forehead, there is a golden necklace, a golden line, and a dot;
on the right cheek, a red dot, and a dot on the chin.
There is a hand-line on the right breast, while there is a wheel on the left breast.
But on the thief's neck was a golden necklace; I am the four-armed one. ||12||
Above the vulva is the emblem of Kāmadeva, consisting of a bow and arrows.
There are lines on the thighs like lotuses, and a svastika on the right hand. 13.
Dhvaja, Matsya, Vaṃśī, Dhanu, Matsyaka, and Kalaśa—these should be known as the daughters who are portions of Nārāyaṇa. (14)
Whether it be one, or two, or even more than that.
And the signs of awakening are seen in the daughters of Brahmā who have descended to earth. ||15||
When the glorious Nārāyaṇa became a human being in human form, then in his right hand were the banner, the thunderbolt, the lotus, and the flute.
The svastika, the bow and arrow, the trident, and likewise the fish;
the lotus, the conch, and the discus; the sun, the elephant, and the peacock. (17)
Upon my descent, however, one, two, or three [of these] will certainly come to pass.
In the heart, there shall be an auspicious mark of Lakṣmī in the form of a golden line. ||18||
On the chest, upon the skin, there may be an auspicious line formed by a golden necklace.
Indeed, there shall be three-fold folds of skin hanging down upon the abdomen. ||19||
On the linga there should be a black dot, and on the forehead there should be a tilaka.
There was also a single line extending from both sides of his forehead.
On the left thigh, there was a large, pale, spotted piece of cloth from the Bhallava region.
Likewise, a black dot may appear upon the right calf. ||21||
There will be a Guru-phatrika on both his feet, which is auspicious.
That body was golden-hued, delightful, and adorned with beauty. ||22||
Her eyes, filled with love for Rājīva, have reddish corners and are endowed with compassion.
With a frown and side-long glances, possessing waves of beautiful, curved, and broken arches.
The svastika, banner, barley-corn, goad, staff, eight-sided [diamond], lotus, and conch are [the signs].
A half-moon, a jar, a cow’s footprint, a pit, a triangle, a hoof-print, a crescent moon, and a bow. ||24||
Then, on the southern petal, those nine [symbols] beginning with the svastika are likewise [to be placed].
On the surface of the forest [of the mandala], there are indeed seven lines beginning with the half-moon.
He in whom one, two, or even three [of these qualities] are seen is Acyuta;
he is indeed an incarnation of Hari, the Blessed Lord, born from a portion of Hari.
He should be known as untainted, the destroyer of sin and suffering;
even amidst the great enjoyments of women, wealth, and the like, he remains unimpeded—he is indeed the Lord.
Even while abiding within illusion, he makes that illusion divine.
But through his own yoga, he purifies even the most sinful who have come to him. ||28||
Those who worship him out of desire, anger, fear, greed, or envy—all of them, through his majesty, attain liberation from which there is no rebirth. (29)
Having completely burnt away all substances that are inherently stable, the fire remains free from any residue.
Having completely burnt away all karmas, Kṛṣṇa remains untainted.
Just as impure metals and the like, when cast into fire, become pure, so too, when impure desires and the like are offered to Hari, they likewise become pure. ||31||
Of Hari, who possesses immeasurable power and whose nature is indeed pure.
But through connection with the Lord, who consists of parts, men and women are purified. ||32||
He whose two excellent conch-shells are on the middle fingers of both hands, and likewise six wheels on the other [fingers] as well as on the two thumbs; 33.
He himself, the Blessed One, would indeed have two wheels at the edges;
those two hands are known as "lotuses," and likewise upon the palm of the left hand.
He in whose center there is a vertical line extending downwards is indeed the Blessed One;
wherever he places his hand, that place truly becomes imperishable. //35//
This embodied soul, endowed with any one of the aforementioned signs, may be in the form of a woman or a man, and may be either a householder or a renunciant. (36)
Thus, I am Nārāyaṇa manifest, always performing the dance of humanity; though acting like an ignorant man, I uplift all beings.
In some instances, I manifest only a very slight degree of sovereignty;
this is solely for the sake of accomplishing the purpose of my devotees, and not for the sake of establishing my own greatness.
But worldly people are sinful, seeking only to accomplish their own self-interest.
Having accomplished their own purpose, those evildoers depart far away from me. (39)
Therefore, I do not indeed display any miraculous wonder;
for true devotees attain Me even without such a marvel.
Those by whom the Blessed One has been ascertained through the marks declared in the scriptures should not seek for wonders, nor should they grasp at any abnormal defects. ||41||
The partial incarnation (aṃśāvatāra), having accomplished all his tasks, sees, smells, destroys, and enjoys;
he sleeps, embraces, kisses, urinates, and drinks the divine Lord. 42.
The lord who possesses eight wheels shall become the husband of ten million women.
For he is served by the fortune of a sovereign over kings, just like a king himself.
This one, who is omniscient and the embodiment of Vyāsa, is an ocean of all branches of knowledge;
he is the Lord Manava himself, manifest and superior even to Bṛhaspati. (44)
O Lakṣmī, having observed these signs described by me with certainty, and having recognized her as Nārāyaṇī or Hari, one should practice surrender (prapatti). ||45||
One should serve with one's whole being and practice the offering of all one's possessions.
Through devotion, love, and passion, he shall quickly become a partaker of liberation. ||46||

Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter, titled "Description of the Divine Marks and Other Characteristics of the Incarnations of Nārāyaṇa and the Men and Women of the Kṛta Yuga," in the first section, the *Kṛtayugasantāna*, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Lakṣmī said:
O compassionate one, O supreme bliss, O God of gods, O ocean of mercy!
Everything that characterizes Brahmā has been told in its entirety, yet it remains unprecedented. (1)
Indeed, through great merit and compassion, this may be obtained to hear;
for who else but you is truly capable of discerning the marks of the gods? (2)
Whether you appear in the form of a woman or in the form of a man, whenever you are encountered bearing your characteristic marks, then liberation shall come to those women through their offspring.
How could your presence be possible for subjects who are devoid of merit?
As long as it is not directly attained, one should not consider liberation achieved.
How could the virtuous and righteous women of the world ever go with respect to the dwellings of all householders that are so hideous? || 5 ||
Furthermore, because the virtuous and the truly excellent are indifferent to everything, householders will find no opportunity [to serve them]; how then can liberation come to pass? (6)
And due to the differences between the ages, the householder's life has become manifold and filled with deceptions.
It is increased by improper conduct, falsehood, unrighteousness, deceit, and so forth.
One who is intent on nourishing his family, greedy, and indeed of evil conduct.
It causes harm to others, accomplishes one's own ends, and is defiled within. || 8 ||
It involves great exertion for meager enjoyment and is a deception practiced by the nominal stems themselves.
It is always surrounded by children, food, wealth, clothing, and vehicles.
It is worn out by the toil of acquisition and remains occupied day and night.
How can one who is drawn away by objects such as sensual desires attain liberation? ||1.30.10||
Tell me that by which a householder’s family, though devoid of the company of the virtuous and likewise lacking in the performance of good deeds, may attain liberation. (11)
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
"O Lakṣmī, what you have spoken is true regarding a man devoid of merit."
Even when the company of the virtuous is attained, it indeed departs far away due to one's lack of fortune.
Envy, lack of trust, lack of faith, and the absence of devotion—these are indeed [the obstacles].
Atheism and the constant conceit that one is superior to all others; (13)
Furthermore, he should always and in every way perceive only faults [in himself], and he should constantly avoid excessive desire for greatness, honor, and respect. (14)
Ignorance, foolishness, hypocrisy, a tamasic nature, censoriousness, demoniacalness, enmity, and likewise an accumulation of sins—[these are the qualities of the ignorant]. (15)
Lack of meritorious blessings and being deprived of divine fortune—these faults always destroy one's association with the virtuous. (16)
A wife is obtained through merit; a husband is obtained through austerity;
a son is obtained through charity; and prosperity is attained through sacrificial fees.
By means of a lamp, sight is obtained; indeed, by means of ghee, life is obtained.
The metal is obtained by means of juices; knowledge is attained through the scripture. ||18||
Success is attained through effort; knowledge is attained through practice;
heaven is attained through sacrifice; and pleasure is obtained through a wife. ||19||
Happiness is attained through righteousness, and indeed, a lineage is obtained through women.
Fame is attained through good conduct, and serenity is attained through devotion. 1.30.20
A master is won over by service; a greedy man is won over by wealth.
The hungry man is satisfied by foods, but the proud man is broken by pride.
The arrogant man rules through doubt; the hero rushes forward with speed.
Even by performing various such deeds, one does not attain association with the virtuous. ||22||
O virtuous lady, it is said that the company of the righteous is difficult for all to attain.
But for those unfortunate householders who act solely for their own self-interest, [there is no such merit]. ||23||
And for the sake of protection, for the sake of liberation, or indeed for the sake of the next world.
Having indeed completely renounced the state of offering oneself to the Self residing within my own form as being separate from me.
I have created divine devotion to the husband, which accomplishes all goals.
The service rendered by a woman to her husband is here called *pātivratya* (devotion to her husband). ||25||
Service consisting of devotion to her husband took on the form of a maiden.
Holding heaven and liberation in his hands, he placed meritorious deeds at his feet.
Having placed the gods within his body and concealed the sacrifices in his womb,
he placed all the sacred fords upon his palms and the wish-fulfilling trees upon his thighs.
And [he saw] wish-fulfilling cows upon her breasts, as well as a wish-granting gem in her heart.
The creepers of merit are in his hair, and the moon and sun are in his two eyes. ||28||
One should hold the Dharma together with its lineage in the mind and speech, as well as whatever spiritual accomplishments there may be.
Having grasped the four aims of human life by the hair on his head. ||29||
Having properly grasped the guardians of the directions in his ears, the lords up to [the one on] the forehead, and all the incarnations of Śrī Hari within himself; || 1.30.30 ||
Having placed the two *sat* syllables on the tongue and the word "ānanda" in the belly, and having beautifully positioned the two paths called *arci* and *dhūmra* on the two lips; 31.
Delightful, divine, and brilliantly radiant, adorned with a halo of light, she possesses blossoming youth and breasts, being twelve years of age and fully matured. (32)
Having reached the state of the arising of passion, she was moistened and possessed of the menses;
with a golden hue and fine lines of hair, she captivated the beauty of desire. ||33||
Modest, rich in truthful conduct, she is identical in form with Nārāyaṇa.
The goddess is unbroken, eternal, worthy of the highest honor, and subtly fickle. ||34||
The virtuous Satī, known for her devotion to her husband, stood before Hari with her hands joined in *añjali*; having bowed down, she remained there and requested his instruction. (35)
"Command me, O Lord Hari, Nārāyaṇa, Teacher of the World!
For what purpose have I been born, and what task is expected of me? (36)
I, Nārāyaṇa, also joined her together in every way.
"You must indeed always remain together with the group of women. ||37||
In Rādhā, in Ramā, in Lakṣmī, in the Śrīs, and in the virtuous women who are mistresses, who sustain life, who are chaste, and who bestow liberation; ||38||
O fortunate one, O beautiful woman, dwell forever among the womankind.
Dwell among the wives in the house of a married couple. (39)
Because of your dwelling here, this household has become defiled or even sinful.
Being pure, he will go effortlessly to the worlds known as heaven and liberation.
By those [qualities] through which you are propitiated, you too must remain present therein.
O sinless one, you must always remain in the house of the performer of a thousand sacrifices.
O sinless one, you must always remain in the house of those who serve the Pitṛs;
O sinless one, you must always remain in the house of those who know Brahman as the Self. 42.
O sinless one, you must remain in the house of this devotee who has offered himself to you.
O sinless one, you must stay in the house of this Brahmin who performs the six duties.
"O sinless one, you must remain within the body of this woman who is devoted to her lifelong vow."
O sinless one, you must always remain within the body of the Sāṃkhya-yoginīs.
O sinless one, you must remain within the bodies of these virtuous women who have ascended to yoga;
for those whose husband no longer possesses the sacred fire, I am considered their husband. (45)
O sinless one, you must always abide by the duties of widows;
by my power, these worlds shall be led to the imperishable state. 46.
Saying "Om," she accepted this and requested that very thing once again.
"May my form be distinct for each individual body. ||47||
"Otherwise, my attainment of all virtuous women would not be possible.
"So be it," Hari replied; thereafter she assumed the form of Ananta.
Devoted to her husband, that maiden, having been sent away again and again, went wherever she was assigned a dwelling and remained in all those places. (49)
The Self does not enter into many women across many creations;
for those with desire, it provides excellent heavens, but for those without desire, it provides liberation.
The goddess Nārāyaṇī, the consort of Śrī Hari, grants [her blessings] in every house.
And in age after age, throughout the worlds within the cosmic egg, she is the one who carries [souls] across the lower realms.
Therefore, a woman devoted to her husband should be served and honored, for she is indeed my own body.
She is always to be beheld, to be fed, to be honored, and to be bowed down to. ||52||
She too must be awakened as a virtuous woman; she is not inferior to my own body.
In this world, these have been performed by me for the sake of uplifting those who are lowly. ||53||
Virtuous women devoted to their husbands are indeed my own forms.
Their desire was not for the sake of pleasure, but rather for the service of their husband.
Their passion was not for the sake of passion, but for the pleasure of their husband; their delight was not for the sake of enjoyment, but for the sake of producing offspring for their husband.
Their enjoyment does not lead to the pleasure of the husband, but rather to his delight;
their touch is not for the sake of coolness, but rather for the husband’s peace.
Their discharge is not for the sake of attachment, but rather for the satisfaction of the husband.
Their offspring does not lead to suffering for the husband, for it brings him what is desired. ||57||
Their vow is not for their own sake, but indeed for the liberation of their husband.
Their lifespan was not for the sake of creation, but indeed for the husband’s attainment of the further shore. ||58||
Their death is not for the sake of grief, but rather for the purpose of removing the husband's sorrow.
Their blessing leads not to delusion for the husband, but rather to the removal of his delusion.

Their home is always a vessel for merit; their body is always a vessel for the gods; their dharma is always a vessel for happiness; and their attainment is always a vessel for the divine abode. 1.30.60.
Their course leads to the abode of the Imperishable; their intellect is a beautiful night for the moon of Brahman;
their action brings about the state beyond the qualities (nirguṇa); their fortitude attains union with Śrī Hari. 61.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, this means of purification for the sins of householders has been proclaimed by me; let it be understood that it has also been performed. (62)
