To a god, a funeral offering (śrāddha) becomes nectar; to a mortal, food; to an animal, grass;
to a serpent, wind; and in whatever womb [one is reborn], that shall be one's sustenance after death.
Thus, by becoming that very food, the food of the śrāddha is obtained by living beings in all wombs;
therefore, the śrāddha is an eternal dharma.

Thus ends the one hundred and fifty-eighth chapter, titled "The Description of the Fruits of Lunar Days and Constellations, the Worthy Recipient, the Various Ancestors, and the General Nature of What is to be Given at the Śrāddha Ceremony in Dāmodara-kuṇḍa on Revatācala," within the first section, the Kṛtayuga-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: O Lakṣmī, there is the Nārāyaṇahrada where Hari himself,
having arrived together with Lakṣmī and Garuḍa, performed his ritual ablutions.
Long ago in the Kṛta age, O Lakṣmī, there was a Brāhmaṇa born from a portion of Nārāyaṇa who resided in Kuṅkumavāpī and was devoted to the dharma of bhakti.
Brahmadeva, devoted to his wife, came in person on the full moon day of Kārttika for the purpose of visiting Revatādri; he bathed in the Dāmodara pool.
Having performed the *śrāddha* ceremony for Dāmodara according to the rules of the great ritual of worship,
and having worshipped Dāmodara, he held a festival of dance.
With devotion, he fed virtuous brahmins on the twelfth day;
Dāmodara became pleased and desired to grant him his own vision.
Just as he was proceeding forward after bowing down to Dāmodara,
the god Dāmodara appeared before him in the form of a brahmin.
Having met the ascetic in his true form, he said, "Oṃ, obeisance.
Having mutually paid their respects, those two Brahmins proceeded toward the mountain.
As he proceeded toward the front, a traveling pilgrim said:
"O Brahmin, there is a beautiful and great lake up here."
The water, flowing from the subterranean springs, consists of the river Svarṇarekhā;
it issues from within the mountain's belly, is inexhaustible, and is like nectar.
"Having drunk water, we shall go toward the abode of Bhava. Having thus addressed one another, the two brahmins went to the water in the Nārāyaṇa lake.
Beholding the unfathomable forest and the dense foliage of the trees, their minds became serene; they took a moment’s rest.
Upon seeing the sage of the heretics, the mind of that man devoted to his wife became as tranquil as it was during his practice of yoga. (12)
The ascetic, however, having filled his own water-pot with water from that lake and then gone to the shore, made Pativratā drink it.
Then, by drinking that water at that very moment, the sensory functions of Patnīvrata were pacified and returned to their original state.
The functions of the organs of action and knowledge indeed merge into the mind;
that mental function, in turn, goes to dissolution into the sense of "I" (the ego).
Then his sense of "I-ness" (ahaṃbhāva) becomes dissolved into the intellect (buddhi);
and when the intellect itself attains a state of dissolution into the reality of the individual self (jīvātmatattva), [the self likewise dissolves]. || 16 ||
At that moment, he beheld his own state as Brahman—
a divine form consisting of light, all-pervading, and without boundaries.
The form of one's own self, resembling ten million times ten million suns, has been beheld;
by means of the eye of the Self, the Self itself has been seen by itself.
For he is indeed a mass of infinite bliss, a treasure-trove of infinite happiness;
he is filled with infinite wonders and possesses innumerable marvels. (19)
Endowed with infinite sovereignty, he beholds infinite abodes;
his body hairs are like millions of cosmic eggs, each resembling an infinite lotus-atom.
In the meantime, the Brahmin, observing his vow toward his wife, beheld his own self;
then, there he saw the imperishable Brahman, a great abode consisting of splendor.
He beheld that place as being without limit or brilliance, like the abode of the Supreme Brahman;
there stood this pilgrim brahmin, possessing the very form of Nārāyaṇa.
He was seated upon a beautiful, divine golden lion-throne set with jewels,
attended by infinite and endless liberated souls who were devoted to the Dharma.
Surrounded by countless slender celestial nymphs who were dear to him, both of them returned, accepting the honors and worship offered by the local inhabitants.
In the divine assembly hall within the abode of Brahmā, where sacred discourse proceeds,
those two gods arrived and, having been honored by the members of the assembly, took their seats.
They sat down upon two most excellent seats prepared for that purpose,
while the discourse concerning the immersion in the Nārāyaṇa lake was being related.
By that act, liberation is indeed desired for them here in this abode;
and those people who remember us, stationed in the abode of Brahmā, as liberated beings [attain the same]. ||27||
Those devotees who bathe in that lake and those who drink its water—
their fruit shall be eternally inexhaustible, and it arises for them here in this abode.
Those who drink water while repeatedly recollecting us as their ancestors,
their ancestors shall attain liberation in that abode.
Those people who, recollecting Nārāyaṇa, drink the water—
here, Hari himself, as Nārāyaṇa, [bestows his grace] upon them because of that meritorious act.
"He becomes gracious and satisfied; by that we are always satisfied"—having heard such excellent verses as these, both gods [listened]. (31)
Having accepted the hospitality and worship offered by the inhabitants of that place, they then departed for Goloka, the supreme abode filled with Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs.
In the midst of millions of cowherds and cowherdesses, a pilgrim Brahmin was indeed seen by Patnīvraata, standing there in the form of Kṛṣṇa.
Honored by the inhabitants of that place, Kṛṣṇa heard the proclamation of the Rasa dance;
indeed, through the power of bathing in the Nārāyaṇa lake, he reached the temple of Kṛṣṇa.
Many who have been liberated come there and find satisfaction through the contact with the grains;
Kṛṣṇa becomes pleased by the ritual baths, festivals, and other such observances held there. (35)
"Since all of Goloka is eternally satisfied when Kṛṣṇa is pleased,"—
having heard this, those two gods went to the great abode of Vaikuṇṭha.
Likewise saluted by those present and seated upon their own thrones, those two divine brahmins there became Nārāyaṇas. (37)
There was not even an atom’s worth of deficiency in those two, whose essence is Nārāyaṇa; they both became four-armed and were attended by the singular Śrī. (38)
Having been honored and served, those two beheld each other’s form and heard the auspicious, divine praise uttered by Lakṣmī and the others. (39)
For whoever performs bathing, drinking, and libations at the Nārāyaṇa lake for the sake of another, they shall indeed become residents of Vaikuṇṭha.
Hari himself accepts the great worship performed by him;
the glorious Nārāyaṇa will certainly be pleased forever. 41.
"Upon obtaining his favor, we shall always be satisfied—Om!
Having heard these words consisting of bliss, they attained as it were nectar. (42)
In that immortal abode, upon an excellent seat offered by its inhabitants, those two took their seats, being repeatedly honored and respected. (43)
And having heard the story related by Lakṣmī concerning that most divine and great place called Raivata, [situated] in the waters of the Svarṇarekhā river, [the two of them departed]. 44.
By bathing in the Nārāyaṇa lake, by drinking its water, and likewise by performing libations there, the Lord Nārāyaṇa becomes truly satisfied and certainly pleased. (45)
By the grace and satisfaction of that [Lord], we are considered to be eternally satisfied;
for having heard of those two Nārāyaṇas in this world of both the material and the personal. (46)
Having gone to the world of Prādhānapuruṣa, and then to the Avyākṛta world, they likewise went to the world called Hairaṇyakośa and to the Vairāja world. ||47||
In Śvetadvīpa and at Badarī, in the Vaiṣṇava abode of Kṣīra, likewise in Sādāśiva, in Māyāloka, and in the enclosures (āvaraṇas). ||48||
Having gone to the worlds of the lords, they were honored by those dwelling there;
saluted and treated with hospitality, they heard auspicious stories there. (49)
By bathing in the Nārāyaṇa lake, by giving gifts, by drinking its water, and by offering libations;
Nārāyaṇa indeed becomes pleased by virtue of His grace.
We are always satisfied here with that very divine nectar;
it is the lake of Nārāyaṇa, the abode of Brahman, and indeed the imperishable itself. ||5 1||
That water is His abode; it is satisfaction, indeed the very liquid of bliss.
For that which is the happiness and joy of the form of Nārāyaṇa is precisely that. 52.
"By the grace of Hari, we are always satisfied here," said those two Brahmins, who were Nārāyaṇa and Īśvara in human form. (53)
Then, having seen that they had arrived at the world of truth (satyaloka) on the level known as Vairāja,
many of the sages, ancestors, and seers residing there [welcomed them].
And likewise in the assembly of Brahmā, she was present with Sarasvatī and the others, as well as Gāyatrī, Sāvitrī, Asiknī, and Sandhyā. ||55||
With Paliknī and Viriṇī, as well as Śatarūpā and the others, with Rati, Sṛṣṭi, Mohinī, Kadrū, and the women of the ascetics; ||56||
The two gods were saluted, worshipped, honored, and seated upon mats;
having heard their divine discourse, the Nārāyaṇa lake was blessed. (57)
Wherever the Brahmins nourish us through this libation, by that person who has performed the libation there even once on the full moon day of Kārttika. ||58||
Our eternal satisfaction arises from hundreds of billions of lotus-born Brahmās;
yet there are also those twice-born ones who abide on earth, renowned for their devotion to their wives. (59)
There they will perform the ancestral rites (śrāddha), worship, and likewise the libations (tarpaṇa);
by that, inexhaustible satisfaction shall surely arise again, leading to happiness upon happiness.
Having heard this, the two of them then arrived at Kailāsa in the presence of Śiva;
there, they were honored by Pārvatī, Śambhu, and the Gaṇas.
Having been seated upon an excellent throne and having heard that story,
they were at the divine Nārāyaṇa lake in the close presence of Bhavēśvara.
In the former age of Satya, we were indeed gratified by the Brahmins in the waters of the Svarṇarekhā;
we remain satisfied here even until this present time.
"Then these two Brahmins, having gone there, will perform a libation;
at that time, we shall certainly attain great satisfaction once again. (64)
Then, above Dhruva, in the world of Viṣṇu, in the solar orb, in the orb of Agni, and in the regions of Mahas, Janas, and Tapas; ||65||
Having gone to both the world of the guardians of the quarters in heaven and the worlds [below],
they both went to Bhuvarloka, where they heard of the excellent propitiation.
"By the libation performed previously at the Nārāyaṇa lake, we have indeed been satisfied up until now; furthermore, these two will perform it again. (67)
"By that libation, we shall indeed attain eternal satisfaction for many years.
Having heard this, those two abodes of compassion proceeded along the southern path.
The Śrāvaṇa ancestors were seen, and the ancestors who are hungry ghosts (pretas) were seen;
the ancestors of Yama were seen, and the realms of Yama were seen. (69)
And in each of those places, by contact with the body of Nārāyaṇa and through the touch of the wind, those living beings indeed became happy in an instant.
Being greatly distressed, they said to those two: "O Lords, please grant us deliverance; you two are meritorious brahmins, givers of merit, who have come within the range of our vision. (71)
"O auspicious ones, perform for our satisfaction the ancestral rite (śrāddha), the libation (tarpaṇa), and the bath in this Nārāyaṇahrada; thus we shall attain divine satisfaction. (72)
Then those two arrived on the ground, and there, by all the living beings situated within the four pits, they— those abodes of compassion— were entreated for the sake of satiation.
In this manner, by means of his profound meditative absorption, Nārāyaṇa revealed everything, down to the very limits of the netherworld (pātāla), to Patnīvrata in every respect.
The inhabitants there requested the destruction of their suffering at that divine Nārāyaṇa-hrada, where the two [deities] reside in the waters of the Svarṇarekhā.
"And for our sake, O two gods, you shall perform the libation;
by that, eternal satisfaction and liberation shall indeed come to us. (76)
Having heard this request, they arrived within a moment at the place where the Nārāyaṇahrada lake was located, where the twice-born man devoted to his wife resided.
Emerging from his meditative absorption, he was struck with wonder:
"Aha! What have I seen? Where am I, and where indeed have they gone? (78)
"Who is this wandering Brahmin, and what is this dream that has come to pass?"—
at that moment, Hari Nārāyaṇa appeared there with four arms.
The Lord was seated upon the shoulder of Garuḍa, with Lakṣmī resting in His embrace,
and was honored by His attendants with auspicious words proclaiming victory.
Having then beheld the Lord Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, he was filled with joy;
having offered salutations and performed worship, the god prostrated himself at His feet. (8.1)
With a heart bowed in devotion, the brahmin spoke with a faltering voice:
"O Lord, what is this that has been shown? How can a brahmin be a sectarian pilgrim? (82)
What is the cause here, O Kṛṣṇa, that I have been delivered by the compassionate one?
Oh, what great fortune and good luck is mine, that I have attained the sight of Hari! (83)
What do I consider to be a greater fruit of pilgrimage than this:
that you, the Lord Dāmodara Nārāyaṇa himself, are present here? (84)
For my uplift, you assumed the guise of a sectarian teacher;
I bow to you; I am graced by you; I am sought after by you; and I am beloved by you. (85)
There is no deficiency in my liberation, since you, who are considered a caravan-leader, have met with me in person as Nārāyaṇa on the Raivata plateau. (86)
And indeed, within that samādhi, the creation of Brahmā was shown, as well as another, the creation of Īśa, the abodes, and likewise the other, the creation of the worlds. 87.
The creation of Yama and the creation of the Nagas—nothing remains for me to see; indeed, everything has been shown to me. Instruct me, what shall I do for you?
Then Nārāyaṇa spoke to the twice-born man regarding his vow of devotion to his wife:
"Listen, O Brāhmaṇa, to this verse; I shall describe who you are. (89)
He who is Kṛṣṇa himself in Goloka, and his beloved Rukmiṇī—
those two deities [reside] at Kuṅkumavāpī for the sake of the welfare of all people.
The two mental sons named Kambharā and Gopāla were manifested;
Kambharā became Rukmiṇī, and he who was named Gopāla became Kṛṣṇa. (91)
In that Aśvapaṭṭamahātīrtha during the Kṛtayuga,
you indeed were Nārāyaṇa himself, the Lord and Sovereign of Vaikuṇṭha.
Having brought that wife named Pativratā, who was Lakṣmī herself, to that place, you indeed manifested here on the surface of the earth as Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa. ||93||
Formerly, I indeed made both of you Brahmins;
when you alone were the mind-born root of creation upon the earth. (94)
Then indeed, the detailed expansion of your lineage became manifest in the imperishable world of cows (Goloka), in Vaikuṇṭha, and likewise in the unmanifest.
In the nectar, in the white splendor, in the milk, and in the shining ocean—
indeed, throughout the fourteen worlds, those born of your lineage shall exist.
I have shown them to you, yet you are Nārāyaṇa himself—the eternal, all-pervading Lord who grants satisfaction by satiating the living beings of creation. ||97||
Thus I have shown you that which is primary—namely, yourself and those who are your parents.
Now, having arrived here, you must indeed perform worship, libations, and other rites for me. (98)
Because he performed [austerities] at Dāmodara, I, Hari myself, was pleased;
I desired to grant him a vision, and therefore I have brought him here from that place. ||99||
In the beautiful and most splendid Nārāyaṇa-hrada, my sacred bathing place, I have been seen by you in this secluded spot; indeed, this is an ocean of grace.
"O Brahmin, you must not think otherwise regarding my awakening; for you are indeed none other than I.
I am Kṛṣṇa and you are Viṣṇu; we are both the nourishers of the world. (101)
Therefore, since this Nārāyaṇa lake bestows satisfaction upon the worlds, one should perform śrāddha and libations here for the sake of the gratification of all. || 102 ||
"You are the preceptor and I am indeed the patron here;
furthermore, I have cows by my side who yield milk in Goloka. (103)
The trees and creepers yield fruit, and the earth is considered the giver of grain;
every kind of sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) is present here in abundance before me.
"Perform here a great *śrāddha* and a universal libation (*tarpaṇa*");
having thus commanded those two gods, they bathed there in that auspicious lake."
At that time, the gods and goddesses had assembled there,
as did the world-protectors, the guardians of the quarters, the rivers, and the mountains.
Innumerable wish-fulfilling cows arrived from Goloka,
all the Ramās from Vaikuṇṭha, as well as all other holy beings.
The great sages, the ascetics, the trees, the creepers, and the aged—
all have indeed arrived here, bringing the requisites for the śrāddha ceremony.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa himself, indeed Dāmodara, was the sacrificer;
Nārāyaṇa himself, observing the vow of fidelity to his wife, became the performer of the Śrāddha rites.
That which is given with faith is indeed called *śrāddha*, and it is considered a form of worship; that [worship] should certainly be performed for all [deities], beginning with Nārāyaṇa. (1.159.11)
Devotion consisting of the total surrender [of oneself] is considered *śrāddha* toward Nārāyaṇa and others;
devotion consisting of the offering of satisfaction is considered *śrāddha* toward the departed ancestors (*preta*) and others. (11.1)

Thus ends the one hundred and fifty-ninth chapter, titled "The Description of the Brahmin named Patnīvratā’s pilgrimage to Raivatācala, his direct vision [of the Lord] through the worship of Dāmodara and other rites, the vision of all abodes and all worlds in meditative absorption, the manifestation of himself as an incarnation of Nārāyaṇa, and his arrival at the Nārāyaṇa-hrada for the performance of the Śrāddha," in the first section concerning the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga in the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī; thereafter, both Nārāyaṇa and the two brāhmaṇas sat down in the grove of Tulasī at Nārāyaṇaghaṭṭa.
Having made a formal resolve for the sake of the śrāddha ceremony, they were equipped with all necessary utensils and provided with darbha grass,
funeral cakes (piṇḍas), fruits, flowers, milk-rice (pāyasa), cooked food, and other offerings.
Wherever a śrāddha is offered from the hands of the two Nārāyaṇas,
it shall uplift one hundred and seven generations of families belonging to the seven gotras.
The father, the mother, the wife, the sister, the daughter, and likewise the father’s sister and the mother’s sister—these indeed are the seven lineages (gotras). || 4 ||
Twenty-four [muhūrtas] belong to the father, twenty likewise to the mother;
sixteen are to be known for the wife, and twelve are recorded for the sister. || 5 ||
One should know that there were eleven daughters, ten paternal aunts, and eight maternal aunts; thus, the total number of families was one hundred and one.
Having bathed in the Nārāyaṇa lake, those two best of the twice-born performed libations there for the sake of attaining happiness in the three worlds.

May the conscious beings born from the creation of Brahmā, the creation of Īśa, and the creation of the individual soul—the classes of beings such as Bhagavat, Brahmā, Īśvara, and Jīva—be satisfied. (8)
I gratify with water Hari, the Lord of all, who dwells in the imperishable abode of the Supreme Brahman; may he be satisfied for eternal years.
To the Supreme Self, who transcends the imperishable, the Puruṣottama who resides within the self,
by whom all this is pervaded— to Him I offer this morsel of food.
Whatever food there is—whether it be solid (bhakṣya), soft (bhojya), lickable (lehya), or suckable (coṣya)—this fourfold food offered to Śrī Hari may indeed bring satisfaction to Hari. || 11 ||
To that abode which is called the Imperishable (akṣara), which is all-pervading and the object of service—to that abode this water is offered; may it attain eternal satisfaction. 12.

For those who are liberated and those who have been so from time immemorial, those who are yet to be liberated and those who will go [to liberation] in the future, as well as those who abide in form and those who abide in the external world—[all these are encompassed]. || 14 ||
Just as the pearls are released, so too may the goddesses and those others who reside therein attain eternal satisfaction through this water. 15.

For them, there was food consisting of milk-rice as the principal dish along with plantains and other fruits—namely, the four kinds of food: that which is chewed (bhakṣya), that which is eaten (bhojya), that which is licked (lehya), and that which is sucked (coṣya). || 16 ||
O best of the imperishable, this ball of rice has been given by me into your hand;
give it to all of them, so that they may attain eternal satisfaction. (17)
All sovereign powers, virtues, and manifestations, as well as the divine marks of the Form and whatever ornaments there may be— || 18 ||
Indeed, all weapons, various splendors, and spears of manifold forms that abide within the form of Hari [were present]. (19)
With faith, I offer water to those whose forms are both manifest and unmanifest;
I gratify them with this water, may they be satisfied for eternal years.
For them, there was food consisting of the four kinds— namely, that which is chewed, eaten, licked, and sucked— along with milk-rice as the primary dish and fruits such as plantains.
"O Janārdana, this ball of rice is given by me into your hand;
give it to all of them, so that they may attain eternal satisfaction. (22)
May they attain eternal satisfaction through this śrāddha;
through the satisfaction of Hari, may there be eternal satisfaction for those who abide in Hari.
And those sovereign splendors that exist in the imperishable abode and among the liberated, as well as other powers of capability, qualities, and prosperities; ||24||
That which is to be enjoyed, the instruments of enjoyment, and the means of enjoyment—namely, palaces, ramparts, cattle, living beings, gardens, fields, and pleasant places. (25)
Whatever exists is entirely of the nature of the abode of Brahman, and whatever exists is of the nature of liberation.
Indeed, food is of four kinds: that which is to be chewed, that which is to be swallowed, that which is to be licked, and that which is to be sucked. ||26||
Whatever divine and sentient beings always dwell there, may they all attain eternal satisfaction through this water. (27)
To him [he offered] auspicious food of four kinds—eatables, chewables, lickables, and drinkables—consisting of milk-rice and other primary foods, along with plantains and other fruits. (28)
O Janārdana, this ball of food is given by me into your hand;
give it to all of them, so that they may attain eternal satisfaction. (29)
Nārāyaṇa is the imperishable abode; those who are liberated are His manifestations.
May they all attain eternal satisfaction through this śrāddha.

In that regard, those who are Sāṃkhya-yoginīs, as well as devotion (bhakti), worship (upāsti), liberation (mukti), the Command (ājñā), the desire for liberation (mumukṣā), discourse (kathā), news (vārtā), and initiation (dīkṣaṇā); ||| 3.1 ||
Parāvidyā, Ramā, Seva, Jayā, and the other female attendants are there;
likewise, the forest groves, rivers, mountains, and millions of liberated souls.
Gardens and monasteries, grounds designated by letters, the elements, mines, excavations, elevations, and peaks; ||33||
All the celestial palaces likewise contained various classes of attendants:
musicians, dancers, storytellers, and flute-players. (34)
Servants, sacrificial priests, chanters of the Sāmans, those engaged in strenuous efforts, temple attendants, artists, and circles of both renunciant and non-renunciant followers; ||35||
Thus, in the divine, imperishable abode, whatever beings and whatever things exist there, I gratify them with water; may they be satisfied for eternal years.
For them, there was food consisting of milk-rice and other primary dishes, along with plantains and other fruits, as well as the four kinds of food: that which is chewed, eaten, licked, and sucked.
O Janārdana, this ball of food is given by me into your hand;
give it to all of them, so that they may attain eternal satisfaction. (28)
Then, [salutations] to the divine Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who was entreated by Rādhā, Virajā, and others, as well as by Rukmiṇī, and who makes his abode in Goloka. ||39||
"May this water offered by me stand before you for the sake of satisfaction; likewise, may the four kinds of food, including milk-rice, fruits, and so forth, [be present]. (1.160.40)
"O Janārdana, this ball of rice is given by me into your hand;
may they all attain eternal satisfaction through this śrāddha. (41)
Vasudeva and Devakī, Nanda and Yaśodā, as well as Uddhava, Sātyaki, Garga, Akrūra, and other Sātvatas. ||42||
Rukmiṇī, Satyabhāmā, and likewise his beloved Jāmbavatī;
Kālindī, Mitravindā, and another Satyabhāmā. (43)
There were two queens there named Bhadrā and Lakṣmaṇā,
as well as a circle of sixteen thousand wives.
Sarasvatī, the celestial attendants, the cowherds and cowherdesses, the cows who are Surabhis, the wish-fulfilling cows, and the dark-blue bulls. ||45||
Elephants with four tusks, horses, and likewise Garuḍas; trees, creepers, swans, parrots, cranes, and peacocks. ||46||
Those who are musicians, dancers, singers, and servants, as well as those considered to be the friends of Rādhā and the companions of the queens; ||47||
Those who are the thirty-three Gopikās at the sixteenth gate, as well as these hundreds of beloveds of Hari at the other gates— ||48||
The gatekeepers were Śrīdāmā, Sudāmā, Subala, Supārśva, Ratnabhānu, and likewise Śakrabhānu. (49)
Devabhānu, Vasubhānu, Sūryabhānu, Candrabha, and Vīrabhānu, as well as other gopīs, female companions, and cowherds.
Suśīlā, Candrakalā, Yamunā, Mādhavī, Rati, Kadambamālā, Sukuntī, Jāhnavī, and Svayaṃprabhā. (51)
Padmamukhī, Sāvitrī, Gāyatrī, Sumukhī, Sudhā, Padmālayā, Pārijātā, Sugaurī, and Sarvamaṅgalā. ||52||
Kālikā, Kamalā, Durgā, Bhāratī, Sarasvatī, Gaṅgā, Ambikā, Madhumatī, Campāparṇā, and Sundarī. ||53||
Kṛṣṇapriyā, Brahmasatī, Nandinī, and likewise Nandanā;
as well as the attendants (pārṣadas), the Kumāras, and those who are considered the handmaidens (kiṃkarīs). ||54||
The Pārijāta and Vṛnda trees, the imperishable Bhāṇḍīraka banyan tree, the Kalpa trees, and whatever other forests exist that possess consciousness; ||55||
May all sentient beings residing in Goloka, such as Śataśṛṅga and others, attain eternal satisfaction through this śrāddha offering. (56)
I satisfy them with water; may they be satiated for eternal years.
Whatever food there is of the four kinds—eatable, chewable, lickable, and drinkable—[may it be theirs].
"O Janārdana, these rice-balls have been offered by me into your hand;
give them to all of them, so that they may attain eternal satisfaction. (58)
Then, I satisfy with water the Lord Nārāyaṇa, who resides in the abode of Mahāvaikuṇṭha, accompanied by Lakṣmī and Ramā.
May this water offered by me stand before the glorious Lord Hari;
likewise, may the fourfold food, including milk-rice, fruits, and so forth, be accepted.
"O Supporter of the World, this ball of food is given by me into your hand;
accept it and attain eternal satisfaction through this śrāddha. (61)
Mahālakṣmī, Mahāmāyā, and those Ramās who are beloved by Hari; there also are Dharaṇī, Līlā, Vimalā, and Utkarṣiṇī.
Jñānā, Kriyā, Yogā, Prahvī, Satyeśanī, as well as Padmā, Jayā, Pāñcālī, Bhārgavī, Lalitā, and Ramā. (63)
Pārvatī, Prabhā, Māṇikyā, Lakṣmī, Īśvarī, as well as Amṛtā, Pradīpā, Kṛṣṇā, and Kuṃbhastanī. ||64||
Amūlyā, Takṣiṇī, Premā, Caturā, Maṇidhanyakā, Ūjjayinī, Nandanā, Ojasvatī, and Kurujāminī. (65)
Navavratā, Manovārā, Ratnā, Jāhnavikā, as well as Laḍḍumānā, Muktā, Amṛtā, and Mauktikamānadā. (66)
Kastūrī, Śāntidā, Haṃsā, Kāntā, Revā, Savitṛjā, Mūlajā, Rūṭikā, Mañjulikā, Devī, and Nirmalā. (67)
Godāvarī, Rallayātā, Jaṭilā, Dayā, Ramā, Pānapātrī, Pracampā, Miṣṭagopikā—all born of my love. 68.
Manujā, Vañjulīpuṣpā, Mahiṣī, Hemajā, Rājatī, Padmā, Nalinī, and Mādhavī are the beloved consorts of the Supreme Self. (69)
Likewise, there were the devotees Dharmadeva, Nanda, and Sunanda;
as well as Śrutadeva, Jayanta, Vijaya, and Jaya.
Caṇḍa and Pracaṇḍa, Puṣpadanta and Sātvata, Viṣvaksena and Garuḍa, as well as Prabala and Bala. (71)
Kumuda and Kumudākṣa are among the attendants who are there;
as are Kūrma, Śeṣa, Garuḍa, Haṃsa, the Vedas, and the Mantras.
May they all attain satisfaction through this water from the sacred ford, along with food to be chewed, swallowed, licked, and sucked, as well as milk-rice, fruits, and the like. (73)
I offer these rice-balls into the hand of Hari; may they be satisfied—those who play instruments, those who sing, the devotees, and the sūtas, māgadhas, and bards. (74)

The female dancers, the male dancers, the gatekeepers, and those who are attendants; likewise, the female devotees of Nārāyaṇa and others, as well as the male devotees of Nārāyaṇa who are equal to them. (75)
Ramā, Rukmiṇī, Sītā, Padmā, Padmālayā, Śivā,
Sudakṣiṇā, and Suśīlā— these are the female attendants of the Blessed One.
Bhadra and Subhadra, Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ, as well as Śubha;
Puṇḍarīka, Vāmana, Śaṅkukarṇa, and others likewise. (77)
The high-souled and highly fortunate Vaiṣṇavas and Sātvatas, the Siddhas, the Kalpa-trees, and the forests and gardens endowed with consciousness; ||78||
Sāketa, the two Panasa trees, the maidens who are the energies of Viṣṇu, the gatekeepers, the weapons, and the Vedas in the form of attendants. ||79||
Prahlāda, Nārada, Puṇḍarīka, Parāśara,
Ambarīṣa, and Dhruva— these indeed are the dwellers of Vaikuṇṭha.
May all the female servants of Hari, as well as his male and female slaves, attain eternal satisfaction through this water. 8.1.
"O Supporter of the World, these four kinds of food—soft foods, milk-rice, fruits, and so forth—are the funeral cakes (piṇḍas) offered by me into your hand. (82)
Grant these to all of them, so that they may attain eternal satisfaction.
Now, in the second Vaikuṇṭha, beyond the covering of water— ||8.3||
Divya and Nārāyaṇa were his [sons], and his beloveds were the lotus-eyed Vimalā, Sumatī, Śyāmā, Suśīlā, and likewise Kuśalā. (84)
Dīpāvalī, Jayantī, Ramā, Bhāgīrathī, as well as Sukhā, Kanakā, Vidyullatā, and Candrakalā; ||85||
There were hundreds of thousands of women and divine-bodied attendants,
as well as Bharata, Śatrughna, Lakṣmaṇa, Śeṣa, and Śarada.
The city was Devavatī; situated therein were millions of divine lords, celestial birds, divine trees, and likewise weapons. (87)
May they all attain satisfaction through that water and that food;
the fourfold food consists of milk, cooked grains, ripe fruits, and so forth. (88)
"O Supporter of the World, these balls of rice have been placed by me in your hand;
give them to all of them, so that they may attain eternal satisfaction. (89)
Then [he beheld] the third Vaikuṇṭha, the abode known as Śvetadvīpa;
there he saw Śrī Hari Nārāyaṇa, accompanied by Lakṣmī.
With these excellent waters from the sacred fords, I offer libations; may he be satisfied.
I offer the four kinds of sweet food, milk-rice, fruits, and so forth. (91)
"I offer this; let the funeral cake (piṇḍa) given by me be accepted.
May Sanaka and the other great sages, as well as the yogis, be present there. (9.2)
Voḍhu, Pañcaśikha, and he known as Sanatsujāta, as well as other sages such as Tanu and the rest who dwell there. (93)
Other virtuous women and virtuous men, as well as the ascetics who dwell there—
Ananta, Vainateya, Haṃsa, Karī, and the excellent Vaiṣṇavas.
The Great Goddess Īśāvāsya, Jāhnavī, Kamalā, Ramā, Sāvitrī, as well as Śāntā, Kāntā, Brāhmī, and Sarojanī. (95)
And likewise, the female slaves there were Wisdom, Intelligence, Fortitude, Forbearance, Faith, Retention, Tranquility, Learning, Discernment, and Memory. (96)
Rain, intellect, thought, and the forest-glories are indeed her handmaidens;
and those conscious ascetics who have attained liberation are her male and female servants. (97)
May they all attain eternal satisfaction with this water,
along with the four kinds of delicious food, milk-rice, fruits, and so forth.
"O Janārdana, these funeral cakes have been placed by me in your hand;
give them to all those [ancestors], so that they may attain eternal satisfaction. (99)
Then [he beheld] Nārāyaṇa, the teacher of the world, who dwells in the ocean of milk,
accompanied by Lakṣmī and Śeṣa, and attended by Garuḍa and others.
I satiate him with water; may this Janārdana be satisfied for me.
O Lord, I offer you this milky rice-ball along with its fruit in my hand.
I gratify you along with your devotees; may you be satisfied for eternal years!
Mārkaṇḍeya, Bali, Bāṇa, Aśvatthāman, Hanumān, and Varāha [are likewise gratified]. (102)
Nimi, Bibhīṣaṇa, Paraśurāma, Vyāsa, Manu, as well as Satyavrata, Nanda, Gaya, and other attendants.
And other servant goddesses were there: Narmadā, Tapatī, Tuṅgabhadrā, Kāverī, Gaṅgā, and likewise Godāvarī.
The Sindhu, the Phalgu, the Gaṇḍakī, the Tāmraparṇī, the Sarasvatī, the Karatoyā, the Karmanāśā, the Sābhramatī, and the Gomatī.
Ojasvatī, Bhadrāvatī, Sarayū, Svarṇarakṣikā, Indradyumna, Puṣkara, and likewise Nārāyaṇasara. ||106||
Aśvapaṭṭasara and the Mānasa lake;
likewise, there are rivers, streams, lakes, and oceans.
To those long-lived, embodied devotees who dwell there,
[he offered] water for Nārāyaṇa and a śrāddha consisting of successful milk-rice (pāyasa).
O Sustainer of the World, I place these rice-balls (piṇḍas) into your hand;
give them to all of them, so that they may attain eternal satisfaction. 109.
Then [he saw] Vāsudeva and likewise Saṃkarṣaṇa, who abide in the abode of the indeterminate, who delight in the Infinite (bhūman) worshipped by Rāmā, and who are served by their devotees.
Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Mahākāla, and Puruṣa;
likewise, the Mahāpuruṣa and the Prakṛtipuruṣa are present here.
I indeed gratify with water Pradhānapuruṣa, Mahāviṣṇu, and Mahāramā, together with their male and female servants.
May they all attain eternal satisfaction through this śrāddha, with the four kinds of food, such as milk-rice, boiled rice, fruits, and so forth.
[He saw] the Lord Ramā-Nārāyaṇa, established in the abode of immortality,
as well as the two ascetics Nara and Nārāyaṇa residing at Badarikāśrama.
Matsya, Kūrma, Varāha, and those dwelling in their respective abodes;
Dattātreya, Kapila, Pṛthu, Haṃsa, and Vāmana.
Ṛṣabha, Nṛhari, Paraśurāma, Yajña, the Kumāras,
Hayagrīva, Nārada, Hari, Buddha, and likewise Manu.
I satisfy Vyāsa, those residing in their respective abodes, the liberated attendants (pārṣadas), as well as male and female servants and devotees, with water.
May they all attain eternal satisfaction through this śrāddha, with the four kinds of food, such as milk-rice, boiled rice, fruits, and so forth. 118.
"These balls of rice have been offered by me, descending into your hand;
give them to all of them, so that they may attain eternal satisfaction. (11.9)
Hiraṇyagarbha, Vairāja, the lords of the eight enclosures,
Viṣṇu, Sadāśiva, Mūla, Māyā, and whatever other principles (tattvas) there may be.
And those respective deities, as well as their conscious qualities,
and other non-supreme conscious beings who have gone to their various respective places.
I indeed satisfy with water the Vairājas, the Cetanas, and the Sauras; likewise the Āgneyas, the Cetanas, and all the worlds of Īśa.
May they all attain satisfaction through the fourfold provisions of food, such as milk-rice, cooked rice, fruits, and so forth, by being offered into the hands of Nārāyaṇa. 123.
"These balls of rice have been offered by me; may they be satisfied for eternal years—those others who have a thousand mouths, and those Viṣṇus with hundreds and so forth of faces."
May the Brahmās, as well as the Śambhus and those with various faces, numbering in the tens of millions and accompanied by their Śaktis, be satisfied with the waters of this sacred ford.
"O Janārdana, these funeral cakes (piṇḍas) have been offered by me into your hand with milk-rice, four kinds of cooked food, and likewise with offered fruits and other offerings. (126)
Grant these to all of them, so that they may attain eternal satisfaction:
the three qualities, the fourfold internal organs, and the ten external organs.
May the ten elements, the ten vital breaths, and the conscious faculties—the instruments of action—attain satisfaction through the food, fruit, and water that have been offered. (128)
Liṅga, Bāṇa, Sthālā, Śambhu, Satī, Kārtika, Gaṇeśa, Kṣema, Lābha, Ṛddhi, Siddhi, and Śivayogin. (129)
The Yoginīs, Hanumān, Durgā, and the goddesses Kumārikās;
the eleven Rudras, ten million [attendants], and the twelve hundred luminaries.
Gaṅgā, Vīrabhadra, Jalandhara, Tāraka, Tārakākṣa, Gaja, Mahiṣa, and Caṇḍa as well. (131)
Pracaṇḍa, Nanda, Upananda, Śṛṅgin, Bhṛṅgirīṭika, Kirīṭin, Candramas, Vahni, and Maṅgala as well. || 1.32 ||
Durvāsas, Kālabhīru, Viṣamuṇḍa and other excellent attendants, as well as the trident, Vāsuki, the rudrākṣa, and the bull [are present]. || 133 ||
The peacock, the mouse, the lion, Kailāsa, and its various manifestations; Karṇaghaṇṭa, Meghanāda, and other hosts of attendants numbering in the tens of millions—[these are his]. (13.4)
And those who are the powers (śaktis) of Pārvatī, such as Mahākālī and others, as well as Kailāsa and all the conscious beings belonging to that [realm] who are devotees of Śiva (śaivas). || 135 ||
May all those male and female servants be satisfied with the waters of the sacred ford, as well as with the four kinds of food, fruits, drinks, and whatever milk-rice (pāyasa) is suitable.
"O Janārdana, these rice-balls have been offered by me into your hand;
give them to all those [ancestors], so that they may attain eternal satisfaction. (1.37)
May all those who are devotees of Śiva be satisfied for eternal ages;
as well as Brahmā, the sons of Brahmā, and those who are the wives of Brahmā.
Sarasvatī, Gāyatrī, Sāvitrī, Viriṇī, as well as Asiknī, Paliknī, Śatarūpā, and Kadrukī. || 139 ||
Rati, Sandhyā, Sṛṣṭi, Vidyā, Avidyā, and Mohinī; and likewise the eighty-eight thousand Bālakhilyas.
Likewise, there were sixty thousand others known as the Bālakhilyas, as well as ten thousand five hundred Haryaśvas and Śabalāśvas. || 141 ||
And there were five hundred and one sons born of the lineage of Brahmā, as well as the celestial sages headed by Nārada and the great ṛṣis headed by Sanaka. || 142 ||
The seven sages, Dakṣa and the others, merit and demerit along with their lineages, as well as the Agniṣvātta, Barhiṣad, Ājyapa, and Somapa [ancestors]. (143)
The Pitṛs, likewise the Meghas, the four [Rudras], Madana, Rati, the five arrows, the flowers, and also the Brahmachārins. (144)

Those who have an upward stream (ūrdhvasrotas), as well as those who have gone to the world of truth (satyaloka)— the possessors of knowledge, ascetics, renunciants, and likewise those who have renounced— [attain this].
May those who have made their abode in the world of Brahmā, as well as the Sādhyas and the virtuous ones (Sādhus),
all attain eternal satisfaction through this śrāddha.
I gratify [you] with the waters of the Svarṇarekhā, with excellent milk-rice and other offerings, with the four kinds of food, fruits, and drinks; may you be satisfied for eternal years. 147.
May these rice-balls, offered into the hand of Hari, satisfy you;
and likewise those who are other sages and those belonging to the various Manvantaras. (148)
Vyāsa and the disciples of Vyāsa, sages endowed with the splendor of Brahman, Brahmins devoted to their wives, as well as the social classes and the stages of life (varṇas and āśramas). 149.
The Vedas, the Śāstras, the Ākhyānas, and even the Upavyākhyānas; the histories of the East and the West, as well as biographies, narratives, and tales. || 1.160.15 ||
The meters, the musical notes, the *rāgas*, the *rāgiṇīs*, and the compositions; the dramatic modes, the styles, as well as hunger, thirst, fire, and the bodily constituents. || 1591 ||
May those who possess form and consciousness attain satisfaction through these waters;
may they be satiated by milk-rice, cooked rice, and the four types of food for eternal years.
The sages who dwell among the great people and practice austerities, as well as the ancestors;
the year, the months, the fortnights, the days, and the nights. || 153 ||
Pāvaka, Pavamāna, Pāṅkteya, Paktipāvana, Gārhapatya, Dākṣiṇātya, Āvasathya, and Agnihotraja. || 154 ||
Ārārtrika, Nāciketa, Bārhaspatya, Cūllija, Vānaprasthya, Sānyasya, Bhauma, and also Udarya. (155)

The celestial fire, the one born from ore, the corpse-fire, the cremation-ground fire, the forest fire, the wild fire, the fire born of sacrifice, the flame-mouthed fire, and likewise the submarine fire. || 156 ||
These indeed are those who are called Pitṛs, as well as Vaiśravaṇa and the others;
likewise the Pretas, the Pitṛs of Yama, the hell-beings, and those belonging to Śravaṇa. || 157 ||

There are also messengers and other ancestors, as well as those who undergo torments; there are those born in one's own lineage and those born in other lineages, including those among the stationary beings. 158.
Likewise, those born from the wind who have arisen among moving beings, and the Pitṛs, as well as the Munis, Ṛṣis, Āryas, and others, who appear differently in every Kalpa; || 1.59 ||
"May these ancestors be satisfied by these waters for eternal years.
[I offer] the four kinds of food, such as milk-rice, fruit, and so forth."
I offer the food of sages and the food fit for the worthy into the hand of Hari.
O Janārdana, these rice-balls have been given by me into your hand.

Grant these to all of them so that they may attain eternal satisfaction—those who are the guardians of the quarters, the guardians of the worlds, and likewise those who are the guardians of heaven. (162)
O Indra, today there are the eight [siddhis] beginning with Aṇimā, as well as the eight supernatural powers (siddhis) beginning with Aṇimā;
likewise, the eight Vasus beginning with Āpa, the eight directions, and the nine planets.
The nine treasures (nidhi), the Vidyādharas, the six Mothers, Tārās, Ketus, minor stars, and Dhūmraketus; || 1.64 ||
The twelve Suns, the twelve Ādityas, the three Moons along with their digits, the twenty-seven lunar mansions, and the thirty-three deities. || 165 ||
The Maruts, the Vidyadharas, the Sadhyas, and the Visvedevas;
the Siddhas, Caranas, Gandharvas, Sutas, Magadhas, and Bandins. || 166 ||
May the Kinnaras, men, and women be satisfied with the water offered;
and may they receive food, nectar-like milk-rice, cooked grains, ripe fruits, and the like.
All four kinds of food, as well as many varieties of drinks—these morsels have been placed by me into your hand, O Janārdana. (16.8)
Grant them, and to all of them, eternal satisfaction;
may they all attain eternal satisfaction through this śrāddha. || 169 ||

Those who have gone to the Bhuvarloka and likewise those who dwell in the intermediate space (antarīkṣa), the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas who are supported by the wind and whose bodies are composed of wind; || 1.160.170 ||
Bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, kūṣmāṇḍas, and vināyakas; vetālas, bhairavas, and others, as well as mārakas and janakas. || 171 ||
The Mātulas, Rāhavas, and others who are dark-colored and black;
as well as the Ḍākinīs, Śākinīs, Yoginīs, and Bhakṣiṇīs. (172)
Vetālinī, Khañjinī, Śītalā, and likewise Mātṛkā; Mārikā, Bālikī, Kṛtyā, Hikkā, and also Tānikā. || 173 ||
The attractors, the great plagues, fevers—both cold and hot—as well as diseases, royal maladies, intense torments, old age, and so forth. || 1.74 ||
States, powers, specific incapacities, as well as the sick;
mantras, tantras, and yantras; oaths and bonds. (175)
Nooses, missiles, weapons, lightning, and likewise foul weather; the confusion of the directions, firebrands whirled into circles, clouds, mists, and blinding darkness. (176)
Likewise, whirlwinds, portents, earthquakes, winds and rains, calamities, assailants, and those such as showers of dust— [all these shall cease].
May they all always attain satisfaction with these waters of the sacred fords;
may they be gratified by these waters and offerings, remaining satisfied for eternal years.
Food made of black gram, food consisting of rice and sesame, and food from the air are of the *tāmasa* nature;
various kinds of food are *rājasa*, and milk-rice (*pāyasa*) is of four types.
"I give food, fruit, and drink, each according to what is appropriate;
with those various foods, I have offered the funeral cakes (piṇḍas) into the hands of Hari."
Grant these to all of them, so that they may attain eternal satisfaction;
may they all be forever satisfied by this *śrāddha* offering. 18.1.
Those dwelling on the earth—whether born from a womb, born from an egg, born from sweat, or born from a sprout—all sentient beings, as well as Brāhmaṇas and Kṣatriyas, [are likewise]. 182.

Vaiśyas, Śūdras, those of mixed castes, Cāṇḍālas, and likewise those who have fallen [from their status]; those born in the natural order (anuloma), those born in the inverse order (pratiloma), the hairless ones, and the half-human beings (ardhamānava). || 183 ||
Those who are lifelong celibates, householders, forest-dwellers, and likewise renunciants;
as well as Śaivas, Vaiṣṇavas, Śāktas, Vaidikas, and those others [who follow different paths]. || 184 ||
Those born from cow-hides, those born from water, those born from land, and likewise those born from the sky;
small living beings and large ones, as well as insects, winged creatures, and birds. (185)
Likewise, the deities of the household, extending even to the blades of grass;
the village gods, the forest gods, and the guardians of the fields as well. (186)
Within the body are the deities of the six cakras, and in the skull reside the gurus and deities;
likewise, there are forests, mountains, wildernesses, and rivers.
Rivers, ponds, groves, and lakes; ditches and likewise natural excavations, as well as oceans and highlands. || 188 ||
Battlefields, desert regions, and all places of the gods;
sacred trees, temple-shrines, sanctuaries, and riverbanks. || 189 ||

The temples of the goddesses have become dilapidated; the lands, villages, hamlets, and market towns, as well as the cities, royal capitals, ancient strongholds, and great metropolises [have likewise fallen into ruin].
Whatever conscious beings are there, including those who preside over them, may they all forever attain satisfaction through these waters that have been offered. (191)
And for them, [he provided] various kinds of food: those belonging to fire, to wind, to water, and to earth, as well as those produced by rain and those that were transformed.
With the four kinds of food suitable for consumption, such as milk-rice and the like, as well as with vapors, droplets from clouds, the juices of trees, and mud. || 193 ||
With the cool rays of the moon, with the fiery rays of the sun, with other poisons such as fruits and the like, and even with froth, I perform this śrāddha here; may you be satisfied.
May these waters please them; may they be satisfied for eternal years.
These rice-balls, which bestow satisfaction upon them, have been offered by me into the hand of Hari.
Grant these to all of them, so that they may attain eternal satisfaction;
likewise for the mothers, the maternal grandmothers, and the maternal great-grandmothers.
One should likewise [offer to] the fathers, grandfathers, and great-grandfathers;
brothers, sisters, brothers' wives, sons-in-law, maternal uncles, and others.
[He saw] his brothers' sons and others, his wives, the family members of his father-in-law, his father's sisters, his mother's sisters, and his daughters who were excellent yoginīs. || 198 ||
I gratify his sons, daughters, grandsons, and others with water and other offerings, as well as with foods such as milk-rice, the four types of cooked grains, and fruits. (199)
I perform the śrāddha for them; may they attain eternal satisfaction.
O Janārdana, these rice-balls have been offered by me into your hand.
Give these to all of them so that they may attain eternal satisfaction;
I gratify them with water and food—may they be satisfied for eternal years. (20.1)
The Prācetasas, Nāciketas, Mārutas, Kālakeyas, Yāmyas, Saṃśaptakas, Vārkṣas, those born from the earth, Śalabhas, and so forth—[he conquered them all]. (202)
Likewise, he [slew] the Daityas, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas dwelling in the worlds such as Talātala,
as well as the serpents, reptiles, Nāgas, and others who reside there.
I gratify them with cool, desired water, food, fruits, and milk-rice; I offer these funeral cakes (piṇḍas) to them, so that they may be satisfied for eternal years.
I propitiate my chosen deity, as well as Brahmā, the supreme preceptor, and the teacher, with the waters of sacred fords, milk-rice offerings, and fruits. (205)
May they all attain eternal satisfaction through this śrāddha.
O Janārdana, this piṇḍa is offered by me into your hand. (206)
Grant these to all of them, so that they may attain eternal satisfaction: "All this is pervaded by the Lord; may the Supreme Lord be gratified. (207)

Those who belong to the past, the future, and the present, and those who have traversed the paths of coming and going—I gratify them with food and water; may they be satisfied for eternal years. (208)
Likewise, those dwelling in the netherworld and those residing upon the Lokāloka mountain—may they all attain satisfaction through these preparations of milk, fruits, water, and the like. (209)
And those vital breaths that are unremembered, inattentive, and yet to come—I satisfy them all likewise with fruits, food, and water. (1.160.210)
"O Janārdana, these rice-balls have been given by me into your hand;
give them to all of them, so that they may attain eternal satisfaction. (2.11)
The Śrāddha performed by Nārāyaṇa and caused to be performed by Nārāyaṇa satisfied the three worlds; indeed, they attained eternal happiness.
And all those who had gathered there, having received eternal satisfaction, returned each to their own world; thus the śrāddha was made complete.
Through the constant offering of libations (tarpaṇa) to them, there arises eternal satisfaction;
likewise, for the performer of the śrāddha, there is nourishment, sovereignty, long life, and progeny.
Varied prosperity attends him, and liberation attends him in due course;
[he is honored] by the deities, by the ancestors, and even by the great yogis. (215)
Salutations always be offered to Svāhā and to Svadhā;
this mantra, which increases prosperity, longevity, and strength, should be recited during a Śrāddha ceremony.
I shall proclaim the auspicious Saptārcis, which grants all desires and by means of which the ancestors are gratified through recitation and observance.
I always bow down to those ancestors of radiant splendor—both formless and embodied—who are absorbed in meditation and possess the eye of yoga. 218.
I bow to those who are the progenitors of Indra and the other gods, as well as of Bhaga and Mārīci, of the seven ṛṣis, and of the Pitṛs—the bestowers of all desires. (219)
Having paid homage to Manu and the other lords of the gods, as well as to the Sun and the Moon, and indeed to all those ancestors who bestow prosperity; 1.160.220.
Then, with palms joined in reverence, I pay homage to the ancestors and grandfathers of the stars, including their courses and so forth, as well as to Heaven and Earth.
With palms joined in reverence, I bow to those who are the progenitors of the divine sages, who are honored by all the worlds, and who are the constant bestowers of fearlessness.
With palms joined in reverence, I bow to Prajāpati, Kaśyapa, Soma, and Varuṇa, and to the Lords of Yoga.
Salutations to the seven groups of ancestors in the seven worlds;
and salutations indeed to the Self-Existent Brahmā, who possesses the eye of yoga.
A person endowed with this ritual obtains three boons;
on earth, the ancestors bestow food, long life, and sons.
He who, endowed with supreme devotion, full of faith, and having conquered his senses,
recites the Saptarṣi [mantra], shall become the sole sovereign of the earth.
What more need be said? This is a place that grants liberation to all, [yet it remains] surrounded by horned beasts, fanged creatures, serpents, poison, fire, women, and water.
One who dies while playing and has no other refuge is born in the womb of a preta;
likewise, one who dies having done what is displeasing to the nāgas, or one struck by lightning.
Some were indeed executed by the king himself on charges of theft;
others, while sporting with the wives of others, were killed out of hatred by those husbands. || 22 || 9 ||
Having engaged in conflict with those who were unequal, mixed castes, and outcasts such as the Cāṇḍālas,
they were slain by them and took refuge among those very Cāṇḍālas and others.
Those who give cows, fire, or poison, as well as heretics of cruel intellect,
generally [meet their end] through anger by means of poison, fire, weapons, hanging, or water.
Those who cause [beings] to fall from a mountain or a tree, those who are deeply afflicted, those who live by ignoble crafts, and those who preside over the five slaughter-houses; ||232||
Those who were born as serpents in a sacrifice, those who were mostly wretched or eunuchs, those struck by the punishment of the virtuous, and those who were slain by Brahmins; ||233||
Those who are perpetrators of great sins, those who have fallen, and those who cause intermixture of castes—whether dead or alive, whether by their own action or by that of another. (234)
"Indeed, they attain purity by bathing in the waters of the Nārāyaṇa lake.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, I have related to you this supreme majesty of the lake.
It pacifies all sins and bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation upon the ancestors;
the man who listens to it with devotion during a śrāddha ceremony, on a festival day, or daily [attains these benefits]. (236)
Or, O lady of beautiful hips, one who causes this to be heard shall also become a partaker of the world of Brahmā.
This is a meritorious rite for well-being, bringing wealth and granting heaven to men. (237)
This divine rite, consisting of worship and śrāddha offerings dedicated to the two Hari-s, bestows fame, longevity, and increases one's sons and grandsons. (238)
Having bathed in the Dāmodara pool and likewise in the Mṛgīkuṇḍa, and having bathed in the Nārāyaṇahrada, one should perform the Śrāddha; such is the established rule. (239)

Thus ends the one hundred and sixtieth chapter, titled "The Description of the Performance of Universal Śrāddha and Tarpaṇa for the Two Nārāyaṇas in the Waters of the Nārāyaṇa Lake, the Praise of the Seven-Flamed Fire (Saptārcis), and the Resulting Fruits," in the first section on the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga within the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, concerning the locations of Brahmaloka, Goloka, Vaikuṇṭha, Śveta, Badarikāśrama, Amṛta, Avyākṛta, the Ocean of Milk, and so forth, as well as the Golakhagola and Bhūgola.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī, then the two gods Dāmodara and Narāyaṇa, having fed all the assembled Brahmās and deities, [proceeded]. || 1 ||
They both accepted that grace and the milk-rice (pāyasa) offered to Hari;
then Dāmodara spoke of the majesty of Nārāyaṇa.
This is the most secret sacred field, bringing happiness to all living beings;
it bestows liberation upon all creatures, whether they be devotees of Viṣṇu or Śiva.

A killer of a Brahmin, a killer of a cow, a killer of one's mother, a killer of one's teacher, a killer of a child, and a killer of a woman—by bathing here in this lake, they are liberated; of this there is no doubt.
Having bathed here and become a doer of good deeds, one who dies shall go to the supreme state;
those devotees of Hari who dwell in this sacred field are indeed performers of meritorious acts.
Indeed, those capable of uplifting others are considered equal to Nārāyaṇa;
having torn asunder the web of birth and bondage, they lead others to the abode of Hari.
The *iḍā* is considered to be powerful and auspicious, while the *piṅgalā* is regarded as beneficial; there is the *suṣumṇā*, known as Svarṇarekhā, through which one may attain liberation.
Indeed, where the attainment of liberation occurs without effort—even for those of various castes, those who perform forbidden acts, and the despised Cāṇḍālas—[there is no doubt]. (8)
For those whose bodies are filled with sins as well as the most heinous crimes,
the sacred field of Vastrāpatha is considered the supreme remedy.
I lead all those who are wicked, blind, wretched, miserable, sinful, and doers of evil deeds to the supreme goal through my compassion.
Those men who have indeed gone to Vastrāpatha, having performed great meritorious deeds, become truly imperishable, free from old age, and bodiless (liberated). || 11 ||
Whether through ignorance or knowledge, whatever unwholesome action has been committed by a woman or a man out of a corrupt mind, [may it all be purified]. (12)
For one who has entered Vastrāpatha, all that [sin] shall be reduced to ashes;
he is as if always sacrificing with sacrifice and always bestowing gifts. (13)
A man who dwells on Mount Raivata is always an ascetic;
on Mount Raivata, penance and truth are practiced by all living beings with their whole being.
That destination which is ordained for men who dwell on the Raivata mountain is not attained at Kurukṣetra, nor at Gaṅgādvāra, nor at Puṣkara. (15)
Those of evil deeds who are touched by the dust raised by the wind while it rests eternally upon Mount Raivata indeed attain the supreme goal. (16)
He who dwells on Mount Revata with a self-controlled mind and concentrated focus is considered equal to one who subsists on air alone, even if he were enjoying the three worlds. ||17||
One who dwells on Mount Raivata, eating meat sparingly and having conquered the senses,
has indeed performed the very observances of the Cāturmāsya.
Having overcome the fear of birth and death, he attains the supreme goal;
he proceeds to the meritorious state of ultimate liberation as well as the state of yoga.
Indeed, the goal of Brahman cannot be attained even in hundreds of other births;
yet it is reached through the strength of Raivata and likewise by the power of Śrī Hari.
He who remains on Mount Raivata for one month, eating but a single meal a day,
destroys in that single month all the sin committed throughout his entire life.
He who does not abandon Raivata even when struck by obstacles shall cast off old age and death, for this birth is indeed perishable.
But those who serve Mount Raivata until the fall of their bodies, upon death, indeed go to the divine worlds by means of a swan-vehicle. ||23||
Even a person whose mind is pervaded by saṃsāra and who has abandoned the practice for liberation, if he dies on Mount Raivata, shall not enter saṃsāra again. (24)
This supreme sacred ford on earth is the cause of both heaven and liberation;
for one who meets their death there, there is no doubt that they attain emancipation. (25)
The state which a yogi might attain after a thousand previous births,
one attains as supreme liberation upon death on Mount Raivata.
Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras, and those of mixed castes; even worms, Mlecchas, and those of impure, sinful births. ||27||
Even insects, ants, and whatever other beasts and birds there may be—
when they meet death through time, they too are remembered as lords of gods.

Whether devoid of desire or possessed of desire, even one who has entered the womb of an animal, by giving up their life on Mount Raivata, becomes a partaker of liberation; there is no doubt in this matter. ||29||
Those who have made their dwelling on Mount Raivata, who bathe in the waters of the Svarṇarekhā, and whose minds and lives are centered on Dāmodara, are undoubtedly liberated while living. 1.161.30.
At the time of death on Mount Raivata, Hari himself as Dāmodara imparts the Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa mantra as an ear-whispered prayer.
With a heart of extreme clarity, one should personally [recite it] into the right ear of anyone who is about to die, or indeed of anyone else, for the sake of the dweller on Mount Raivata.
I shall impart my mantra to you; he will certainly become liberated.
No one who dies at Dāmodara ever goes to hell.
All those who are favored by Vāmana attain the supreme goal;
having abandoned their vital breaths here, they never again experience [rebirth] anywhere.
The first is Revatī-kuṇḍa; after that is the one called Dāmodara;
the third is named Nārāyaṇa; and the fourth is Mṛgī-kuṇḍa. ||35||
The fifth is Bhavakuṇḍa, and the sixth is Gaṅgā Gomukhī;
the seventh is Kamaṇḍalu, and the eighth is named Bhairava. (36)
Mārkaṇḍeya is the tenth, and Dattakṛt is the eleventh;
these have been bathed in, drunk from, seen, and even tasted. (37)
For even by touching them, they purify people and lead them to liberation;
their goal is infinite, the very goal that is esteemed by yogins. (38)
Among them, liberation is declared to be the purifier for those who have fallen;
even there, the lake of Nārāyaṇa is the most excellent of all the sacrificial pits.
Just as the Nārāyaṇa lake is, so too is the Dāmodara lake,
where the eternal presence of Śrī Hari and Vāmana resides.
Whatever fruit is recorded for ten Aśvamedha sacrifices, that the righteous-souled one obtains by bathing there; of this there is no doubt. (41)
But he who, having observed the fast, gratifies Brahmins and virtuous men, certainly obtains the fruit of the Sautrāmaṇī sacrifice. ||42||
There, by the offering of a lamp, the sense-faculties flash forth like wisdom; by the offering of an aratnika-lamp, health is always produced. (43)

What need is there for much speaking on this matter? For one who performs duties such as dharma and the like, dedicating them specifically to Śrī Hari, the fruit thereof shall indeed be infinite. (44)
The merit of performing ten horse-sacrifices is proclaimed for the offering of flowers;
the fruit of the agnihotra sacrifice for incense; and the fruit born of the gift of land for fragrant scents.
In this regard, the fruit of gifting a cow is proclaimed for sweeping;
for anointing, it is tenfold, and for garlands, it is remembered as tenfold again.
It is held that [the merit] is a thousandfold when performed with song and a hundred-thousandfold when performed with instrumental music;
those who worship and praise Dāmodara on Mount Raivata [attain this]. 47.
Freed from all sins, they go to the eternal Vaikuṇṭha;
even after hundreds of millions of kalpas, there is no rebirth for them. ||48||
But those who, having attained meditative absorption, being liberated in soul and composed, perform the recitation of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa with their senses restrained; ||49||
Those best of men, having attained their purpose, dwell eternally on Mount Raivata;
having delivered infinite living beings, they proceed to the world of Viṣṇu.
On the full moon day of Māgha as well as Kārttika, virtuous women and virtuous men were seen,
touched, bowed to, honored, and likewise fed.
By whatever means they were served, massaged, attended to, or carried; by whichever people they were thus propitiated. (52)
By them, Ramā was propitiated, and Nārāyaṇa was propitiated;
for there, Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa indeed dwell forever.
In the form of a virtuous woman and a virtuous man, Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa himself wanders in Vastrāpatha for the sake of the welfare of the people. (54)
Through their grace, every mental undertaking is accomplished;
indeed, both worldly and otherworldly goals are certainly achieved. ||55||
By means of body, mind, speech, service, food, and by offerings—by those who [act] here on Mount Raivata at Vastrāpatha. (56)
When the virtuous are properly served, all the deities are effectively served;
Hari himself, being served, grants liberation to his devotee.
Those people who revile the great holy site of Vastrāpatha, as well as the virtuous men, virtuous women, and the deities, will certainly go to hell. (58)
The Blessed One, as Nṛsiṃha, having arrived at Mount Raivata, took up residence in a cave on the banks of the Svarṇanadī. (59)
That place is merit-bestowing and grants liberation; even its dust destroys sin.
What more need be said? In this great holy site, even every single grain of dust [possesses such power].
On Mount Raivata in Vastrāpatha, every leaf, flower, blade of grass, and so forth is divine, a destroyer of sins, and a bestower of liberation; of this there is no doubt. (61)
By King Nārta, a portion known as Saurāṣṭra was established from Goloka in the central abode;
furthermore, [another portion] was taken from the throat of Hari there.
The mountain Raivata, which was brought from the Kaustubha jewel, is made of fire-essence (taijasa);
furthermore, a portion of the constellation Revatī is also situated there.
Furthermore, there are the divine peaks of Meru— Mandara, Kumuda, Aruṇa, and likewise Mount Ūrjayant.
Where Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa reside eternally,
there flows the divine river Svarṇarekhā, as well as the powerful and auspicious Ojasvatī.
Kṛṣṇā, Bhadrā, and other wives of Hari exist in the form of rivers;
likewise, the Sarasvatī and the celestial Gaṅgā flow among the peaks.
Who indeed can reach the limit of the majesty of this King Raivata?
Even all the gods combined cannot do so; therefore, that place is truly a station of liberation (mokṣasthala).
The mountain Raivata has entered into the interior of the earth to an extent ten times greater than its extent outside the surface of the earth.
Those scattered mountains that are seen in Vastrāpatha are perceived only as peaks, and not as mountains.
For when Raivataka Mountain fell into the chasm,
that Raivataka Mountain became ten yojanas in height.
When he descended upon the earth with such speed that his motion became sluggish,
he had indeed completed a hundred yojanas of circling through the sky.
When he repeatedly caused her to whirl from the northeastern direction with diminished speed, then, from the region of her head—
In the southern direction, having violently shattered, separated, and torn away a thousand mountain peaks, it fell down with great extent. (73)
Those peaks of Raivata that fell into the tiger-infested forest shall remain exactly as they are for as long as the moon and stars endure. (74)
Beginning from Somanātha and extending as far as Bhīmanātha on the earth, the peaks have fallen within the region of the tiger-infested forest. (75)
Therefore, those who remember Lord Dāmodara here in this Raivata region at the time of their death shall attain liberation itself. (76)
Having thus taught its greatness, Hari himself, as Dāmodara,
then embraced that brahmin repeatedly, praising his devotion to his wife again and again.
He spoke regarding his departure for the sacred ford and then vanished of his own accord;
thus, O Lakṣmī, has that former deed been narrated by me to you. (78)
Whether recited, caused to be recited, or heard, this [teaching] always bestows liberation;
there is nothing else like it. What more do you wish to hear? (79)

Thus ends the one hundred and sixty-first chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of the Raivata Mountain, Vastrāpatha Field, and the Holy Tīrtha," in the first section on the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga within the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā.
Śrī Lakṣmī said:
O Lord, you have previously mentioned Satī, the goddess Pārvatī, the mother of Gaṇeśa; how did Satī come to be, and when did she exist?
But as for that existence which is universal within the form of Nārāyaṇa—whether it has arisen as the nature of Being (sat), or is this [Being], or what else could it be? (Gāthā)
"Is she herself Satī or Pārvatī, or is Pārvatī someone else who is the beloved of Śiva?
O Kṛṣṇa, O Nārāyaṇa, O Acyuta, sever this doubt of mine. (3)
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
You have asked a most excellent and secret question concerning matters from time immemorial;
even though they know it, others do not understand such a narrative.
Listen, Lakṣmī, I shall relate that story exactly as it is; having heard it, you too will surely understand what the nature of a virtuous woman truly is. 5.
Endowed with all sovereignty and all powers, the illustrious Puruṣottama remains alone in the imperishable abode during every great re-creation.
Having withdrawn everything else into himself, he alone shines forth;
for the Blessed Lord, the King of Kings, does not delight in being solitary.
Then, from the left side of his form, he longed for a second [form] that would possess many liberated abodes,
qualities, lordships, and attendants.
He [beheld] incarnations who were not lords yet appeared as lords, possessing divine forms;
numerous male and female servants, as well as the three eternal qualities (guṇas).
The Blessed One, Hari, the sovereign lord of all beings, manifested that universal sovereignty which is the governing essence inherent in Hari.
She existed from beginningless time and then manifested;
she is existence consisting of the three qualities (guṇas), the mother of all creation. || 11 ||
Mahāmāyā indeed consists of the qualities of sattva, rajas, and tamas;
she is the state of equilibrium, that Māyā who is the form of Brahman and the beloved of Hari.
She is indeed Rādhā by form, Mahālakṣmī by form, and the very essence of Ramā;
she repeatedly becomes Lakṣmī by form and Sāvitrī by form. (13)
When I become Rudra from the forehead of Vairāja,
then that Māyā indeed becomes my wife Rudrāṇī.
Thus, I manifest there in the form of Śiva;
and in each such place, my companion arises along with me.
She herself was my wife, that auspicious mother in the form of Satī;
listen to me, my beloved, regarding everything concerning how she came to be born as one possessing a physical birth.
Just as the wife of Vairāja gave birth to Brahmā and the others, so indeed did that goddess Mānā become the mother of Brahmā and the rest. 17.
And from the forehead of Brahmā, Rudra Śambhu was indeed born;
at that time, the wife of Śambhu became the daughter-in-law of Brahmā.
When she was born as the daughter of Dakṣa, she indeed became the granddaughter of Brahmā; yet she was Satī, whose very nature is existence.
When Śambhu became the son of Virāj as the brother of Brahmā,
she was then proclaimed to be the wife of Brahmā’s brother.
Thus, Mahāmāyā, whose essential nature is that of Mahālakṣmī,
having herself become whatever is required for the task, exists as the sustainer of creation.
When Brahmā was born from the lotus at the navel of Vairāja,
Viṣṇu was born as his brother upon seeing his asceticism.
When the two of them grew great in size, a quarrel arose; for its cessation, a ray of splendor from Śrī Hari appeared between them.
Then, indeed, in that ray, the Lord Śiva was seen;
and along with him, Māyā too was seen by Śiva at that time.
Then Brahmā requested those two as his assistants;
likewise, Sadāśiva himself was requested from the forehead of Vairāja.
Then Śambhu arose in his own form, and Śivā also appeared as his consort;
she was born together with Śiva and remained stationed at his left side.
At that time, Śiva indeed existed in the form of half-woman and half-man;
then, for the sake of a particular purpose, Śivā herself became a woman separate from him.
Listen, Lakṣmī, I shall tell you how she who destroys the Daityas came to be; I shall tell you when she manifests for the sake of accomplishing the purpose of the gods. (58)
At that time, she is called "the arisen" (utpannā) in the world, even though she is eternal;
however, once upon a time, in the first Kṛta Yuga, Brahmā himself [manifested her]. ||29||
Then, while remaining established in austerity within the lotus, Śiva became absorbed in meditative concentration (samādhi),
immersed in dhyāna and free from all thought of creation.
Viṣṇu, however, remained like a yogi upon his bed of Śeṣa during the repose;
then, when the time for the commencement of creation had mostly arrived, it was morning.
O Lotus-born one, while Viṣṇu was in the state of waking, an itching arose there again and again due to the contact with the Malaya breeze.
Then, by Viṣṇu’s application of the tip of a golden probe,
the itching was removed from the earwax, and two pellets were extracted.
Having cast those two out, he threw the two pills into the water;
from them arose the two terrible asuras known as Madhu and Kaiṭabha.
Born from the ear-wax, endowed with great strength and prowess,
they suddenly approached the surface of the water after bowing to Viṣṇu.
There, they beheld a wonderful lotus accompanied by Brahmā;
seeing that, the two of them prepared to slay Brahmā.
Then Brahmā, having become afraid, praised Janārdana;
with a one-pointed mind, he offered praise again and again. (37)
Then, repeatedly requesting for his own protection,
the Blessed Lord Hari rose up once more and fought with those two.
For five thousand years, the omnipresent Lord Hari, using his arms as weapons,
remained there to delude those two Asuras.
He remembered Mahāmāyā, who resides as half the body of Śiva;
instantly, she emerged from the form of Śiva in the distinct form of a woman.
Having become like a maidservant, the Queen of the Gods approached and stood before him;
then the Blessed One indeed accepted her into his very eyes.
He said to her, "O Mahāmāyā, let it pervade me in every way—quickly through my eyes, mouth, nose, arms, heart, thighs, and feet. (42)
"Act so that those two may behold me as a beautiful woman who causes delusion, and that Māyā herself—the auspicious, delusive Śivā—may personally accept my command. (43)
Then, just as a curtain was produced by me over the form of Viṣṇu, Viṣṇu was within and Māyā was outside, like a mother with Viṣṇu in her womb. ||44||
At that moment, she was seen by them, and they beheld her;
yet upon seeing her, whose very nature was splendor, the two Daityas were bewildered.
Then those two, intoxicated by their great strength and deluded by Mahāmāyā, said:
"O lady of auspicious appearance, choose a boon for us."
The Blessed One remained there concealed behind a curtain of illusion;
drawing their minds toward him, he spoke to them with great love.
"May both of them be pleased with me today and become my victims;
what need have I for any other boon here? By this much alone, my purpose is fulfilled. (48)
Deluded by the mental construction of desire and deprived of the path of knowledge,
they then became devoid of discernment regarding what ought and ought not to be done.
Seeing water on all sides within the lotus-dwelling of Brahmā,
they both said, "Kill it, for there is a portion of the earth where we two are devoid of water."
At that time, in the first Kṛta-yuga, the water indeed became dissolved;
the earth, devoid of water, was seen as being in the form of a sphere.
Then, by the Blessed One, the bearer of the conch, discus, and mace,
having acted there with his discus, the two of them had their heads severed at the waist.
This deluding illusion became known by the name Mohanī;
the Lord Brahmā, pleased with her, praised her with palms joined in reverence.
Homage to the mother, homage to the sister; let there be repeated homage to the daughter.
Homage be to the brother’s wife; repeated homage to you, O auspicious one. ||54||
Salutations to the Consort; salutations to the Power who accomplishes all tasks;
salutations indeed to the Goddess Vaiṣṇavī; repeated salutations to her who is the left limb [of the Lord]. ||55||
You are Lakṣmī and she is Sāvitrī; you are the supreme Goddess, the Mother.
By you alone is everything sustained, and by you this world is created.
O Goddess, this world is protected by you, and you always consume it at the end;
you are the Great Knowledge, the Great Illusion, the Great Intelligence, and the Great Memory.
You are Mahāmohā, you are Mahādevī, you are Mahāsurī;
you are Śrī, you are Īśvarī, you are Brahmāṇī, the helper of the gods. ||58||
Armed with a sword, a trident, a mace, a discus, a conch, and a bow;
equipped with a *bhuśuṇḍī*, an iron club, a *prāśa* weapon, arrows, and excellent lances.
Whatever object exists anywhere, whether real or unreal, and comprising the totality of all things— of all that, you are the power which accomplishes this effect.
The slender lady is the half-body of Śambhu, Ramā is the half-body of Viṣṇu, and Brāhmī is the half-body of the Creator; dwell among the gods who are to be created. (61)
Thus being sought after by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and the wielder of the Pināka (Śiva), that enchanting goddess,
herself the source of delusion, established her residence among them.
Having attained an invisible state, Viṣṇu went to the ocean of milk. Brahmā, seeing the creation within Viṣṇu’s body as it was before, brought that [creation] forth.
Among the ṛṣis, munis, ancestors, gods, celestial beings, humans,
daityas, serpents, and immobile things, that Mohinī dwelt within them all.
Indeed, that Great Illusion (Mahāmāyā), who embodies splendor, power, grace, and form, and who accomplishes all tasks, dwelt within the senses. 65.
The beautiful-bodied woman displayed various forms belonging to each respective species;
it was by her alone that beauty was born among men and women.
Then, after some time, that Goddess of the Universe, the destroyer of the demon Mahiṣāsura and the fulfiller of the gods' purpose, manifested herself. 67.

Thus ends the one hundred and sixty-second chapter, titled "The Description of the Forms of Rādhā, Lakṣmī, Sāvitrī, Śivā, and Others as the Great Māyā Constituting the Half-Body of the Supreme Brahman within the Lineage of the Kṛta Yuga in the First Part of the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā," and the Description of the Assumed Form of Mohinī for the Purpose of Destroying Madhu and Kaiṭabha.
Śrī Lakṣmī said: When and how did the asura named Mahiṣa come into being?
I wish to hear about his destruction by the Goddess; please tell me. (1)
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, who was this Mahiṣa, and how did he attain the state of an asura? And learn from me how his destruction was brought about by the Goddess and in what manner.
In ancient times, two extremely fierce Daityas who caused agitation to the world,
Rambha and Karamba, performed austerities for the sake of obtaining sons.
For many groups of years, Karaṃbha alone remained in the water;
having become a crocodile, Mahendra struck him in the water with his tusk.
When his brother was lost, Rambha became overwhelmed with extreme anger;
that great asura desired to offer his own head into the fire after having severed it.
As soon as he took up his sword and was indeed about to strike, Vahni restrained him, saying, "Do not act rashly!"
"Do not die; I shall grant you whatever you desire, so speak without delay.
Rambhā said, "May there be a son for me who conquers the three worlds. (7)
He shall be invincible by all the gods, surpassing you in splendor,
able to assume any form at will, skilled in the knowledge of weapons, and possessed of great strength and prowess.
