And Dakṣa, the lord of the prajāpatis, offered praise by uttering one hundred and eight names:
"The Supreme Brahman, the imperishable letters, the eternal Supreme Goddess. (82)
She is Muktānī, omnipresent, Māyā, Satyā, Lakṣmī, and Nirañjanā; she is the Cit-śakti dwelling within all, Tārā, the bestower of nectar, and Ramā. 83.
She is of the nature of space, unfallen, the essence of cause and effect, composed of the creative powers (kalās);
she is the Mistress of Prāṇa, the Great Mother, the Primary Matter, and likewise Nature (prakṛti). ||84||

She is knowledge, the manifestation of power, the ether, the source of sound, consisting of resonance, the progenitor, the womb of all, the ancient one, the immutable, the divine energy of the Puruṣa, and the auspicious Śivā. (85)

The Knower of the Field (kṣetrajñā), the Pervasive (vyāpinī), the Manifest (vyaktā), the Unmanifest (avyaktā), the Three-Guṇa (triguṇā), the Dissolution (layā), the Earthly (bhūmī), the Undifferentiated (avyākṛti), the Source (yoni), the Lightning-like (vaidyutī), and likewise the Deluding (mohinī). ||86||
She is the form of Viṣṇu, the intellect, the great mental creation;
she is Īśvarāṇī, Śarvāṇī, Bhavānī, and likewise Ambikā. ||87||
She is the devoted wife, Rudrāṇī, the Yoginī, Śrī, Sumaṅgalā, Sāvitrī, Kamalā, Gaṅgā, Pārvatī, and Sarasvatī. ||88||
Speech, Fame, Annapūrṇā, Svadhā, Svāhā, Jagadbharā, Sudhā, Siddhi, Stuti, Medhā, Śruti, Nīti, and likewise Smṛti. ||89||
Haṃsā, Kālī, Kauśikī, Kātyāyanī, Caṇḍikā, Durgā, Sādhvī, Gaurī, Trinetrā, and Brahmacāriṇī. ||1.169.90||
Vibhāvarī, Dīkṣā, Gīti, Mohinī, Avidyā, Dakṣiṇā, Bhargā, Sandhyā, Dhātrī, Prabhā, and Bhū. (9.1)
Having praised her with one hundred and eight names, Dakṣa himself, bowing again to the Goddess of gods with palms joined in reverence, spoke this: ||95||
"You have seen my sovereign form; now show me your gentle form.
Having withdrawn [the former], he then showed him another form once again.
Then, for twelve years, he was gentle, fair-complexioned, and of radiant form;
richly fragrant, two-eyed, two-armed, and endowed with dark locks of hair. (94)
With the soles of his lotus feet red and the sprouts of his hands deeply crimson, his every limb was beautifully adorned and his forehead shone with a tilaka mark. ||95||
With a gentle smile and beautiful red lips, accompanied by the tinkling of anklets, he wore golden necklaces upon his chest and rings upon his fingers. (96)
Richly adorned with the great beauty of golden garments, lovely and tender in every limb, she possessed the divine form of a beautiful maiden, enchanting like ten million Cupids. (97)
Seeing her, Dakṣa, his soul greatly delighted, spoke to the Supreme Goddess:
"Today my birth has become fruitful; today my ascetic penance has become fruitful. (98)
Today, waves of my merit have arrived in the form of my daughter;
today, I behold Nārāyaṇī, the mother of the world. (99)
Today I behold the Goddess Śivā, the primordial nature;
I am blessed, I have accomplished my purpose, and I am most completely fulfilled.
Today, indeed, the sight of you, the Mother of the World, has been granted to me;
you, who possess my daughter’s own form, have arrived as the Mother of the World.
Therefore, what greater gain could there be for me than this, wherein the gods are established?
For you indeed are that supreme, infinite, and most excellent power.
You alone are supreme bliss; you alone are the bestower of bliss.
Only when united with you does the Lord experience the bliss of his own self.
The auspicious, all-pervading, subtle, supreme, and eternal Brahman abides within you non-differently; you exist as being composed of that supreme Brahman.
Salutations be unto you, O Great Goddess; salutations to you, O Supreme Sovereign.
Salutations to the Blessed Mistress, to Śivā; to you, repeated salutations.
I am composed of you, I have you as my support, and you alone are my refuge;
I go to you for shelter—be gracious, O Supreme Goddess! (106)
"There is no one equal to me in the world, whether a god or even a dānava;
for she was born of her own accord as my daughter, like a mother to the world."
Oh, this dark-skinned maiden is your mother, and yet she is the mother of the Mother of the World! Oh, how great is her merit today! 108.
Protect me always, O Queen of the Immortals, together with Cāmuṇḍā;
I bow at your lotus feet and go for refuge to Śiva.
"Oh, how great is my good fortune through this union with the Great Goddess!
Command me, O Great Goddess, O Daughter of Śaṅkara; what shall I do?"
Having spoken these words, Dakṣa Prajāpati then stood at her side with palms joined in reverence, gazing intently at Gaurī.
He meditated upon his own daughter, the Goddess Satī, who is of the nature of the Supreme Brahman, who consists of infinite auspiciousness, and who has transcended all transformations. || 11 2 ||
Devoid of beginning, middle, and end, situated beyond darkness,
she is the source of the universe, her form accessible through the wisdom of Vedānta.
She who consists of pure bliss, who is designated by the syllable Om, who grants refuge,
who dwells within all beings, and who is known as both Prakṛti and Puruṣa.
She who has the form of both Pradhāna and Puruṣa, whose form is Prāṇa, who consists of mind,
who is the support of all, who is omnipresent, and who is white, black, and red.
She is the embodiment of sovereignty and wisdom, the personification of Dharma, the bestower of supreme liberation,
the very form of Mahāviṣṇu, and likewise composed of the golden cosmic egg.
She who pervades the station of Parameṣṭhin, who belongs to the Vairāja realm, who possesses the power of the Sun,
who has a thousand hands, feet, and faces, and who is of the nature of Nārāyaṇa within the waters.
She who upholds the law of dissolution, known as the destruction at the end of the age,
the fierce goddess endowed with three eyes, possessing the coils of a thousand hoods like the lord of serpents.
He recognized his own daughter as a supreme, auspicious girl with very tender limbs in the form of a young maiden, who was established at the beginning, middle, and end [of all things]. 119.
Then Ambikā, having remembered Śiva, spoke with a smile to her father:
"O Father, through exclusive devotion, you ought to attain my state."
"Indeed, that form of mine which is my own supreme, wondrous, and divine form has been seen directly by you; it cannot be attained through all sacrifices, austerities, or gifts."
Being devoted to that and intent upon that, go to that alone for refuge;
behold that with your mind, meditate upon that, and worship that.
"By means of my supreme devotion, I shall soon deliver you from this ocean of worldly existence, for you are established in the yoga of the Lord."
"O Prajāpati, I am indeed attained by you through meditation, the yoga of action, devotion, and knowledge; not otherwise, even by ten million ritual acts."
Constantly perform for the sake of liberation the duties prescribed by the Śruti and Smṛti according to one's caste and stage of life, together with knowledge of the supreme self. 125.
From dharma devotion is born; through devotion the Supreme is attained.
The dharma of sacrifice was proclaimed by the Śruti, for dharma indeed shone forth from the Veda.
This supreme, ancient designation in the form of the Veda belongs to me alone;
and there is no scripture other than the Veda that expresses dharma.
Out of compassion for the social classes (varṇas), Virāṭ himself,
by my command, became Svāyaṃbhuva Manu and proclaimed the Vedic dharmas.
When the teachings have disappeared at the end of the ages, the great seers reveal them again in age after age by the command of Brahmā.
When the time for universal dissolution arrives, all those who have perfected their souls enter the supreme state along with Brahmā at the end of Hari’s lifespan.
Therefore, with every effort, one should resort to the Veda for the sake of dharma;
devotion joined with the knowledge of dharma shall reveal the Supreme Brahman. || 131 ||
Listen to how such a form was manifested by me:
Nārāyaṇa is himself Brahman, and likewise Nārāyaṇī. (132)
From an external perspective there is a distinction between the two, but not even slightly from an internal vision;
yet that very Supreme Brahman sometimes manifests as Kṛṣṇa.
He alone becomes Rādhā and sports as he pleases;
he alone also becomes the Supreme Brahman, Nārāyaṇa.
He himself arises as Nārāyaṇī, Ramā, and Lakṣmī;
he sports according to his will, and there is not even the slightest difference [between them]. 35.
He is indeed the Supreme Brahman; he is Brahmā, and likewise Brahmāṇī is born from him.
He alone becomes Viṣṇu, and Vaiṣṇavī is also he alone.
Śiva is indeed Rudra, and Rudrāṇī is Śiva herself; I am Satī, Śivā, and Raudrī, manifested here in your home.
I am of the nature of the Supreme Brahman, and I have come forth for the sake of Śiva;
and the Lord Śiva himself is likewise of the nature of the Supreme Brahman.
The Lord shines upon Kailāsa, while I, the Goddess, abide in your home;
therefore, in every way, he is my devotee and is solely devoted to me.
"Having taken refuge in me with your mind, worship me alone everywhere;
for whatever form of mine is within the range of your mind, O dear one, [worship that]."
Becoming devoted to that and intent upon that, be dedicated to his worship;
O dear one, you must entreat Śiva for my sake.
And this daughter Śivā of yours must be given in marriage to Śiva alone, for the purpose of establishing righteousness and by the command of Brahmā. (142)
Born from the dark one, she has taken refuge in you alone as her father;
you shall bestow her upon Mahendra, for that Śaṅkara is well-pleased with him.
Therefore, all the gods and others pay homage to you with devotion;
together with me, who am offered [to you], go for refuge to Śaṅkara. 144.
Having thus instructed Dakṣa, Satī was indeed born as a young girl;
Dakṣa was supremely pleased, recognizing his daughter as the Supreme Goddess. 145.

Thus ends the one hundred and sixty-ninth chapter, titled "The Description of the Auspicious Great Festival of Satī’s Birth from Vibhāvarī, the Divine Satī’s Appearance to Dakṣa, Her Hymn of Praise, Her Meditation on Her Son, and the Oneness of Śivā and Śiva with the Supreme Brahman," in the first section, the Kṛta-yuga lineage, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Lakṣmī said:
"O Hari, who indeed is this Vibhāvarī, who, though being Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, was born as the goddess whose essence is Brahmā? Please dispel my doubt."
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī, how Satī became the night, Vibhāvarī;
while the glorious Lord Kṛṣṇa was shining resplendently in the abode of Goloka.
He is the Lord, the sovereign of Goloka, whose nature is the Supreme Brahman;
and she who is Mahāmāyā, the primordial Prakṛti, who dwells to the left of Brahman.
Standing somewhere to Kṛṣṇa’s left, she shone with her form merged [with him];
Kṛṣṇa did not delight in being alone, so he then desired a second.
Then, from the left side of Kṛṣṇa’s body, a beautiful maiden appeared;
she ran and brought a flower born from a royal campaka tree.
Placing her feet upon Kṛṣṇa’s feet, she herself supported him during the rāsa dance;
therefore, Rādhā was then addressed as "Kāryasiddhikarī" (the one who accomplishes all tasks).
Having taken her beloved Kṛṣṇa with her, she entered a bower of trees;
he gave her the bliss of passion, and she too bestowed upon him the intoxication of love.
And when that great bliss had fully set in, Rādhā fell asleep;
then she said to Kṛṣṇa, "O Kṛṣṇa, why do you not move? (8)
Kṛṣṇa said, "My dear, sleep has come upon you for a moment due to fatigue.
Rādhā then became angry at that sleep, which was like a young girl.
Having stood by His side, bowed down, and indeed closed her eyes, Rādhā then looked at Him and said: "O Sleep, O destroyer of pleasure!"
"Let there be no dwelling for you in Goloka; go to the Vairāja-puruṣa! You are a destroyer of all bliss, characterized by darkness (tāmasī), and associated with Rudra."
O Goddess, may you always be of the nature of *tamas*, the eternal destroyer;
you are the state of sleep, the support for the cognition of non-existence, and the annihilator of mental fluctuations.
Be ever sufficient for the destruction of the fierce Asuras;
remain eternally prepared against the hosts of Daityas as the embodiment of darkness (Tāmasī).
In the creation, Rudrāṇī, united with Rudra, brought about the cessation of the senses of all living beings everywhere and established their maintenance.
For you shall become the night (rātri) because the shining (bhāna) of the sun (rāna) has ceased;
and since that shining has departed, you shall be called Vibhāvarī. || 15 ||
Brahmā himself will take you, the daughter of Vairāja, as his wife at the time of creation;
and he [Viṣṇu] will give the goddess Vibhāvarī to Dakṣa as a daughter.
Dakṣa will give his excellent daughter Satī to Śambhu;
she, the goddess Kālī Caṇḍikā, shall indeed destroy the asuras.
As such, you shall become Kālī, as well as Rātri, Vibhāvarī, and Nidrākā; having become the companion of Rudra, you will sport in the nature of darkness (tāmasī).
By the command of Hari, out of desire, and likewise due to the necessity of future events,
that very night, Vibhāvarī, became the daughter of Dakṣa.
Śrī Lakṣmī said:
Indeed, it is heard that when Śambhu was born from the Vairāja Puruṣa, the power of Śambhu (Śāmbhavī Śakti) was born along with him.
Is there a difference between this Śivā and this Night, or not? For Śivā is always the wife, while Night is merely another form of jāyā (the wife). (21)
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: O Goddess, you have asked what is fitting regarding my profound activities;
this is not known by others as to what has happened at any time.
Listen to what occurred previously, that which ought to be known by you;
I shall relate the remainder of the story concerning the primordial nature of Śiva.
Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of all, the cause of all causes,
shines in the imperishable and supreme abode, served by those who are liberated.
Whenever and however he desires to create, then he certainly creates it; what was accomplished by him at that time, I shall tell you in due course.
When Rādhā was born from the very limb of the Supreme Brahman,
He assumed the form of Kṛṣṇa and made Goloka His abode for her sake.
And she was the wife of Kṛṣṇa, dearer to him than his own life;
a goddess sixteen years of age, in whom fresh youth had blossomed. (27)
Clad in garments pure as fire, her limbs were tender and radiant;
burdened by the weight of her full hips, the beautiful woman was most enchanting. (28)
Her lips were red, soft, and beautiful; her hips and breasts were full;
and she was enchanting with rows of teeth that gleamed like strings of pearls. (29)
Her face possessed a mass of splendor exceeding that of ten million full moons;
her eyes were as expansive as lotus petals, and she was adorned with exquisite hair-arrangements and other ornaments.
Her face was exceedingly beautiful, like a sesame flower or the beak of a parrot;
her pair of cheeks possessed a golden hue and were intensely radiant with splendor. ||3 1||
Her ears were beautifully adorned with ornaments of gold, gems, and jewels;
she was further embellished with sandalwood, agallochum, musk, vermilion, saffron, and other such substances.
With leaves placed upon her two skull-cups, with her hair-knot woven with flowers, and with a streak of vermilion applied to her forehead, she has her braided hair arranged upon her head. (33)
Her feet shone with the luster of the petals of land-lotuses, and she moved with the slow, majestic gait of a swan or an elephant, her broad chest swelling with grace. (34)
Necklaces of gems, necklaces of jewels, a captivating garland of forest flowers, necklaces fashioned from diamonds, and jeweled armlets and bracelets.
Wearing bracelets fashioned from the essence of the seven precious gems and jeweled armlets, she,
being virtuous, bore a girdle of golden bells that tinkled melodiously.
She is resplendent with tinkling anklets fashioned from priceless jewels, and she bears a lotus-stalk enriched with various kinds of gems. (37)
With her palms, nails, lips, and hands as beautiful as red lac,
she sat smiling upon half of her husband’s jeweled lion-throne.
Then, from her pores, there immediately emerged a multitude of cowherd women,
equal to her in dress, form, and appearance, and possessed of perpetual youth.
And a multitude of gopīs, numbering hundreds of millions of lakhs, manifested eternally in Goloka, known by the name Kṛṣṇadāsīs (the female servants of Kṛṣṇa). 1.170.40.
Then, from the pores of Kṛṣṇa’s body, the entire multitude of cowherds immediately manifested, identical in form, dress, and other attributes.
That host of Kṛṣṇa’s servants indeed numbered thirty crores;
they manifested instantly from the pores of Kṛṣṇa’s skin. 42.
There were herds of cattle of many colors, eternally possessed of stable youth; likewise, there were Surabhi-cows, bulls, heifers, and calves. ||43||
At that time, auspicious and beautiful omens appeared;
among them was a single bull equal in strength to ten million lions.
For the sake of obtaining a vehicle for Śambhu, Kṛṣṇa protected the charming [swan];
from the pores of the nails of Kṛṣṇa’s feet, a row of very white swans emerged. 45.
An exceedingly beautiful woman, possessing the constant marks of both male and female, appeared for the sake of obtaining a royal swan as a vehicle for them. 46.
Kṛṣṇa protected Sudhavala, who possessed great strength and prowess;
from the cavity of Kṛṣṇa’s left ear emerged one who was most enchanting.
A permanent host of white horses appeared;
among them, one was the whitest for the purpose of becoming the vehicle of Dharma.
The Lord Kṛṣṇa himself protected some and gave others to the gods;
from the cavity of Kṛṣṇa’s right ear, one of beautiful form [emerged].
A row of lions of great strength and prowess appeared;
among them, Kṛṣṇa gave one of great might to Vibhāvarī.
Having considered whatever was to be enjoyed at that time, the yogi Kṛṣṇa fashioned five divine chariots that were all-pervading.
Inlaid with various jewels, moving at the speed of thought, exceedingly vast, one hundred yojanas in length and extending a hundred yojanas upward.
It possessed a hundred thousand wheels, was free from the affliction of wind, and was endowed with a hundred thousand pleasure-pavilions;
it shone with pleasure-gardens and was adorned with couches for enjoyment and the like.
In every house there was the illumination of hundreds of thousands of jewel-lamps,
augmented by divine archways, jars, banners, and various other wonders.
Adorned with jewels, mirrors, chowries, umbrellas, and pearl-latticed windows,
it was beautifully embellished with strings of supreme gems, pearls, rubies, and diamonds.
Adorned with blue, red, yellow, and white lotuses,
one of these was bestowed upon the one whose nature is that of a resident of Vaikuṇṭha.
Another was offered to the one who dwells in the indeterminate state and possesses his own essential form;
the third, however, was offered to the one who possesses his own essential form as Mahāviṣṇu.
The fourth was for Rādhikā, and the fifth was kept for himself;
thus the Guhyakas manifested from the secret region of Kṛṣṇa.
Kubera, the lord of the Guhyakas, and Sundarī, the Guhyakī, as well as the attendants (pārṣadas), manifested from the mouth of Kṛṣṇa. ||59||
Clad in yellow garments and wearing forest garlands, they were dark-complexioned, four-armed,
and adorned with crowns, jeweled earrings, and conch, discus, mace, and lotus emblems.
In Vaikuṇṭha, he gave many four-armed attendants to Nārāyaṇa;
others were made two-armed, dark-complexioned, and resembling Kṛṣṇa.
The Vaiṣṇavas and the male and female servants were made devoted to Kṛṣṇa;
they were protected in their own service while meditating upon His lotus feet.
From the left eye of Kṛṣṇa there emerged the wielder of the trident,
white in complexion, characterized by tamas, possessing three eyes, and bearing the crescent moon on his forehead.
Wearing a tiger skin, holding a hand-drum (ḍamaru) in his hand, and possessing matted hair,
he is the illustrious Īśāna, the sovereign lord of the guardians of the directions.
Likewise, other Gaṇas appeared, bearing tridents and battle-axes, with the moon as their crest-jewel, three-eyed, and of massive form. ||65||
Surās numbering thirty million appeared from every location of Kṛṣṇa’s form;
they all remained stationed according to their respective places.
Rati, Mūrti, Sāvitrī, Manoramā, Sarasvatī, Mahālakṣmī, Satī, and Lakṣmī emerged from the lotus of his heart. (67)
He gave Mahālakṣmī to Nārāyaṇa and Sarasvatī [to him];
he gave Sāvitrī to Brahmā, and respectfully offered his own form to Dharma. (68)
He gave Rati, rich in beauty, to Kāma; the delightful one to Kubera;
Lakṣmī to Viṣṇu; and he offered Satī to Śiva.
Then the yogi Śiva, bowing down to the infallible Kṛṣṇa, said:
"Now I shall no longer assume a material nature like an ordinary being."
[She is] opposed to yoga, knowledge, celibacy, service, and devotion;
she is the binder of the desire for liberation, full of desire, and the increaser of passion. ||71||
[She is] the hunger that does not destroy asceticism, which consumes the satisfaction of the mind,
and which takes the form of a firm shackle within the terrible prison of worldly existence.
It constantly generates delusion, cuts off right understanding, always possesses the essence of sensual enjoyment, and increases the desire for sense objects. ||73||

The creeper composed of excrement and urine that binds the tree of the body, which casts away all other pursuits for the sake of sexual pleasure and is entirely absorbed in its own self-interest; ||74||
It destroys one's independence, consists of the abode of sorrow and delusion, is firm, has concentration and meditation as its hidden limbs, and is opposed to the meditation upon Brahman. ||75||
"I do not desire a wife, O Lord; grant me my desired boon:
may my love for devotion to you and for the state of being your servant increase incessantly. (76)

In the chanting of your name, in serving at your feet, in the act of worship, in hearing, in proclaiming, in praising, in remembering, and in cultivating the feeling of friendship [toward you], [may there be success]. (77)
Whether awake or dreaming, I wander only after you;
no satisfaction arises for me in meditation upon you, nor in yoga, nor in ascetic practices.
In your invocation, offering of the seat, water for sipping, ritual bathing, and service;
in the offering of perfume, flowers, incense, garments, lamps, and the anointing with sandalwood paste. ||79||
In the offering of food, water, betel-leaf, the ārārtika lamp, hymns of praise, and prostration;
in bowing down, circumambulation, adorning [the deity], and the presentation of auspicious fruits. (1.170.80)
O Treasure of Compassion, grant me such [merit] that no satiety may arise even from the offering of myself and from the enjoyment of Your eternal grace. (8.1)
Sārṣṭi, sālokya, sārūpya, sāmīpya, sāmya, and līnatā do not equal even a sixteenth part of the portion of the bliss of devotion to You. (82)
Atomicity, levity, extension, radiance, magnanimity, as well as lordship, mastery, and the fulfillment of all desires. ||83||
Omniscience, far-sightedness, as well as hearing from afar, entering the bodies of others, perfection of speech, and the power of the wish-fulfilling creeper; //84//
The great power over birth and destruction, as well as immortality—even these sixteen perfections do not equal a sixteenth part of devotion. (85)
Yogas, austerities, gifts, vows, and fasts;
fame, renown, truthful speech, righteousness, sacred fords, and the worship of the gods. ||86||
Beholding the images of the gods, traversing the entire circle of the earth, the enjoyment of all celestial pleasures, and even bathing in all the oceans—[these are attained]. (87)
All the ritual purificatory baths (avabhṛtha), the states of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa, as well as the state of Vairāja and whatever other kinds of prosperities there may be; ||88||
They do not equal even a sixteenth part of a fraction of a portion of your devotion;
therefore, O Lord, nothing other than devotion should be requested by me. (89)
Neither the virtuous wife nor the unfaithful one is desired by me, for both these natures are alike;
the happiness found in dispassion is not such as that which is found in passion.
Having heard these words of Śaṅkara, the Blessed One spoke with a smile:
"O Śambhu, if Satī, your Prakṛti, is not to be brought back by you now," (9.1)
May that auspicious Yoganidrā dwell within my eyes;
whenever you have need of her, I shall grant you the night. (92)
"Until that time, she shall provide service to my eyes," having spoken thus, the Blessed One took Śivā by the eyes.
And Śambhu protected his Vaiṣṇava son from the service of the demons;
then Kṛṣṇa said to Śambhu, "Perform service to me in every way. (94)
As long as his necessary task regarding creation does not present itself, he remains one who is worshipped by ascetics, those perfected in yoga, the wise, the gods, and the Vaiṣṇavas. (95)
Attain the state of immortality and become a conqueror of death;
by my boon, obtain the perfection of omniscience in the Vedas, Śāstras, and all other branches of knowledge. 96.
Behold here indeed the effortless destruction of countless Brahmās, [accomplished] by means of his knowledge, splendor, power, age, fame, and glory. (97)
By valor, austerity, and splendor, become equal to me;
you are dearer to me than my own life, O Śiva, supreme among devotees. (98)
"You ought to act upon my meaningful words at this time;
I shall fulfill your request, my son, so dwell in my house. (99)
"You shall fulfill both my word and your own word;
having assumed your natural form at the proper time, you shall perform the act of adornment."
You are not merely an ascetic; you are a lord as great as I.
Be a householder at the proper time, and likewise become an ascetic at the proper time according to your desire.
Now listen to what you said regarding the suffering in union with a wife:
a wicked woman brings suffering to her husband, but not one who is devoted to her husband.
She who is born of a great family, belonging to a noble lineage and proud of her kin, makes her beloved happy by means of service known as the surrender of herself. (103)
The husband is her kinsman, the husband is her sustainer, the husband is her supreme deity;
the husband alone is the Supreme Brahman, and the husband is everything for the women of his own family.
Whether fallen or not fallen, whether wretched or powerful, whether firm or weak—the husband alone is indeed the all-in-all for women of noble family. (1.05)
She who is born of an unworthy family and is tainted by the bad character of her parents will certainly be enjoyed by others and will always be intent on reviling her husband. (1.06)
Kṛṣṇa is my husband, Viṣṇu is my husband, and Śambhu is always my husband;
for noble women, all the gods are seen within the god who is their husband.
Such is that auspicious, great, and virtuous Śivā of yours;
O Śiva, she shall indeed become the auspicious Prakṛti of both Śiva and Viṣṇu.
O Lord of gods, dwell in Goloka as long as your creative activity does not manifest within this creation;
remain ever immersed in my meditative absorption or intent upon my service.
Having spoken thus, Kṛṣṇa established him in his own service,
granting him the duration of a thousand cycles of the Vairāja gods for a single day of Goloka.
What count can there be of the creators of the minor brahmāṇḍas who perish therein, when even Brahmā and Viṣṇu shall emerge from the body of Vairāja? (111)
Then, within that stream of splendor, Sadāśiva will indeed manifest;
the splendor shall become the Liṅga and Śiva the Mūrti, and they will attain renown in the world. || 112 ||
That virtuous woman shall become Śivā, dwelling by the side of Śiva;
thereafter, in the course of time, she shall become Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa.
Then the Blessed One spoke to Śivā, the resident of his eyes:
"Now remain, my child, within my two eyes in Goloka."
In due time, you shall worship Śambhu, the son of Virāṭ and the refuge of Śivā;
then, having manifested once more from within the splendors of all the gods, [you shall attain your goal].
Having withdrawn all the Daityas, she will become the dweller of the Vindhya mountains;
she will become the daughter of Dakṣa, Suśīlā, the wife of Śambhu.
Then, having cast off her body due to the censure of her husband at the sacrifice,
she will become Pārvatī in Menā, the wife of the mountain king.
"You shall become Caṇḍikā, the performer of many deeds and the fierce one;
you shall have many names, many forms, and you shall be of the nature of Tamas."
Among the gods of the five abodes (Pañcāyatana), Śivā and her son Śiva shall indeed be the foremost among all the Viśvedevas by my grace.
In villages and indeed in cities, you shall be worshipped as the village deity;
there, you will exist bearing various names and other such designations.
And there, those attendants of yours will be great beings, desiring to obtain the fruits of the perfected goals: dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa.
Those who shall worship you there at that holy and excellent pilgrimage site on earth,
their fame, renown, and sovereignty will increase greatly.
With these blessings, Mādhava gratified Śiva and Śivā;
he protected Śiva through his service and protected Śivā within his own eyes.
Because she resides in the eye, Nidrā has become auspicious (Śivā) and is always a bringer of happiness.
Nidrā, Vibhāvarī, and Rātri are one and the same; she is not another.
Born from the heart of Kṛṣṇa, Śivā resided in His two eyes;
by the word of Rādhikā, Nidrā departed from the eyes of Vairāja.
And there, Śivā was eternally manifested together with Śambhu;
she alone resides within the senses of Nārāyaṇa in the Ocean of Milk.
She alone is established as the multitude of senses within all the foremost gods;
she alone [arises] from the senses and so forth of the glorious Nārāyaṇa reclining upon Śeṣa.
Śivā, Śakti, Yoganidrā, Rātri, Vibhāvarī, Satī, Kātyāyanī, Kauśikī, Caṇḍikā, Kālī, and Pārvatī. || 128 ||

"O Lakṣmī, thus has been described to you the form of Satī, which is of the nature of the Real, as it was manifested through the sequential process according to necessity and according to its effects. (1.29)

Thus, in the first book of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, within the lineage of the Kṛta Yuga, in the narrative of Satī’s life: the curse upon Kṛṣṇa’s eyes for their sleep during Rādhā’s dalliance in Goloka; the manifestation from the limbs of Śrī Kṛṣṇa of the forms of Rādhā, the cowherds, the cowherdesses, the herds of cows, the swans, the five white horses, the lion, the chariot, Śiva, Śivā, Mahālakṣmī, Sarasvatī, Rati, Sāvitrī, and others; Satī’s dedication to Śiva and Śiva’s renunciation; and the subsequent state of Śivā as the daughter of Vairāja residing in Kṛṣṇa’s eye, followed by her becoming Kātyāyanī, born from the senses of the Lord of Devas.
The one hundred and seventieth chapter, titled "The Description of Satī as the Daughter of Dakṣa and Pārvatī as the Daughter of Himālaya," and so forth.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Then, from the Vairāja Puruṣa, the Unborn (Brahmā) arose from the lotus at his navel; and Viṣṇu was born from his heart. Thus, indeed, were Viṣṇu and Padmajā (Brahmā).
"Mahāmaha" and "Mahān"—these two were disputing for preeminence;
between them, a great radiance of light then arose. ||2||
There, the third deity, Śambhu, indeed manifested;
he was sent from Goloka for the protection of the gods within this cosmic egg.
Śaṅkara himself was joyfully sent here by Śrī Kṛṣṇa;
he has arisen by the will of Hari as a Vaiṣṇava and the best among devotees. 4.
At that very moment, a ray from the form of Hari entered the eyes of Virāja and,
by His power, became exceedingly steady for him.
From his forehead emerged Maheśvara, rich in rays;
that ray was indeed a divine arrow, the very emblem of Brahmā. ||6||
There, Maheśa was born as the son of Vairāja, the stainless Suta;
and Śivā indeed resided within his body, unmanifested on the left side.
She arrived by the command of Kṛṣṇa, yet Śiva did not know her at that time;
for Śiva knew only his own self as the God there, apart from Śivā.
However, that invisible Śivā, who existed as the form of Śambhu’s power (śakti) on his left side and was situated in his black eye, became the two eyes of Śiva. 9.
Impelled by Brahmā, that night became the daughter of Dakṣa;
by his command, Dakṣa gave her the name Satī.
Then the mother, having properly prepared her daughter according to the prescribed rites,
gave her breast milk and other nourishment through the ritual of infant feeding.
Protected by her nurse Vīriṇī and nurtured by her skillful mother, she grew up; indeed, all excellent virtues entered into her even during her childhood.
Even while engaged in play in the midst of her friends, she would, by her very nature,
occasionally draw an image of Lord Śambhu here and there.
While singing songs appropriate for childhood, she repeatedly sang of Rudra Hara;
thus, being full of devotion, she remembered Hara, the destroyer of the god of love.
In her, her parents' compassion grew exceedingly great at all times;
though she was but a child, she was mature in virtue and delighted those who gave her birth.
Once, Nārada and Brahmā went to the palace of Dakṣa;
there they saw the auspicious Satī seated at Dakṣa’s side.
Both were saluted by their father, and Satī was also saluted;
at the conclusion of the prostrations, having looked upon Satī, she was seated on the auspicious throne offered by Dakṣa.
Having been honored according to the rites of hospitality while they remained there, the two spoke with joy;
Brahmā said to the sage, "O Nārada, behold Maheśvarī! (18)
"Whose wife would be most suitable? Observe the lines and tell me.
Then Nārada, having bowed there to the Queen of the Gods, said: "O Sukanyā," [he continued].
"Come, let me see the lines on your hand; who might you be?"—when this was said, the maiden then showed the palm of her hand with a smile. (1.171.20)
The bow, the fish, as well as the banner (ketu), the svastika, the trident, the lamp, the lotus, the arrow, the goad, the conch, and the discus. || 21 ||
An axe, an arrow, and a spear—these six are on the left hands and six on the right;
these were seen by Nārada in sequence through the line.
On his forehead is a third eye, and a digit of the moon is curved upon his brow;
on his heart is the auspicious form of Śiva, consisting of a beautiful golden line.
Above the navel is the mark of a shield, and below it the sign of a sword;
likewise, there is a bow joined with an arrow, and at the two feet, a lion and a bull.
The pinnacle, the creeper, the nāgadalā, and likewise the lion-throne—these are seen above as lines, and these very things are perceived by means of the line. (25)
This was also told by Nārada to Brahmā and to Dakṣa:
"She is indeed neither the daughter of Manu, nor divine, nor anyone else."
She is the mother of the world, the most venerable among the venerable, and indeed the supreme Vaiṣṇavī;
she is the consort of Kṛṣṇa, the left-hand side of Nārāyaṇa, and the Supreme Sovereign.
Whether she be the consort of Brahmā, the supreme goddess who is the consort of Viṣṇu, or the consort of Śiva—none other than these can be the Mother of the World. ||28||
I believe Śarva resides in her heart; the moon of his eyes is upon her forehead;
the line of his trident is on her hand; and his bull and his lion are upon her feet. (29)
Therefore, this jewel belongs to Śiva alone and certainly to no one else;
having heard this, she quickly became bashful with her face cast down and laughed.
Then he went inside the house and informed his mother of that;
and at that time, Asiknī, having come out from the house, [met] those two there.

Having been saluted with prostrations and honored with water, food, fruits, and other offerings, the two elders were then worshipped by Dakṣa; while they remained there, [Dakṣa] departed from the house once again.
Taking her own drawing of Bharga-Citra, she came outside and,
smiling, showed it to the great sage with the meaning "Om."
She bowed to Nārada and prostrated before Brahmā;
then Brahmā, placing his joined palms upon her head, spoke.
O virtuous lady, may you obtain as your husband that god who desires you and whom you likewise desire— the omniscient Lord of the universe.
O auspicious lady, may he who has not taken another wife, nor does take one, nor will ever take one—may that peerless husband be yours. (36)
Having spoken thus and remained for a very long time in the house of Dakṣa,
they were dismissed by him and returned to their own abode, O daughter of the ocean.
Then Dakṣa became pleased, considering himself fortunate;
and Satī, for her part, attained a certain measure of youthful maturity.
And Dakṣa reflected: "Śiva is a bridegroom worthy of Satī;
my daughter's childhood has passed, and likewise her maidenhood is gone. (39)
I shall, by all means, give this maiden— who has reached the bloom of youth within, who is fit for marriage, and who is enriched with a golden form through her austerities— to Bharga.
Satī herself desired to attain Bharga in that manner within her heart;
and having understood her father's resolve, she spoke to her mother. (41)
O Mother, for the sake of Śaṅkara, show me the penances, vows, and so forth;
by your command, I shall indeed perform the vow for the gratification of Śiva. (42)
Having received her mother’s command, that virtuous woman, firm in her vows, sought to attain Śiva and worshipped him at home with various religious observances. 43.

On the eighth lunar day of the bright fortnight of the month of Īṣa, which was an auspicious occasion, he worshipped Śaṅkara with offerings of rice mixed with jaggery and salt, along with the sixteen primary articles of worship.
On the fourteenth day of the month of Kārttika, Satī worshipped Śaṅkara with cakes, milk-rice,
and the sixteen primary offerings.
On the eighth day of the dark fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa, Satī worshipped Śaṅkara with rice mixed with sesame and barley, along with the sixteen primary offerings and other services.
On the seventh day of the bright fortnight of the month of Pauṣa, having kept a vigil during the night,
that virtuous woman worshipped Śaṅkara in the morning with kṛśara rice.
On the full moon day of the month of Māgha, having kept a vigil throughout the night, she,
wearing wet clothes, performed the worship of Śaṅkara on the bank of the river.
On the night of Śivarātri in the month of Phālguna, she observed the vow of keeping vigil;
with sixteen actors and their assistants, she worshipped Him day and night. (49)
On the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, he worshipped Śiva with Palāśa and Damanaka flowers, along with the sixteen primary offerings and others, both by day and by night.
On the third day of the bright fortnight of the month of Rādha, Satī worshipped Śaṅkara with sixteen new offerings of rice cooked with sesame seeds and barley.
On the night of the full moon of the month of Jyeṣṭha, the virtuous Satī, remaining without food during her vow, worshipped Śaṅkara with garments and large flowers.
On the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, the virtuous Satī, dressed in black garments,
worshipped Śambhu with Bṛhatī flowers during her vow.
On the eighth and fourteenth days of the bright fortnight of the month of Śrāvaṇa,
she worshipped Śiva with sacred threads, garments, and purifying offerings.
On the thirteenth day of the dark fortnight of Bhādrapada, having worshipped [the deity] with many flowers and fruits, Satī partook of a meal of water on the fourteenth day.
Observing her vows with great self-restraint, Satī performed the Śiva-vrata for more than a month, subsisting on various kinds of leaves, flowers, and fruits produced in that season.
Constantly devoted to the worship of Śiva throughout all months,
she remained firm in her vow and remembered nothing else besides him.
Having thus completed the entire Nandā-vrata, the virtuous ascetic woman meditated upon Śiva with focused devotion, like a yoginī established in her spiritual disciplines.
Though her limbs were emaciated by asceticism, she became an embodiment of splendor, beautiful in form, composed of the essence of Śiva, gentle, and worthy of resting upon the lap of Śiva. (59)
On the occasion of Satī’s birth anniversary and the great festival of her twelfth year,
Dakṣa invited the gods, the Manus, and other great sages.
At that time, O beloved, all the gods and sages from every side—myself, Brahmā, the guardians of the quarters, the protectors of the worlds, the deities, and so forth—[were present]. (61)
Then all the gods went to Dakṣa’s house to bestow their blessings, and they were duly honored in the great assembly hall.
They bestowed blessings upon Satī, and Satī bowed to them;
she who had been seen before was now so nourished by her asceticism that she seemed as if she were no longer half-formed.
Having seen such intense austerity and knowing it was solely for the sake of Śiva,
all the gods and others were delighted and repeatedly bowed to the Goddess.
They said: "Do not perform such extremely severe penance;
Śarva, the Great God, will certainly become your husband. (65)
Having thus offered blessings and accepted the respectful offering,
they then praised her penance as she had reached the state of perfection.
Having received Dakṣa’s words and Satī’s desire, the sages and gods,
having performed worship and bowed to Satī, departed for Mount Kailāsa.
Brahmā accompanied by Sāvitrī, Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa likewise, Viṣṇu together with Ramā, and the gods accompanied by their goddesses.
The seven sages, together with their wives, as well as the Manus,
went to the peak of Kailāsa, where the god Maheśvara resides.
Having gone there, they bowed to Śambhu and, seeing the peaceful yogi,
joyfully praised him with various hymns while their hands were joined in reverent salutation.
Homage to the one whose nature is the imperishable syllable, homage to the self that is the dark eye;
homage to the one known as Sadāśiva, homage to you who are the worship of light. ||7 1||
Salutations to you who have the form of the son of Vairāja; salutations to you whose nature is celibacy.
Salutations to you whose nature is Brahman; salutations to you who are eternally peaceful. ||72||
Salutations again and again to the one who is devoid of qualities yet rich in attributes, to the devotee of Viṣṇu;
salutations to You, whose body is the unmanifest night and who are changeless.
Salutation to Maheśa, the Supreme Lord, the Sovereign of Śiva;
salutation to him who occasionally performs acts of peace and who effects occasional dissolution. ||74||
Salutations to Śeṣa; salutations to you who are the very form of Saṃkarṣaṇa.
Salutations to you who are clothed in dispassion, yet possess true passion. ||75||
Salutations to You, Śiva, whose station and true nature are not known even by the gods, the ṛṣis, the siddhas, the virtuous women, and the virtuous men. ||76||
Salutations to that Supreme Lord, whose state yogis always strive to behold; salutations again and again to Him who is established in yoga.
Homage to you who are endowed with infinite accomplishments and who are beyond the reach of words;
homage to you who are self-luminous and established in nirvāṇa. ||78||
Salutations to you, the wise one; salutations to you, the inactive knower of the Self; salutations to you, who are swiftly pleased by austerity and the giver of all. (79)
Salutations to you, the three-eyed one, accompanied by the moon, the presiding lord of all;
salutations to you, the refuge for those who have come for protection and the bestower of the desired objects sought.
Salutations to you, the bestower of sovereign powers and the giver of liberation;
salutations to you, the fulfiller of the desires of devotees and the ocean of the sacred traditions. ||81||
Salutations to You, the self-luminous, the eternal, and the inner witness;
whether with desires or free from desires, Your devotees have come for refuge. (82)
Salutations to you, because they do not turn back until they have attained perfection;
indeed, a certain maiden is performing intense austerity for your sake. (83)
How can you be so merciless? Be gracious; salutations to you!
O Śaṅkara, for the sake of the continuous flow of the world's affairs, please exercise your discernment. (84)
Since You are attainable through internal yoga, we bow to You and offer praise;
You are neither a god, nor an asura, nor a mortal, nor an animal, nor a bird, nor a beast. (85)
Neither woman, nor eunuch, nor man—whatever you are, that you are; homage to you! We bow down to the creator of the dissolution of the universe and the sustainer of the universe. 86.

Salutations to Him whom the followers of Sāṃkhya perceive through knowledge, whom the yogis perceive in meditative absorption, and whom the devotees perceive through grace— Him who consists of the three Vedas.
Salutations to the one who uplifts his devotees; salutations to you of hidden splendor!
Salutations to the manifest God, the direct experience beyond the senses. ||88||

Salutations to you who sport in the Night of Time (Kālarātri), and salutations to you who were entreated by the daughter of Dakṣa; salutations to you who have entered into worldly activity, and salutations to you who have withdrawn from it.
"O Lord who fulfills the desires of your devotees, fulfill the desire of the Creator!
Having praised him thus, they remained silent; and upon hearing this, Śambhu indeed laughed.
Having seen the gods, the sages, and others accompanied by their wives, he accorded them a welcome and hospitality as was fitting, and then inquired about the reason for their visit.
O Viṣṇu, O Brahmā, O gods, and O foremost sages among the ṛṣis!
Tell me truly the reason for your arrival.
"All have arrived with their wives; what task remains for me?
Thus was Brahmā questioned, being urged by Viṣṇu at that time.
He spoke to Śambhu in sweet words: "O Lord, nothing is unknown to you;
nevertheless, O Master, listen, for it must be told due to the nature of worldly custom. (94)
In particular, we—gods, humans, and others—exist for the sake of shared objects;
and the asuras are born repeatedly in manifold ways during creation. (95)
Among them, some are to be slain by me, and some are to be slain by Hari;
others who are exceedingly cruel are to be slain by you, O Goddess, and likewise others are to be slain by you.
Moreover, others indeed become subject to slaughter by a son born of your own prowess;
until those wicked ones have been destroyed, there can be no fearless stability for the world.
While you remain established on the path of yoga, free from attachment and aversion,
and possessing a nature consisting solely of compassion, they could never be destroyed.
If the nourishment of those performing austerities by means of boons is certain, then how will the Sāttvika creation remain stable? (99)
Therefore, it is indeed fitting that the tasks of creation, maintenance, and destruction should be performed by us alone among those who have risen above both the righteous and the unrighteous.
We, however, are indeed of a single nature, though appearing distinct due to the difference in their effects;
if the difference in effects is not established, then a difference in form is purposeless. (101)
I and Viṣṇu, together with our wives, have been born in a noble manner for the sake of a specific purpose;
likewise, you too should become possessed of a wife for the welfare of the universe.
Accept this one beautiful woman as your wife;
having married her, perform for the world the most important task.
Just as Padmālayā belongs to Viṣṇu and Sāvitrī belongs to me,
so too, O Śambhu, accept a beloved wife as your companion.
Śambhu, smiling, spoke to Brahmā and Viṣṇu regarding the ultimate truth:
"O Brahmā, O Hari, you two are always most dear to me."
"From the sight of you two today, a great joy arises within me;
for you have both determined what is necessary for my sake regarding worldly affairs."
It may indeed be appropriate, yet it does not please my heart, for I am an ascetic, dispassionate, and one who has transcended the path of yoga.
For the man of knowledge who is free from desire, who delights in his own self, who has completely withdrawn from worldly activity, and who perceives the Self—what need has he for a woman? (108)
For me, whose self is fixed in yoga, there is indeed constant bliss;
I do not become a remnant of the bliss obtained through association with others.
Marriage is a fierce bondage for both parties to one another;
why then should a yogi who is free from desire be led away by force?
"Therefore, my desire for my wife is not true; I am telling you all the truth.
Having heard this, Viṣṇu, as shown by Śrī Kṛṣṇa, then spoke to Śambhu. || 11 1 ||
"Whatever was promised in Goloka, when the task of creation occurs and whenever you may have need, then I shall give you the Night."
Having grasped the true nature [of reality] at the proper time, you shall practice the erotic sentiment;
likewise, at the proper time be a householder, and at the proper time become an ascetic according to your desire.
A widower is not considered auspicious for this occasion anywhere;
even the residence of a widower among those with their wives would bring fear.
Having become impartial, one should be honored only among those who are impartial, not among those who are partial;
the partial shall perish among the impartial, and the impartial shall perish because of the partial. (1.15)
The equality of householders who perform the duties of creation and governance must always be maintained; therefore, you should now be accompanied by a wife.
Indeed, a brother separated from his wife is no ground for trust among women;
nor is he fit for sacrifices or ancestral rites without his wife.
One who is diligent in action but devoid of women is always inauspicious;
likewise, one who is not diligent in action but joined with women shall also be inauspicious.
O Śambhu, you who are appointed to the task of creation, do not dwell with me as one who brings ill fortune;
rather, having reflected upon this, remain among us always becoming a source of great auspiciousness.
"O Śaṅkara, remember the words of Kṛṣṇa and remain with your wife.
Having heard these words of Viṣṇu and having recalled the speech of Kṛṣṇa, he then [acted accordingly].
Having reflected upon the dharma that consists in attaining Śiva, who is eternally accomplished, Śaṅkara said:
"O Viṣṇu, I shall always perform what you have spoken, for it is beneficial."
"Considering your most weighty words and the command of Śrī Hari, I shall indeed perform the marriage; I am always subject to Kṛṣṇa."
But listen to the kind of woman whom I shall take as my beloved—
one who will be firm enough to receive and sustain my splendor.
Just as I am a yogi and a possessor of knowledge, she too shall become like me; equal to me in battle, in yoga, in realized wisdom, in virtues, in sovereignty, and in delight.
If it is not thus, you must always remain happily without marriage;
therefore, give me your wife in marriage, provided that she is equal to me.
"In that case, let there be a single wager for me; she must behave toward me accordingly.
If there is no trust in my word, she shall be abandoned by me. (126)
Having heard these words of Śambhu, Viṣṇu and Brahmā laughed and said to him:
"Such as she is, our most beloved, whom we have searched for so long."
In Goloka, she who is Śivā resides in the heart of Kṛṣṇa; having resided in the eyes of Vairāja, she became Taijasī within the senses of the gods.
O Śambhu, she who dwells within the circle of senses of Śrī Hari as he reclines upon Śeṣa is Night (Rātri), the dark one (Vibhāvarī); and she who is on your left side is Śivā.
Being eternally and inseparably connected, that virtuous daughter of Dakṣa would become a wife endowed with a splendor and strength even greater than yours.
O Lord of Gods, she performs penance for your sake with firm vows;
desiring to obtain you as her husband, that maiden remains in the house of Dakṣa. (131)
Go and grant her a boon, O Maheśvara; show her compassion.
Bestow upon her a boon that grants her every desire, and marry her with great affection.
Fulfill the intention of the gods who have come here;
may there be supreme auspiciousness, and may we behold that festival. (133)
Having heard this, Śaṅkara said, "Om; it is accepted by me.
I shall go to bestow the fruit of my penance; you, O gods, should also go.
You shall see me again at the time of the marriage festival."
Thus commanded and honored, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, the gods, and the others [departed].
Having uttered words of blessing, "May your heart's desire be fulfilled," they,
together with their wives, returned to their respective abodes, exceedingly joyful.

Thus, in the first section, the *Kṛtayugasantāna*, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*: the birth of Śambhu from the forehead of Vairāja; the arrival of Brahmā and Nārada after the manifestation of Śivā in the house of Dakṣa; the determination of her status as Śiva’s wife by means of the lines and marks described by Nārada; Satī’s performance of a year-long vow of austerity; and on the twelfth anniversary of Satī’s birth-festival (*jayantī*), the arrival of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and the gods with their wives, and the departure of Brahmā and the others for Kailāsa upon beholding Satī’s penance.
The one hundred and seventy-first chapter, titled "The Instruction Given to Śaṅkara for the Purpose of Bestowing the Boon of Satī’s Hand in Marriage," etc.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen to me, my dear Lakṣmī; for the sake of his beloved, Śambhu, being eager and with his consciousness awakened, became anxious about going to the house of Dakṣa.
Then, having fasted again on the eighth day of the bright fortnight in the month of Āśvina,
she worshipped Śaṅkara with sixteen offerings.
Thus, when the Nandā-vow was completed on the ninth day,
the Lord Śiva, beautiful in all his limbs, became manifest before her eyes.
He is fair-complexioned, five-faced, three-eyed, and has the moon as his crest-jewel;
he is serene in nature, blue-throated, four-armed, and adorned with the serpent Vāsuki.
Adorned with a trident, rudrākṣa beads, a lotus, and sacred ash,
his matted hair was graced by the Gaṅgā, and his entire body shone like gold.
His body possessed great loveliness, beauty, and delicacy; he was more enchanting than ten million Cupids, and his face was equal to ten million moons.
Overcome by blossoming youth and entirely captivating to women,
he beheld Śaṅkara before his very eyes and considered Satī to be his own wealth.
Extremely thrilled in her heart, yet with her face bowed down in great modesty,
she paid homage at the feet of Śambhu and drank in his face with her eyes.
She considered her own Mahodayā to have offered her entire being through her mind;
then Hara, although he desired a beloved wife for his heart, [reflected].
In order to experience that eternal affection arising from the depths of her heart,
and to hear her beloved words, Satī spoke to her who was firm in her vows.
