For him by whom a mark of gopīcandana is indeed made on the neck, or on the forehead, or on the two arms, there is liberation; of this there is no doubt.
A woman—whether she be with a husband, a widow, a maiden, a young girl, or even one who is destitute—who has turned the moon into dust by the pollen from her hair; ||23||
She may be a courtesan, a servant, or a slave; one who has found refuge, or one who is dependent;
or she may be independent, distracted, senseless, or fickle-minded. (24)
Whether she be wealthy or a pauper, learned or a fool,
deceitful or likewise [otherwise], a thief, lustful, or full of latent desires— whatever her nature may be.
One is instantly purified of sins and joined with millions of merits;
one becomes divine like Gopī and attains fitness for the lap of Kṛṣṇa. (26)
Having enjoyed inexhaustible pleasures in heaven for ten million yugas,
and being honored by the gods, she shall at the end go to the abode of Goloka.
There, having become a cowherd girl equal to Rādhā, she rejoices with Kṛṣṇa;
and whatever insects, moths, or flies there are in Gopīsarovara, [they likewise rejoice].
All beings— beasts, birds, reptiles, ants, wild animals, and so forth—
will certainly go to Goloka when they meet their death.
Bathed with black earth and immersed in the clay of the cowherd girls,
he is submerged in the lake of divine love and has been appointed as the ruler of Goloka.
Such a state is not attained through sacrifices, nor by gifts, nor by recitations, nor by Vedic study or austerities, as it is attained even by the dust of a gopī. || 31 ||
Gomatī, Gopikātāla, Gopālakṛṣṇa,
Gopīdhūlī, and the gift of cows— these five words beginning with the letter 'ga' bestow liberation.
By those who have attained the five *ga*s, everything has indeed been attained;
by him who has attained Kṛṣṇa-Hari, what remains here for him? (33)
If even a single speck of the dust from Gopī falls into the mouth of anyone at the time of death, that person also attains liberation; of this there is no doubt.
For one who dies either on the banks of the Gomatī, in front of the Gopikā-tāla tree, or in its vicinity,
Goloka-dhāma is certainly ordained for them by the attendants of Viṣṇu.
Even birds traveling through the path of the sky have gone to heaven;
how much more so those who float upon the surface of the Gopikātālā?
Even if an offering or even water has not been presented to Hari,
it shall indeed become His grace provided it is mixed with Gopīcandana.
If, due to irregularities in place, time, or other factors, one does not obtain food pleasing to Hari, then one should add a grain of rice to the meal or the drink.
Then one should indeed eat and drink, for that produces serenity;
truly, there would be transgression for one who eats without having offered [the food].
A person afflicted by the pain of possession by spirits, ghosts, or demons,
should indeed wear a beautiful pill of Gopīcandana around the neck.
One should consume the dust from the feet of the cowherd girls and bathe in that water;
with a concentrated mind, one should always place a crescent moon-mark upon the middle of the forehead.
When this is done, possession by piśācas and other spirits will certainly perish;
the meritorious soul becomes healthy and is purified in every respect. (42)
Even for a poor person, fortune indeed increases, bestowing prosperity;
likewise, there shall be the destruction of disease and the destruction of suffering. ||43||
Through their connection with the divine form of Kṛṣṇa, even the clay particles have attained divinity;
thus, they are considered to be free from all qualities (nirguṇa) and bestowers of liberation.
Through union with Kṛṣṇa, the cows, who are the Gomatī and the Gopikās, possess the form of Kṛṣṇa;
they lead the living beings who have come into their presence to the state of the attributeless Self.

Those who are connected to Kṛṣṇa—whether insentient matter or sentient beings, and whether beyond the modes of nature or otherwise—liberate others just like Kṛṣṇa himself, provided their minds are fixed on Kṛṣṇa. (46)
Desire, greed, anger, pride, delusion, and envy—these, having abandoned their own nature as defects, attain the state of virtues in Kṛṣṇa. (47)
Women, men, animals, asuras, weapons, vehicles, clothing, food, and drink—all would become devoid of quality. (48)
Even Māyā, though devoid of qualities, becomes divine through association with Him;
what more need be said regarding that which is united with the quality-less Kṛṣṇa? 49.
Blessed indeed is the cowherd caste, blessed likewise is the lineage of cows;
blessed is the lineage of Goloka, which is filled with the bliss of Kṛṣṇa.
Thus ends the two hundred and twenty-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Greatness of Gopīcandana," in the first section, the Kṛtayuga-santāna, of the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Thereafter, one should go to the Brahmakuṇḍa, a holy place that destroys all sins,
surrounded by the deities for the purpose of beholding Kṛṣṇa.
And Brahmā arrived at the city of Dvāravatī during the festival, as did Varuṇa,
Indra, Yama, Kubera, and likewise the Sun and the Moon.
And other guardians of the directions and others arrived for the purpose of witnessing that assembly which had been arranged by Brahmā.
In that very place is a great holy site, and on its bank is Brahmakuṇḍa;
there the Sun was installed by Brahmā, and he remains there forever.
That is declared to be Sūryatīrtha, which destroys all sins;
having seen both Brahmatīrtha and Sūryatīrtha, the Moon created a lake.
That lake became famous by the name Candra;
it is the abode of the Sun, the primordial seat, and bestows the merit of a thousand śrāddhas.

On the seventh day of the bright fortnight of Māgha, having bathed and smeared the ground for the Sun, one performs that which is delightful, brings satisfaction to the ancestors, and destroys ten million sins.
That person who shall worship the Sun with offerings of flowers and incense, and with water, leaves, fruits, ritual substances, and sacrificial fees; || 8 ||
Having enjoyed all desires here, he will go to the world of Brahmā;
and from there, in the presence of Brahmā and the temple of the Sun, || 9 ||
Having caused a temple to be built for Sāvitrī and having established her in that sanctuary within the chariot of the Sun, he himself [worshipped] her by the name Sāvitrī.
The Lotus-born [Brahmā] worshipped the Goddess in her image according to the prescribed rites;
likewise, he honored the site of Candrasaras and the beautiful temple of Sāvitrī.
That supreme sacred site was created by the Creator, the Supreme Lord;
Brahmā himself likewise took up residence within his own form.
By the rite of installation, the Unborn One performed his own consecration.
And that Brahma-tīrtha was born there, which destroys the power of diseases and mental afflictions.
Those who, having seen [it], shall worship Brahmā, Sāvitrī, Sūrya, and likewise Candramas, they shall go to the supreme goal.
Then the auspicious Gāyatrī was established there by Brahmā, and the auspicious rite for her installation was performed by him himself.
This is the supreme Gāyatrītīrtha, which bestows the world of Brahmā;
one should worship those gods and goddesses there with flowers, water-offerings (arghya), water, and saffron.
One should bathe and worship [the deity] with devotion, using garments, food offerings, and meals,
as well as ornaments, vessels, camphor, cardamom, and other such items.
One should worship with betel leaves and saffron with great devotion;
one should meditate upon Him, bow down, and, full of zeal, prostrate like a staff, saying "Obeisance! (namaḥ). || 18 ||
With a lamp, a sacrificial thread, Tulasī, Karavīra flowers,
other fragrant blossoms, offerings of light (ārātrika), and likewise with hymns of praise.
One should worship those gods together with Viṣṇu by performing circumambulations;
one should worship Kṛṣṇa there, and one should also worship the Śālagrāma.
Then one should worship Śaṅkara together with Pārvatī and his attendants;
having worshipped them, one should bathe Sāvitrī, and thus the fruit of the pilgrimage shall be attained. ||21||
From that, there shall be neither widowhood, nor misfortune, nor barrenness;
indeed, there shall never be the state of having children who die, nor the state of being childless in any way.
Wealth, grain, land, and prosperity, as well as the attainment of sons, grandsons, and so forth, accrue day by day to one who worships the Sun and the other [planets]. (23)
Kṛṣṇa will become fully satisfied and the pilgrimage will be fruitful;
therefore, one should worship Kṛṣṇa there together with Rukmiṇī. ||24||
Then Brahmā created the Brahmaliṅga lake there,
and likewise Indra made a most beautiful lake there.
He established Brahmā and Mahendra together with Śacī there;
by bathing at that site of Indra’s station, people attain both heaven and truth.
Having bathed, worshipped, and beheld Brahmeśvara, Indreśvara, and Vṛddhīśvara, one is liberated from worldly existence. ||27||
What is performed on the eighth and fourteenth days yields inexhaustible merit;
through a śrāddha offered there, eternal satisfaction arises for the ancestors.
Especially, however, they should be worshipped when the sun is situated in Capricorn, at dawn on the occasion of the Uttarāyaṇa-saṃkrānti, Śivarātri, and other such festivals. (29)
Having bathed in those very lakes, one should visit those respective holy sites;
and by worshipping those deities, one becomes a partaker of liberation—of this there is no doubt.
And likewise, Śaṅkara, together with Satī, performed his ablutions there;
having bathed in that water as well, he worshipped Śaṅkara and Satī.
Having bathed there together with Brahmā and Viṣṇu, the wielder of the Pināka bow became known on the surface of the earth as Mahādeva-saras.
There, at the Mahādeva-sarovara, the libation for the ancestors (tarpaṇa) and the ancestral rite (śrāddha) bestow inexhaustible happiness; through its mere sight, one is liberated from sin.
Bathing, giving gifts, recitation, burnt offerings, self-study of scripture, and the worship of the gods [yield great merit].
All that becomes a bestower of inexhaustible fruit for the one who performs it. ||34||
There is no misfortune for a man, nor is there childlessness for a woman;
having bathed here in the Gaurī-saras, one shall obtain all desires. (35)
And Varuṇa, having seen all those very places,
caused a divine lake to be constructed there under his own name.
On its bank, he established the goddess Vāruṇī as his own form, the deity of the waters, and worshipped her with devotion.
On the full moon day of the month of Bhādrapada, having performed the viewing of Varuṇa, one should perform the Śrāddha and the libation (tarpaṇa); therein the fruit is inexhaustible.
One should give water-pots, curd-rice, and excellent food;
likewise cows, garments, gems, cooked foods, and savory juices.
Having said, "May Viṣṇu be pleased with me," one should likewise give an umbrella and other gifts to a virtuous Brahmin or a virtuous woman; thus the fruit becomes inexhaustible.
The donor attains the state of Brahmā, reaching which he does not grieve;
and having seen the lake of Varuṇa, Kubera created a lake [there]. (41)
Thereafter, he became renowned by the name Kuberasara.
Having bathed at Kuberadarśana and performed the rites on the bank, one should feed [the brahmins]. ||42||
One should likewise fumigate the Brahmins, the virtuous men, and the virtuous women, as well as the sacrificial fee;
one should also give a gift of gold, for then the Lord of Wealth (Kubera) is quickly pleased. 43.
This increases prosperity and shall bear fruit a thousandfold.
Silver, gold, copper, brass, or tin. ||44||
Whether it be a diamond, a gem, a jewel, or fine garments and the like;
wealth, grain, as well as cows, buffaloes, and even maidens. ||45||
Clothing, a bedstead, a meditation ball and so forth, a water-pot, or even a bowl;
flowers, fruit, sweet food, oil, or even fragrance—[these are all to be offered]. (46)
Camphor and other articles of adornment such as sandalwood paste, as well as sandals, an umbrella, a fly-whisk, and a vehicle; ||47||
A vehicle, a woman, a son, a servant, livestock, one's own property, a cart, as well as a chest, ornaments, and other things, food, drink, and meals. ||48||
Whatever one might give—a broom, or a mortar, or a grinding stone, as well as a hearth, a water-pot, or a cooking pot—all that becomes the gift of a thousand. ||49||
Having remembered Kṛṣṇa and Kubera, and having meditated upon Sūrya and Śiva,
and having remembered the great goddesses beginning with Rukmiṇī, one should give that which bestows infinite results.
A person who performs the rites at Kubera-tīrtha certainly attains great merit, a great heavenly realm, and finally the imperishable abode of Hari.
Thereafter, one should go to the supreme purifying holy site of Pañcanada,
as well as to Gomatī, Lakṣmīgaṅgā, and Dvārāvatī.
Having likewise beheld Gopītāla and other lakes,
the lords of creatures established the sacred ford consisting of the five rivers.
The five rivers were summoned and arrived there with great haste;
then he indeed called for Marīci, Gomatī, Matrī, and Lakṣmaṇā.
Aṅgiras summoned the Candrabhāgā, Pulaha the Kuśāvatī,
and Kratu called forth the river Jāmbavatī there.
In those [rivers] bathed the sons of Brahmā and all the deities;
that sacred ford, known as Pañcanada, is the supreme bestower of liberation.
One should bathe there according to the prescribed rite, and water for honor (argha) should also be offered:
"May the rivers accept this argha; may they become bestowers of heaven and liberation. (57)
One should perform ablutions, drink water, and likewise satisfy the ancestors;
one should give five jewels and seven grains to the twice-born.
One should give whatever object one desires to the poor, the blind, and the wretched;
such a person attains all their wishes and goes to the world of Viṣṇu. ||59||
Endowed with sons and grandsons, he shall attain supreme happiness;
and all his ancestors who have become pretas shall attain liberation at that place.
From there, one should certainly go to the great tirtha known as Siddheśvara;
that very linga was established by the four perfected ones (siddhas) beginning with Sanaka. 61.
And nearby, they dug a well of sweet water, which became renowned as Ṛṣitīrtha; by drinking its water, one is liberated from sin. ||62||
Merely by bathing with devotion, the world of Brahmā is attained;
yet there are those who are wicked, slanderers, deceivers, and deceitful people. (63)
By merely bathing at Ṛṣitīrtha, one is purified; of this there is no doubt—especially on the equinoxes, on the lunar days of the Manus, and at the commencement of the Yugas.
He who dwells at Ṛṣitīrtha and worships Siddheśa on the night of Śivarātri during the dark fortnight of the month of Māgha, while chanting the eternal Supreme Brahman, [attains the highest goal].
Having bathed and worshipped the deity, one should perform prostrations and the libation (tarpaṇa);
likewise, one should perform the ancestral rite (śrāddha) and bestow various kinds of gifts.
Liberation comes into his very hands; of this there is no doubt.
In this case, especially, delicious fruits should be offered. (67)
He gave śyāmāka and nīvāra grains, coral, sesame seeds as well,
śāli rice, the seven types of grain, and parched flour mixed with sugar.
Clarified butter, garlands, betel, perfumes, garments, cow’s milk,
and likewise dinaras, should be given to the poor, the naked, the Brahmins, and the virtuous.
One should bathe Siddheśvara with milk; one shall become a partaker of liberation.
When there is a vision of the Great God Siddheśvara, human beings [attain this state].
Those without sons shall become possessed of sons and grandsons in every way;
those without wealth shall become wealthy and shall experience happiness. (71)
Maidens shall obtain virtuous husbands and the wealth of good fortune;
their misdeeds shall dissolve away, and their merit shall increase. (72)
From there, O Mahālakṣmī, one should go to the unsurpassed Gadātīrtha,
where by bathing a person obtains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.
There, having bowed to the Blessed One in his boar-form, and having saluted, praised, and worshipped him, one is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu. ||74||
There, at the junction of the first Yuga, the Lord himself, in the form of the Boar (Vārāha),
arrived and rested for a moment, having set down his mace.
Then, desiring a vision of Kṛṣṇa, one should go to Nāgatīrtha;
there the Nāgas, having come from Pātāla, stayed for a moment in Dvārakā. (76)
Having bathed there, one shall attain the Supreme Brahman; of this there is no doubt.
Thence, one should go to the great and supreme holy site named Candrabhāgā.
Having bathed there with devotion, a person shall attain the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice.
The Candrabhāgā river holds a spear in her hand and carries a sword and a shield.
She who was the sister of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, who caused fear to Kaṃsa and other demons—by the mere sight of her, one may attain all desires. (79)
From there, one should go to the sacred ford named Muktidvāra,
where the Gomatī river was brought by Vasiṣṭha and remains established.
By placing that water upon one's head, one shall attain the heavenly world;
thereafter, one should go to the unsurpassed Kālindī-saras tīrtha. ||8 1||
Yamī, the daughter of the Sun, has come here and remains present in every way;
she is eternally devoted to the service of Kṛṣṇa, and through bathing [here], one shall attain liberation. 82.
From there, one should go to Sāmbatīrtha, a most purifying sacred site;
in ancient times, Śambhu, accompanied by Ambā, became the son of Kṛṣṇa.
His place is a great holy site, the Sāmbatīrtha, which bestows excellent liberation;
having bathed there with devotion, a person shall obtain a golden form.
From there, one should go to the river Lakṣmī, which is resorted to by Nāyaṇas;
for there Lakṣmī herself dwelt in the form of water, longing for Kṛṣṇa. 85.
By the mere touch of which one is liberated from all sins;
from there, one should go to Kambusaras and drink its pure water.
Where the water of Śaṅkha was indeed held by Nārāyaṇa, there it became that lake, and Śaṅkha remained established there. ||87||
That is declared to be Śaravatīrtha; having bathed there, one shall attain liberation.
Then one should go to the Jāleśvara tīrtha, which purifies the world. (88)
Long ago, the sons of Yadu were cursed here by the sage Kaṇva with a web of curses for the destruction of the Yadu lineage. (89)
The Great God Jāleśvara was installed there by the boys for the sake of pacifying that curse; that sacred site is supremely bestowing of happiness.
Having worshipped Jāleśa, one shall attain the world of Śiva;
from there, one should go to the supremely purifying Jaratkāru-tīrtha. ||91||
There indeed dwells a certain Naga maiden named Jaratkarvi,
who was married by the sage Jaratkaru for the sake of delivering her ancestors.
By the attainment of a son, the ancestors are entirely delivered by him;
and that sacred site (tīrtha) indeed delivers the ancestors through bathing and giving gifts.
Indeed, there is the Ānakadundubhi-tīrtha, as well as the Akrūra-tīrtha, the Bala-tīrtha, the Ugrasena-tīrtha, and the Arjuna-tīrtha. ||94||
Devakī-tīrtha is the foremost, as is Rohiṇī-tīrtha;
Subhadrā-tīrtha is likewise, as is Kardama-tīrtha.
There are the holy sites (tīrthas) of Kṛṣṇa’s attendants, as well as the holy sites of his wives, and also the holy sites of his devotees, all of which have produced wonders here. (96)
There are millions of famous and now vanished sacred sites;
but where Goloka itself exists in person, what is there that does not exist? 97.
There are indeed holy fords at every step; of this there is no doubt.
They have been repeatedly washed by the waters of the ocean and covered with dust. (98)
Even the dust of this place bestows liberation, its wind destroys sin, and its water grants the body of a daughter of Diti through union with Kṛṣṇa; of this there is no doubt. (99)
Dvārakā is the gateway to liberation, the gateway to heaven, and the gateway to happiness;
O Lakṣmī, that sacred ford known as Dvārakā should indeed always be resorted to.

Thus ends the two hundred and twenty-sixth chapter, titled "The Display of the Thirty-Six Holy Places, including the Brahma-kuṇḍa, the Sun, Varuṇa, Kubera, Prabhiti-devasaras, Varā, and the Five Rivers at Dvārakā," in the first section, the Kṛta-yuga lineage, of the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī, to those gatekeepers who dwell in every direction;
stationed all around Dvārakā, they protect the domain of Kṛṣṇa. || 1 ||
In the east, Jayanta, the son of Indra, always resides;
his disciples, the Danujas, likewise remain there as obedient followers of his command.
Vajranābha, Sunābha, Vajrabāhu, Mahāhanu, Vajradaṃṣṭra, Vajradhārī, Vajrahā, and Vajralocana. || 3 ||
Śvetamūrdhā, Śvetamālī, Naranātha, Vināyaka, Sūrya, the seven Mothers, as well as Śambhu and Takṣaka. || 4 ||
Kārttikeya, the rājasa [demon] named Dīrgharoman, the gandharva Viśvāvasu, and likewise the apsaras Menakā; || 5 ||
Sanatkumāra, Vasiṣṭha, and Nyagrodha the great banyan tree;
then, in the direction of Agni (the southeast), Jvālāmukha and Aruṇākṣaka stand.
Kuśa, who dwells in cremation grounds, who eats flesh and drinks blood;
Kṛṣṇa, who wears black matted hair, as well as Trāsana and Bhañjana. || 7 ||
Agni, Sthālī, Apsaras, Gandharva, and likewise Amāvāsu;
then in the southern quarter [are] Daṇḍapāṇi, Mahāsvara,
Pāśahasta, Trinetra, Ativarta, and Māraṇa.
Dundubhisvaraka, Kharasvara, Ghargharava, Maunapriya, Mallika, Durdarśa, and Vināyaka. || 9 ||
Mahiṣīka, Sūrya, Bhūṣaṇa, Catura,
Citrāṅgada, Sugandha, and the Apsaras named Urvaśī.
Goraja, Dānava, Śāla, Mahādruma,
and the eternal sage Agastya are the guardians of the southern gate.
Then, in the direction of Nairṛta (the southwest), there are Gomukha, Muṇḍana,
as well as Nagna, Kambalī, Rodana, and Hasana.
Lambagrīva, Bhrūvikāra, Dvijambhaka, Sūryaka, Muśalin, and Menakā protect the southwestern direction (Nairṛtī). 13.
Then, in the western direction, there is Svastika, who has a conch for a head,
a beautiful face, blue garments, feet and hands, and whose source is the root.
Ekapāda, Ekanetra, Sthūlajaṅgha, Mahacchiras, Puṣpadanta, Gaṇeśa, Sūrya, and Satrājiteśvara. || 15 ||
Tumburu and Ghṛtācī, Mahodara and Sarīsṛpa, Ghaṭotkaca and Pañcajana, Kāśyapa and Kapālinī. || 16 ||
The Aśvattha tree and Kapila protect the western direction;
furthermore, Bhañjana and Bhairava are likewise in the northwestern quarter.
Ghaṭodara, Kālika, Daṇḍaka, Mardana, Ruru, Ṣaṅga, Sarvabhuja, Ghṛṇī, and Supārśva are those born in the direction of Vāyu (the northwest). || 18 ||
Then, in the north, there is Sūrya at Mūlasthāna, Śiva as Indreśvara,
Kaṇṭheśvarī, Khañjana, Vāsuki, and the Dānava Kūrma.
Sanaka, the Rākṣasa named Golaka, Nārada,
the Apsaras Raṃbhā, and the Plakṣa tree protect the northern direction.
Now, in the northeast, there are Kilīka, Durdhara, Bhairavānana,
Dīrghāsya, Meghavaktra, Karāla, and likewise Vikaca.
Mūka, Balibhuk, Balipriya, and Māṃsabhuja—
all these guardians of the directions reside there, O Lotus-born One.
Jayanta, the foremost of all, protects the *pattala* [enclosure];
having worshipped these, the great worship of Kṛṣṇa’s task is indeed accomplished. ||23||
Then, by the command of Kṛṣṇa, the worship and vision of Rukmiṇīgaṇeśa must be performed according to the prescribed rite at the gateway.
And Bhīṣmaka, having prepared a festival to give Rukmiṇī to Kṛṣṇa,
was opposed by Rukmin, who did not agree with his words.
And when the Blessed Lord Hari Kṛṣṇa carried away Rukmiṇī from Ambikāsthala, Rukmin then made a vow.
"I shall certainly not withdraw from the battle without having slain Kṛṣṇa," saying this,
Rukmaka went with speed to do battle against Kṛṣṇa.
Having been bound by Kṛṣṇa, he too had half of his beard shaved off;
through this humiliation, he became determined to die.
He was protected by the Blessed Lord for the sake of pleasing Rukmiṇī.
He was indeed honored by the hosts and even appointed as their leader. ||29||
Therefore, worship of Kṛṣṇa must always be performed for his satisfaction;
thereafter, one should also fully honor Durvāsas and Baladeva.
One should worship Śrī Kṛṣṇa in his temple, which resembles his own abode;
[one thereby obtains] the fruit of all sacrifices and the fruit of all sacrificial fees. || 31 ||
Through worship, one obtains the fruit of all yogas, the fruit of knowledge, the fruit of the Ganges, as well as the fruit of all gifts and the fruit of liberation.
Then one should joyfully worship the Lord Trivikrama as Vāmana.
Once, however, the kingdom of King Bali existed upon the surface of the earth.
Then Durvāsas arrived at Cakratīrtha to bathe;
there he was struck excessively by the gods with their knees and fists.
And the great asura named Ruru restrained them;
meanwhile, Durvāsas, having been protected, then departed for Kailāsa.
In the meantime, O King, the Blessed Lord Vāmana himself,
stationed at the gate of Bali, conquered the earth with three paces.
Then Durvāsas felt anxious about what would bring him happiness;
he sought refuge with Vāmana, who was served by Bali.
Then, beholding the sage approaching, Bali, the lord of the Daityas,
rose to meet him, offered him honor, and seated him upon a throne.
Bowing down, he said, "Tell me the reason for your arrival here.
And Durvāsas, having seen the four-armed Viṣṇu at the gate of Bali, [spoke].
Weeping and sighing repeatedly with great intensity, he cried out, "Save me! Save me!
Seeing the brahmin in such distress, the compassionate Mādhava spoke.
"O Sage, tell me quickly why and from what cause have you fallen into this suffering?
Durvāsas replied, "O Blessed One, having recognized that this sacred ford (tīrtha) bestows liberation... (41)
Having gone to Cakratīrtha to bathe, even before he had completed his ablutions,
he was seized by the neck by the Daityas and struck violently with their fists.
Having forcibly seized their garments, kusha grass, and unbroken rice, he was driven out while being reviled: "If he returns, we shall kill him! (43)
"After bathing here at Cakratīrtha, I shall then take my meal;
therefore, O Govinda, bathe me and protect me, who have come to you for refuge. (44)
Having said, "I have desisted," the wrathful sage Durvāsas,
the blessed Lord who is devoted to Brahman, spoke to that Brāhmaṇa.
"Having slain the Daityas, I shall perform my ablutions; come with me!
And the Blessed Lord Trivikrama arrived together with the sage. 46.
And Kṛṣṇa said, "O sage, perform your bath for the sake of peace.
Having heard those words, Durvāsas performed his bath with haste.
The twice-born one began to perform his daily rites, such as the twilight prayers;
meanwhile, the Dānava Durmukha stood there with eyes bloodshot with rage.
He arrived and indeed desired to kill Durvāsas;
Kṛṣṇa, however, effortlessly severed the head of Durmukha with his discus.
Then the Daityas, experts in weaponry, assembled for the sake of battle;
[the gods] Viṣṇu, Saṃkarṣaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, and Vāmana arrived from all sides.
In battle, they struck down the Daityas with arrows, missiles, and weapons—
namely Duḥsaha, Kūrmapṛṣṭha, Golaka, and Vedadūṣaka.
They slew the destroyer of sacrifices and the slayer of the sacrifice, as well as the ender of dharma;
then Kuśa arrived, having resolved upon battle. ||52||
An army division (anīka) consists of ten thousand elephants, likewise ten thousand (ayuta) [elephants];
two ayutas of chariots, and ten ayutas of horses. 53.
Vakraga, Dīrghanakha, Nighasa, Prasava, as well as Ūrdhvabāhu, Vakraśiras, Kañcuka, and Śilonmukha; || 54 ||
Yajñadhmā, as well as Rāhu, Babaraka, Mahāhanu, Sunāman, and Vasunāman—the Daityas—went forth for battle. (55)
Then Kuśa, desiring victory, worshipped Mahādeva and, seizing a sword in his hand, rushed with speed toward Keśava. ||56||
He said: "If I conquer, my fame shall indeed be incomparable; or, if I am struck down by you, I shall go to the supreme goal. (57)
Having spoken thus, he effortlessly severed the head of the fleeing man;
fallen into the presence of Śiva, he was restored to life and rose up again. ||98||
Having bowed to Viṣṇu, he said: "What harm has been done to you by these Daityas?
Having bathed Durvāsas, do as you wish. (59)
Kṛṣṇa said: "Indeed, the holy ford has been blocked by you in every way;
therefore, I shall slay all the Dānavas—of this there is no doubt."
Then Kuśa fought with Kṛṣṇa with great speed;
filled with wrath, the Blessed One struck off his head with his discus.
Then his body and head were cast by the Daityas into the temple of Śiva; at that very moment, indeed, through the grace of Śaṅkara, he [was restored].
Suddenly appearing and seizing his mace, he stood ready for battle;
for he had indeed been made immortal by the gratified Mahādeva.
Furthermore, his head having been split by Hari with His own mace,
Kuśa was then cast into a pit and covered with earth and stones.
Then Viṣṇu installed a Śiva-liṅga upon him;
although he was restored to life, he did not rise again, and he spoke: [65]
"O Viṣṇu, this Śiva-liṅga which has been installed by you upon me—let it be known by my name as 'Kuśeśa'. (66)
And at Kuśasthalī, Kṛṣṇa likewise established a great holy site (tīrtha) called Kuśeśa,
saying "Let it be so," for the sake of bestowing grace upon Kuśa.
Then, on another occasion, Mādhava destroyed all the other Dānavas;
some had gone to the subterranean realm (rasātala), while others remained in a state of servitude.
Vāmana, as well as Viṣṇu, Ananta, and the sage Krodhana—
these and others, having established their abodes in Dvāravatī, remain there forever.
And by their second form, those holy places truly exist as Kṛṣṇa, Viṣṇu, Vāmana, Saṃkarṣaṇa, and Durvāsas.
The Tīrthaṅkara should be worshipped with perfumes, flowers, food offerings,
ornaments, garments, fruits, betel, unbroken grains, sandalwood, and saffron.
With incense for the night vigil, with lamps, musical instruments, and hymns of praise, as well as with circumambulations, ritual fees, eulogies, and prostrations; ||72||
Having worshipped with all kinds of offerings, one should keep a vigil at night;
and on the eighth and twelfth days of the month of Bhādrapada, having worshipped those deities.
Having bathed Hari-Kṛṣṇa and worshipped him according to the prescribed rites, one attains the abode of Goloka, reaching which one no longer grieves.
Having worshipped Tulasī, one should then worship Durvāsas;
thereafter, one should worship Gaṇeśa and Vainateya.
One should worship Rukmiṇī according to one's ability with the sixteen secondary articles;
then planetary afflictions will not arise, nor will diseases occur. (76)
Affliction by spirits, ghosts, and the like shall perish through the worship of Rukmiṇī;
one should bathe Rukmiṇī with curd, milk, and likewise with honey. (77)
With sugar, ghee, fragrant scents, and sweet-smelling sandalwood; with excellent unguents and superior oils, and then with waters prepared for the consecration.
With sandalwood paste, saffron, musk, and likewise with saffron filaments,
one should anoint Mahālakṣmī and Rukmiṇī with great devotion.
The sonless shall have a son, and the one without wealth shall obtain wealth;
he shall acquire servants, employees, cattle, and cows, as well as enjoyments and riches.
One should worship with *mālatī* flowers, fragrant *śatapatra* lilies,
*karavīra*, *mallikā*, *tulasī*, and royal *campaka* blossoms.
One should adorn the Goddess with karavīra and ketaka flowers, with incenses, garments, and wealth, as well as with ornaments, jewels, gems, and decorations.
For one who worships in this manner, there shall never be anyone in the family who is destitute.
He shall not be childless, nor unfortunate, nor a servant of the base. ||8.3||
Then one should offer the favorite food, such as various kinds of snacks and meals, and with a sincere heart,
one should present betel leaf along with camphor.
Then one should offer fruit, water, and likewise the arghya;
thereafter, the ārātrika, and having performed the nīrājana with camphor, one should then offer the water from a conch shell.
One should whirl it in all directions as a means of protection and wear it upon the head;
one should prostrate on the ground like a staff, saying, "Salutation to the beloved of Kṛṣṇa."
Then one should give various gifts to the wife of the Brahmin,
such as vermilion, necklaces, garments, perfumes, flowers, and saffron.
He also provided collyrium, betel, and ever-new foods and delicacies;
then likewise [he honored] Queen Satyabhāmā and Jāmbavatī as well. 88.
And having worshipped Mitravindā, Kālindī, Bhadrā, and likewise Agnijitī, he gratified them with sixteen offerings of milk-rice (pāyasa). ||89||
The worshiper attains all desires both in this world and in the hereafter;
therefore, with every effort, so too do queens who are beloved by Kṛṣṇa.
When they are propitiated with supreme devotion, they shall become bestowers of heaven and liberation;
their life is fruitful, and their desires are fulfilled. (91)
On the eighth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Māgha, on the twelfth day of Caitra,
and likewise on the eighth day of Vaiśākha, Jyeṣṭha, Bhādrapada, and Kārttika.
When that [twelfth lunar day] of the bright fortnight is conjoined with the day of Kṛṣṇa (Wednesday) and is worshipped,
it indeed bestows long life and an imperishable lineage of sons.
Whoever causes a very firm temple for Rukmiṇī and Kṛṣṇa to be built,
his residence shall be in the abode of Goloka, within the palace of Kṛṣṇa itself.
And whoever shall cause the arrangement for the perpetual offering of food (naivedya) to be fully established, there shall be the constant attainment of the Lord's grace in his abode. (95)
Whoever offers garments, fans, umbrellas, chowries, water-pots, and so forth to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, for him there is an infinite reward in His abode. (96)
For the servant of the feet of Kṛṣṇa’s splendor, there are always abundant and divine riches, as well as women who are the objects of Kṛṣṇa’s enjoyment. 97.

He who bathes in all sacred fords and gives gifts according to his ability does not obtain even a fraction of the fruit of all sacrifices in the Kali age as he does from the worship of the glory of Kṛṣṇa.
O Mahālakṣmī, except for the meritorious Dvāravatī, liberation is truly not obtained anywhere else in the Kali age; and that divine field of mine exists there.
Thus has been told to you the supreme and most excellent majesty of the sacred ford;
by hearing and reciting this, a person shall obtain the fruit of that holy site.

Thus ends the two hundred and twenty-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Names of the Guardians of the Dwārakā Region, the Destruction of the Kuśāda Daityas for the Purpose of Durvāsas’s Bath, and the Tīrthas such as Kuśeśvara, Vāmana, and Paṭṭarājñī," in the first section on the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga within the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Those who hear and read the greatness of Kṛṣṇa in the Kali age are considered to have their residence forever in the abodes of Vaikuṇṭha and Goloka.
For one to whom the stories of Kṛṣṇa are always dearer than even life itself,
nothing desired is difficult to attain, both in this world and in the next.
Whatever fruit is obtained from residing in Kāśī for a thousand Manvantaras,
that same fruit is obtained by residing in Dvāravatī for five days.
Even a dog-cooker (outcaste) living here shall attain the state of ascetics;
for one who has set out toward Dvārakā, there shall be merit at every step.
The Lotus-born One has declared that the fruit obtained from bathing during a solar eclipse at Kurukṣetra is the same as the fruit that occurs here upon seeing [the deity] during a lunar eclipse.
Whatever fruit is obtained at Puṣkara by bathing during the month of Kārtika over the course of ten million years,
that same fruit accrues to an embodied being who dwells constantly in Dvārakā.
O beloved, whatever fruit is obtained by a hundred men in Avantī,
that same fruit may be attained in Dvārakā by staying for even a single day.
The merit of beholding Kṛṣṇa is considered superior to ten million vows;
the fruit of serving Rukmiṇī and Kṛṣṇa is liberation in Goloka.
Blessed are they and fulfilled are they who have beheld the orb of Kṛṣṇa;
and so too is he who performs the worship of Kṛṣṇa on the twelfth lunar day with true devotion.
One who causes a bath with milk obtains the fruit born of a hundred horse-sacrifices;
that which is performed with *darbha* grass is ten times more effective than with milk, and that with clarified butter is ten times greater than the former.
Honey is ten times the value of ghee; according to Śaṅkha, that is increased tenfold [for silver];
and water from flowers and water from *darbha* grass increase tenfold beyond that.
Bathing with mantra-water and scented water, and even ten times more than that,
or bathing with sugarcane juice, is equal to performing a hundred horse-sacrifices.
Bathing in the waters of a sacred ford (tīrtha) is traditionally held to be ten times more meritorious than that;
one with desires shall attain heaven, while one free from desire shall attain liberation.
Whatever person should wipe dry with a cloth one whose body is wet from bathing in the Kṛṣṇa [lake],
for that person the sins of a hundred thousand lifetimes become wiped away.
Whoever bathes Hari and offers him a garland of flowers shall obtain merit equal to the fruit of giving ten million gold coins (niṣkas). || 15 ||
If one thousand names of Kṛṣṇa are recited at the time of bathing,
for every single syllable, there arises merit equal to that of giving away a hundred Kapilā cows.
And he who performs dancing or singing before Kṛṣṇa at the time of his bath becomes a beloved of Kṛṣṇa in Goloka. || 17 ||
At the time of bathing, for those who cry out "Victory to Hari! Victory to Kṛṣṇa!
and clap their hands, there is no emergence from the confinement of the womb.
Those who worship with garments, incense, and golden ornaments shall dwell in Vaikuṇṭha for a hundred manvantaras, and thereafter [attain liberation].
By serving Kṛṣṇa with ketakī flowers, tulasī blossoms, or other flowers, one attains eternal residence in Goloka.
And those women who worship the Lord of Rukmiṇī with Mālatī play together with their husbands in the seven celestial realms. ||21||
After a full hundred manvantaras, they shall attain Goloka—
the realm of those who practice yoga, perform sacrifices, give gifts, and frequent sacred fords.
Likewise, for those who are devoted to their fathers and mothers, who observe the vow of the twelfth day (dvādaśī), and who perform the night vigil on the eleventh day (ekādaśī) while dancing; ||23||
Whatever fruit is obtained by those who sing, those who remember, those who proclaim the Vedas, and likewise by those who recite the thousand names of Viṣṇu; || 24 ||
The fruit of that [merit] arises from offering Tulasī during the worship of Kṛṣṇa;
moreover, the fruit of the worship of Rukmiṇī and Kṛṣṇa is even greater than that. ||25||
Just as Lakṣmī is dear to Viṣṇu, Tulasī is even more so;
for wherever Tulasī is present, Hari is indeed worshipped.
In that regard, he shall obtain the fruit of a pilgrimage to Dvārakā;
by worshipping Kṛṣṇa even with a single Ketakī flower, one gains the merit born of a horse-sacrifice for every blossom.
Indeed, at the end one attains the fruit and reaches the state of Goloka;
by worshipping Kṛṣṇa with jasmine flowers, one attains the abode of Hari.
One should worship Hari, the Lord of Śrī, with fresh leaves and flowers;
having enjoyed divine and human pleasures, he goes to the abode of Hari.
This eight-syllabled mantra is: "Śrīkṛṣṇaḥ śaraṇaṃ mama" (Śrī Kṛṣṇa is my refuge).
Reciting that [mantra], one should worship Kṛṣṇa with fragrant sandalwood paste.
If one were to attain equality with Kṛṣṇa through camphor and musk,
then he who offers incense to Hari with clarified butter and guggulu shall shake off all sin and become beautiful in the imperishable realm.
During the dark fortnight, he causes a garland of lamps to be maintained day after day.
He who offers various kinds of food offerings to Kṛṣṇa shall indeed become the king of the seven islands; such is the fruit for each and every island.
His ancestors, indeed being satisfied, shall attain eternal liberation.
[One should offer] betel-leaf with camphor, combined with areca nut and other powdered ingredients. (34)
For one who gives to Kṛṣṇa, there is no rebirth in this illusory world;
water that is cool and rich with fragrance should be offered to Kṛṣṇa for His satisfaction. (35)
There shall be eternal satisfaction for him from drinking the eternal nectar and other such drinks,
as well as from offering fruits that are beautiful, sweet, and ripe.
Furthermore, for one who likewise gives [food] solely for the sake of cleansing the mouth, there shall be eternal satisfaction in Goloka, and he shall possess fragrant breath. (37)

He who causes a flower garden to be made around the temple of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, which is the abode of the sovereign of the universe and the place where Śrī Kṛṣṇa performs His divine strides (prakramaṇa). ||38||
She who offers a fan or a whisk to Kṛṣṇa sports in the Puṣpaka celestial chariot with tens of millions of gods.
In her abode, Kṛṣṇa himself kisses the lotus-face of the bed-maker;
and Keśava sleeps upon the bed together with her.
Whoever causes a pavilion for Śrī Kṛṣṇa to be constructed with plantain pillars,
for him the Apsarases, who are like plantains, perform service.
The person who brings beauty to the temple of Kṛṣṇa with banners shall always dwell in the world of the Sun, like the Sun himself. (42)
One should perfume the temple of Hari with the finest fragrances of incense and sandalwood; his abode shall indeed become perfumed in heaven.
She who always performs the massaging of Kṛṣṇa’s feet with her heart becomes Ramā and rejoices together with Kṛṣṇa in Goloka. (44)
Having prepared fresh food, she should feed Śrī Kṛṣṇa;
she indeed becomes Lakṣmī forever and shall worship Śrī Hari in Vaikuṇṭha. ||45||
Those people on earth who always perform service to Śrī Kṛṣṇa are surrounded by celestial maidens in heaven and served by hosts of apsarases.
Whoever erects an auspicious flagstaff upon the Śrīkṛṣṇa peak shall have a mansion with a flagstaff in the supreme, imperishable abode. ||47||
For whoever causes a painting to be made in the temple of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, a celestial chariot composed of paintings will certainly appear in his abode. ||48||
And he who offers a mirror before Kṛṣṇa shall go to the world of Soma;
having enjoyed pleasures until the end of the kalpa, he shall go to the eternal Goloka. ||49||
One should give a multi-ribbed umbrella made of fine linen to the wielder of the Śārṅga bow;
having become a sovereign emperor among the worlds of Virāja, he shall indeed go to Hari.
One should give a vehicle, a celestial chariot, a mount, a couch, a grass mat, or a straw mat;
having become like Kubera until the end of the kalpa, they attain liberation at the conclusion.
One should perform the *ārātrika* rite for Hari with many wicks, ghee, and other offerings;
for him, the *ārātrika* is performed daily by millions of deities.
Whoever whirls a water-filled conch shell over Keśava shall become a resident in the Milk Ocean in the presence of Kṛṣṇa. (53)
One should perform circumambulation of Kṛṣṇa; at every step, there is the fruit of gifting the entire earth.
One should perform prostrations like a staff; the fruit shall be that of an Aśvamedha sacrifice. (54)
One should perform the chanting (kīrtana) of Śrī Hari and obtain the fruit of the Sāmaveda;
one should dance before Hari, which destroys ten million sins. 55.
For one who dwells in Dvārakā, there is the fruit born of residing in the abode of Goloka;
and for one who drinks the water of the Gomatī, there is liberation.
At Gaṅgādvāra, at Prayāga, at the Gaṅgā, in Kurujāṅgala, at Puṣkara, at Prabhāsa, at Śrīsthala, and at Śuklatīrtha; ||57||
Indeed, for one who resorts to Dvārakā, the Gomatī, Kṛṣṇa, and Gopītāla on a single day here, the fruit of a thousand cāndrāyaṇa fasts is obtained.

Thus ends the two hundred and twenty-eighth chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness and Fruits of Worshipping Kṛṣṇa while Residing in Dvārakā," in the first section, the *Kṛtayuga-santāna*, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Mahālakṣmī; likewise, Dvārikā and Gomatī were established by Kṛṣṇa in the Kali age as a ladder to heaven—Gomatī being such a ladder.

Where there are stones marked with the discus, born from the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean, which constantly grant happiness to those who resort to them and bestow liberation through mere bathing.
Even when merely seen, they cause those who behold them to attain supreme liberation;
who would not serve that city where even the clay grants liberation? (3)
A certain Brāhmaṇa from Avanti, named Somaśarman, was a devotee of Śiva; he did not know the vow of any other deity.
He would certainly observe the fourteenth lunar day, yet he did not hold Viṣṇu in high regard;
every year, however, he used to visit Somanātha for an audience.
Seventy thousand years passed for him until he became decrepit;
indeed, there were tens of millions of people on the pilgrimage to Somanātha.
Having made that a great sacred site (mahātīrtha) and having gone to Raivata, they all then departed for a pilgrimage to Dvārakā; the twice-born one did not go.
Somaśarman went to his own home and slept alone;
and in a dream, his fathers and grandfathers arrived.
And the kinsmen of the elder lineage, together with their great-grandfathers,
exist in the form of *pretas*, pervaded by hunger, fierce, and filled with grief.
Seeing them, he was overcome with fear and, trembling, said: "Who are you, of such fierce appearance? From where and for what reason have you come? (1.229.10)
The pretas said to that son: "We are your grandfathers;
suffering and famished, we have come here into your presence. (11)
The son said: "I have given, practiced austerity, offered oblations, and fed others for the sake of attaining your satisfaction; and you likewise have performed those same acts. (12)
"How is it that you remain in the state of a preta? Tell me the reason for this.
The pretas said: "Listen, my son; indeed, the day of Hari was violated."
Neither by us nor by you has the day of Hari been observed;
by that fault, this sorrow-inducing state of being a ghost (preta) has been chosen for us.
Nor is there any deliverance for you from this most grievous sin;
for you do not observe the vow of the Blessed One, nor do you undertake the pilgrimage.
"O son, you do not honor Kṛṣṇa, nor do you go to Dvārakā;
you worship only the god Śaṅkara and you revile the Lord."
Because of that fault, they have attained the state of a preta, and you too shall attain it;
for Śambhu will not grant a good rebirth to those who hate Viṣṇu.
Śaṅkara is a devotee of Viṣṇu and stands as the foremost among Vaiṣṇavas;
he does not accept worship from one who reviles Kṛṣṇa.
For those devoid of devotion to Hari and those who have abandoned the vow of the twelfth day (Dvādaśī),
sin does not perish and the state of being a ghost (preta) does not cease.
But even when Śaṅkara is being worshipped, if the worship of Keśava is omitted,
there occurs the sin of cow-slaughter, which brings about the painful suffering of hell.
First Keśava is to be worshipped, afterwards Śrī Śaṅkara deserves worship;
after that, the gods are to be worshipped, and then others—such is the established order.
Out of a nihilistic disposition, you do not worship Hari himself;
neither the worship of Śiva, nor that of the Sun, nor that of Brahmā protects you. Indeed, the state of being a ghost born from the day of a lunar eclipse does not depart.
He who observes the third lunar day (tithi) of Vaiśākha when it is pierced [by the second day]. || 23 ||
The gods do not accept his sacrificial offering (havya), nor do the ancestors accept his ancestral offering (kavya);
if he performs them out of delusion, his state as a preta is indeed certain. (24)
The twelfth and the full moon days are like a single day for one's parents throughout the year; one who observes them as overlapped by the preceding day falls into hell. (25)
Having bowed to Somanātha, you do not go to Dvārakā;
you do not perform service to Kṛṣṇa, and thus there is no fruit for your pilgrimage.
Therefore, after seeing Someśvara, one should proceed to the city of Dvārakā;
for he who goes to Dvārakā without having seen the god Someśvara [does not attain the full fruit]. ||27||
O son, he shall fall into a terrible hell along with his ancestors;
thus we have all fallen, and now we have been cast down by you once again.
And our departure from the realm of Yama is not seen by us [otherwise] than through contact with the waters of the Gomatī and by beholding the face of Kṛṣṇa. (29)
O son, by performing the śrāddha at Gopī-saras, the ancestors cross over;
having gone to Kṛṣṇa’s Dvārakā, they behold the face of the Lord Hari. (1.229.30)
Perform the ancestral rites (śrāddha) and acts of charity at the confluence of the Gomati with the ocean;
perform the libations (tarpaṇa) at Gopikātāla and offer yourself to Kṛṣṇa.
When Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the God of Gods, who is served by Rukmiṇī, is worshipped, your merit shall become pure and our goal shall be attained. (32)
When worshipped, we bestow prosperity extending to sons and grandsons;
liberated from the state of being a preta, we shall attain the supreme goal.
Indeed, for him at the confluence of the Gomatī and the Niradhu, there is no state of being a preta;
by the offering of śrāddha there, his ancestors attain satisfaction and liberation. (34)
Whatever fruit is obtained there by thousands of crores of sacred fords and by those performing ancestral rites (śrāddha),
all that fruit is obtained in Dvārakā by the offering of water.
Whatever fruit is obtained from feeding ascetics and also from feeding Kṛṣṇa, that auspicious fruit, which brings satisfaction for ten million kalpas, is attained here. ||36||
The liberation of the inhabitants of Dvārakā is considered eternal in every respect;
for them there is no return, even in hundreds of millions of kalpas.
Any woman who, being widowed, constantly takes refuge in Dvārakā, she indeed becomes Lakṣmī herself, acting for the pleasure of Kṛṣṇa. 38.
Having gone to Kṛṣṇa’s city, he who worships Kṛṣṇa with tulasī leaves has obtained the fruit of his birth, and his ancestors have been delivered. (39)
And whoever wears a garland of Tulasī leaves that has been worn by Kṛṣṇa,
for every leaf, the fruit of ten horse-sacrifices is produced.

One who performs a śrāddha or an act of charity while wearing a garland of tulasī shall find that even a very small offering to the ancestors and the deities becomes multiplied ten millionfold. ||41||
Upon seeing a garland made of Tulasī wood, the Yāma-guards flee;
for in whatever house there is Tulasī wood—whether its leaves be dry or fresh—42.
In his house, there shall never be any transfer of sin.
Therefore, O son, a Vaiṣṇava should indeed wear a garland of Tulasī.
Having become [this form], go to Dvārakā, the auspicious city of Hari, and perform the śrāddha ceremony;
offer libations with the waters of the sacred fords and thereby secure liberation from this state.
O son, you must observe Unmolanī, Śayanī, Triḥspṛśā, Pakṣavardhinī, Jayantī, Vijayā, and Jayā. (45)
The Kṛṣṇāṣṭamī should be observed; it destroys all sins, bestows all prosperity, and grants liberation—go and perform it with happiness. (46)
Having heard this from his ancestors who had become *pretas*, the twice-born Candraśarman went to Dvārakā, which was like the eternal abode of Goloka. (47)
Where Śrī Rukmiṇī and Kṛṣṇa reside, there holy places of pilgrimage always exist;
where sacrifices and deities abide, and where stainless sages dwell. ||48||
Dvārakā, which is served by Kinnaras, Siddhas, and Gandharvas,
is where the Gomatī flows like a ladder for ascending to heaven.
That city, upon entering whose boundary the mountains of sin are destroyed,
was beheld by the best of the twice-born with his clear vision.
Having attained joy there, the twice-born man bowed with devotion to the Gomatī, the temple of Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa himself, the ocean, and Dvārāvatī. ||51||
And he considered himself to have accomplished his purpose, blessed, and endowed with the dawning of good fortune;
"Now there is no further need for me of thousands of millions of sacred pilgrimage sites. (52)
The twelfth lunar day of the bright fortnight of the month of Vaiśākha, presided over by Madhusūdana, has arrived; it is known as Triḥspṛśā, which destroys ten million sins.
"Ah! What a rise of merit has occurred; today I have beheld Dvārakā!
Thinking thus, he touched water, bathed, and offered libations to the deities. (54)
Having reached Cakratīrtha, he worshipped the stone marked with the discus;
he beheld Kṛṣṇa and performed his worship with the sixteen types of offerings.
Filled with devotion, he performed the worship of Śiva and offered funeral cakes (piṇḍas) to the ancestors, having given water according to the prescribed rite.
The bathing of Hari with milk, anointing him with sandalwood paste, incense, lamps, food offerings, fresh grain, and tubers and roots. ||57||
Betel-leaf, camphor, clothing, fruit, and likewise the offering of lights;
circumambulation, prostration, hymn of praise, and a handful of flowers. ||58||
Having performed prostrations like a staff and likewise observed a vigil with patience,
he indeed offered his prayers when three watches of the night had passed.
O Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, O Hare Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, salutations be unto You!
For those who are wretched, blind, and submerged in suffering, You alone are the refuge and the happiness.
The fruit of service at your feet is eternal great bliss;
indeed, all suffering shall perish for those who observe your Dvādaśī.
May all the sin born of the *daśamī-vedha* committed by my ancestors go to destruction, and may my ancestors attain liberation. (62)
O Lord of Gods, O Master of the World, act in such a way that my ancestors may be freed from the state of being hungry ghosts and attain liberation. (63)
"By me, a devotee of Śivaprabha, even you have been slighted;
for neither worship nor salutation, nor pilgrimage, nor even a sight of you has ever been performed by me. (64)
May whatever great sin has been produced by that always go to destruction for me;
for neither was the pilgrimage to Dvārakā performed, nor was Kṛṣṇa served here. (65)
"O Gomatī, you have not bathed; O Hari, wipe away that fault!
From this day forward, I am your Vaiṣṇava servant, O Keśava. (66)
I shall perform your worship, your vow, your recitation, and your service; I shall apply [sandalwood paste], chant your praises, offer hymns of praise, and pay homage to you. (67)
O Hari, I shall always listen to your stories, carry the water from washing your feet, and consume the food offerings dedicated to you.
Be gracious, O Blessed One; burn away my sin and grant liberation to my ancestors; accept this prayer, O Lord. (69)
Having heard these words, the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa indeed appeared, saying:
"O Candracarya, I am pleased with your devotion, as are your ancestors."
"And you, having shaken off all evils, shall go to my abode";
having said this, Kṛṣṇa vanished, and the ancestors appeared before him.
They said, "O son, by your effort, we have attained liberation without a doubt, through the gift of water from the Gomatī, the offering of funeral cakes (piṇḍa), and the sight [of you]. (72)
Released from the womb of a preta, we go to the supreme destination.
Blessed are those fathers in the world whose son [has gone] to Dvārakā. (73)
Having gone [to the sacred sites], she should always cause her ancestors to cross over by means of service to Kṛṣṇa and other such acts;
blessed is that widow who performs the pilgrimage of Kṛṣṇa. (74)
Even if he be an outcaste, if he performs pilgrimage with his mind fixed on Kṛṣṇa, he surely delivers his father, his master, and a hundred generations of his lineage.
Surrounded by his ancestors, he attains supreme liberation;
for in him reside all sacred fords, all the gods, and likewise all sacrifices.
People come to Dvārakā three times a day into the presence of Kṛṣṇa;
therefore, a person obtains here the fruit of all sacred fords.
He who, having seen Someśvara, does not behold Dvārakā—shame on his son and his lineage; his ancestors remain in hell. (78)
Brahmā, Rudra, as well as Sūrya, Mahendra, and the other deities;
humans, kings, Brahmins, serpents, nāgas, and foot-soldiers. ||79||
Rivers and streams, mountains and forests, groves and gardens, cities, villages, towns, oceans, and lakes.
The hosts of yakṣas, gandharvas, siddhas, and likewise vidyādharas;
the apsarases, serpents, Dhanada, and the daityas and rākṣasas. ||81||
The sages, the munis, the yogas, Sanaka and the other virtuous ones, as well as the virtuous women, the circle of yoginīs, and the Sāṃkhya-yoginīs—[all these are present]. (82)
The lunar mansions, the planetary conjunctions, the fixed stars, and the guardians of the world—whatever indeed exists within the three worlds, whether stationary or moving. ||83||
Indeed, it remains constantly in the presence of Śrī Kṛṣṇa every single day;
it never abandons the meritorious city of Dvārakā, which is adorned by Kṛṣṇa. (84)
"O son, because you have served her and we ourselves have seen Kṛṣṇa, we have been released from the womb of ghosts; we are going to the supreme goal. (85)
"May it be well with you; we shall not go to that divine abode, Goloka.
O son, you have attained the feet of Kṛṣṇa, and you shall go to that realm. (86)
In the Kali age, the Vedas yield no fruit, nor do gifts or sacrifices;
however, the Gomatī is considered in every way to be the bestower of fruits, heaven, and liberation. 87.
In the Kali age, Kāśī, Mathurā, Avantī, Revatācala, Ayodhyā, Kuṅkumavāpī, Kāñcī, and Puruṣottama [are the sacred sites]. ||88||
Śālagrāma, the river Māyā, Badarī, and likewise Gayā;
Kurukṣetra, Bhṛgukṣetra, Puṣkara, and Śuklatīrtha. ||89||
Prayāga, Prabhāsa, and Hāṭakeśvara;
Gaṅgādvāra, Vārāha, and the confluence of the Gaṅgā with the ocean. ||1.229.90||
O son, [there are] Naimiṣa, the Daṇḍaka forest, as well as Vṛndāvana,
the region of Sindhukṣetra, Arbuda, and all other forests.
Likewise, there are forests, sacred abodes, and other such places;
mountains, mountain springs, holy fords, snow-capped peaks, and woods. (92)
All the rivers and oceans were eager to serve Kṛṣṇa;
they longed for the destruction of their sins and desired divine bliss. ||93||
In the Kali age, they shall remain at Dvārakā on the banks of the Gomatī;
indeed, there is no city equal to Dvārakā in the three worlds. (94)

Upon the completion of your full lifespan, your death shall be divine, occurring on a Wednesday during the bright fortnight of the month of Vaiśākha, at the time of the triple-contact (triḥspṛśā). || 95 ||
"Your journey to the abode of Hari shall be through the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra)," said his ancestors, who appeared in the form of four-armed deities. 96.
Abiding in a divine celestial chariot, they departed for that abode of Goloka;
Somaśarman, having become a Vaiṣṇava, went to his own home.
When the end of his life had arrived, he went to the city of Dvāravatī;
there, following the instruction of Kṛṣṇa, he cast off his life-breaths and attained liberation. 98.
For those who hear and likewise read this account of the greatness arising from Dvārakā, all the fruit indeed arises, and in the end, liberation shall certainly be attained. (99)

Thus ends the two hundred and twenty-ninth chapter, titled "The Description of the Liberation of the Ancestors of Somaśarman, a Devotee of Śiva, through a Pilgrimage to Dvārakā," in the first section, the Kṛtayuga-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Śaṅkhoddhāra is a great holy place (tīrtha) where the demon Śaṅkha was uplifted by Kṛṣṇa, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow; one should go there for the sake of liberation.
The sacred fords beginning with Prabhāsa, the rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā, as well as the mountains, oceans, holy fields, and divine shrines and trees. || 2 ||
Sacrifices such as the Aśvamedha and others, deities such as Mahendra and others, sages such as Bhṛgu and others, and Gandharvas foremost among whom is Tumburu; (3)
And the lords of wealth, Kubera and others; the attendants, Viṣvaksena and others;
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa; as well as the Siddhas and the Apsarases. (4)
Now, what is the use of saying more? The three worlds, both insentient and sentient, abide within the Śaṅkhoddhāra [tīrtha], having entered into contact with the inner self.
Those who constantly remember the great lake Śaṅkhoddhāra at home shall not return again until the dissolution of all beings.
But those who remember Śaṅkhoddhāra and Śaṅkhin with their minds,
they dwell in the world of Kṛṣṇa together with hundreds of millions of their kin.
Whatever fruit is obtained at the Sarasvatī during ten million solar eclipses,
that same fruit a man attains who, with devotion, feeds ascetics constantly for a hundred years.
And at Śaṅkhoddhāra, O beloved of mine, the three and a half crores of sacred fords do not equal even a sixteenth part of the merit of one who bathes there.
Residence at Śaṅkhoddhāra yields the fruit of all sacred fords;
even thousands of killings of Brahmins and acts of approaching those who should not be approached [are purified].
Sins go to destruction for one who touches the water from the Śaṅkhoddhāra;
he who gives a cow, a house, or gold obtains the fruit born of ten million such gifts.
The fruit obtained by residing at Kurukṣetra and by dying in the Gaṅgā is attained merely by bathing in the Gomatī and by beholding [the deity] situated within the conch.
In the midst of the waters of the ocean lies Dvārakā, which is exceedingly difficult to conquer;
situated in its center is the Lord, the bearer of the conch, the destroyer of sins.
Thence one should go to the Piṇḍāraka Tīrtha, which destroys all sins,
where Kṛṣṇa himself, with four arms, is ever present.
Having bathed there where the river Rukmavatī flows, one is liberated;
for there is the world-renowned pond of the sage Agastya.
Having bathed and likewise performed the Śrāddha rite, the son indeed liberates the ancestors;
there is a sacrificial enclosure and a holy ford (tīrtha) where the first Prajāpati [performed sacrifice]. || 16 ||
He indeed performed a sacrifice according to the prescribed rites for the welfare of all the worlds,
wherein the hands of the Daitya, the destroyer of sacrifices, were cut off.
Having seen that by Viṣṇu, the God of gods, one is indeed released from sin;
for there, the ancestors truly desire rice-balls for their complete satisfaction.
When the Śrāddha is performed in Vaiśākha, one is liberated from the three types of sin;
furthermore, charity, Śrāddha, vows, recitation, and libations should also be performed.
For a person traveling toward Dvārakā, the fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices and a hundred Rājasūya sacrifices shall be attained at every step.
And for one who remembers Piṇḍāraka, that fruit is certain;
likewise, having seen Śrī Kṛṣṇa in the temple at Śaṅkhoddhāra, one sees the Holder of the Conch (Śaṅkhin).
By beholding the four-armed Lord at Piṇḍāraka, one attains liberation.
Śrī, Kṛṣṇa, Cakratīrtha, Piṇḍāraka, the Gomatī river,
gopīcandana, and tulasī are indeed difficult to find in the Kali age.
They, however, meet in Dvāravatī on account of their devotion to Kṛṣṇa. ||23||
Vardhinī, Dvārakā, Gaṅgā, Lakṣmī, Govinda, Gomatī, Gopikā, Tāla, and Mṛttikā—these are indeed difficult to attain. (24)
For that devotee on whose part vigilance arose on the twelfth day of the waxing moon,
the cycle of rebirth has been entirely burnt away.
O beloved, he who performs a vigil on the day of Trispṛśā before the body of Keśava certainly becomes absorbed [in Him]. (26)
A swing should be given to Kṛṣṇa; the merit thereof is infinite.
It may be made of gold, silver, wood, or likewise of cloth.
Indeed, that [gift] should be given to Viṣṇu; its fruit is residence in Vaikuṇṭha.
And one should swing Hari-Kṛṣṇa repeatedly and gently upon a swing.
One should also perform a vigil here, which is meritorious and bestows liberation;
likewise, the gift of a daughter, the ancestral rites at Gayā, and the planting of an Aśvattha tree [yield great merit]. (29)
O Lakṣmī, keeping a vigil on the twelfth day is equal to ten thousand horse-sacrifices; at every moment, the fruit of a horse-sacrifice shall be attained.
All the gods, sacred fords, liberated souls, and likewise sages come together on the night of the Lord’s vigil on the eleventh day. 3.1.
Indeed, the dust from the feet of Kṛṣṇa as he walked from his home toward the temple for the sake of the vigil— [is to be honored]. (32)
For as many [leaves] as they touch, for that many thousands of years they shall enjoy pleasures in heaven, and thereafter attain the abode of Goloka. || 32 ||
Once, during a vigil, the goddess Pārvatī said to Śaṅkara:
"O Śambhu, why indeed do you dance at night while playing the ḍamaru drum? (34)
Śambhu said: "O Goddess, I shall observe the vigil on the day of Hari for the sake of pleasing Kṛṣṇa, wherein no indolence whatsoever may occur. (35)
By any means whatsoever, one must certainly remain awake through song, fine dance, and the chanting of the praises of the Lord of the Gods.
Through play, through conversation and discourse, through the clapping of hands, and through service, [they worship] with a festival created by a multitude of men and women. ||37||
A devotee who remembers Kṛṣṇa must indeed remain awake;
he should act in such a way that neither laziness nor negligence occurs.
"Thus, for the sake of pleasing Kṛṣṇa, I perform this dance-keeping-of-wakefulness;
you, however, must do this as well, remembering the Lord of Kamalā. (39)
On the eleventh day one must not eat, and likewise a vigil should be observed;
even he who has come there to a social gathering attains the supreme goal.
Even heaps of sin as vast as Mount Meru and Mandara are all carried away like a pile of cotton during the vigil for Kṛṣṇa.
The vigil (jāgara) dear to Kṛṣṇa is superior even to all sacred fords and sacrifices;
all the gods come together at the vigil dear to Kṛṣṇa.
"Women become dear to the heart during the vigil for the beloved of Kṛṣṇa. Having said this, even Hara ceased speaking, O beloved of Kṛṣṇa. (43)

Thus ends the two hundred and thirtieth chapter, titled "The Praise of the Śaṅkhoddhāra Tīrtha, Piṇḍāraka Tīrtha, the River Rukmavatī, Agastya’s Tank, the Sacrificial Tīrtha, and the Vows and Vigilances of Ekādaśī and Dvādaśī," in the first section on the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga within the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī, when Jupiter had entered the zodiac sign of Leo,
the sage Nārada went to the hermitage of Gautama on the banks of the Godāvarī.
Having seen that all the purifying holy places had arrived from every direction and were staying for the duration of the rainy season, he resided there for one year.
Vārāṇasī, Kurukṣetra, Madhupurī, Avantikā, Māyā, Kāñcī, Sāketā, Gayā, and Kuṅkumavāpikā. || 3 ||
The three Gayās, the sacred field of Hari-Hara, Puruṣottama,
Prabhāsa and other such forests, hermitages, the Gaṅgā, and the Sarasvatī.
The Tāpī, Payoṣṇī, Sarayū, Bhīmarathī, and Gaṇḍakī;
the Kṛṣṇā, Svarṇā, and Kāverī; as well as lakes, springs, and the Yamunā. || 5 ||
Those mountains, continents, and islands that exist throughout the fourteen worlds are situated here on the banks of the Godāvarī.
When Jupiter was in Leo, the Sindhu, Puṣkara, and other rivers, as well as the boundary mountains, were filled with great joy for one year.
Prayāga, the Vedas and Śāstras, the Siddhas, Ṛṣis, and deities, the ancestors, the gods of heaven, the Brahmins, and the yogis and holy men [all reside there].
The virtuous goddesses and the gods rained down in great joy;
and having beheld them, the great sages Gautama, Nārada, and others took up residence there.
Having washed away their own sins offered by the heretics,
they indeed prepared to go to the Gautamī river.
At that time, the Godāvarī was among the sacred fords (tīrthas), and she spoke to Nārada:
"O Nārada, all these sacred fords have come into being through my connection."
Sinless beings were born, yet they bestowed sins upon me;
therefore, I must certainly go somewhere to cast off that burden of sin.
"Now, O Lord, being consumed by the fires of those various sins, where shall I go, O Sage? I am exceedingly distressed; what shall I do hereafter? (13)
Having heard that, Nārada meditated for a moment and remained silent;
at that very time, the lord of sages, the yogi Gautama, arrived there.
They say that the sages are the true holy places; however, by your grace, O Gautamī, since you have arrived upon the surface of the earth, we too have indeed been purified.
Likewise, those who perform our water-libations at the Godāvarī are indeed freed from sin;
O Gautama, reflect upon that.
Gautama thought: "Such is that holy ford which destroys sin;
nevertheless, at that time, it did not appear with such power within his wisdom. (17)
Having observed silence, Gautama meditated upon Śrī Kṛṣṇa;
meanwhile, the Goddess of Speech, speaking from the sky, spoke to her in a cheering manner.
May the holy sages and others listen; out of compassion I shall relate:
there exists [a place] situated along the shore of the western ocean. (19)
And there is the excellent sacred field of Dvārakā, where the auspicious Gomatī river flows,
and where Mahāviṣṇu eternally resides, facing the west.
That [fire] is the burner even of all those fierce heaps of sins;
therefore, O deities, go to the Gautamī for the burning away of your sins. || 21 ||
Having heard that it was the most excellent field, the deities of the sacred fords shouted: "Victory! Victory! We have won; we are blessed, most blessed! (22)
Having spoken thus, they all departed for Dvārakā, which was protected by Kṛṣṇa;
for residence in Dvārakā is difficult to attain, and the sight of Kṛṣṇa is difficult to obtain. (23)
The bathing in the Gomatī is difficult to attain, as is the sight of Rukmiṇī;
yet the meritorious sight of Dvārakā shall come to pass for us.
Nārada, Gautama, the Godāvarī, the sacred fords (tīrthas), and the deities—
all of them respectfully approached the boundary of Dvārāvatī.
Having questioned Nārada with joy regarding the procedure for the sacred ford, he spoke to them;
indeed, Nārada knows the procedure exactly as it is.
Having bathed in the Gomatī and then worshipped Gomatī,
one should seek a vision of Kṛṣṇa and feed virtuous brāhmaṇas.
Having partaken of the grace of Kṛṣṇa, the pilgrim should sleep upon the ground;
and at dawn, having bathed again and worshipped the Supreme Lord, [he should proceed].
Having performed circumambulation and having prostrated before the true guru, one should likewise engage in singing, chanting, and the devotional worship of Śrī Hari. (29)
One should strictly protect one's celibacy and restrain the senses;
furthermore, one should perform the massaging of the feet for the gods and the virtuous.
One should perform a visit and worship, and give gifts according to one's ability.
Even that which is done to a small extent, according to one's capacity, becomes multiplied ten-millionfold. || 31 ||
The fruit arising from the gift of the entire earth is equal to the fruit of giving even a single morsel of food;
when one virtuous person is fed, the fruit is that of ten thousand Rājasūya sacrifices.
One should give sandals, food and drink, shoes, umbrellas, woolen blankets, garments, and water-vessels to Kṛṣṇa for his satisfaction.
For one whose hands, feet, mind, tongue, and organ of generation are restrained, the merit of the sacred fords is infinite.
One should avoid the food of others, the cooking of others, and the possessions of others;
one should listen to the sacred stories of Viṣṇu and chant the name of Hari.
A festival should be celebrated with the sounds of singing and musical instruments;
likewise, one should offer the ritual waving of lights (ārātrika), the fruit, and the food offering (naivedya). || 36 ||
Likewise, one should cause the worship of Kṛṣṇa to be performed with sixteen articles;
indeed, it is impossible to describe its fruit even by means of the number of Yugas.
Thus addressed by Nārada, those holy sages of the sacred fords performed everything exactly as instructed at the tīrtha, filled with devotion.
Some listen to his stories, others describe his various qualities;
some sing his glory, while others remember Śrī Hari. (39)
Some chant his name, some behold him;
others proceed with festivals, and still others dance at that time.
Some simultaneously roar the cry of victory for Hari again and again;
some sweep the house of Hari, while others chant the Vaiṣṇava mantra.
Immersed in love, they laugh, they touch the lotus feet of the saintly, and when meeting on the path, they always sing the praises of his virtues. (42)
Having formed a circle, they perform the rites of the heretics;
seeing them, those slayers of Brahmins seek purification—I tell you the truth, the very truth. (43)
All these indeed are Vaiṣṇavas, appearing in the forms of men and women;
they are the holy fords such as Prayāga, the sacred fields, the mountains, and the oceans.
All of them, assuming human forms and forming a procession, indeed set forth;
then the goddesses who are rivers, such as the Gaṅgā and others, went there in the forms of women.
Kuṃkumavāpikā set out, taking her own sacred waters;
at that time, there was indeed a divine assembly of those situated on the fourteenth step. 46.
At that time, everyone indeed performed instrumental music and chanting within the Saṅgha;
then the great procession of Dvārakā was carried out by the Saṅgha. || 47 ||
The bath was taken in the Gomatī river, the vision of Kṛṣṇa was obtained, and the entire ritual of pilgrimage was performed; thus, all sin has been destroyed. (48)

At that time, the Godāvarī, joined by the assembly, became exceedingly pure. I shall describe how even the dust of those traveling on the road at that moment, when touched, bestows the merit of horse-sacrifices. 49.
For those traveling on the path to Dvārakā, with every single step taken,
there shall accrue the merit of thousands of sacrifices for every particle of dust.
Nārada said to all those divine assemblies of sectarians:
"Indeed, there are thousands of heaps of your masses of merit. (51)
By those who have performed the pilgrimage to Gomatītīrtha and likewise beheld Śrī Hari,
you [have visited] all the sacred fords and holy places in their entirety.
Blessed are you all, since you have seen Kṛṣṇapura;
for you, O all you excellent rivers, behold this sacred place. (53)
Dvārakā is the destroyer of the sins of men, the most excellent among the best of holy places;
Dvārakā, the beloved of Kṛṣṇa, brings glory to the entire universe. 54.
Gomatī, Kṛṣṇadeva, and Rukmiṇī, the beloved of Hari—this [place] shines forth, superior to all, resembling Goloka itself. (55)
One should understand that this is indeed Vaikuṇṭha; it is a very image of Vaikuṇṭha itself, as described by Nārada at that time during his praise.
Then Dvārakā, personified as the Gomatī river, arrived out of a desire for a welcome; she was saluted by the gods and the sacred pilgrimage sites as well. 57.
And then Nārada spoke: "They pay homage to your feet, as do Dvārakā, Gomatī, Gautamī, and Prayāgarāja. (98)
The Gaṅgā, the Narmadā, the Sūryaputrī (Yamunā), the Prācī Sarasvatī, the Candrabhāgā, the Sarayū, the Kṣiprā, and the Kuṅkumavāpikā. ||59||
The Sindhu, the Śoṇa, the Gaṇḍakī, the Vipāśā, and likewise the Tapatī;
the Kṛṣṇā, the Bhīmarathī, the Svarṇā, and the Payoṣṇī—these indeed bow down to you.
This Vārāṇasī indeed bows down at your feet;
Kurukṣetra, Mathurā, and Avantikā also surely pay homage to you.
Māyāpurī, Ayodhyā, Gayā, Kāñcī, and Viśālā bow down to you;
as do Śālagrāma, the great sacred field, Prabhāsa, and Puruṣottama.
The seven oceans, Dhenuka, Daśārṇa, Daṇḍaka, Arbuda, Kurukṣetra, Dharmāraṇya, and Kālaka. ||63||
Also Nārāyaṇasaras, Puṣkara, and Gokula;
as well as Mānasa, Meru, Kailāsa, Mandara, and Himavat.
As Nārada was speaking thus, Vindhya bowed at his feet in Dvārakā, which is served by Kṛṣṇa; indeed, Dvārakā was filled with joy in its heart.
Remembering Gomatī with his hands, he spoke these charming words:
"You are blessed; you have arrived, and this is a great gain for me. (66)
I welcome you all; please partake of the food of Kṛṣṇa, drink the nectar of Kṛṣṇa’s feet, and remain here indeed.
Indeed, through contact with me, who am united with Kṛṣṇa, and by the grace of Śrī Hari, all your sins have been utterly consumed. 68.
Thus, at that time, he gladdened everyone with words of welcome;
and indeed, the hosts of deities, beginning with Brahmā, were seen in the sky. 69.
Śiva and Śivā, joined by their hosts, along with the Yakṣas, Gandharvas, and Kiraṇas;
the Maruts, the world-protectors, as well as the Siddhas and Vidyādharas.
All the Ādityas, the planets, as well as the sages beginning with Bhṛgu, the great sages beginning with Sanaka, and the Vairājas who are supreme lords; ||71||
Devoted to their husbands, they danced and descended [from the mountain] filled with great joy;
having bathed on the earth in the Gomatī river, they beheld Kṛṣṇa.
Having drunk the clear water and seen the assembly of the Tīrthikas, they were struck with supreme wonder and cried out, "Victory to the Tīrthas! (73)
Delighted in their hearts, they indeed made proclamations again and again; and Dvārakā offered them a welcome and due honor.
And by Gomatī as well, the washing away of the sins of all was accomplished;
then all the gods and sacred fords bowed down simultaneously with devotion.
The assembly of gods and the assembly of holy men bowed to one another;
then they all bowed simultaneously and became filled with joy.
Having recognized the preeminence of Dvārakā and likewise the preeminence of the Gomatī, they then spoke, crying "Kṛṣṇa!
Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!
and "Victory to Kṛṣṇa!", extolling the splendor of the Gomatī, of Dvārakā, and of Kṛṣṇa.
And worship with divine garments and divine fragrant ointments. ||78||
With divine ornaments of devotion consisting of excellent gems, diamonds, and the like;
with celestial garlands and decorations; and with camphor, agallochum, and sandalwood.
With tulasī filaments, incense, lustrations, circumambulations, and various divine offerings of sweet foods and drinks; || 1.231.80 ||
With betel leaves and sweet spices, with beloved offerings, and likewise with highly auspicious substances such as chowries, fans, and the like.
Having performed worship and feeling their purpose fulfilled, they danced before Hari;
then Kṛṣṇa himself appeared and spoke to them with a smile.
O holy fords, as well as gods, goddesses, mountains, and great sages: I am pleased with you by virtue of this performance of the rite for the holy fords; may there be peace for you. (83)
Then the holy places and others said, "We have been delivered by the Supreme Self; O All-pervading Lord, by your grace we have obtained our desired boon. (84)
May there be for you an unfailing devotion to your lotus feet;
and may this Dvārakā always be worthy of worship by all. 85.
Having spoken thus, both of the two assemblies then likewise consecrated Dvārakā and the Gomatī river in the sovereignty over all sacred fords (tīrthas). ||86||
With palms joined in reverence, they repeatedly performed worship with divine offerings;
