One should perform the Nīrājana rite for the Guru while swinging him on a swing, and likewise swing Lord Hari—Bālakṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, and Harinārāyaṇa. (71)
Or he should delight [the deity] in beautiful water, in a garden, or even in a palace;
and he should have dancing, singing, and instrumental music performed in its vicinity.
One should indeed give gifts of food, clothing, water, flowers, and fruit;
one should feed children, virtuous people, and Brahmins, and offer morsels of grass to cows.
One who has not taken a vow should recite the accounts concerning Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the stories of Puruṣottama, or the narrative of the Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā. (74)
One should fashion a rosary with beads named Kṛṣṇa, Hari, Kṛṣṇa, and Nārāyaṇa, and repeatedly perform japa, worship, remembrance, and chanting [of His names]. (75)
Prostration, servitude, attendance, and even the massaging of the feet; as well as sweeping, ministering, and the washing of the temple of Viṣṇu.
One should perform auspicious service to the guru, which nourishes one's vows;
for when the guru is pleased, the vow becomes complete and the heart's desire is indeed fulfilled. ||77||
This entire collection is complete, bestowing heaven, liberation, and other blessings;
it is for Gaurīs, virtuous women, chaste wives, boys, girls, and widows with husbands living. (78)
One should feed those who are destitute and without refuge, bestow gifts upon them, and provide a home, a livelihood, a field, a garden, or a wage. (79)
One should provide various kinds of assistance so that he may attain satisfaction;
by that, indeed, the month known as Puruṣottama shall bear fruit.
One should always offer auspicious water-born flowers to the deity in the temple,
as well as uncooked grains, vegetables, salt, sugar, and so forth.
Fruits, rice, mung beans, split pulses, ghee-wicks, clarified butter, oil, wild rice, black pepper, and excellent cumin. ||82||
One should give ginger, methikā, curd, milk, and buttermilk;
likewise, the leaves, bhājikā, dates, and excellent surājikā.
Roots of plants, almonds, pieces of wood, as well as clods of earth, bricks, bamboo vessels, vessels made of metal, and earthen pots; ||84||
One should provide mouthfuls of fodder for the sake of cows and other animals, and even for crows and other birds;
likewise, one should give grains for the sake of ants and the like, as well as flour and similar substances.
At Śrī Puruṣottama, one should give chickpeas to those living in the water, cakes to dogs and other such creatures, and water to the trees and creepers.
One should offer water upon Śiva for the sake of long peppers and jujubes; one should likewise present water for the sake of wood-apples, bilva fruits, and banyan trees. (87)
One should offer water and food to the *tulasī* plants, the lotuses, and the flowering creepers as well, and one should provide them with secure sustenance. (88)

In this manner, one should also cause gifts of garments and other articles to be given; moreover, one should sleep on the ground, observe celibacy, and remain tranquil when [the practice] is intensified. (89)
Having indeed become virtuous for a month and being endowed with vows like a virtuous woman,
one should perform meritorious deeds for oneself both in this world and for supreme liberation hereafter.
The husband, the wife, the female servant, the son, the daughter, and kinsmen;
the wives of kinsmen, mothers, fathers, and grandfathers. ||91||
The mother, the maternal grandmother, and those who are boys and girls; the disciples, the sister, dependents, guests, and those who have sought refuge. ||92||
All those people in the house, one's own kinsmen, and the members of the family should indeed observe the vow during the month of Puruṣottama. (93)
By means of a single meal, or eating at night, or by fruit, or by food obtained unasked, or even by water, milk, curd, or by *nīvāra* grain and the like; ||94||
Having maintained their bodily sustenance even with fried vegetables, they should perform the vow of the month of Puruṣottama according to their ability. ||95||
One should perform it with a single meal, or even with food obtained through alms;
or one may subsist by gleaning ears of grain, or one may practice living on water alone.
Or one should consume food offered to the gods in the evening after having worshipped Janārdana;
[one should also seek] the constant vision of the gods and the nectar of the feet of the virtuous. 97.
It should be drunk, worn upon the head, and likewise used for smearing the dust [on the body];
the water from the feet of Hari should always be drunk by both woman and man during the vow. (98)
One should adopt the reclining posture on a bed, avoid desire and anger, abstain from shaving, and refrain from sexual intercourse. (99)
The tongue must perform austerity through renunciation of what has been obtained and acquired; likewise, there must be no touching of men by women, nor any touching of women by men. (1.293.10)
Indeed, during the intercalary month at Śrī Puruṣottama, one must avoid [certain activities] in every way;
one should not go outside the house, or one may go only for the purpose of visiting sacred pilgrimage sites.
One should dwell in a garden, in a park, or likewise in a field;
in a forest, in a wilderness, on sacred ground, among holy men, and in the company of virtuous women.
Dwelling on ground dedicated to renunciation, or on the banks of a sacred ford, or at its boundary,
or in an excellent leaf-hut, or dwelling in the open sky is considered superior.
Hearing and chanting the names of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, as well as remembering Him, serving His feet, worshiping Him, and likewise bowing down to Him— 104.
One should practice devotion consisting of such activities as servitude, the offering of oneself and one's possessions, and constant contemplation of Kṛṣṇa, when impurity is predominant.
This impurity (mala) takes or seizes liberation (mukti), therefore it is called *māsa*. Since illusion (*māyā*) dissolves (*līyate*) by means of this, this impurity is declared to be *māsa*. (106)
The month in which Lakṣmī measures (māti) me is therefore proclaimed as Māla;
indeed, the letter 'ma' is the final syllable of the name Puruṣottama.
The first syllable of Lakṣmī is dropped; Ma is joined with Kṛṣṇa and Śrī. Hari is the washer away of impurity (mala), by whom that "ma" is dissolved. 108.
Whatever gift or meritorious act is performed during the intercalary month (malamāsa), its fruit is indeed greater; for the intercalary month is truly superior. 109.
Where Nārāyaṇa Kṛṣṇa is established in every house day after day,
he accepts auspicious worship in that Puruṣottama.
In this month, Śrī Puruṣottama, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, is delighted by Ramā, Lakṣmī, Pārvatī, Prabhā, and likewise by Māṇikī.
From Goloka, from Vaikuṇṭha, and from the unmanifest abode,
he indeed comes to this world for the sake of being seen by the worlds.
Who performs virtuous deeds such as worship, offerings, and vows, as well as bathing, ritual worship, and giving of gifts during my month? (1.13)
In this manner, the god always beholds from the path of the sky in the early morning those devotees who have bathed and are performing acts of devotion toward the deity of the planet.
Having beheld with divine vision those men who were givers of gifts, protectors of their vows, and beloved by others, Puruṣottama, accompanied by Śrī, [appeared]. || 1.15 ||
When pleased and satisfied, Kṛṣṇa bestows prosperity, granting him the ability to perform what is beneficial, to go to his abode, and to dwell there for a long time. 1.16.
O Lakṣmī, at my request, make the dwellings of those observing the vow of Puruṣottama-māsa completely filled with every prosperity. 1.17
May you never dwell in the house of those who disregard the intercalary month;
and wherever I have no residence, there may you also have none.
Having thus instructed him, Hari— having received the food offering presented both in the morning and at midday— returns indeed to his own abode.
In the evening, Hari himself comes again with his own wives to each house to accept services such as the offering of the lustration lamp (ārātrika).
Having received ghee-lamps, incense, flowers, water, and excellent food—
all these— he departs from his own abode once he has been bid farewell.
Thus, the omnipresent Lord Śrī Hari beholds them constantly for an additional month out of compassion for His devotees; therefore, the two Śrī Puruṣottamas are to be worshipped.

Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-third chapter, titled "The Description of the Duties of Vows, Austerities, Charity, Bathing, Worship, and Observances on the First Day," within the *Māhātmya* of the Month of Śrī Puruṣottama, in the first section concerning the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga, in the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
O Lakṣmī, I shall now tell you how the Lord of the month of Puruṣottama, that ocean of mercy known as Puruṣottama himself, came to be so designated. || 1 ||
Once, on the full moon day, sages likewise arrived at the hermitage of Śrī Nara-Nārāyaṇa for the purpose of beholding Śrī Hari.
The sages possessed of divine knowledge and masters of the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences—Patnīvat, Lomaśa, Mārkaṇḍeya, and Nārada—[were there]. (3)
Vyāsa, Paila, Sumantu, Devala, Asita, Kāśyapa, Jābāli, Sumati, Yājñavalkya, and Pippalāyana. || 4 ||
Vāmadeva, Sutīkṣṇa, Parvata, Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, Āpastamba, Śarabhaṅga, Kapila, Raibhya, and Āruṇi; || 5 ||
Kātyāyana, Rathītara, Ṛbhu, Māṇḍavya, Ekata, Dvita, Trita, Agastya, Mudgala, and Kratu Gautama. || 6 ||
Kauśika, Gālava, Babhru, Atri, Śakti, Budha, Vasu,
Bodhāyana, Pṛthu, Dhūmra, Śaṅku, Saṃkṛti, and Ārtihan.
Kauṇḍinya, Śini, Vibhāṇḍaka, Paṅka, Dhūmapa, Jamadagni, Kaṇāda, Garga, Mauna, and Bhārgava. || 8 ||
Bharadvāja, Karkaśa, Śatānanda, Śaunaka, Viśāla, Viṣṇuvṛddha, Jarjara, Tanu, and Jaya. || 9 ||
Pāra, Pāśadhara, Pūra, Jaṅgama, Jaimini, Makha, Uddālaka, Mahāṣeṇa, Āmalakī, and Piṅgala. || 10 ||
Śāṇḍīraka, Prabhu, Atri, Karuṇa, Śvetaketuka, Romapāda, Kadru, Jājali, Cyavana, and Śama. || 11 ||
Dīrghatamas, Pṛthuśravas, Śvetāśvatara Āsuri, Jaigīṣavya, Avaṭya, Dharma, and Bharga Aiśvara. || 12 ||
Vasiṣṭha, Marīci, Pulaha, and Pulastya—
these and thousands of others [went] to the hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa.
Those most devoted to Brahman, who act for the benefit of the world and whose nature is to perform service for others, gathered there with millions of disciples in order to behold him. (14)
Having prostrated themselves like a staff before Nārāyaṇa and proclaimed his victory,
all those who had reached the further shore of the Vedas, being duly honored, sat down before him.
And they [beheld] that Lord Nārāyaṇa—tranquil, gentle, clad in bark garments, with a serene countenance, and the refuge of the fourth goal of human existence. || 16 ||
He is an ocean of the bliss of all divine and auspicious qualities without exception;
he wears the vertical mark (ūrdhvapuṇḍra), possesses divine matted locks, and is endowed with divine splendor.
Resplendent with divine necklaces and other ornaments, wearing a garland of *tulasī*,
reciting the supreme Brahman upon his rosary, he is the infallible Acyuta, the worthy refuge.
They beheld him, like one in deep meditation, with his senses conquered, his very form being asceticism, his face adorned with the discus of splendor, and his entire being centered upon Badarī.
Then the gods and the ancestors arrived there,
as did all the rivers, sacred fords, holy fields, and forests.
Forests, cities, lakes, and likewise oceans, as well as perfected ones (*siddhas*) and yogis, all arrived there filled with great joy. (21)
Some were without food, some subsisted on fruits, and some on foam;
some took air, water, or leaves as their sustenance, while others subsisted on mere breath.
Desiring to see Nārāyaṇa, they attained supreme peace upon seeing him;
they all bowed down to that great sage, Nārāyaṇa. (23)
Then, seeing it firmly attached to the Supreme Brahman and radiating intense luster, they all stood before the illustrious Hari and forbade him from proceeding further.
The Yugas and the Sandhyās, the years and likewise the sacrificial sessions (Kratu), as well as the months, fortnights, days, and nights, all came together. ||25||
The units of time—kalās, kāṣṭhās, muhūrtas, ghaṭikās, and likewise praharas—arrived, richly accompanied by their families, together with their masters, and possessing beautiful forms. (26)
Among them, Kārttika indeed has Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa as its presiding deity,
and Mārgaśīrṣa likewise has Ramā-Vāsudeva as its presiding deity.
Pauṣa has the Sun known as Saṃkrāntiśaktiśrīviṣṇu as its presiding deity;
Māgha has Vasantavijayāmādhava as its supreme deity.
Phālguna has Mahārātri, Lakṣmī, and Brahmā as his presiding deities;
Caitra, however, has Pārthivī, Śakti, Sītā, and Śyāmā as its presiding deities. ||29||
Vaiśākha has Hayaśiras, Durgā, and Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha as its presiding deities;
Jyeṣṭha has Gaṅgā, Mahālakṣmī, and Trivikrama as its presiding deities.
Āṣāḍha has Mahāvidyā Lakṣmī Vyāsa as his presiding deity;
Śrāvaṇa has Vārṣikī Dolāramā Kṛṣṇā as his presiding deity.
The month of Bhādrapada has Mahāgaurī and Vāmana-Brahmā as its presiding deities;
Āśvina has Śāradā-Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa as its presiding deities.
In the hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa, they shone together with their Lord;
indeed, among them there was not even one who was without a master or lacked a lord. (33)
By the greatness of their union with their respective lords, all are endowed with good fortune;
they abide in their respective offices, bestowing fruits upon all.
Thereafter, the lordless intercalary month arrived;
it was redundant, like a tail, and loathed by everyone. || 35 ||
Dark-complexioned and filthy, deprived of food and drink, lacking both bathing and worship, he was untouchable and despised by all. ||36||
There, all of them spoke to him, who was helpless and loathsome:
"This intercalary month is unworthy, being devoid of the sun's transit. (37)
Untouchable due to his nature as filth, he is censured in auspicious rites;
he is the dissolution of effort, the loss of profit, and one bereft of fortune. (38)
Having arrived from somewhere, let those who possess a lord keep him at a distance;
Dakṣa gave twenty-seven daughters to the Moon.
From that, this impurity indeed arose among them;
it emerged in the form of their leavings, causing the three defects.
"Let this impurity, which lasts for two and a half years, be removed.
Hearing these words of theirs, his mind was seized with anxiety.
With that burning heart, he became as if about to die;
and though far away, he stood as if within reach, beholding me situated at Badarī.
Having all beheld him, they became established in meditative absorption;
Māla, summoning his fortitude, acted at my signal.
He reached the abode of Vaikuṇṭha, where I dwell and take delight;
having arrived for the sake of my deliverance, he then beheld me.
Weeping with a broken heart, he fell prostrate upon the ground like a staff;
with palms joined and eyes closed, he spoke these words for his own welfare.
O Protector, ocean of compassion, granter of refuge to the wretched, protect me, a miserable one who has been insulted by others and has come before you as a defiled sinner. 46.
Devoid of a lord, defiled, excluded from auspicious rites, and cast out by the gods—O you who are compassionate toward the wretched, protect me! 47.
Satyavrata, Gajendra, Dharma, Sureśvara, and the others—you who are the protector and the one who will be the protector, O Viṣṇu, O Supreme Lord, protect me! 48.
Having spoken thus, with eyes clouded and gaze cast downward, he became silent;
seeing him in such a state, Hari, filled with compassion, spoke.
"My child, do not be dejected; I shall rescue you, so do not grieve.
Tell me your sorrow, and I will dispel it; you truly ought not to lament."
One who has come for refuge to me is not destined for even a trace of suffering;
having reached the sorrowless bliss of Vaikuṇṭha, you shall no longer be a partaker of grief.
Having found consolation, Malamāsa spoke while bowing to Hari:
"You are omniscient; you are the inner self of all, and you know everything exactly as it is. (52)
Nevertheless, O Lord, I tell you that my suffering is equal to death;
[I perceive] the kalās, the kāṣṭhās, the muhūrtas, the dhaṭikās, the days, and the years. (53)

All the fortnights, months, and yugas rejoice when presided over by their master; my own origin is from that which has been left overnight, from the leavings of leavings, and from the refuse of refuse.
For me, there is always impurity, the state of being of the nature of filth, untouchability, disrespect, lack of ownership, humiliation, and inauspiciousness. (55)
I have no agency, no fruitfulness, and no authority whatsoever [for this task], even by those such as the sages, gods, and supreme deities who have come to the Badarī hermitage. (56)
He was reviled with insults such as "you [unworthy] month," rendered untouchable, cast out, deprived of his ritual duties, threatened, and afflicted in every way. (57)
Therefore, I desire death as a boon rather than a wretched life;
you, however, are a supreme person, a benefactor who cannot endure the suffering of others. (58)
O Lords, bring about my welfare; otherwise, I am a base and meritless man who will die, I will die, I will die—of this there is no doubt. (59)
Having spoken thus, he fell at the feet of Śrī Nārāyaṇa, crying:
"Protect me, protect me, O Lord of the World! Protect me, O Kṛṣṇa, O Consort of Ramā! (60)
"Protect me, O Lord of Lakṣmī, O Master; I have come to you for refuge.
To him who had spoken thus, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Hari whose abode is Vaikuṇṭha, [replied].
He said, "Arise! May it be well with you; do not grieve, behold me.
Come together with me to the Lord, the Sovereign of Goloka. (62)
[He meditated on] Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama) situated among the multitude of gopīs,
the two-armed, darkly beautiful one who causes his flute to resound.
He has lotus-like eyes, a face like the full moon, and is the abode of the god of love;
he wears yellow garments and is adorned with a forest garland and the jewel Kaustubha.
His chest was smeared with sandalwood paste and adorned with a tilaka of musk; he was endowed with a crown, earrings, and a staff-like ring set with excellent jewels. ||65||
The ancient Supreme Person, whose chest is adorned with the Śrīvatsa mark, seated upon a lion-throne, and surrounded by hosts of cowherds and cowherdesses.
"Let us go; that Hari Kṛṣṇa will dispel your sorrow.
Having said this, Hari took him by the hand and went to Goloka.
The glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa was present, accompanied by all the materials for worship; likewise, various articles were prepared for the sake of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Rādhikā. 68.
Jewels, ornaments, garments, and household articles;
delightful fragrant liquids, as well as drinks and foods. ||69||
The Lord indeed gave fruits, mouth-fresheners, divine golden ornaments and the like, and countless articles worthy of a king.
Having taken him with them, they reached Goloka and Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa;
they both bathed in the Virajā river and went to Śataśṛṅga.
Here, the impurities of the intercalary month are destroyed by the flood of Virajā;
indeed, for one who bathes on the second lunar day of the intercalary month, all impurities are truly removed.
The merits acquired over many lifetimes will perish from their very root;
yet those people who observe the vow shall attain the merit of bathing in the Virajā.
Merely by bathing there, one shall attain Goloka; of this there is no doubt.
And having beheld the site of the Rāsa-maṇḍala, Vṛndāvana, and the rest, [the same result is attained]. (74)
Placing dust upon his head, he beheld the excellent *bhāṇḍīra* and *vaṭa* trees,
as well as the principal fortress, and entered the place inhabited by the cowherd women.
They went to the dwelling situated within the sixteen gate-towers, into the interior of the palace near Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. ||76||
Beholding the divine pair, the two of them prostrated themselves like a staff; honored by the two gracious ones, they bowed at their feet.
Having been well-honored, the two of them sat down on appropriate seats;
then Kṛṣṇa, with joy, took Nārāyaṇa by the hand.
He closed his eyes, placing his arms around his chest and resting his chest against them,
repeatedly seating Nārāyaṇa upon the lion-throne on the banner.
Endowed with laughter and cheerfulness, the Lord made an inquiry;
then Nārāyaṇa explained the reason for his arrival.
Then the Lord himself was worshipped by Nārāyaṇa;
the Master, together with Rādhā, was bathed with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta). ||81||
Afterwards, the Lord was bathed with milk and then bathed with water;
he was then wrapped in a cloth and worshipped with sandalwood paste and other offerings. ||82||
Adorned with ornaments and decorated with divine garments and the like, [he is honored] with incense, lamps, *ārārtika* offerings, circumambulations, hymns of praise, and so forth. ||83||
The Lord was honored with offerings of vessels made of gold, gems, and precious stones,
and was gratified with various fruits, juices, and foods.
Then Rādhikā and the other wives of Kṛṣṇa were honored with suitable turbans,
and Śrī Kṛṣṇa himself was also worshipped at that time according to their capacity, even during the intercalary month (malamāsa).
Having attained grace, Māsa and Mala also received a true blessing;
Śrī Kṛṣṇa, joined by Rādhā, spoke to them with favor. (86)
Just as I have been worshipped here by you on this second day, so shall I be worshipped in the world on your lunar day—the second—both at dawn and at night. (87)
Those people who worship Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa according to their ability, I shall then accept them all together with Rādhā. (88)
On the second day, the Lord, whose form is of gold, should especially be bathed with cow’s milk, or else with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) or with water. 89.
He who possesses great devotion should be adorned with gold, garments, ornaments, and substances such as sandalwood paste;
he should be adorned with the requisites for personal service. 90.

He is to be worshipped with incense, lamps, and the like, as well as with bracelets, crowns, and other ornaments; he is to be gratified with sweet foods and likewise with jewel-encrusted decorations and such.
I am to be worshipped exceedingly, and I shall be satisfied in every way;
I will bestow upon them various and innumerable riches as a reward.
Just as I exist in this world, so shall I grant [you] that, of this there is no doubt;
and in the end, I shall grant you the opulent Goloka and eternal happiness.
Having received this blessing, even the intercalary month (malamāsa) became fortunate;
in the presence of Nārāyaṇa, he indeed became possessed of exceeding majesty.
Then he said to Kṛṣṇa: "O Lord, prospered by your grace, act for me in such a way that I may once again possess a master. (95)
O dispeller of the blinding darkness of ignorance, O illuminator of the path of knowledge, O you who explain the processes of the arising and destruction of innumerable globes! 96.
O Lord of divine and beautiful form, visible to those who are worthy and devoted;
You are worshipped with four arms bearing the conch, discus, mace, and lotus as Your weapons. 97.
Served by the consorts of countless Lakṣmīs, you are dark as the petal of a blue lotus, with eyes as red as a lotus. (98)
O you whose face outshines the splendor of ten million autumnal full moons;
O you who are enchanting as the abode of the playful beauty of ten million gods of love! 99.
His chest was resplendent with the Śrīvatsa mark and adorned with the shining Kaustubha gem and necklaces;
he was radiant with a crown and armlets set with millions of excellent jewels.
O Viṣṇu, O Lord Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, who bestows auspiciousness upon your devotees;
having cast away all inauspiciousness, bring about my welfare. 101.
Thus praised, Kṛṣṇa then became pleased and said:
"By the recitation of this hymn, people shall obtain the fruit of their merit."
Devotion to Kṛṣṇa will arise, which shall increase one's sons and grandsons;
there will be an end to ill-repute, and fame shall come to pass.
Whatever objects have been offered in worship,
I declare that I shall bestow them upon my devotee multiplied a hundred thousandfold.
On the second day of the intercalary month, I am to be worshipped by infinite beings;
I shall grant whatever is desired to that seeker of vows, even if it be infinite.
Water should be given to a banyan tree, food to a virtuous Brahmin, and a garment to an excellent maiden; this should be done for the attainment of fruits.
Raw grains should be given to a virtuous devotee of Viṣṇu;
gold should be bestowed as a gift upon a woman who seeks knowledge. (107)
On the second day, all auspicious gifts should indeed be given doubled;
one shall obtain a fruit multiplied ten millionfold both in this world and in the next.
Speaking thus, Kṛṣṇa addressed Nārāyaṇa again and again:
"O Nārāyaṇa! O Hari! O Lord of Lakṣmī! O Sun of Vaikuṇṭha! (109)
O Lord, I know the entire account of the intercalary month (malamāsa),
especially as it was told by you, the Lord of Śrī.
But this is an intercalary month, devoid of the sun's transit; it is impure, unworthy, and excluded from auspicious rites. (111)
Thinking thus, although he was rejected by the gods of creation, he has indeed come to my house;
therefore, he is not soiled today.
He is divine, he is perfectly pure, and he is worthy of worship in every respect;
however, let it now be considered who shall be his master. (113)
I am the lord of the dark fortnights of other months as well;
likewise, you too are the lord—let this be reflected upon.
Therefore, in the thirteenth month, you have no claim of ownership over us;
for that reason, let us indeed go to where Śrī Puruṣottama resides.
The King of Kings shines in the supreme, imperishable abode, from whom innumerable incarnations such as myself arise. (11.6)
Since the abodes such as Goloka are indeed portions of His own abode,
He, having reflected upon this, will surely conceive of Himself as its Lord.
The original source, however, is the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama;
whomever He shall unite with this [power], he will become its master.
Having reflected thus, Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa is superior;
the three [of them] went to the imperishable abode where Śrī Puruṣottama resides.

Thus, in the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, within the first section concerning the continuity of the Kṛta-yuga, in the *Māhātmya* of the month of Puruṣottama, at Badarikāśrama—where sages, munis, mountains, rivers, trees, creepers, gods, years, months, and others had gathered for the purpose of beholding Nara and Nārāyaṇa—the intercalary month (*malamāsa*) was treated with contempt due to its perceived impurity; [this section describes] the departure of that intercalary month to Vaikuṇṭha, its subsequent journey to Goloka along with Nārāyaṇa there, and its attainment of great fortune following the worship of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Rādhikā by those inhabitants.

Having received the blessings and gathered [them], the departure toward the world of the Imperishable Brahman (*akṣarabrahmaloka*) for the sake of attaining its lordship; this is the two hundred and ninety-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of the Departure."
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī, how Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, and Adhimā went from Goloka in an instant by way of the divine path through the sky. || 1 ||
That imperishable abode which is endowed with the fullness of truth, consciousness, and bliss.
Having bathed in the Brahmahrada, they took on the forms of the Supreme Person.
And having become so, they beheld circles of liberated souls,
each possessing two arms, being eight years of age, and having forms corresponding to their beauty.
Equal to ten million Nārāyaṇas in beauty, splendor, and perfect accomplishments,
they were indeed ten million times more beautiful than even Goloka.
Seeing those who possessed such forms of the Supreme Person,
the three of them became filled with wonder and their minds were captivated.
Having beheld the gardens and palaces, and having seen the pearls, celestial chariots, and various articles of luxury, they were filled with wonder.

Having perceived the imperishable reality within his own abodes, he became dispassionate toward them; for when compared with the objects of the imperishable realm, those born of his own abodes were found lacking.
At that time, however, those [beings] perceived only a vast, joyless void;
yet they brought back the substance which had been taken from Vaikuṇṭha for the worship of Puruṣottama.
Or rather, all that appeared joyless from Goloka;
it was seen by them as if devoid of luster, though its true nature is self-effulgent.
Then, with their hopes indeed shattered regarding the matter of receiving gifts,
they looked about there for the Brahma-lake.
Extending for infinite yojanas and consisting of divine water of exquisite taste,
by bathing in which an object attains the state of being fit for enjoyment by the illustrious Puruṣottama.
Those three, having bathed joyfully in the Brahma-lake, received gifts consecrated by him; thus, at that time, everything became fit for use.
Then, having questioned the guards, they saw a vast palace extending for a hundred thousand yojanas; thereafter, three of them were released from the gate.
They entered where the king of kings, the Supreme Person, the Lord, resided,
attended by countless liberated divine beings.
Seeing Kṛṣṇa and Nārāyaṇa arrived, the Lord Puruṣottama rejoiced exceedingly as they bowed to him again and again.
He inquired after their welfare and their eternal well-being regarding their respective abodes.
By the grace of the Blessed One, everything is well and very auspicious.
Having spoken thus, those two, Nara and Nārāyaṇa, shone resplendently upon their seats;
even the intercalary month, having performed itself like a fifth staff, stood there.
That supreme man stood by their side like a servant;
then the Lord of Letters questioned him in return.
"Who is this, and for what purpose has he come here to my abode with you two?
I think he has come seeking great gain, having taken refuge in this sanctuary. (19)
When the Lord of All asked thus, both Kṛṣṇa and Nārāyaṇa honored him with infinite divine gifts.
First, there was the thorough washing of the feet with the waters of the Brahma-lake,
followed by an immersion in the five nectars of divine essence.
Having consecrated the Lord of the Imperishable with waters consisting of the essence of rasa, and having duly worshipped both of them with liquid substances such as sandalwood paste; ||22||
With joy, they offered garments, ornaments, necklaces, and so forth;
as well as an umbrella, chowries, jewels, sandals, a staff, and other such items. (23)
Finger-rings, armlets, crowns, chains, and ornaments for the neck;
golden flower-earrings, garlands, girdles, bracelets, and so forth. (24)
Eatables, foods, things to be licked, and things to be sucked, mixed with sugar and honey;
food fit for eating, delicious drinks, and various items for chewing and the like. ||25||
Then they offered whatever was appropriate to be presented: golden garments, seats, vessels, divine fruits, juices, and so forth. (26)
Having performed the nightly lamp-offering and offered hymns of praise, they sat down comfortably;
and having accepted the hospitality and honors, they spoke concerning the intercalary month.
This month is an intercalary month, a "defiled" month, which is censured by all months and by the sages, and is forbidden for auspicious rites. (28)
Therefore, this good fortune of his was indeed created by me, Kṛṣṇa;
however, without his presiding deity, he does not deserve to be counted among them.
This great suffering of his cannot be warded off except by you;
therefore, out of compassion, please make him free from fear and full of joy. (30)
"And for our sake, his suffering must be dispelled.
Upon hearing this, the venerable Puruṣottama, who transcends the syllables, spoke.
"O Kṛṣṇa, what you have done here is most appropriate, since you have come here;
and it is also auspicious that Nārāyaṇa has likewise arrived here today. (32)
"By performing this during the intercalary month (malamāsa), you two shall attain fame in the world;
that which was held in your hands has been taken by me into my own hand. (33)
Therefore, I shall make him equal to myself, standing above all;
indeed, I shall fashion him so that he is endowed with qualities just like my own.
By means of my powers, my status as one worthy of worship, and likewise by my excellent valor, I make myself equal to you; what else remains to be desired? (35)
The destruction of all sins, the granting of true resolve, the bestowing of the fruits of desires, and the conferring of similarity with Me. ||36||
May the intercalary month be endowed with these powers: the capacity to lead one to heaven and other realms, and the quality of bestowing the state of liberation. //37//
All my other virtues have been surrendered to the intercalary month;
likewise, even my designation as "Puruṣottama" has been offered for its satisfaction. (38)
I alone shall be its master, Brahmā, Īśa, and Puruṣottama;
the entire world shall bear my name, and it will indeed take that name. (39)
Having shaken off his own sins, he will become a purifier;
indeed, having become my very self, he will be worshiped by the world. ||40||
Worthy of universal veneration, this month shall become the most excellent of all months;
indeed, by relying upon it, people shall become observers of vows, reciters of prayers, and worshippers.
By my power, those who are givers, those who perform ablutions, those who feed others, and even those who perform some small act of merit [attain this]. (42)

And having shaken off the afflictions of suffering, poverty, distress, mental anguish, and disease, [they are endowed] with happiness, prosperity, wealth, wives, offspring, and the abundance of health. ||43||
The royal palaces will become magnificent and filled with festivities,
adorned with ornaments, garments, vessels, and various articles of luxury.
With male and female servants, friends, attendants, decorated grounds, security, prosperity, strength, and freedom from want, there will be great festivals. (45)
They will be endowed with food, drink, and objects of enjoyment, with the manifestation of the knowledge of existence and so forth, and with gardens, vehicles, mounts, and the like. (46)
They will be perpetually radiant with juices, tree fruits, flowers, herds of cattle, gold and silver, and with gems, jewels, diamonds, and the like. ||47||
For those who observe the vow of the month of Puruṣottama have indeed turned toward me;
they shall obtain everything from me, just as people obtain everything from a wish-fulfilling gem.
Whether it be the world of heaven, that of Brahmā, Vairāja, or Vaiṣṇava;
or that of Rudra, or the earthly realm—whatever state they deem fit, they shall attain.
By observing the intercalary month, they shall obtain wives, husbands, homes, palatial mansions, virtuous sons, and the splendor of beauty—all imperishable and inexhaustible. (50)
Whether possessing desires or free from desires, they shall indeed obtain their most cherished object from this;
for both the one with desire and the one without desire, I am the Supreme Person.
Thus, this [work] has been made to fulfill the desires of the people and to grant liberation;
just as I am perfectly complete, so too has this been made imperishable.
Thus, those who possess this longing and those who are free from longing, having worshipped [the deity], will attain their own desired goal and obtain liberation. ||93||
By worshipping this, the actions of those who perform rituals are reduced to ashes;
the divine Self, supremely pure, shall come to me alone in the Imperishable.
Indeed, for my sake, ascetics, celibate students, the virtuous, the great-souled ones, yogins, and likewise practitioners of austerity have exerted themselves with great effort. (95)
The Yoginīs, the Sāṃkhya-yoginīs, the virtuous wives, the truthful ones, and likewise those without husbands;
the dispassionate men and women, who show great reverence for Nirvāṇa. (56)
Free from delusion, likewise expounders of Brahman, and devoted to the practice of renunciation,
they strive for a thousand years, up to a million years.
Nevertheless, these do not at all go to my supreme and most transcendent abode;
however, those who are devotees of Puruṣottama go to my abode within a month.
Other ascetics were peaceful, abstaining from food and free from desire;
they subsisted on leaves, flowers, and fruits, or consumed nothing but water.
Subsisting on mere air, feeding on vapors, inhaling smoke, dwelling in water, and likewise enduring cold and heat; ||60||

With withered bodies, broken channels of the penis, and having entered the apertures of the *brahma-randhra*, they are fit for entering the bodies of others, even though they are endowed with firmness in their vows. (61)
Indeed, without devotion to me, they do not go to my abode;
however, those who observe the vow of the month of Puruṣottama belong to me.
Those devotees of mine who observe vows shall,
by my grace, reach my eternal and immortal state within a mere month.
Therefore, O Kṛṣṇa and Nārāyaṇa, this month has been placed by me at the very head for your sake; it is the accomplisher of all desires and goals. (64)
Those people who shall serve Śrī Puruṣottama for a month will attain the perfection of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa. || 65 ||
Therefore, let this month, which is the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), be served by all;
it is like a most excellent field, superior for the sprouting of seeds.
The Supreme Person bestows ten millionfold merit as its fruit;
having enjoyed [the rewards] in heaven, those who perform the Cāturmāsya sacrifices return once again.
Those who sacrifice for the Supreme Person go to the imperishable and eternal state;
he rescues seven hundred and seven generations of his lineage.
One who observes a vow during another month certainly does not transcend rebirth;
however, one who observes a vow in my month does not go to rebirth at all. 69.
In this month, I myself dwell here as the presiding deity;
his name was also made after mine, and therefore I am indeed identical with him.
I shall fulfill the desires of all those who take refuge in him;
I shall not count their offenses, for they are his devotees in every respect. (71)
Compared to my own devotion, the devotion directed toward me is dear to me;
there shall be no delay in fulfilling the desires of those who are devoted to me month by month.
Excluding my devotee alone, I fulfill the desires of all others;
indeed, I grant everything to them because they worship me for a month.
They are indeed very dear to me, even more so than millions of liberated souls;
for having reached my month, they are freed from the need for recitation, charity, and other such rites. (74)

Those who are devoid of ritual bathing and worship, who obstruct virtuous deeds, and who have abandoned the construction of wells, tanks, ponds, and other works of public utility (pūrta), as well as sacrifices (yajña); ||75||
Those who hate deities, sacred fords, the twice-born, holy men, virtuous women, and temples, and who are revilers, shall become eaters of crow-dung. (76)
They shall become lepers, like dogs and jackals, without any refuge;
for those who are unfortunate and slanderous, there shall be no happiness by day or night.
Those lowest of men who cause suffering to those observing vows during my month shall become donkeys, bound by the nooses of others' beatings. (78)
Those who revile my month, those who are corrupters of the Dharma, and those envious ones who create obstacles on this path of devotion—[may they be destroyed]. (79)
Those who, having reached Puruṣottama every third year, will become tree-juice-drinkers and gluttons. (80)
Those who do not perform what is beneficial for themselves will go to my abode; having become intensely miserable here, pervaded by the fire of the noose of suffering. 8.1.
The giver of fortune, the bestower of prosperity, and therefore the granter of victory over death—this month of mine, Puruṣottama, must not be spent in vain. ||82||
Maidens and young women, both married and unmarried, co-wives, women, the elderly, and those who are fortunate as well as unfortunate. (83)
Those who, whether in a state of unhappiness or even great happiness, shall perform vows, give gifts, and worship me during my month solely for the sake of attaining their own desired ends; ||84||
I am the Lord Puruṣottama, the bestower of everything—bathing, garlands, service to the gods, and whatever other meritorious deeds there may be. 85.
I bestow righteousness, desire, as well as wealth, happiness, and liberation;
I grant food, the power of digestion, the capacity for sexual pleasure, and an excellent husband.
I grant sons, grandsons, male and female servants, and whatever else is desired;
I become the bestower of happiness upon one's brothers, father, and family. 87.
O Supreme among Men, all that makes the month, the women, and even myself empty shall become empty; all good fortune shall fall into voidness.
Those wealthy householders who spend their month in vain without performing acts such as giving charity—because of them, my treasury shall fall into emptiness. (89)
If even those celibate students, forest-dwellers, and ascetics who follow the path of renunciation pass a month without devotion, [then what need is there to speak of others]? 90.
Indeed, even all those ascetics become devoid of liberation [if they do not visit him];
likewise, Śūdras, women, and the classes of servants [attain it by visiting] Śrī Puruṣottama.
If they pass their time without serving the Guru and the God, they too shall be bereft of prosperity and afflicted by suffering and poverty. (92)
The guru is to be served; Hari is to be served; parents and other elders are to be served;
the cow is to be served; the husband is to be served; and a chaste wife is to be served, just as I am. (93)
"Wherever I may abide, I shall grant the fruit in every way;
therefore, Śrī Puruṣottama is to be served by all with their whole being. (94)
One should strive for one's own spiritual welfare through dharma and devotion, which lead to liberation;
neither widowhood nor separation from a husband shall be brought about by the intercalary month (malamāsa). || 95 ||
O months of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, listen certainly to my words;
indeed, by my command, all those worlds that exist within the cosmic egg [shall do so]. 96.
"Wherever this month exists, there in every way they shall worship me in my essential form as the presiding presence. (97)
Those devotees of mine shall attain my eternal abode—the imperishable Goloka, Vaikuṇṭha, or the immortal realm of Īśvara. ||98||
By my grace, through the power of this month, those various devotees shall go to my supreme abode according to their respective desires. (99)
"On the third lunar day of my month, I have been worshipped by you both;
likewise, for those who shall worship me then, their desires will be fulfilled. (100)
"By means of bathing, giving gifts, chanting prayers, and other such acts, everything will certainly come to pass;
O Lakṣmīśa, O Rādhikeśvara, do not worry. (101)
"Having taken Puruṣottama, go each to your own respective world. Having received this command and bowed down, those three departed.
Listen, Lakṣmī: those who bathe in abundant waters on the third lunar day have effectively bathed in the Brahmahrada as well as in the Brahmasarovara.
Indeed, whatever bath has been performed shall become meritorious for me,
as well as the worship offered by those two and whatever was dedicated there.
Likewise, those people who shall perform worship to me in this month and shall also give gifts, their merit shall become eternal. || 105 ||
Since my worship was performed by those two on the third lunar day,
human beings as well must perform the great worship on the third lunar day.
A great worship must be performed for Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, and Puruṣottama as well, which bestows happiness, liberation, and other blessings. 107.
Just as I am in the abode of Brahmā, so am I another self consisting of the month;
I am entirely within the cosmic egg, and likewise I abide within the inner heart.
I am Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, served by Rādhā, Lakṣmī, and others;
I know everything, whereas others do not know me in such a way.
"I sport together with Pārvatī and with Māṇikī;
though possessing many forms, know me to be truly one alone, O lady of my body. (110)

Thus, in the first section, the *Kṛtayuga-santāna*, of the *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*, within the *Puruṣottama-māsa-māhātmya*, [this is the account of] the departure of Śrī-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa and the intercalary months to the Abode of the Imperishable (*akṣara-dhāma*); following the bath in the *Brahma-hrada* and *Brahma-sarovara*, the arrival at the presence of Śrī-Puruṣottama, His worship, and the offering of one's own self; the subsequent attainment by the intercalary month of the sovereignty and the name "Puruṣottama"; the description of the fruits of worship, charity, and other rites performed on the third lunar day; and further [details concerning] the months of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
The two hundred and ninety-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of Departing to One's Own Abode," etc.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī; having thus gone to Goloka, those three also rested there for a moment.
Kṛṣṇa was worshipped by the two of them.
The greatness of Puruṣottama manifested in many ways in Goloka;
having bowed to Kṛṣṇa, Nara and Nārāyaṇa departed for Adhomāsa.
Then, even there in Vaikuṇṭha, the month attained greatness;
indeed, Hari caused the month of Puruṣottama to dwell there as well.
Having attained his residence, even for a month he rejoices together with Viṣṇu;
having become the lord of the months, he remains established in dignity.
Then, having been honored here with great respect by Mahālakṣmī,
he was likewise quickly honored by Nārāyaṇa throughout every single universe.
And on the afternoon of the third day, having dispatched his own attendants, he proclaimed:
"This most excellent intercalary month has indeed been announced."
This [place] is named Puruṣottama, with Puruṣottama as its presiding deity;
it was made by Puruṣottamanātha a bestower of heaven and a bestower of liberation.
Indeed, his own virtues have been offered to him; he is not inferior to Puruṣottama in worship, salutation, recitation, giving, bathing, or even in religious observances.
This bestower of the yoga of Puruṣottama is equal to Puruṣottama himself;
whether they be men or women, gods or goddesses, or even those that are stationary or moving. || 9 ||
By my will, they shall perform the entire rite of the intercalary month— including both the vow and the worship— with sincerity and at the same time.
They shall obtain everything they desire; this I, Nārāyaṇa, declare.
What then need be said regarding this vow performed throughout the three periods of the day? || 11 ||
Regarding the monthly vow, however, nothing at all remains to be told by me;
therefore, one should worship [the deity] once, twice, or three times a day. 12.
A woman shall obtain her desire, and a man likewise shall attain his wish;
whether for a moment, half a moment, or a ghaṭikā—in the evening, at dawn, or at midday.
This Supreme Person, Nārāyaṇa, is to be worshipped according to one's ability and according to the available materials; I speak this here, with the Supreme Person as my witness. (14)
And in this month named Puruṣottama, they shall worship me with devotion for even a single moment, with Śrī Kṛṣṇa as their witness.
They shall attain heaven and the world of Īśa, as well as their own desired goals;
they shall attain me, the ocean of bliss, the Supreme Brahman, higher than the highest.
Those who, by the will of Nārāyaṇa, worship me here with devotion,
shall indeed attain me, Nārāyaṇa, who resides in Vaikuṇṭha.
Those who, by the will of the glorious Kṛṣṇa, worship me here with devotion,
shall indeed attain me, Mādhava, who resides in Goloka.
Those people who, desiring the Supreme Person, shall worship me when I have gone to the abode of Brahmā, will indeed attain me, the Supreme Person.
Whatever form embodied beings here worship me in, they shall attain that very form and likewise reach me there.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, it was proclaimed again and again throughout the cosmic eggs by the messengers and attendants of divine form with great kettledrums.
On the night of the third day of the intercalary month, he was indeed honored, worshipped, and properly fed by many millions [of beings], yet he experienced great exhaustion.
On the fourth day, however, at dawn, he was exceedingly gratified by the inhabitants of the two worlds of the seven [continents] through their baths, vows, worship, gifts, and other such acts.
Many immobile beings as well as sentient beings who observed vows gathered at the abode of Hari by the hundreds of thousands and tens of millions.
On the morning of the fourth day,
however, Goddess Ramā, traveling in a celestial chariot accompanied by ten million maidservants, arrived from the ocean of nectar at Vaikuṇṭha.
Having assumed the form of a young bride and adorned with a garland for the groom,
she was equal to Lakṣmī in every limb, lacking not even in the slightest degree.
By the command of Nārāyaṇa, she was duly honored by Lakṣmī and the others; then, having been welcomed by Nārāyaṇa himself, she was seated upon his lap.
Seeing that wonder, Lakṣmī and the others were indeed struck with amazement, wondering:
"How was this woman, in the form of a wife, so quickly accepted by her husbands? (28)
Then Lakṣmī was questioned by Ramā to learn of those events:
"How and from where did she come, and how did Nārāyaṇa become her husband? (29)
Whose daughter is she, and how was she obtained? Having done what did you bring this Nārāyaṇa?
O fair-browed sister, tell me everything; it must be related, for it leads to supreme happiness.
Honored and fed by Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa as well,
she indeed began to relate her own history exactly as it had occurred.
Having placed the garland of choice upon the neck of Hari and standing before him,
she drank the water from the big toe of Nārāyaṇa and performed a circumambulation.
Having fashioned a beautiful crescent moon on her forehead with saffron and rice grains,
and having placed half of the bridegroom’s garland around her own neck, she then [offered] milk-rice.
Having fed Hari and given him betel as his gracious gift, he himself took a handful of flowers onto the lap of Nārāyaṇa. (34)
Having offered rice-grains and parched grain while standing at her seat, she, having become his wife, spoke these words: "Listen, Lakṣmī, to this joyous utterance. (35)
While all the male devotees and female devotees were listening, Ramā said to Mahālakṣmī, who is worthy of my worship: "O Mahālakṣmī, during the movement of the third night... (36)
O Dundubhi, who art well-known by all as Nārāyaṇa,
I shall fulfill the desires of the worshipper during the intercalary month.
Even I, as a maiden in the house of the Ocean of Milk, heard of him and desired Nārāyaṇa, the Lord and husband of Lakṣmī, as my husband.
On the third day of the intercalary month, having observed a vow without food or water in the evening,
I bathed and worshipped Hari.
Having consulted my father and the Ocean of Milk, and by his command,
he constructed a pavilion adorned with plantain pillars and leafy arches.
And having had a beautiful and most splendid swing constructed in its center, he should place there a golden image of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, resplendent with jewels. (41)
Having bathed him with all the oceanic waters, having worshipped him with devotion using jewels, and having adorned him with divine garments and ornaments such as unguents and the like; ||42||
Having worshipped with incense, lamps, foods, and drinks, and having saluted with the waving of lights, hymns of praise, and circumambulations; ||43||
Having offered a handful of flowers and again formed a mental resolve:
"O Soul of the Universe, O Nārāyaṇa, become my husband for the sake of Ramā. (44)
Having thus offered praise and drunk the nectar of his feet,
Śrī Hari was lovingly put to sleep by me upon a very soft couch.
"I meditated upon him while asleep; thereafter, I shall serve Hari by massaging his feet"—thus he was observed. (46)
For a moment in my dream, Hari was seen by me upon my own bed; smiling, he seemed to draw me toward him with his affectionate side-long glance. (47)
"O Ramā, having heard you speak thus, I accept you as my beloved through this vow;
O dear one, I shall return again in the morning to lead you to my world. (48)
Having thus quickly caused them to hear this, he himself vanished from sight;
that very Lord Nārāyaṇa, the husband of Lakṣmī, now shines forth.
When Nārāyaṇa had departed, during the moment known as Brāhma on the fourth day of the intercalary month, I meditated upon that Supreme Person.
Having bathed and having bathed the Lord lying upon his bed with great devotion using milk and other substances as well as water, and having rubbed him with sandalwood paste and the like; ||51||
Having presented various ornaments, he was honored like a bridegroom;
a highly precious yellow garment and a yellow body-protector were bestowed upon him. (52)
He wore a cloak richly adorned with golden stars and an excellent upper garment;
on his head was a golden crown, and he had armlets and earrings upon his ears.
A *tilaka* mark on the forehead, collyrium on the eyes and eyebrows, sandalwood paste as dots on the cheeks, and a small crescent moon on the chin. (54)
A covering of flowers on the forehead and an excellent garland around the neck; golden necklaces upon the chest and auspicious bracelets on the hands. (55)
There are finger-rings on the fingers, armlets on both arms, garlands of *tulasī* flowers, and a golden sword in the hand. (56)
There was also a coconut fruit in his hand, a girdle at his waist,
and beautiful golden sandals on his feet.
The fruit of desire is indeed in the forearm; in the hand, auspicious milk-rice (pāyasa);
betel, drinking water, and the juicy grape-fruit. (58)
Then follows the offering of betel nut, the gift of a choice garland as a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā),
and one hundred and eight oblations of clarified butter into the circle of fire.
Perform the night-lit lamp ceremony with five wicks and four circumambulations;
you are the most excellent, the giver of boons, and the bestower—be favorable to my truthful word. (60)

The offering of a handful of flowers, as well as the arghya water, prostration, the request for forgiveness, the dismissal, the drinking of the water from the feet, and the consumption of the remnants. ||61||
Meditation upon what was seen in a dream, waiting for its arrival, wondering when it would come, and the joyful worship by the name of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. (62)
He gave food to young girls and maidens as well;
his meditation was fixed upon Nārāyaṇa, and his body resided in the house that is the Ocean of Milk.

When Hari is worshipped during the intercalary month (adhimāsa) with his full retinue, [the devotee prays: "May my eyes be fixed upon the supreme path in the sky, and may my self reside in Vaikuṇṭha. (64)
Having bowed to my father and taken a small amount of milk as my breaking of the fast,
while I remained in his abode, this very Nārāyaṇa appeared.
He appeared before me, resplendent with a form corresponding to his nature;
gracious and exceedingly radiant, he indeed touched me with his hand.
Drawing me close to him, he said to me, "Come here; for on the third lunar day of the intercalary month, you have worshipped me at this very time. (67)
"O venerable one, having been well-attended to at night and highly honored on the fourth day,
I have indeed been won over by your vow this very morning."
O fair-browed one, just as I have been worshipped by you today through your meditation, so have I attained [my goal], O auspicious one; you are my beloved, my fortunate one. (69)
"Come together with me; you have become my eternal bride. By virtue of your vow, all these female servants of yours shall also come to my house. (70)
"Let my maidservants come; I shall delight with them in every way.
Having thought thus, the excellent one revealed himself as Garuḍa. (71)
Whatever vehicles and conveyances there are here by the thousands, I have gone and reported all of them to my father. (72)
He too, having arrived there, placed me in the hand of Hari;
with my duty accomplished by the command of my father, I mounted the bird.
Sent forth by her father with an army and preceded by honors,
she arrived at the city of Hari, having taken with her her dowry.
This very Nārāyaṇa has been seen here in this palace;
behold, O beautiful lady, he is present right here along with me. (75)
"Indeed, by the fruit of worshipping Him on this night at dawn during the intercalary month, I have obtained a virtuous husband and have come here to meet Nārāyaṇa. (76)
She was indeed led by that very Kṛṣṇa and brought into his lap;
she was made a new bride and a wife, a dweller in Vaikuṇṭha.
"I am your friend and servant, Ramā, always desiring your grace;
thus, O sinless one, have I obtained the fruit of this intercalary month. (78)
Just as I have performed the worship of Nārāyaṇa, so shall she do;
whether she be a girl or a young woman, she will attain this very Nārāyaṇa. (79)
Having worshipped Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa in every way during an intercalary month,
[one should do so] either in the morning, at midday, or at midnight on the fourth lunar day.
In whatever manner they shall worship him, he will fulfill it accordingly:
with wealth, sons, happiness, a wife, a husband, grain, and a good home.
Vehicles, mounts, splendor, beauty, supreme sovereignty, kingdom, power, a beloved wife, male and female servants, and all forms of wealth—[he bestows these]. (82)

Objects of enjoyment connected with pleasures, foods to be eaten and drinks to be drunk in infinite variety, divine substances abiding in their true essence—whatever is desired, [he enjoys] sexual delights and pleasure. (83)
The worlds of heaven devoted to truth, the abodes of Parameṣṭhin, as well as the Vairāja realms, the grounds of Vaikuṇṭha, and the grounds of Dhenu; ||84||
Those who worship Nārāyaṇa indeed conceive Goloka, as well as the imperishable, the divine, and even that which is non-divine, during the intercalary month. ||85||
Men, women, and the gods and goddesses dwelling on the fourteen levels shall all obtain their desired objects through the longing for Puruṣottama. (86)
O Lakṣmī, just as I have become equal to the eternal ones with very little effort, so too shall another woman become possessed of great good fortune.
Even if a woman who is a widow should worship Kṛṣṇa like me during the intercalary month, she will certainly attain Vaikuṇṭha. (88)
Having obtained Nārāyaṇa as her husband, she shall always be possessed of good fortune, whether she be old, or diseased, or even despised by her kinsmen. (89)

She who has fallen away from her religious duties, who is possessed by remorse, who is helpless, alone, destitute, a widow, and an unchaste woman—[these are the ones for whom the offering is intended]. (90)
Whether she be a wanton woman or a lustful one who has united with anyone at all,
she is devoid of kinsmen, devoid of vows, and a companion of beasts.
Always greedy for the pleasure of the tongue, consuming wine, meat, and the like—how much more so?
She is a locus of defects such as menstruation and the like, and is established in the defect of caste-confusion (saṃkara). ||92||
Whether she be a woman who has taken refuge among outcasts and the like and is devoid of proper refinement, or any other woman who possesses the connection with auspicious refinement; ||93||
Having heard this narrative and performed the vow according to one's ability during the intercalary month,
with the desire for the attainment of Hari, one should observe eating once a day, eating only at night, or eating food unasked.
Even by consuming fruits and drinking water through the power of Śrī Hari, she,
being exceedingly purifying, wipes away all sins and even the most heinous crimes.
Whether she be a courtesan, a professional dancer, a singer, a procuress, a pimp, or a beautician, she becomes a purifier of the assembly. (96)
Whosoever she may be in this world, having become one whose form is pure, she becomes like gold, being both the field of Viṣṇu and the object of his compassion. (97)
Divine, pure, free from sin, and endowed with a multitude of merits, she was rendered exceedingly sanctified by the grace of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa-Viṣṇu. 98.
Having purified those who are equal to himself as well as others through his association,
he shall go to that eternal, supreme abode of Viṣṇu.
O Lakṣmī, I, Ramā, am established in every way upon the lap of Nārāyaṇa;
I tell you again the truth: she shall attain the abode of Hari.

Whether he be a eunuch or one like a eunuch, or she be a female eunuch or one resembling a eunuch; or whether she be without menses or devoid of consciousness, she is like a female monkey who has fallen from her vow. 101.
Whoever she may be, by performing a vow during the month at Śrī Puruṣottama, she shall attain the boon of Nārāyaṇa.

Whether he is free from desire himself or has caused others to become free from desire, having attained liberation in every way, he will certainly reach the divine abode of the syllables of Hari; of this there is no doubt.
What more need I say? Even illusion itself would become non-illusory through union with Him; so what need is there to mention the attainment of liberation for women?
Therefore, the vow of the intercalary month must be performed by all means;
for by its power, one may attain everything—enjoyment, liberation, and likewise heaven. (106)
"And I am situated here, O eldest one, to be observed with grace.
Having spoken thus, she bowed down to that Lakṣmī, who increases affection.
Nārāyaṇa also led her to his palaces;
he delighted her with her cherished desires and fulfilled her aspirations.
"In this way, how did Ramā become dear to him? How did she become the beloved of Nārāyaṇa?
This story of her being the daughter of the Ocean of Milk has been told to you. (108)
By merely hearing, reciting, and worshipping this, a person shall obtain the fruit arising from the vow of the intercalary month (adhimāsa). || 109 ||

Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Abode of Vaikuṇṭha for Nārāyaṇa and Adhimāsa, the Proclamation by the Sound of the Dundubhi Drum in the Cosmic Eggs for the Purpose of the Adhimāsa Vow, and how Rāmā, the Daughter of the Ocean of Milk, Attained the Status of Wife to Nārāyaṇa in Vaikuṇṭha by Performing the Vows and Worship on the Evening of the Third and the Morning of the Fourth [Tithi]," in the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, within the first section, the *Kṛtayuga-Santāna*, concerning the majesty of the month of Puruṣottama.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: O Lakṣmī, listen to the auspicious story of Śāradā;
having performed the vow and worship on the fifth day of the intercalary month (adhimāsa). || 1 ||
She attained incomparable sovereignty and eternal maidenhood,
as well as the absence of menstruation and the ability to extend her mouth to any [desired] extent.
Likewise, Śāradā obtained the divine and imperishable status of wife to the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, as well as veneration in the world just like Padmā.
While she possesses the state of being a wife, she maintains her maidenhood; while she possesses the state of a bride, she maintains her virginity.
This coexistence of two contradictory attributes in her arises from pleasing Lord Hari.
O Lakṣmī, listen to this most meritorious story concerning the month of Puruṣottama, which is filled with wonders and endowed with the power of the intercalary month.
Emerging from the body of the primordial Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa who resides in the Brahma-abode,
the beautiful Śāradā, known as Brahmavidyā, manifested herself.
Having come to the world of Vairāja by the command of Nārāyaṇa,
she attained absorption into Vairāja along with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara.
That maiden, born together with him, was Vairājī, the daughter of Śarada;
as a young girl, she dwelt for a long time in her father’s house.
Consisting of the knowledge of Brahman, she eternally contemplates the body—
that purpose for which I, as a deity, have been manifested by Brahmā.
Indeed, in the creation of the Creator, [speech] stands face-to-face with him;
therefore, if I were to go among the creations having become a creation of the Creator, [I would be surpassed]. (10)
"If I remain here as a maiden, being both impure and uninitiated, I shall indeed become untouchable and forever excluded by all. (11)
In that case, death alone shall be my refuge there;
for this body of a young maiden, conceived in the womb, is indeed sinful.
He is indeed suitable for some kind of action, yet not entirely so;
he is born from the male organ and grows within the womb and the belly. (13)
Submerged in the water consisting of urine, he emerged through the opening of the urinary tract;
even in infancy, he was covered by impure filth consisting of excrement and urine, which is untouchable and unclean.
A body devoid of the purificatory rite of the sacred thread is always impure;
it consists of a foul essence made up of impurities such as phlegm, fat, and other morbid humors. || 15 ||
While she remains in the state of a maiden, how could the female body be auspicious? Purity exists only in the act of marriage; otherwise, it never occurs.
Even marriage bestows great suffering, as does subjection to a man, and the performance of impure acts while dependent on the organ of excretion. (17)

Dwelling in the womb within the belly of urine, being smeared with the impurities of birth, the state of *sūtaka* (postnatal impurity), and in every way the suffering of painful labor, the discharge of blood, and the succession of filth; || 18 ||
The production of excrement and urine, the downward flow of vital air, and impurity in every respect exist in the state of wifehood during the act of sexual intercourse. (19)
Therefore, the state of being dependent on another as a wife causes excessive suffering.
What should be done? Where should one go? For a woman has been made dependent on another. (20)
A woman’s body is dependent on others, to be enjoyed by others, and exists for the sake of others;
he who has committed such an evil deed attains the state of womanhood. (21)
Therefore, I must not become dependent on another woman;
for such dependence is like the impurity of a woman during her menses, which causes defilement and brings about evil. (22)
I shall not be subject to that dependence by which even that [desired object] might not be attained;
if what is desired by me does not come to pass, I shall die, without a doubt. (23)
Freedom from impurity, purity, and the absence of menstruation—as well as being devoid of the duties of a wife and remaining in maidenhood, just as I am—[these are the qualities]. (24)
"Since effort must be made so that [the goal] may be eternal, one should act accordingly from now on.
Thinking thus constantly, she sought the means for its accomplishment. (25)
He heard the drum for Viṣṇu’s month-long vow;
indeed, the desires of those observing the vow of the month of Puruṣottama [are fulfilled]. (26)
The illustrious Puruṣottama said that they will become fully perfected:
"People shall worship me once a day or twice a day. (27)
Whether he be a man, a woman, or a eunuch, by even a fraction of my compassion, he shall indeed obtain that which is unobtainable; I shall grant him everything he desires.
Hearing the proclamation, the maiden Śāradā, daughter of Vairāja, was filled with great joy and set her mind upon the performance of the vow. (29)
On that fifth lunar day, having risen very early in the morning upon hearing the sound of the drum,
she bathed and likewise meditated upon the form of Hari.
Having gathered divine articles of worship in his own abode,
he worshipped the Lord Viṣṇu Nārāyaṇa with devotion.
Having invoked Lakṣmī, Nārāyaṇa, Śrī Hari, Puruṣottama, and gold,
and having spread out a seat, one should offer water for the feet, the arghya offering, and water for sipping.
Having offered these and bathed Kṛṣṇa with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta), as well as with water, the essence of nectar, and fragrant liquid substances; ||33||
Then, having massaged his body in many ways, he prepared for adornment;
having put on his ornaments and decorations, as well as his garments.
Having worshipped with musk, sandalwood, unbroken rice grains, and saffron, and having fully honored [the deity] with Tulasī flowers, Mandāra, and Campaka blossoms; ||35||
Having gratified [the deity] with incense, lamps, excellent food offerings, fruits, drinks, and chewables, as well as with betel leaves, he then performed the *ārātrika* ceremony.
Having performed circumambulation and praise, that young maiden prostrated herself like a staff; she asked for forgiveness for her transgression and prayed for her desired object. (37)
O Lord Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, who are worthy of being proclaimed by the celestial drum;
O Śrī Puruṣottama, dweller in Brahmaloka, Goloka, and Vaikuṇṭha! 38.
"You grant whatever is desired to a devoted follower who performs vows;
therefore, grant that to me as well, so that I may choose it. (39)
My maidenhood is eternal; may I never experience menstruation, and likewise, even though it be so, may I never again be subject to impurity. (40)
May husbandhood, which is most auspicious and brings good fortune, be mine forever;
and may I never possess a womb, even while remaining in the state of a wife. ||41||
I beg this which is indeed difficult to obtain, though it is entirely contrary to my body;
for you are a speaker of truth, having undertaken a vow for a single lifetime. (42)
"If you give when the intercalary month has been honored, then give it to me likewise;
otherwise, O Lord, do not sound the drum with falsehood. (43)
I give you a parasol, O Lord; I also give you two fly-whisks.
I present you with sandals and a soft bed. (44)
I offer myself, surrendered for the purpose of massaging Your feet;
O protector of those who have sought refuge, You who fulfill the desires of Your devotees! 45.
Accept this handful of flowers, or take my hand—or do not;
O Lord, grant me that which I have requested, for it is indeed eternal and bestows happiness.
A maiden shall not be a wife, nor shall a wife be a maiden;
for there are many faults in the state of being a wife, lest they should touch me. (47)
O Lord of Compassion, grant that even while I am in my maidenhood, no faults may touch me, if indeed the drum is true to its purpose.
For you, the Lord, there is nothing whatsoever that cannot be done—whether to create, to not create, or to do otherwise; otherwise, your drum would be in vain. (49)
Having thus offered praise and presented an *arghya* offering accompanied by fruits to Viṣṇu,
the maiden Śāradā then caused him to increase [in prosperity] with unbroken grains (*akṣata*).
Having offered the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) consisting of her own self-offering into the heart of the Lord, she dismissed him while meditating upon Nārāyaṇa. ||5 1 ||
Then Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Lakṣmī, the illustrious Puruṣottama, the husband of Ramā, appeared before them, smiling gently.
With his right hand granting fearlessness and touching [her] on the head with his left, he said:
"O Śāradā, what is in your mind? Reveal it. (53)
"I am pleased with your worship, O you who practice the vow of trust!
O fair-browed one, I am forever bound by you with the noose of trust. (54)
I am capable of giving you everything; nevertheless, hear my words:
virginity and the state of being a wife are never seen together in any single place. (55)
Therefore, choose one of these two; I shall grant it to you:
either maidenhood for Kalaka in this world, or [long] life for yourself. (56)
Therefore, choose here the status of being my wife, which bestows good fortune; I shall grant it to you.
Furthermore, O maiden, choose whatever other desire you have, and I shall grant that as well.
"I shall grant you either a kingdom of women, a great kingdom, or a kingdom of illusion.
Do not choose anything contrary [to my intent], O maiden; speak after due reflection, do not delay. (58)
Having heard these words of Hari, Śāradā said to Keśava: "O Lord, fulfiller of the desires of your devotees, I have requested this from you through my loud proclamation. (59)
For the sake of protecting your own truth, do as you wish;
for there should be no insistence toward a devotee, nor is one who possesses devotion prone to insistence.
I have come to you for refuge; O Lord, remove the anxiety of your devotee.
I am yours, I am your devotee; I have fallen at your feet.
"May the sufferings of women not be mine; grant this desire of your devotee.
Thus was he entreated—beheld, touched, bowed to, and honored with reverence.
Honored, fed, and gazed upon there with exceeding love, the Lord, who removes the distress of his devotees, reflected for the sake of his own devotee: ||63||
"How might her heart's desire be granted?
And by what means could even this longing be fulfilled? (64)
I grant her this great accomplishment (siddhi), which takes the form of both the pervaded and the pervader; I indeed bestow this divine accomplishment that manifests in manifold forms.
Having thus resolved, the Blessed One placed the water from the conch into her mouth;
at that moment, she indeed became the embodiment of all sovereign powers.
Then the Blessed One said: "O Śaradā, she who is of the nature of Śaradā is my wife; she possesses a divine form and dwells eternally in Vaikuṇṭha. (67)
Contemplate that you are free from defects such as those of the womb;
the state of being my wife has been granted to you, devoid of any impurity of birth. (68)
May your divine form be forever untouched by excrement, urine, and the like;
now, O beloved, accept this second form of yours, which consists of speech.
I grant you such a form as that of Sarasvatī herself, endowed with the state of maidenhood and exceedingly delicate; thus become.
Go, in that very form, through the medium of the Vedas among living beings;
let your pervasive form exist as the form of speech in every mouth. (71)
O Śāradā, may you always possess maidenhood within your own essential nature;
and in your activity directed toward the interior, may you remain free from menstruation.
May your virtuous nature and maidenhood always remain so for you;
now, indeed, by some pretext in a third form— ||73||
O Sarasvatī, you who take the form of a river flowing within the waters—you, the stainless maiden—may you remain forever present here, O Śāradā. (74)
May there be no fickleness, outwardness, or passion in you; may you always possess purity and be free from the bodily functions of menstruation. ||75||
Your menstruation has dissolved, free from the state of impurity;
O Śāradā, may no defilement whatsoever remain in you. (76)
Possessing all sovereignty, worthy of worship, and pervasive throughout the worlds, may you be so;
O Sarasvatī, may there be no Rajasic sin among people in you.
If, while you exist externally, menstruation and the like were seen to be produced by the world, then that would be a defect of the worlds; but that is not the case for you.
May the sin committed during menstruation belong to those who speak [of it], and may there always be purity for you; may you possess divine riches. (79)
May you possess both maidenhood and the state of being a wife, pure and as you desire;
you are my wife Śāradā, a maiden and a daughter of Brahmā.
"Everything has been given by me to you; tell me, what else do you desire?
Thus addressed, that goddess said: "But as for those who perform my worship... (8.1)
May those who worship Sarasvatī—the goddess Śāradā, the river, and Speech—attain Vaikuṇṭha through the majesty of their Lord. (82)
Having worshipped Nārāyaṇa in due order on the morning of the fifth day of the intercalary month, I have attained my goal with all my desires fulfilled. (83)
Likewise, let those who worship you, as well as those who worship the intercalary month—men and women alike—come to your feet in Vaikuṇṭha. (84)
It is free from birth, death, old age, disease, suffering, and poverty;
it is eternal, and shines as the embodiment of the mass of existence, consciousness, and bliss. 85.
"So be it," he said, making the sound of a celestial drum resound,
[praising] you who make the intercalary month meaningful, grant the fruit of truth, and bestow prosperity.
Adhimāsa also said to her: "O Puruṣottama, I am indeed the deliverer of those men and those women who are devoted to me and to you. (87)
I shall indeed become the remover of faults, the bestower of happiness, and likewise the granter of the heart's desires;
I shall be the purifier and the giver of perfection—of this there is no doubt.
Having made this prayer to Śāradā, for those who hear what is difficult to obtain, or those who read it, that which is difficult to obtain shall become easy to attain. (89)
The inconceivable shall become well-conceived; the unattainable shall reach the state of being attained;
the impossible shall become possible; and the undesirable shall turn into the desired. (90)
Whether on earth, in heaven, or elsewhere, that which is difficult to attain becomes easily obtained;
for Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa is directly accessible—what need is there to speak of anything else? 9.1.
Nārāyaṇa, indeed, by his own grace bestows much upon him;
for he grants immeasurable fruit for that which is performed here during the intercalary month.
Just as the Goddess Śāradā obtained manifold prosperity, so too does the worshipper obtain manifold worldly enjoyment and liberation. ||93||
Recitation, fire-offerings, vows, charity, meditation, rosaries, austerity, and sacred learning—whatever is performed on the fifth lunar day shall become multiplied a thousandfold and more. (94)
Having spoken thus and having led Śāradā away, Hari went to Vaikuṇṭha;
he sent her, who was the very embodiment of Sarasvatī, back as the progeny of Brahmā.
Freedom from impurity, purity, and the absence of menstrual blood—as well as the non-overpowering of her duties as a wife and her maidenhood—were thus preserved. (96)

Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Attainment of the Status of Nārāyaṇa’s Consort, Purity, Freedom from Menstruation, Virginity, Childlessness, and the State of Being Sarasvatī, by means of the Performance of Vows and Worship on the Fifth Day of the Extra Month by Śāradā, Daughter of Vairāja," within the *Puruṣottama-māsa-māhātmya* of the first section, the *Kṛta-yuga-santāna*, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī, to this divine narrative which bestows happiness and prosperity, which fulfills all desires, which is celestial, and which is united with Puruṣottama. 1.
At the beginning of creation, the Pitṛs had daughters endowed with excellent qualities;
three by name were the daughters of Svadhā: Menā, Dhanyā, and Kalāvatī.
The Yoginīs, endowed with all excellent qualities and capable of assuming any form at will,
while dwelling in their father’s house, heard the drum of Hari.
"This month of Puruṣottama has been observed by me under my own name; for those established in its vow, I shall fulfill their desires at one or two times [a day]. (4)
"I shall fulfill it; Nārāyaṇa himself indeed declares this.
