Having heard this proclamation on the morning of the sixth lunar day while in his father's house, [he set out]. || 5 ||
Today, indeed, a vow to Hari must be undertaken by all three of us,
so that Nārāyaṇa himself will grant our own desired object.
The ancestors shall have eternal satisfaction and indeed perpetual contentment;
having sought the cause for this, one should entreat the illustrious Puruṣottama here.
But Viṣṇu must certainly never be requested for the status of a husband,
because he possesses a great many wives.
Rivalry between co-wives is always suffering, for it is indeed a cutter of happiness;
one must never seek [such a relationship] even as a father or as a brother.
At that time, what happiness indeed could there be for us girls who were ignorant?
For our residence until the time of marriage would have to take place in that very house. || 10 ||
There is separation from kinsmen and from one's father; that indeed is only suffering.
Even as a son, Viṣṇu is certainly never to be entreated.
In cases of beating, correction, verbal abuse, and the like, one may be considered at fault;
however, regarding the nature of one's father-in-law and others, such conduct would result in painful transgression of social bounds.
Fault lies in being too near; neglect occurs when one is too far away. Excessive application and transgression of bounds—even the violation of bounds—bring suffering.
"Therefore, Viṣṇu must be entreated; in what form indeed should he be? Let us three make an agreement with one another. (14)
They maintained a moment of silence, meditating upon Nārāyaṇa;
meanwhile, a voice from the sky spoke to them again and again.
O women, choose Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa as your son-in-law;
by giving your daughter to him, there shall be eternal happiness for you all.
A mother is always said by her daughter herself to be her very own daughter;
she considers herself happy through her daughter, and the gift of a daughter should be regarded as equal to the gift of oneself.
A son-in-law should be treated like a son and is considered a supreme recipient of gifts;
he is to be honored and gratified with various forms of service. (18)
Whatever service was performed by the daughter, may its fruit also belong to the mother;
for the daughter, being entreated by her mother, performs that very service.
Just as a portion belongs to the preceptor for the sake of the disciple, so too is a share obtained by the mother;
there shall be certain attainment of worldly happiness, prosperity, fame, and renown. (20)
"Having decided that many kinds of blessings indeed arise in this world through the power of a son-in-law, seek out a son-in-law. (21)
The parents of that daughter who always dwells in the abode of the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha are considered meritorious; they are regarded as having gone to Vaikuṇṭha themselves at some point.
Likewise, there shall be the deliverance of seven hundred and nine families;
and likewise, the mother, maternal grandfathers, and others shall attain liberation.
"The ancestors always reside in the house of their son-in-law;
therefore, you all should constantly entreat Hari, your son-in-law. (24)
"Furthermore, let there be no rivalry among co-wives there;
for this purpose, they should certainly request [this boon] by performing the vow and worship of the intercalary month. (25)
Then a voice from the sky addressed them, saying, "Cease!
Thereupon, they were both startled and exceedingly delighted, having concluded that it was indeed so.
"May Brahmā become your son-in-law; may Hari become your son-in-law;
may Kṛṣṇa become the son-in-law"—having spoken thus, they indeed undertook their vow.
On the morning of the sixth day, after bathing, all three— Menā, Dhanyā, and Kalāvatī— performed worship using three golden images.
Having performed the rites, they worshipped the gods in due order with the ceremonies beginning with invocation (āvāhana),
and they reverently bathed the three deities with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta).
Having massaged him with sandalwood and other unguents, they bathed him with excellent waters; having wiped him dry, they adorned him with garments, ornaments, and fragrant substances.
With saffron, unbroken grains of rice, musk, fragrant substances, and flowers;
likewise with necklaces, garlands, crowns, and so forth, as well as incense, lamps, and the like.
Having worshipped them with various kinds of sweet food offerings, drinks, betel leaves, and powders, as well as with three umbrellas, beds, chowries, sandals, and other such items. || 32 ||
Having honored the three gods with fruits and sugar,
he should present an *arghya* offering consisting of gems and other items, together with plantain fruit.
Having paid their respects, they gave handfuls of flowers;
then, having requested forgiveness, they entreated him, saying, "O Keśava, become our son-in-law."
O Lord, from the resonance of your drum we have held you within our hearts;
in every way, may you grant us happiness here through the mediation of your daughter. (35)
"This sixth day of the month of Puruṣottama has been observed according to the vow; we shall perform the worship again by taking up the practice of eating only at night. (3.6)
Then, at the very break of dawn, they dismissed those gods;
by them, the daytime vow had been performed through a Brahmin with offerings of clarified butter into the fire.
Having performed the oblation at midday,
they honored with devotion the ancestors, the seers, the gods, and the sages established in the austerity of the people.
They gratified the lords with milk-rice, the essence of milk, cakes, leafy vegetables, and various kinds of sweet juices.
The daughters of the Tṛṣṇikā river, being pleased, joined him with auspicious blessings:
"Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa, and Kṛṣṇa shall bestow the fruits of your vow. (40)
"And may they bring about whatever happiness you desire.
Then, in the evening, she again had them display a garland of lamps.
Having caused a pavilion to be constructed, adorned with plantain pillars and archways of leaves, and beautified by the engravings of golden vessels and mirrors; ||42||
Having caused it to be made variegated with garments and lightning, enchanting with the brilliance of its true paintings, and with gold inlaid with excellent jewels in the center; 43.
Having caused a large, beautiful throne to be fashioned, covered with skins of the makha, mallaka, śipra, and other animals, [he seated] Brahmā, Kṛṣṇa, and Nārāyaṇa upon it.
Having installed the three forms with the accompaniment of song and instrumental music, they performed a magnificent worship there using gold, unbroken grains of rice, and saffron.
With excellent substances dyed with turmeric and other items worthy of auspiciousness,
they performed dancing and singing, mingled with the tinkling of small bells.
Having performed the nightly lamp-offering, the incense and lamps, and the water for the guest-offering (arghya),
one should offer fried cakes (pūrikā), milk to drink, and vegetables grown from mustard leaves.
Having fed them and offered them three drinks of water and excellent fruit, they gave them a moment's rest and remained absorbed in meditation. ||48||
There, Brahmā, Kṛṣṇa, and Narāyaṇa arrived in that meditation;
among them, Menā beheld Kaṭyambara, who was exceedingly well-nourished.
White as frost, wearing a tiger skin, and having the moon as his crest-jewel;
with matted locks, he was pervaded on all sides by the intensely radiant splendor of Brahman.
He who is that very same youth of enchanting form, who, though being the attributeless Brahman itself, has attained the state of possessing attributes and assumed a human form—He alone is He. 5.1.
Śaṅkara, who fulfills all states of being, is accessible through internal mental activity that is free from impurity;
manifesting a rain of serenity through his smiling laughter. (52)
Meanwhile, he did not see his own auspicious daughter, who was seated on his lap, nor did he hear her calling out repeatedly, "O Mother! O Mother! (53).
This Lord Śaṅkara, in the form of Brahmā, said to Menakā:
"O Menakā, you shall be born from Himavat, who is a portion of myself."
And there this maiden shall become your wife, Pārvatī;
you will indeed give her to me, and from me you shall obtain happiness.
By means of the vow observed on even a single day of the month of Puruṣottama, your desired fruit, which bestows all happiness, shall come to pass. (56)
Having spoken thus, the god Śaṅkara vanished—that which is the supreme Brahman.
Then, indeed, Hari himself was seen by Dhanyā, bearing his bow.
Abounding in the beauty of matted hair and bark garments, yet possessing the marks of a true kingdom;
a youth, enchanting to the mind, the divine Vāsudeva who transcends all qualities.
The Lord is endowed with a face encompassed by a halo of radiance and accompanied by a smile;
he is both four-armed and two-armed, resplendent upon a lion-throne.
At his side, she saw her own beautiful daughter Sītā, repeatedly calling out to her with sweet words, "O Mother! O Mother! (60)
The blessed Lord Śrī Rāma, being pleased, said to Dhanyakā:
"O Dhanyā, you shall indeed become the future wife of Janaka."
"This daughter of yours, Sītā, shall become Mahālakṣmī;
you will indeed give her to me, and from me you shall obtain happiness. (62)
O affectionate one, by performing this vow for even a single day of the month of Puruṣottama,
you shall obtain a desired fruit that is full of happiness.
Having spoken thus, the Lord Vāsudeva Nārāyaṇa vanished;
then Kṛṣṇa, accompanied by Sudarśana, was seen by Kalāvatī.
Wearing a crown of peacock feathers, with yellow garments and a flute at his lips, he was later that very same one who became the lord of kings as a cowherd boy. (65)
The Blessed One, the king of kings, was exceedingly beautiful in every way; he possessed the lovely luster of a fresh rain-cloud, being youthful and adorned with ornaments.
Seated upon the most excellent divine lion-throne, the King of Kings,
with two arms, displays his great serenity through a gentle smile.
Standing by his side, Kalāvatī beheld that divine and future daughter Rādhā, who was a treasure-house of beauty corresponding to her form.
Placing her own hand upon Kṛṣṇa’s neck, she was overwhelmed with love and repeatedly called out to him in sweet words, "O Mother! O Mother! (6.9).
Śrī Kṛṣṇa, being well-pleased, touched Rādhā Kalāvatī and said: "In your status as a Vaiśya, this daughter shall indeed become Rādhā. (70)
"You shall indeed give her to me in the vicinity of the Bhāṇḍīra fig tree;
she shall always be my chief wife, for she shall be eternal. (71)
Through me, O daughter, you shall obtain all happiness by means of the vow performed on a single day of the month of Puruṣottama. (72)
"And the fruit you desire shall be of the nature of happiness.
Having spoken thus, Kṛṣṇa vanished from that spot.
Then, after a short time, those three emerged from that meditation;
with serene faces and their purpose accomplished, they bowed repeatedly to Nārāyaṇa.
Having offered handfuls of beautiful flowers and performed that rite during the night,
those maidens broke their fast by feeding one another.
They performed the gift of the forms of Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa, and Kṛṣṇa;
then, indeed, in the first age, they were [received] by the ancestors in due order after no long time.
Menā was married by the prescribed rites to Haimaja, Janaka, Gopa, Dhanya, and Kalāvatī,
and they became their daughters.
In sequence, however, Pārvatī, Sītā, and Rādhā are the embodiments of Brahman and the Supreme Self;
at the commencement of creation, they appear in the form of the primary incarnations for the sake of the presiding authority.
And they were offered to Śiva in the form of Rāma and to Kṛṣṇa;
indeed, having approached those sons-in-law who were incarnations of the Supreme Brahman.
Menā, Dhanyā, and Kalāvatī obtained all their desires;
thus, O Lakṣmī, is the vow of fasting at night and worship performed during the intercalary month.

On the sixth lunar day, by performing [this rite] during the three periods of time before the Supreme Ancient Person (Purāṇapuruṣottama), the fruit of the vow is obtained; sons-in-law are obtained, and Hari himself is attained. 8.1.
These daughters were given by Śambhu, Rāma, and Kṛṣṇa to the eternal [lords];
indeed, they take delight on Kailāsa, in Vaikuṇṭha, and in Goloka.
Therefore, his parents also become eternally liberated,
and they attain his supreme happiness as well as fame according to their desire.
And what more shall I tell you, O Lakṣmī, regarding this world and the next:
a mother truly desires to make her own daughter happy. (84)
Then she should perform the vow pertaining to the intercalary month, as well as the vow and worship on the sixth lunar day, just as it was performed by Menā and the others. (85)
Thereafter, she will indeed obtain Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa as her son-in-law;
thus, they shall all effortlessly attain worldly enjoyment, liberation, and everything else. ||86||
If Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa is the worthy recipient for the gift of a daughter, then therein the four aims of human life reach their highest perfection. (87)
No worldly or other-worldly duty remains to be performed where Hari, the absorber of all, rejoices together with his daughter. (88)
The Lord is pleased with one who has heard [the teachings]; when He is thus pleased, what indeed is difficult to obtain or unattainable in the presence of Kṛṣṇa? (89)
Thus, O Lakṣmī, has that compassion of Nārāyaṇa been described to you;
in the intercalary month, the Unborn One fulfills the mental aspirations of those who observe vows.
If one should desire that a son-in-law be equal to Kṛṣṇa in the power of his virtues, in beauty, in learning, and so forth, then it shall be so. (91)
If he desires, "May one who is world-renowned and an upholder of royal power become my son-in-law," then indeed such [a son] shall be born. ||92||
If a devotee of the Lord should desire, "May my son-in-law be prosperous with wealth and grain and may he live long," so shall it be. (93)
If one desires that my son-in-law should possess the virtues of a Brahmin, or else be endowed with the dharma of a Kṣatriya, it shall be so for the performer of the vow as well. (94)
If one desires that the son-in-law born in the household be a giver of happiness,
and that he possess sons, grandsons, and so forth, it shall be so for the woman who performs the vow.
However, by the grace of Lord Hari, the mother-in-law obtains exactly such a son-in-law as she desires. 96.

Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-eighth chapter, titled "The Attainment of the Fruit Consisting of the Establishment of Relationships with Śaṅkara, Rāma, and Kṛṣṇa as Sons-in-Law," following the sequential acquisition of daughters named Pārvatī, Sītā, and Rādhā by Menā, Dhanyā, and Kalāvatī—the mental daughters of the Pitṛs—through the hearing of the drum of the intercalary month and the performance of the Tri-kāla-vrata on the sixth lunar day, within the *Māhātmya* of the Month of Puruṣottama in the first section, the *Kṛta-yuga-santāna*, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī, to the vow performed by the two daughters of Viśvakarman, who were residing in Satyaloka, due to the sound of the Dundubhi drum. || 1 ||
Of the truthful [beings], of the heavenly worlds such as Svarga, of kings, of the inhabitants of Pātāla, of cities, of palaces, of assemblies, and of those performing sacrificial rites; || 2 ||
The builder of the pavilions was indeed an incarnation of Nārāyaṇa;
his daughter named Siddhi was the elder, and Buddhi was the younger.

O you who possess accomplishment and wisdom, who are beautiful in form and virtuous in conduct, and who worship the gods—having always remembered Nārāyaṇa and bathed in the morning thereafter. || 4 ||
Having bowed at the feet of his parents during the auspicious hour known as Brāhma,
he then lit lamps in his own home and in the temple of the gods.
Having offered fragrant incense, they performed hymns of praise;
and having bowed to the God, they presented flowers, water, sugar, and food.
Then, having entrusted the household duties to one another,
both of them quickly fetch water from the middle of that lake.
Having cleansed the house, she kindles the fire and places a water vessel on the hearth for the purpose of heating it.
Having established the ancestors, the devoted one bathes them;
meanwhile, having taken the bed, bedding, and other items from the house, he prepares the sleeping place.
Then, having secured the couches, swept them, and moved them to a clean place,
he prepares the cleansing of the night-vessels.
Meanwhile, Buddhi washed the damp garments of her parents who had bathed,
hung them on a rope, and went to a garden adjacent to the house.
She quickly brought flowers for the purpose of worshipping the gods and other rites,
just as her mother and father were arriving at the house of Hari.
Having first spread out a seat, he offers water for the sake of the twilight prayers and other rites,
as well as garlands of *tulasī* leaves, lotuses, *kunda*, and *campaka* flowers.
With supreme devotion, he offers for the sake of worshipping the gods and his parents sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, saffron, the five nectars, and water. (14)
Vessels worthy of worship, vessels filled with ghee, sugar, grapes, pomegranate seeds, and various kinds of fruits. || 15 ||
She also brings cardamom, cloves, betel,
and food offerings for her mother who is engaged in worship, and likewise for her father who is engaged in worship.
Having performed ten circumambulations and having offered ten prostrations,
he indeed took up the water that had been used for washing the feet of his mother and father.
While he stands at the side for the sake of service and offers his vision,
Siddhi likewise arrives there in that very same manner.
Having performed circumambulations, prostrations, and other rites born of devotion,
and having drunk the water [offered] out of grace, he returns once more to the vicinity of the hearth in his home.
Then, having thoroughly cleansed the entire collection of utensils in the kitchen for the purpose of cooking and having set them aside, he summoned that intelligent woman. (20)
She prepares various kinds of foods to be chewed, eaten, and drunk;
moreover, she quickly brings about the attainment of milk for her parents. (21)

Then, having scrubbed all the vessels used for worship with clay and purified them, one should perform whatever rites are prescribed for the morning; having done all that, both [the husband and wife] should then [proceed].
Then he practices his studies until the conclusion of the Vaiśvadeva rite;
having performed those two [rites] and fed [the guests], he performs the midday ritual again.
Having set aside portions for guests, cows, and living beings, and having given food to those who depend on them,
they then respectfully partook of their own excellent meal.
In the afternoon, he should perform the cleaning of the kitchen, the purification of the alms-bowl, sweeping, fetching water, and the preparation of food and other provisions. (25)
Having made the body their resting place, they take a moment's rest;
then, having performed the viewing [of the deity] and other rites, solely through the discourse on the sacred fords (tīrtha). || 26 ||
In the evening, having performed the worship of Kṛṣṇa with the sixteen types of offerings, and having fed him with cooked food and desired delicacies with great devotion; || 27 ||
Then, having spread out the bed and other furnishings for both his parents,
he performed the massaging of their feet as well as general service for them.
Whatever daily service to the cows and glorification of the Lord one performs, having made whatever is deficient therein complete and exhaustive, both [these acts] are fulfilled. (29)
Having performed some study, they should take a little sleep;
then, rising at the hour sacred to Brahmā, they should reflect upon the knowledge they have practiced.
Furthermore, both maidens performed their daily duties;
thus, through such service and great devotion, their parents were filled with joy.
They joined them with auspicious blessings, saying, "May you both indeed be happy;
for by virtue of your love for the Lord, may Nārāyaṇa and Lord Hari [protect you]. (3.2)
"In time, that most auspicious one worthy of service shall be attained by you both.
Thus they were the recipients of blessings, as Hari was constantly and repeatedly held within their hearts. (33)
While they were thus desiring Śrī Hari, Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Lord,
I heard the sound of a drum from them in Satyaloka during that vow.
On the seventh day of the intercalary month, at dawn, the awakener of vows indeed awakens the worlds to the observances of the intercalary month.
Whoever among the people within the universe— whether men, women, or others— shall perform [this] according to their ability, I shall be the bestower of their desires.
For I am Śrī Puruṣottama, the giver of what cannot otherwise be obtained;
whether it be monthly, fortnightly, weekly, or even daily.
Whether it be the fast of the night, the forenoon, the afternoon, or the midday;
or fasting on fruits, drinking milk, or subsisting only on water—(38)
Eating roots, eating nivāra rice and so forth, eating only at night, eating during the day, eating only one meal a day, eating sesame seeds, or eating food that has not been asked for; || 39 ||
Having performed [this] according to one's ability, one should worship the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama) with flowers,
or with water, or even with fruits, roots, or saffron.
Having worshipped Puruṣottama with unbroken grains and sandalwood paste, [he should offer] a garment, or well-matured sweet milk, or honey. (41)
With sugar, drinks of water, betel-leaf, clothing and the like, or even with a single leaf, worship me, Puruṣottama, with excessive devotion and love. (42)
Being satisfied with this, may you acquire from me that which is difficult to obtain even during an intercalary month;
now, out of compassion, I shall grant it even when the practice performed is slight. (43)
Whatever may be difficult to accomplish in other months, I shall indeed grant that very thing today multiplied ten millionfold, even if it be but a small amount. (44)
Therefore, I shall certainly not give it away;
so, O people, take even the fruit of the betel nut, which is superior to the station of Brahmā.
By the vow of drinking only water, one attains the state of reclining upon the Ocean of Milk;
by the vow of eating but once a day, one gains the right to Goloka.
By the mere vow of fasting at night, one attains equality with Nārāyaṇa;
even by the offering of leaves and flowers, one possesses the status of Mahendra.
Whether it be a man or a woman, a boy or a girl, by offering even a single lamp, one attains a body like that of the sun, the moon, and so forth. (48)
If she desires even my splendor, I shall grant her both me, the Supreme Person, as her husband, and Lakṣmī as her wife; or if she desires me as her son, I shall grant her both Lakṣmī and myself.
May they accept these boons from us and perform the accumulation [of merit], which arises through the power of virtue and is obtainable by the great rain of supreme compassion. (50)
"Truly, truly, the drum proclaims nothing but the truth:
'Having observed the vow of the intercalary month, let the subjects receive whatever they desire! (51)
Having heard this, both maidens on the morning of the seventh day indeed bowed down before my drum and offered salutations with the water of their folded palms.
Having worshipped with beautiful flowers, they both became filled with joy;
then once again, they heard the auspicious words of compassion from Dundubhi.
"If these two maidens desire me, the Supreme Person, as their husband, then even by the vow of eating but one meal a day, I shall become the husband of them both. (54)
Having performed the midday worship with whatever offerings are available,
and having fed me sweet food, you two shall attain Puruṣottama.
Thinking that he was speaking thus for their own welfare, Siddhi and Buddhi recognized that their own good fortune had arrived. ||56||
Having worshipped his own parents and fed them according to the prescribed rite, and having completed the household duties with flowers, sandalwood, and water; ||57||
Having worshipped the golden image with unbroken grains, sweet foods, incense, lamps, and excellent offerings— whatever things were available in his own home— he honored it.
O auspicious lady, desiring to obtain a husband, they both performed the lustration ceremony (nīrājana) for the god Hari Nārāyaṇa,
who grants the auspicious fruit of one's desires.
Having given [these], they both prayed, "May you be our husband.
Having spoken thus, they respectfully offered handfuls of unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*).
At that moment, the illustrious Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa himself appeared,
youthful and gazing with the arrow of his sidelong glance.
Hari himself grasped both by their forearms with his own hands;
placing his hands upon their heads, he drew both of them toward his chest.
Having addressed her as "O beloved" and gazed upon her again and again, I have truly met her; O beloved, when we have met according to the prescribed rite, I have truly come into being.
Having spoken thus, Kṛṣṇa vanished; for those two always beheld that Hari, the enchanting one, both while awake and likewise in their dreams.
In one place they beheld Kṛṣṇa seated on the lap of Pārvatī with a single trunk, and in another, he was without a trunk yet holding a flute, situated in Goloka.
Then, in another moment, they both beheld that Gaṇeśa, the son of Śaṅkara, who was worthy of being chosen as a bridegroom, possessing a trunk and endowed with a beautiful form.
Seeing him white-complexioned, with beautiful eyes and a handsome brow, endowed with youth, and yet essentially dark (Kṛṣṇa), they fainted again and again.
And once in a dream, while you two girls were making many sweetmeats,
Gaṇeśa was seen by you there, having arrived and seated upon a wooden plank.
While he sat there longing for sweetmeats, others also gave them to him at that time;
standing on both sides, the two of them repeatedly gave him the sweetmeats.
Gaṇeśa, having repeatedly received the fine *sulaḍḍuka* sweets offered by his short trunk which was moved to both sides, placed them into his own mouth. (70)
He placed extremely sweet foods [before them], and with affection, he quickly ate;
then, placing his hands upon the backs of the two girls, he praised them.
Giving a single *laḍḍuka* to each of them, he feeds them both, laughing, making them laugh, delighting, and gladdening them with joy. (72)
Having thus revealed himself, he vanished;
yet the two maidens remained awake and remembered him again and again. (73)
Thus, when Gaṇapati had been born in the heart and the time had arrived,
Viśvakarman learned of his previous history.
Having invoked Gaṇeśa according to the rite prescribed for the auspicious moment, and having offered the two daughters to Gaṇeśa, they summoned Siddhi and Buddhi. (75)
Listen now to the great event that occurred after the marriage:
at that time, two forms were manifested by Gaṇeśa within the house. (76)
One form was that of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and the second was the self of Gaṇeśa;
two most beautiful forms were also created for the two maidens.
Then Śrī Kṛṣṇa, taking those two forms equal to Rādhā upon Garuḍa, went to his own eternal abode, Goloka. (78)
There he indeed delights through his accomplishment and his divine form of intellect;
thus, by those two, the fruit consisting of liberation has been granted for the vow.
Then, by means of another form known as Gaṇeśa, you placed those two upon your own lap and gazed at them repeatedly with love. ||80||
When her cheeks have been kissed and she has been gratified, having gone within the house, the fruit of fresh youthfulness has indeed been attained through sexual union. (81)
Thus, O Lakṣmī, those two obtained the fruit consisting of Kṛṣṇa and Dhava;
each pair attained a divine form that became renowned even in the world. (82)

Or [he may attain it] by honoring one who has attained a state of worshipfulness and stability during an intercalary month, through the vow of eating but once a day, or by worshipping with whatever materials are available. ||82||
In this manner, whatever maiden performs the worship of Puruṣottama on the seventh lunar day, observing a single meal out of her desire for the sake of Kṛṣṇa, the True Lord; ||84||
She will certainly obtain her own divine husband, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, who has manifested as a human being somewhere or other. 85.
Having enjoyed worldly pleasures and experienced many eternal realms, he will thereafter certainly attain Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s Goloka or Vaikuṇṭha. (86)
Therefore, the vow arising from the intercalary month should be performed;
through this, liberation will be attained without effort, and rebirth shall no longer remain.

Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-ninth chapter, titled "The Description of Viśvakarman’s Attainment of the Two Forms through the Vision of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and His Residence in Goloka, along with his Marriage to Gaṇapati-incarnate Kṛṣṇa, following the Hearing of the Drum that Proclaims the Vow of the Extra Month and the Blessings Received through Service to His Parents, by Means of the Ekabhukta Vow on the Seventh Day," in the section on the Greatness of the Month of Puruṣottama within the First Book, the Continuation of the Kṛtayuga, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, Lakṣmī, to what occurred in the past at the beginning of the Yugas, at the start of creation;
six offspring were born to Brahmā from his mind during the night.
From the forehead of this [Brahmā], who was distressed by his ascetic penance, a great Rudra emerged;
and by the command of Brahmā, he filled the world with Rudras.
Seeing those terrifying, cruel beings who were causing the destruction of the world,
Brahmā indeed found no satisfaction and issued his command once again.
Then, for the sake of withdrawing the Rudras, they were indeed withdrawn by their son Rudra;
consequently, the entire world became empty.
Beholding his own home, Satyaloka, to be empty, the Creator of the universe fell into a state of profound indifference, as if he were nothing more than a mere child.
In that house where there is indeed no child, nor the crying of children,
nor their play, nor quarreling, nor the prattle of children is heard.
That house of Kālarātri was indeed like the abode of a king of jackals;
without her son and without her daughter, heaven itself became like hell.
The palaces of the lowly lords resound like battlefields;
the mansion, surrounded solely by a circle of old men, resembles a withered tree. (8)
A family without offspring is like the peak of a withered mountain;
a father without offspring is like a parched ground of fire-mouths.
Without the sound of the sweet chatter of children, the palace becomes as silent as the great dissolution; even the flavors become tasteless without a child. (10)
Even foods that are only slightly warm become unsatisfying;
without him, festivals never again arise as ever-new celebrations. (11)
Without which even those who exert themselves to achieve greatness perish;
their moon-like faces wither like lumps of mud in the summer heat.
In the heat of summer, the minds become as parched as *barburaka* wood, and even drinks become as bitter as the juice of the *nimba* tree. (13)
Children who bring happiness are born to those endowed with merit;
those who bring suffering are born to the poor who have performed evil deeds. (14)
In this matter, the sole cause is the debt incurred from previous births;
furthermore, one must perform new austerity that bestows one's own offspring.
Having thus resolved and restrained the entire circle of his senses, Brahmā practiced austerity for the duration of a single ghaṭikā, remaining established in meditative absorption.
Desiring offspring, he indeed meditated upon them in his heart;
at that moment, Dundubhi, Ghaṇṭa, and Kambu were born from his mind.
There were three sons and three daughters; likewise, there was Ghaṇṭā, Nīrājanā, and Jhallarī—these were the Mānasīs—and thereafter, another triad was born.
The bell-metal vessel, the five vessels, and the incense-holder—these were the mental [offspring];
the three daughters, the three sons, and the three hermaphrodites of Prajāpati.
Nine offspring were born from his mental resolves;
for indeed, whatever kind of intention one has at the time of the ritual consecration or the mental resolve, such it shall be.
O Lotus-born one, such offspring is born; likewise, among those born there, six indeed are talkative and prone to uttering insults. (21)
Kamburghaṇṭa, Dundubhi, Ghaṇṭā, Jhallarī,
and Kāṃsya, as soon as they were born, raised a tumultuous clamor within the house.
Because he had attained equanimity, even the voidness of fate was transcended;
his home became filled with festive joy along with his playing children.
Brahmā was pleased by that; he became attached to fondling and protecting [him], and he regarded the home with its children as an abode of auspiciousness.

The lustration rite (nīrājanā), the five vessels, and the incense-bearer, remaining in a state of silence—these six indeed delight them at that moment through dancing and other such performances. ||25||
Meeting together every morning and evening, those nine indeed perform kīrtana and worship for the sake of their respective duties.
They indeed became devoted to Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa alone;
Brahmā truly rejoiced exceedingly at the acquisition of such offspring.
When time had passed in this manner, on the morning of the eighth day of the intercalary month,
a great drum was heard by them on the bank of the Viṣṇupadī.
While those performing their morning ablutions heard that auspicious [account] there, let all who possess consciousness listen, as well as even the immobile and insentient beings. (29)
Whether they be embodied or formless, boys or girls, and even infants, let them hear this which yields the highest fruit with very little effort. (30)
I am a proponent of Puruṣottama, and I speak according to the truth:
this month is Puruṣottama, and he himself is indeed Puruṣottama.
Transcending all months, he reaches Śrī Puruṣottama;
for Puruṣottama is honored by one who is devoted through mind, action, and speech. (35)
By which [means] he may be honored by Śrī Puruṣottama, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow;
today silence must be observed and food taken only once a day.
Worship should be performed in the morning, at midday, and likewise at night;
the divine form of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa should be meditated upon first.
Having bathed in the morning and bowed to Hari, one should bring the materials for worship;

Then they fashioned an image of Lakṣmī and both father and son worshipped it according to the rules; they observed the vow of eating only at night (nakta-vrata) in accordance with the prescribed rites.
While he was praying at night to Hari, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa,
accompanied by Lakṣmī, He appeared before him.
Beholding that Supreme Person, whose face was completely encircled by a halo of splendor, who was attended by Lakṣmī, and who was smiling very gently; ||78||
O Lord of Compassion, Agni and Suvarṇa pray to you: deliver me, who am possessed of a hot nature and am a consumer! 79.
"O Lord, there is no such thing anywhere; give me food in that manner.
There is indeed no price for a foolish son, nor for gold. (80)
No honor is seen for the sacrificial grass (prastara); therefore, establish its fame.
O Blessed One, O All-pervading Lord, grant it your service forever. 8.111
"I have fallen for refuge at your feet; lift me up along with my sons.
Thus entreated, Hari-Kṛṣṇa, who is Nārāyaṇa, spoke to the fire.
"Abandon your grief, O Kṛśānu; I am indeed pleased by your vow. Born from my mouth, may you always remain my mouth. (8.3)

"I grant you this boon, my son: those who, at the beginning of a sacrifice and other rites, shall offer oblations into the fire situated within the sacrificial pit, they shall place the food for the meal upon you. (84)
Those people who entrust the offering of the Agnihotra to you—through you, all of that must be consumed by me as being identical with me, and not otherwise. (85)
"Those people who give me food and other provisions without fire, I shall not accept from them at all, because of my favor toward you. (86)
"From this day forward, I shall become renowned in the world as 'The Blessed One whose mouth is fire'; therefore, people will provide food and other necessities for my sake. (87)
They shall cast all of that upon you; I will devour it from your mouth.
You must dwell especially within śamī trees, remaining invisible in form. (88)
And likewise, may your presence be in all things, such as diamonds and the like;
so that there may be no burning of objects, yet you remain their dwelling place. (89)
May you, O Fire, be everywhere; may you be happy among all people.
May there be honor for you in every way, and may there be respectful treatment for you in every way. (90)
At the time of the destruction of the wish-fulfilling trees, for the purpose of cooking on hearths and the like, let there be the kindling of you alone in every single household in every way. 9.1.
But when the wish-fulfilling gem and such have perished, and there is a lamp in every house, you will receive honor in every way; therefore, maintain your fortitude for that long. (92)
And with my second divine form as an attendant, O Agni, perform service to me eternally in my abode; you are liberated by me, O sinless one. (93)
When the first cycle of the eon has passed, however, no task whatsoever will indeed be possible for anyone in the absence of fire. (94)
Your value, honor, hospitality, respect, and worship shall all reach their highest pinnacle; of this there is no doubt. ||95||
Moreover, this son of yours, Suvarṇa, is indeed very dear to me;
from this day forward, he must be borne upon my own head by me. (96)
"Let this crown indeed be yours; let my two earrings be yours as well.
Let the chains, bracelets, and rings be the very form of my ornaments. (97)
"Let the waist-bands, food-vessels, and all other articles be made of gold;
your son has been placed by me upon my head as a crown. (98)
Then, as time passes, he will receive honor everywhere;
he will be highly valued, well-concealed, and protected. ||99||
When the wish-fulfilling trees and other such things perish, he shall become a Kalpadru tree;
furthermore, I indeed grant him a divine form of pure gold.
In his fundamental form, he shall always serve me in my abode;
my attendant named Hāṭaka shall dwell in my imperishable realm.
Then, at another time, when a specific task was required,
he, who is of the nature of fire, consisting of great splendor, became known by the name Hāṭakeśvara.
In the netherworld and upon the earth, Mahādeva shall exist;
as my incarnation, he will receive worship everywhere through my power.
Maheśvara will be the bestower of liberation upon his devotees, and in the creation of the entire universe, he will attain renown just like you. || 104 ||
"Just as I, O Blessed One, am all-pervading, so shall the fire pervade the gold;
it shall attain pervasiveness within my creation and shall receive due honor."
"Protection and stability shall also be ensured for all; this will certainly come to pass.
Having spoken thus, Hari himself assumed divine forms for the two of them.
And others led her to their own abodes when she was perfumed with the forms of various objects;
and having fully understood this form and the entire account, the gods and others [acted accordingly].
By means of fire they consume and are satisfied by that food;
and at various places they wear ornaments of gold. (108)
In this way, having performed the worship on the ninth day and the vow of Vahni and likewise Svarṇa, the two became liberated, highly praised, and of great value.
Indeed, wherever those two may go, they always attain purity;
likewise, they always attain growth as well as eternal happiness. (110)
Those people, whether men or women, who shall read the narration of the vow on the ninth day, or who shall hear it, will attain both worldly enjoyment and liberation.

Thus, in the first section, the *Kṛtayuga-santāna*, within the *Puruṣottama-māsa-māhātmya* of the *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*: when the people residing on the *Kalpa-vṛkṣa* showed disregard for Vahni, the son of Virāṭ, and his son Suvarṇa—who were possessed of defects such as combustibility and inertness—the latter, intent on death on Mount Meru, heard the sound of the drum; by performing the worship and vow of the ninth day of the intercalary month (*adhimāsa*), he attained universal respect at sacrifices and other rites, the state of being in the presence of the Lord, and the form of an ornament for the Lord.
The three hundred and first chapter, titled "The Description of Attaining the Abode and Becoming a Divine Retinue," etc.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Furthermore, O Lakṣmī, I shall tell you a story that delights the gods;
in the intercalary month (adhimāsa), there is no end to the grace of Hari.
On the night of the ninth day, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow questioned Dundubhi:
"Is it being proclaimed everywhere, or only in certain places? (2)
The drum spoke: "O Lord, facing whichever direction it may be, I shall proclaim [your name] everywhere from morning until evening. (3)
Indeed, many embodied beings here perform vows;
yet they receive only a small measure of compassion, worldly enjoyment, and liberation from what was done.
At that moment, the Earth herself arrived there to offer her earnest petition:
"O Blessed One, Lord of the gods of gods, Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, Mādhava! (5)
"By you, through your great compassion, the liberation of countless living beings is now being effected during this intercalary month; therefore, I am exceedingly happy."
I too must perform the vow of the God of gods with great devotion:
the liberation of those observing vows during the month of Puruṣottama.
Union with heaven, yoga, wealth, grain, and other riches, as well as sons, grandsons, fame, and whatever else may be desired— may all that be yours.
"Out of compassion, let everything be given; it has attained a state equal to Vaikuṇṭha.
Indeed, I am one of blessed fortune, since your drum is with me. (9)
With a free voice, he proclaims his magnanimity to all:
"And that compassion which was shown by you, the merciful one, during the intercalary month. (10)
That very same compassion has arisen in me toward those living beings who possess merit;
they shall always be free from sin and pure in my presence.
O Blessed One, burdened by the weight of evil, I shall never again be oppressed;
for, through the abundance of those devoted to you, I shall become possessed of merit. (12)
Even during the intercalary month of two and a half years, those people who shall observe your one-day vow— all of them will have their sins shaken off.
"And they shall always be capable of uplifting others for my sake;
thus I am greatly pleased by the attainment of this future well-being. (14)
O Lord, I am oppressed by the burden of the wicked;
for in the future, at that time, unrighteous people will prevail. (15)
O Lord, those Brahmins who are devoid of the Vedas, deprived of the Mother of the Vedas, and lacking in Vedic rites, are merely a burden upon me. (16)
Those who are devoid of purity and contentment, likewise bereft of austerities,
and lacking in self-study and devotion to the Lord, are merely a burden upon me.
Those devoid of the vow of non-violence, backbiters, those bereft of truthfulness, those lacking the vow of non-stealing, and likewise those addicted to sexual intercourse; || 18 ||
Shrouded by craving, they seize the property of others; they are burdensome to me, devoid of compassion, lacking in virtue, and intent on disrespecting others. (1.9)
Those who speak false slanders, those who revile and hate, and those who cannot endure excellence and loftiness—they are always a burden to me. (20)
Those Brahmins who cause suffering to others and themselves, who attribute faults to virtues, and who are intent solely on their own self-interest, remain as a burden upon me.

Deprived of ritual bathing and the twilight prayers, cheated of the worship of the gods and other rites, lacking steadfastness in the Self and other virtues, they are dull-witted and a mere burden upon me. (22)
Those Brahmins who create obstacles to sacrifices, who destroy the Vaiśvadeva offerings, and who are devoid of the cultivation of purificatory rites, are a burden upon me. (23)

Those who do not observe the rules for birth and death impurity, those who propound causality [in a nihilistic sense], the atheists, and Brahmins devoid of the meditation on Brahman are a burden upon me. (24)
Those Brahmins who are devoid of a spirit of devotion, empty of spiritual knowledge, and lacking in the offering of libations to their ancestors, are merely a burden upon me. (25)
Those Brahmins who are devoid of helping others, who are bereft of the merit of giving, and who practice unrighteousness through their tongues and genitals, are merely a burden upon me.
Brahmins who inflict suffering upon others, who obstruct the affairs of others, and who commit offenses against others, are a burden to me. (27)
Those who sow seeds in unsuitable ground, farmers who cultivate barren fields, and Brahmins who strike at dharma through deceit—these are a burden upon me. (28)
Violent and cruel enjoyers of pleasures, they are the cause of others' lamentation;
moving with deceit, hidden by their venom, they are deceivers whose words are as sweet as honey. (29)
Those who sprinkle poison through mere rumors, those who are a burden to me at all times, those who are betrayers of trust, the ungrateful, and those who kill children; ||30||
Those who kill the ignorant, those who kill those who have sought refuge, those who kill their families, and those who kill their mothers, fathers, or wives; ||31||
O Lord, those who destroy the Dharma and destroy liberation are a burden upon me;
they are eaters of forbidden food, those who cause the loss of caste and the mixing of lineages.

Those who cause the destruction of wives and children, those who seize one's livelihood, wealth, or life, those who are wicked in their conduct as assassins, as well as arsonists and poisoners—[these are the ones who must be avoided]. (33)
Those who perform acts of killing, expulsion, and sorcery, who cause abortions and the like, who strike out of place, and who are full of cruel deeds—such burdens have been placed upon me. (34)
Those who are not Brahmins yet claim the status of Brahmins, who are devoid of their own duties and who always destroy the happiness of others, are a constant burden upon me. (35)
Lacking enterprise, ever lazy, subsisting on the fortune of others,
and arrogant even in matters where they have no authority, they are always a burden upon me.
Those who follow wrong paths, who by their own power cause affliction to the weak, and who inflict punishment upon those who deserve no punishment, are always a burden to me. (37)
Those who do not protect those who ought to be protected, nor honor those who are worthy of honor, nor show respect to those who deserve respect—they are a burden upon me. (38)
Those who cause suffering to their livestock, those who fail to protect their dependents, and those who inflict pain upon their servants are always a burden to me. (39)
Teachers who deceive their disciples, and disciples who turn away;
the wealthy who deceive their servants, and laborers who ruin the wealthy. ||40||
Both disciples and teachers have abandoned their respective duties;
they deceive one another, and all of them are a burden upon me. (41)
Servants who kill their masters, masters who torment their servants, and slaves who have abandoned their state of servitude—all such burdensome beings are upon me. (42)
Where there is no king as protector and the subjects do not perform meritorious deeds, those who are deceitful among the subjects, O Queen, all become a burden upon me.
Furthermore, where the Kṣatriya is no protector, the Vaiśya is no giver, and the Śūdra is no servant; [there too, they are a burden].
O Lord, all those who abandon their respective duties are a burden to me.
A daughter or even a daughter-in-law who does not obey her mother’s command is not such [a daughter or daughter-in-law];
and a mother-in-law who does not act for one's welfare is not such [a mother-in-law]. (45)
Where there is no unity between the couple and constant quarreling between the two, the wife feels aversion toward serving her husband, and the husband causes suffering to his wife. (46)
Sons who do not follow their father’s instructions, and a father who reviles his sons—devoid of the relationship between master and servant, they are all a burden upon me. (47)
A religious student who does not abide in the practice of celibacy due to passion, yet proceeds by prioritizing the duties of renunciation while remaining a householder; ||48||
Even a forest-dweller who possesses craving, and one who has renounced yet lacks true relinquishment—those who grasp at other doctrines are all merely burdensome forms. (49)
They cause the mixing of curd, milk, ghee, oil, and meat;
they cause the mixing of food, leaves, grains, vegetables, and flowers. ||50||

Those physicians who cause confusion regarding food, drink, proper administration, and what is fit for consumption, and who bring about the destruction of life—all of them are embodiments of a burden. (51)
Mortals who consume liquor and meat, who subsist on the food of others,
and who cause confusion regarding clothing, ornaments, and other such things, are indeed a burden.

Those who deal in counterfeit goods, those with false measures, those who use deceptive scales and weights, those who employ fraudulent counting, and even those astrologers who are merely a burden—[all these shall be punished]. (53)
Wicked men who deceive through their business dealings, such as taking what is due and giving what is not;
and mortals who forcibly plunder—these are always a burden upon me. (54)
Those on earth who are incompetent, addicted to vices, or like the planet Saturn;
those who are like the eclipse of Rāhu, or likewise like the bite of a serpent; ||55||
Those who are like flat-nosed lepers, or who have the form of jujube thorns;
those who are like fish or hawks, and those whose actions are like those of cranes or cats.
Externally white, red within the heart, and black like collyrium within the self—
whether mortals, gods, or dānavas, whether inhabitants of heaven or dwellers of the netherworld.
All of them are indeed burdensome and are surely performers of evil deeds;
they would afflict me at the time when they lack any sense of magnanimity. (58)

Those for whom there is no vow of the intercalary month, nor for whom there is the Supreme Person, and who possess neither devotion nor a sense of faith—they would be a mere burden upon this earth. (5.9)
Therefore, O Hari Kṛṣṇa, from time to time, I pray to the Supreme Lord for the sake of removing the burden of such beings who are to come into existence. ||60||
"O Keśava, what should I do for the destruction of their burden? Out of a desire for my own welfare, tell me that which is most beneficial for the future. (61)
While the Earth was thus entreating him, Dundubhi said to the Medinī:
"O Pṛthvī, have you not heard what I have proclaimed, which grants all desires? (62)
In the intercalary month, a vow should be performed; it shall indeed become eternal merit.
And the Blessed One, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), will grant you protection.
Now the glorious Lord Hari Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Supreme Master, remains pleased and ready to bestow fruits; therefore, perform the vow of the tenth day.
"At the conclusion of your vow, the Blessed Kṛṣṇa himself will grant you his vision;
and that descendant of Bharata will protect you at all times. (65)
"Go now, O Goddess of gods, and establish yourself in Satyaloka;
there, observe the vow of the tenth day and pass the intercalary month."
If that god does not grant you his vision at the conclusion of your vow,
then you must come here tomorrow evening indeed for the sake of requesting it.
Having been addressed thus by Dundubhi himself, she bowed to the Lord, the Master, and likewise paid homage to Dundubhi, before departing for Satyaloka. ||68||
In his own abode, on the earth, he performed the vow of the tenth day;
having bathed in the morning and meditated upon Hari, he fashioned a golden image.
Having worshipped Hari with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) and bathed him with auspicious waters, one should smear him with fragrant sandalwood and other substances with great devotion. ||70||
With garments, gold, ornaments, saffron, unbroken grains, and excellent leaves;
with tulasī blossoms, lotuses, incense, and lamps. ||71||
Having performed worship with excellent offerings, he gave sweet food to Hari;
thereafter, he offered water, betel-leaf, desired delicacies, fruit, and the arghya offering.
Having performed the lustration ceremony (nīrājana), offered a handful of flowers (kusumāñjali), and likewise performed prostrations, hymns of praise,
circumambulation, and the offering of a priestly fee (dakṣiṇā), he then touched the ground.
He paid homage to the Supreme Self, having indeed observed the vow undertaken on the tenth day; "May my fast, completed during this intercalary month, be fruitful for me. (74)
Having thus worshipped in the morning, he continued to worship for two watches;
then, having fed [the deities] as required, he offered [the oblation] to the wielder of the Śārṅga bow.
In this manner, he worshipped him that very evening with sixteen sacrificial offerings.
The nightly lamp-offering, the food offering, water, betel leaf, and fruit. ||76||
She offered a handful of flowers to Kṛṣṇa and gave him excellent milk-rice;
then she made him drink it and paid homage to the Compassionate One.
He performed dancing and singing with vigil until midnight;
at the hour of midnight, Lord Hari himself, Śrī Puruṣottama, arrived.
"Speak, O Earth! What is desired by you? I am pleased with your vow; choose a boon.
Indeed, for one who observes a vow during an intercalary month, I shall grant every wish. (79)
Such is my vow; therefore, whether it be easy or difficult to obtain, whatever you ask of me, I shall fulfill it in every way—speak to me! (80)
Thus addressed, the Earth spoke there to the Supreme Lord:
"O Blessed One, if you are pleased, and if you are indeed a maker of truthful speech... (8.1)
If you give everything to me, then the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama) is entirely mine;
indeed, I desire nothing else but the Supreme Person as my protector. 82.
"O Lord, I indeed always dwell in your service;
O Master, the protector of beings, grant me such a divine form. (83)
Furthermore, O Great Lord, for the destruction of those who are burdensome and for the eradication of unrighteousness and vices, sport in my world, O Lord!
[Do this] in all months except for the intercalary month (*adhimāsa*), which is performed by the subjects.
To inflame my evil, you have incited me to dwell within me. ||85||
O Lord Janārdana, come in whatever form you wish—whether in a divine or a physical form—so that I may always have your protection, O Master. (86)
If your physical body should ever be successfully produced through proper rites, then I shall become your mother and I will protect my own son. (87)
"I shall cherish you, O Govinda, and I shall feed you with devotion;
I shall perform service for you, so grant whatever is requested according to your desire. (88)
Having spoken thus, she ceased and bowed to Puruṣottama;
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, having heard that which had arisen from the heart of the Earth, [acted accordingly].
And he bestowed upon her a divine form, worthy of service in Vaikuṇṭha;
she became divine, virtuous, and beautiful, with four arms, equal to Ramā.
Having become the earth, the vast Vasumatī, Mādhava then shone forth;
he led that Vasumatī to Vaikuṇṭha upon the waters.
There she remains eternally, having become an exceedingly devoted Vaiṣṇava servant;
then her second form is in the layer of the earth-envelopment.
She is always worthy of dwelling eternally in the abode of the earth;
that goddess is indeed considered the presiding deity of all beings. (93)
Commanded by Nārāyaṇa to remain there as a covering for the earth, that [shell] stays eternally fixed above Satyaloka;
it is the third form of his work, consisting of the earthly elements such as stone and the like.
This entire cosmic egg, consisting of solid matter, was created by Brahmā. ||95||
In that regard, since Hari had indeed promised the Earth that he would come to her whenever she required him to bear her burden, the Earth spoke repeatedly;
and Hari said, "Listen, O Earth, at the commencement of the first age."
When that time has passed, the people will indeed repeatedly become like a heavy burden. 97.
"Even in the first age, for the sake of the work of the gods, I shall now come to you repeatedly through your devotion and by virtue of my granting of boons. (98)
I shall take incarnations and I shall protect you; do not grieve.
I have been gratified by your vow on the tenth day of the intercalary month.
Therefore, indeed, throughout the four ages, for the sake of those respective tasks,
I shall assume ten principal incarnations, and even more than that.
"I shall indeed assume many secondary and non-different divine forms according to need, and in each of those respective forms, I will provide protection for you. (101)
I shall withdraw the gods and destroy the Dānavas;
I shall utterly crush the Daityas and bring you happiness.
"In this way I shall carry the burden; go, O Goddess, as you please. Having addressed her thus, Hari vanished from that place in an instant.
The Earth was also pleased and offered a handful of flowers once more;
having completed the vow, that goddess then bowed to Dundubhi.
She went to her own residence, her palace within the covering of the earth. Thus, O Lakṣmī, having performed the vow pertaining to the intercalary month on the tenth day, she departed.
By name Vasumatī, she became a maidservant residing in Vaikuṇṭha;
yet in age after age, and even day by day, she manifests herself through me.
By my vow, I have made it so that [this] leads to the attainment of all gains;
never has such a gain been bestowed by me through unjust means.
Whatever anyone desires, even with a very small vow of mine, I grant that very thing to them; indeed, there is no "no" in that regard.
Whoever shall hear this story of Vasumatī, and whoever shall read it, will obtain the merit of the vow on the tenth day; of this there is no doubt. (109)

Thus ends the three hundred and second chapter, titled "The Description of the Earth’s Prayer to the Lord in Vaikuṇṭha, the Introduction to Those Who Are a Burden to the Earth, and the Lord’s Promise for the Manifestation of His Incarnations in Every Age through the Tenth-Day Vow," within the *Puruṣottama-māsa-māhātmya* of the first section, the *Kṛta-yuga-santāna*, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*. 1.302.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
O Lakṣmī, listen to the divine story of the Ekādaśī of the intercalary month, which bestows [the grace of] Hari; at the beginning of creation, it was born consisting of ascetic power (tapas).
Born from the chest of Brahmā, the god Dharma exists in embodied form; while the goddess Mūrti has become invisible, she always resides within the body of Dharma.
And she, though arising simultaneously with Dharma as he was born,
appeared according to worldly convention in the form of the daughter of Dakṣa.
Furthermore, according to worldly custom, she was born as the wife of Dharma;
for while Dharma was a god, she remained invisible and unmarried.
Then, O Lakṣmī, that maiden, endowed with celibacy, always served her husband, who was likewise a celibate, with devotion. || 5 ||
Established in Satyaloka within the abode of Veda, she has Dharma as her companion;
indeed, Brahmā alone knows everything regarding her who resides there, while others do not know her as she stands.
From their very childhood, the ignorant indeed constantly perform bathing,
worship, recitation, fire-oblation, meditation, and service to their master.
And he indeed performs bowing and salutation toward the elders, as well as compassion, tranquility, contentment, straightforwardness, beneficence, and so forth. (8)
"Indeed, the qualities of truth, extreme gentleness, and austerity reside within her form;
for that form is a perfected body, established in ascetic penances. || 9 ||
They stood in the rain during the monsoon, in the cold amidst ice water and the like,
in the heat of the five fires, and remained without food during their religious vows.
Constantly wearing wet garments, she would come from the celestial river to her own home,
bow to her husband, and perform the worship of Kṛṣṇa.
Having first bathed her husband with water and other substances and having honored him,
she gives him food, water, solid food, fruits, and so forth.
She herself, with divine knowledge and supreme devotion, constantly worships her husband with tulasī leaves, lotuses, and pārijātaka flowers.

In this manner, having caused her to perform the morning bath every day, the worship of the gods, the honoring of the husband, and the service to the husband, as well as the taking of food and so forth, and having performed them herself; || 14 ||
Dissolved within the body of her husband, she remains forever as his very form;
thus, through this constant union, she is the most excellent of all recipients of love.
To Dharmadeva was born a daughter who indeed bestowed happiness;
and Dharmadeva, in turn, attained supreme satisfaction through her devoted service and obedience.
May she obtain every day and bestow upon her auspicious blessings;
O Mūrtikā, remain ever devoted to your husband and be happy.
"By means of a body obtained through worldly custom, marry and become a wife;
thereafter, become enriched with good fortune, virtuous sons, prosperity, and the like. (18)
Keśava, who is the form of the fruit of eternal devotion, shall be your goal;
he is Hari, Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Brahman, the Lord of Śrī, and the Highest Person (Puruṣottama). || 19 ||
Thus is that ground of benediction, perfumed with great merit;
having risen in the morning on the eleventh day of the intercalary month, one should perform [the rites] as usual.
Having gone there to bathe in the celestial river, she heard the sound of a drum:
"O goddesses, today is the Ekādaśī occurring in the month of Puruṣottama."
Satisfied by her vow, the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa will bestow upon her whatever happiness she desires, both of this world and the next.
Whatever merit I bestow through vows observed on other days of the intercalary month,
I shall grant ten million times that fruit for the vow of Ekādaśī.
Whatever fruit may arise from the observance of other Ekādaśīs,
I shall indeed grant ten billion times that merit through the observance of this one.
I am Brahmā and Īśvara, the presiding deity of the intercalary month;
even there, I am Śrī Puruṣottama, the lord of the eleventh lunar day (Ekādaśī).
This month is meritorious, this day is meritorious, I am a god, and I am the merit of the compassionate one's vow;
to those who follow my command with devotion, I bestow everything according to their desire.

In whatever manner the threefold desire may arise in the mind of the one performing the vow, day by day, I bestow upon them a fruit equal to a parārdha, as well as prosperity, myself, and my own abode. (27)
I give him even my lion-throne; I grant him supernatural powers and wondrous miracles.
Furthermore, I give him the entirety of sovereignty, prosperity, and my own crown adorned with the Kaustubha gem as his ornament.

Just as one rains by compassion during an intercalary month to fulfill the requests of people and to pour forth rain, so shall I not rain anywhere else out of my own desire, except for the sake of the intercalary month. (29)
Let men, women, children, and the elderly perform this vow for my complete satisfaction;
I shall indeed grant them the fruit of my eternal state, which is most divine and higher than the highest.
Or Goloka, or Vaikuṇṭha, or even the unmanifest abode; or Śvetadvīpa, or the solar realm, or others say the earthly realm, or yet another.
"Whatever vow one may desire, I shall grant it out of compassion after [the vow] has been performed;
let my practitioners receive infinite fruit with little effort. (32)
No separate sacrifices are to be performed here, nor is separate austerity to be practiced;
no separate pilgrimage site is required here, for all that is contained within the fruit of this single day.
The milk-vow and the performance of the Putreṣṭi sacrifice are not intended here as separate acts;
for by the vow of Ekādaśī alone, one thinks, "I shall obtain a son. (34)
Performing the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice is not desired as a separate means to achieve [the goal];

Whatever I have done out of love according to my own intellect, please grant forgiveness for any deficiency;
for you, O Lord of Gods, are the intercalary month, O Sovereign who brings the excessive rains.
O Supreme Person, you grant more than what is desired to those who seek;
O Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, Viṣṇu, Lord of Pārvatī, Sovereign of Light! 67.
O Lord of Lakṣmī, O Lord of Māṇikī, O Lord of Sāvitrī, O Sovereign of the Universe!
O Creator of the World, O Beloved of Rādhikā, O Beloved of Kamalā, O Keśava! 68.
"By my vow on this twelfth day, fulfill today whatever is desired by my mind";
having thus petitioned Hari and bowed to him at dawn, midday, and midnight—(69)
Having become entirely absorbed in that [state] and having dedicated all his actions to it,
he should delight [the deity] with dance and song accompanied by instrumental music, and then dismiss him.
Having thus properly undertaken the vow and performed the worship, whether it be a man, a woman, a maiden, a youth, or even a deity, [one should proceed]. (7.1)

Or perhaps they are the consorts of the Lord of the Gods, or women of the sages belonging to the lineage of the Pitṛs, or dwellers of the netherworld; likewise, there are groups of men of such a kind.
Whether they be male lords or female goddesses, whether liberated or yet to be liberated, whatever they desire, they obtain it; I promise this, there is no doubt.
According to one's ability and according to what is required, there is my vow and my worship;
even in the absence of external [implements], there is excellent worship within my heart, distinguished by its internal disposition.
I shall grant it even to him; being pleased by his disposition and his love, I, the Supreme Lord, am raining down compassion today during this intercalary month.
I have not existed in the past, nor shall I exist in the future, just as I am today, the creator of rain;
therefore, out of compassion for me, my devotees should perform some vow. (76)
"May they obtain eternal merit, happiness, and their heart's desire for the world.
Having heard this, the exceedingly beautiful Sāvitrī rejoiced greatly. (77)
Having bowed, she said to Dundubhi: "Listen, O virtuous one, you who act by divine decree!
In meditative absorption, I beheld Brahmā, the Supreme Lord, the Grandfather. (78)
And I saw Sāvitrī seated on his left lap;
she appeared to me in my own form, and at that moment I merged into her as well.
Furthermore, having arisen from my meditative absorption here, I am a young maiden;
this Creator of the universe is my husband, who must be attained while remaining within the mind. (80)
Therefore, on the twelfth day of the intercalary month, I shall perform my vow of eating but one meal and the worship of the God of gods according to my ability. ||8 1||
With this body of mine, the attainment of that eternal abode of Goloka is indeed difficult to reach; yet I possess a physical form that is a manifestation of its splendor.
He possesses a concentrated body born of reality, the offspring of Vairāja;
therefore, my union with Brahmā occurs through that very body, in whatever manner and by whatever means.
"Tell me how that may come to pass; I shall observe the vow of the twelfth day (dvādaśī-vrata).
Having heard this, Puruṣottama spoke to Dundubhī.
Listen, O auspicious Sāvitrī; today indeed have an image of Śrī Puruṣottama fashioned from the gold that was the son of Agni. (85)
Likewise, have an image of Lakṣmī fashioned from gold;
and likewise, make Brahmā and his Sāvitrī out of gold. (86)
"Having performed worship according to your capacity, give gifts to a worthy recipient (supātra). Thus, indeed, in this vow today, there is both worship and giving. (87)
"By performing this, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person, will be pleased with you;
He will accomplish every purpose for you. Do not worry, O maiden. (88)
Having heard this from Sāvitrī regarding her vow on the morning of the twelfth day, [the king] gathered gold from a portion of Mount Meru through the power of yoga. (89)
And there, by means of her sovereignty, she beheld Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa,
as well as Brahmā and Sāvitrī in their very golden forms.

Having performed [the preliminary rites], having invoked [the deity], having bathed, adorned, and worshipped [him], and having fed and given [him] drink, he made a request and performed the *nīrājana* ceremony. ||9 1 ||
Having asked for forgiveness, praised them, and communicated the purpose dwelling in his heart,
Hari himself dismissed those gods just as he was about to do so.
Before Sāvitrī, the Lord appeared together with Lakṣmī;
he had a gracious countenance, was enriched by every splendor, and was the bestower of boons. (93)
He said to her, "Speak, O auspicious lady; what is in your mind?
Sāvitrī replied to the Lord of Gods, "Grant me the yoga of Brahmā."
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa said: "That which was established in your mind has been born; O Sāvitrī, close your eyes and meditate upon me for a moment. (95)
All that was in his mind shall come to pass before his very eyes;
he practiced exactly as it had been proclaimed by Nārāyaṇa with great reverence. (96)
At that very moment, Nārāyaṇa Kṛṣṇa vanished;
then, having performed worship thus in the morning, he did likewise at midday as well.
In the evening as well, she likewise performed worship and kept a vigil;
she placed Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Lakṣmī, and indeed the Unborn One upon the swing.
Having placed the Sāvitrī [mantra] there and repeatedly swinging the girl, Śrī Puruṣottama then returned to that spot and spoke once more. ||99||
O Goddess, having offered handfuls of flowers, water for honor (arghya), fruit, and water, perform the dismissal for me here; I am going to that imperishable abode.
Go this very day to the Vairāja realm from which Brahmā was born;
enter that Vairāja state in its subtle form before that [creation] occurs.
"O daughter of Vairāja, become a maiden from his navel;
as soon as you are born, Vairāja will give you, a young woman, to Aja."
By the very command of the Lord, he shall appoint you to a task;
O auspicious lady, go, may it be well with you, and may your good fortune be eternal.
Having spoken thus, Śrī Hari Nārāyaṇa vanished there; and Sāvitrī, having offered a handful of flowers to the form of Śrī Hari, [proceeded].
Having offered the *arghya* and a *śrīphala* fruit, he performed the dismissal of the deities;
he gave gifts of gold for the sake of the splendor of Brahman to the images.
And having received a blessing from the Guru known as Patnīvratā, who dwells in the abode of Goloka,
become a beautiful woman endowed with good fortune.
"Be the consort of Brahmā and the progenitor of the worlds! Having spoken thus, she bowed to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa and immediately vanished from sight.
Then, having attained birth, that maiden Sāvitrī entered his nostril as a young woman. (108)
Knowing that she had been born for the sake of Brahmā,
the Virāṭ gave her, who had just appeared, to the assembly of the lords according to the prescribed rite.
Having obtained Brahmā as her husband, the Lord, that Mother of the World also became one whose desires were fulfilled, for Brahmā possesses four faces.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, I have told you the cause of Sāvitrī’s attainment of the status of Brahmā’s wife due to her observance of the Dvādaśī vow; it is as it happened, and it bestows desired fruits.

Thus ends the three hundred and fourth chapter, titled "The Description of how Brahmā, while in meditative absorption, beheld the creation of the Lord of Jīvas and Brahmā by Sāvitrī—a manifestation of Rādhikā—and seeing his own state within her womb, desired to obtain her as his wife; and upon hearing the sound of a drum, that daughter of Vairāja attained Brahmā as her husband through the vow of Dvādaśī," in the section on the Greatness of the Month of Puruṣottama within the lineage of the Kṛta Yuga in the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī, to the account of the four daughters of Brahmā in former times;
by the vow on the thirteenth day in the intercalary month, Puruṣottama [was attained]. || 1 ||
He himself became their husband and gave them his imperishable abode as a home;
out of compassion, the Lord granted them eternal worldly enjoyment and liberation. || 2 ||
O Lakṣmī, in the first Kṛta Yuga, in ancient times, for the purpose of creation, Brahmā [created] the boys named Sanaka, Sananda, Sanātana, and Sanatkumāra.
Four [beings] were created, endowed with sovereignty, strength, and splendor;
and for the sake of their conjugal union, four Śaktis were indeed fashioned for them.
By name they were Jayā, Lalitā, Pārvatī, Prabhā, and Śubhā;
they were as similar as those [names], and they were Mānasīs and Mānasas respectively.
Having created four pairs, he became exceedingly pleased upon seeing that these [beings],
as soon as they were born, were indeed possessed of consciousness.
To appoint them to the task of creation, the Creator of the Universe spoke to each one individually:
"O Sanaka, accept this Jayā, who has been prepared for you."
"Sanandana, accept this Lalitā who has been prepared for you;
Sanātana, accept this Pārvatī who has been given to you. (8)
"Accept this radiance given by me; make it your companion.
Becoming pairs, indeed four pairs [shall you be]."
Let them create a mental creation entirely in the form of couples;
such a tradition of domestic dharma was obtained from Goloka.
In Vaikuṇṭha as well, such a tradition of domestic duties was observed;
by the command of Kṛṣṇa, we respectfully adopt these household duties.
Likewise, you sons, having likewise accepted the duties of householders esteemed by your father and having fulfilled them, may you indeed become happy in this world.
Having appointed you to the task of creation,
I too shall once again be freed from the burden of creation and thus have fulfilled my purpose.
In the dharma of the household, O sons, lineages always become saviors;
in the dharma of the household, even women become bestowers of happiness.
In the dharma of the householder, sacrificial rites arise from devotion:
the honoring of guests, the worship of the gods, and the worship of the virtuous. (15)
Hospitality toward those in other stages of life arises, as does giving that bestows heavenly rewards;
moreover, the fulfillment of desires is protected and wealth is acquired. (16)
The three goals of human life culminate in liberation, which is attained eternally thereafter;
yet, without the duties of the household, there can indeed be no cessation of the flow of the *guṇas*. (17)
Whether in childhood or in youth, knowledge does not arise that bestows dispassion;
therefore, one should indeed pacify the mind only after first providing it with enjoyment. 18.
But for those whose minds are perfectly tranquil, eternal liberation occurs;
therefore, my sons, perform the duties that ensure the stability of creation.
Having thus heard these words of Brahmā, the four sons of the Creator— already wise and likewise possessed of yoga— [proceeded] from the east.
Only these knowers of Brahman are firmly resolved upon the goal of liberation;
liberation does not come through action, O father, for action is indeed bondage.
Even there, the domestic rituals are indeed bonds;
the duty of a woman does not become a cause for liberation.
Furthermore, driven by passion, one performs action after action;
for in that state, the goals of dharma, artha, and kāma certainly do not exist at all. (23)
Therefore, O father, without knowledge, the dharma of household life is fraught with danger;
the dharma of household life is a burden, just as you desire it to be abandoned.
Likewise, we do not intend to carry that burden from this day forward;
for, O sons, those who are called "tārakas" are indeed those for whom knowledge alone is the means of crossing over (tāraka).
That indeed is what is called "son" for the wise and the yogis;
but for those who perform ritual actions and whose souls are not free from the desire to act, there are only "daughters" and "sons. (26)
May our lineage, O knowers of Brahman, become liberated;
may they be the guides on the path of Brahman and dwellers in the world of Brahman. (27)
For the sake of our impermanent lineage, we shall not pursue domestic life; association with women is delightful outwardly, but in its ultimate consequence, it is misery within.
What person who knows the truth would serve that [worldly state], having abandoned his own innate happiness?
The happiness of the Self is declared to be supreme; any happiness other than that leads to the end. (29)
O Grandfather, those sacrifices and rituals prescribed for the duties of householders are not equal even to a fraction of the work of propitiating Brahman.
For us who possess knowledge, the propitiation of Brahman alone is considered the sacrifice here;
when the propitiation of Brahman is performed, the honoring of guests is thereby accomplished.
The worship of the gods and other rites have been performed, and the honoring of the virtuous has been accomplished;
for when Hari is constantly honored, everything indeed becomes honored.
O Father, the gift of the knowledge of Brahman is eternal;
it is obtained in heaven, and that alone is indeed the station of liberation.
That which is not intermingled with suffering and the like, and which is not swallowed up at the end—
attained through the power of true resolve— that is the eternal state in heaven.

The law of time (death) falls upon one who possesses craving, but not upon anyone who delights in the Self; for such a person, there is no need for wealth consisting of food, water, and clothing, nor for any other objects of value. //35//
For one who conducts oneself in this manner, liberation rests in the palm of the hand;
it consists in the renunciation of the flow of qualities through the duties of a householder. 36.
One must awaken from mere hope; indeed, those who abide in the nature of the gunas are submerged, for they possess neither childhood nor has youth ever arrived.
And within the Self of all, there indeed exists a cessation devoid of enjoyment;
it is the mind perfectly colored by Brahman, whose very form is peace. (38)
For them, liberation—whether with the body or without the body—is not taught;
he is indeed said to be eternally liberated, he is indeed considered eternally liberated. ||39||
Untouched by joy, resentment, fear, or agitation, he is indeed liberated.
Therefore, we are not entitled to creation; we are merely the instruments of Brahmā. (40)
Free from duality, we shall also make others devoid of duality;
this indeed is the father of his father’s father’s father’s father. (41)
The Dharma consisting of the Upaniṣads belongs to him who is known as Puruṣottama;
