we shall go before that very Supreme Self by means of it. (42)
Whatever indeed ought to be done hereafter, let that be performed this very day;
provided there exists within one’s own treasury the means for its execution. (43)
But for us, through the grace of our father, self-restraint arises spontaneously and, being a source of happiness, serves as the means to liberation. (44)
Therefore, O father, from our childhood we shall dwell in liberation, and not otherwise;
for when we are liberated, you too will be liberated—of this there is no doubt.
"Know indeed that we sons, the Tārakas, are truly as our names imply;
and these maidens are yoginīs, embodiments of knowledge and realized wisdom. (46)
“They shall attain Brahman itself in a very short time; do not grieve.
Having spoken thus to his sons, he departed toward the river Viṣṇupadī.
And the maidens Jayā, Lalitā, Pārvatī, and Prabha, perfected in the yoga of the supreme self, remembered Puruṣottama. ||48||
They worshipped Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa with constant devotion and performed the recitation: "Oṃ, obeisance unto You, Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. (49)
Thus, on the thirteenth day, at the very dawn of the Satyaloka, the compassionate proclamation of the drum was heard as it resounded. (50)
Whosoever she may be—whether endowed with Brahman or separated from Brahman, whether a newborn girl or a woman of beautiful form who is free from passion. ||5.1||
Whether she be an elder woman, or fortunate, or a married woman, or one who has left her husband; whether she be full of passion, or self-possessed, or even one who strives for liberation. ||5.2||
Whether protectorless or having a protector, conditioned or even unconditioned; whether well-situated or situated in the unmade, she is characterized by her departure. ||53||
Whether she has given her word or not, whether she is worthy of giving or devoid of the act of giving,
or even if she was created for the purpose of giving— such a woman should observe the Trayodaśī vow.
I, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person, am the bestower of their desires; whatever new thing each of them requires here during this intercalary month, I shall provide.
Whether it be inaccessible or easily accessible, obtainable or unobtainable—whether obtained through merit, obtained through wealth, or obtained even by means of spiritual practices. (56)
Whether it be inconceivable or conceivable, eternal or transient,
enjoyable or indeed non-enjoyable— whatever else she desires in her heart.
Being well-pleased, I, Puruṣottama, shall grant all of that upon the performance of the vow of eating but one meal on the thirteenth lunar day.
One should indeed observe the vow with faith, preceded by my worship, either by eating only at midnight or by subsisting on fruits alone. (59)
I, the Supreme Lord, am her leader, her guide, her protector, and her nourisher; I am the doer of good, the giver of refuge, and likewise her delighter. (60)
Whether they be men, women, or others, whoever worships during the intercalary month on the thirteenth lunar day with sandalwood and other offerings—I shall grant them whatever they desire. (61)
With one hundred and eight, or indeed with fifty-six,
or with thirty-two services, and with the sixteen and other such ritual substances.
Or they may worship me with whatever leaves, flowers, water, food, and rice they happen to obtain, or even mentally, with offerings made out of love.
Let people offer me either a handful of flowers or a handful of love;
I shall also fulfill their hearts with the gift of my grace.
Let them not hesitate; let them speak or uphold it, let them form a resolve within their hearts, for I shall bestow it upon those who have taken the vow.
Having heard this on the morning of the thirteenth day,
Jayā, Lalitā, Pāravatī, and Prabhā went there to visit Hari.
Then they approached that Dundubhi and asked, "What indeed do you give?
Dundubhi replied, "I give either heaven or Puruṣottama."
I give as the price for the Trayodaśī vow my husband Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, along with his wealth and even his abode known as Akṣara.
In the intercalary month, I become the giver of the surplus; even in a minor vow, I am manifest as the very soul of the intercalary month within the circle of creation.
I grant the eternal Brahman— the truth in heaven, the state of Parameṣṭhin, Vairāja, Bhaumana, Dhruva, Goloka, and Vaikuṇṭha.
"What do you ladies desire? I shall grant the excellent fruit of your vow.
Hearing this, the four of them then joyfully spoke to Dundubhi:
As soon as we were all born, we were indeed unrefined; may we now become refined through union with Kṛṣṇa, united with his divine abode. ||72||
May that Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa come to us;
through this vow, we desire nothing other than to become His maidservants today. (73)
Then Dundubhi said: "O ladies, today indeed with joy, having bathed in the morning, you should worship Puruṣottama made of gold."
With whatever services are obtained, and with mental offerings imbued with devotion, Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, who is the refuge for those hungry for love, will accept them. (79)
"You possess divine forms worthy of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa;
having performed the vows and worship today, may you attain the supreme Hari. (76)
Having spoken thus, Dundubhi departed from that place to another;
Jayā, Lalitā, Pārvatī, Vrata, and Prabhā performed [the rites]. (77)
Having bathed and returned home, they constructed an excellent pavilion and worshipped Puruṣottama on the morning of the thirteenth day.
Having prepared a lion-throne in the center and placed there a golden image of Hari, they invoked the deity and joyfully offered water and other articles of worship.
Having caused [the deity] to be bathed with the waters of the five nectars (pañcāmṛta), [he offered] garments,
all ornaments, and [unguents such as] saffron and sandalwood.
Incense, lamps, excellent food offerings, water, flowers, fruits, and so forth;
betel, fans, umbrellas, chowries, and the waving of lights, and so on. ||81||
They performed circumambulation, offered praise, and presented patience, an arghya offering, and a handful of flowers, saying:
"O God of gods, Hari, Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, Lord of the universe! (82)
"Accept the tribute from us, your slave-girls; we are indeed your slaves.
Having thus resolved, they offered handfuls of flowers with voices choked with emotion. (83)
At midday as well, having worshipped the Lord in this very same manner and fed Hari,
they likewise worshipped Him in the evening and performed the lustration ceremony (nīrājana) for Hari.
And they gave him sweet food, and Hari became satisfied and content;
having kept a vigil at night before Hari, they performed the nocturnal rites. (85)
They danced and sang a sweet song accompanied by rhythmic timing;
at that moment, the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Puruṣottama manifested himself.
The Blessed One, possessing fourfold forms, assumed each of those [mudrās] individually;
with his four forms, he placed those four garlands upon his left side.
Having bowed his neck, he accepted what was offered by them;
being pleased, he repeatedly touched and joyfully embraced them. (88)
Inaccessible, inconceivable, unreal, and indeed indescribable—having bestowed happiness upon them both quickly and having placed [them] upon Garuḍa. (89)
Having bowed to the Creator and received his dowry as well as his blessings, [she departed].
And by Brahmā, according to the prescribed rite, they were offered to Nārāyaṇa. ||90||
Having caused the wedding to be performed, Kṛṣṇakānta departed for his own abode—that which is the imperishable, supreme light, the all-pervading, most excellent Brahman. 91.
Because all other abodes had indeed become manifest from that [supreme state],
Śrī Kṛṣṇa Puruṣottama went with those wives to that excellent realm.
Jayā, Lalitā, Pārvatī, and Prabhā were in the supreme sky;
these very ones, having been liberated in the ether, became the wives of Hari.
Having performed this vow on the thirteenth day at Śrī Puruṣottama, those who have gone to the imperishable abode rejoice like gods, equal to the beloved of the gods.
Having performed the worship of Śrī Kṛṣṇa in the month of Māsa, they attained the supreme state;
for even a very small [act] yields a fruit that is eternally divine and indeed infinite. (95)
Those who, with minds fixed on Kṛṣṇa, shall hear or read this chapter, for them too there will be that same fruit; of this there is no doubt. (96)

Thus ends the three hundred and fifth chapter, titled "The Description of how the Daughters of Brahmā—named Jayā, Lalitā, Pārvatī, and Prabhā—who were created for the sake of Sanaka and the others, attained the status of wives to Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa in the abode of Śrī Puruṣottama by means of the vow of the thirteenth day of the month of Puruṣottama, while Sanaka and the others maintained a state of detachment," in the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, within the first section, the *Kṛtayuga-Santāna*, concerning the majesty of the month of Puruṣottama. || 1.305 ||
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī, supreme and primordial one, to that account concerning Dundubhi which occurred on the fourteenth lunar day in the first Vaikuṇṭha.
Within the boundary of the abode of the Imperishable Brahman, however, there exists Vaikuṇṭha, the foremost and most excellent residence, which resembles Goloka. || 2 ||
There indeed dwell the Kalpa trees of perfect form;
their daughter, Śrī, always resides there as a maiden.
She possesses a divine splendor whose nature is the celestial realm; she is the Goddess presided over by consciousness, whose very form is the support of all.
And the daughter of that sovereign power is the maiden Māṇikyā;
and there in Vaikuṇṭha exists the divine ocean of milk and nectar.
His daughter is the maiden Lakṣmī, who is identical with you;
these three goddesses indeed shine there in that abode.
She had three friends who were her companions— three maidens exceedingly delicate,
Māṇikyā, Śrī, and Lakṣmī, who were always knowers of Brahman.
Those women who are yoginīs of the knowledge of Brahman as the Self and are devoted to Hari constantly perform service to Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
They constantly meditate with devotion upon his very image in their homes;
these three are the divine manifestation, the wish-fulfilling tree, and the ocean of milk.
Seeing the daughters' practice of meditation and other virtues, they indeed rejoice again and again;
becoming embodiments of bliss, they bestow blessings upon them. (10)
In infinite abodes there exist many wives of Kṛṣṇa; you and others like you are indeed the supreme consorts beloved by the Supreme Brahman.
"Those who possess the form of sovereigns over kings, and for whom there are none others superior anywhere—having received such blessings from their father, they shine, ever-increasing. (12)
In the morning, they bathe while remembering Hari and then meditate upon Hari;
they construct a divine pavilion, resplendent with archways of lightning.
It was adorned with pillars and other features inlaid with various jewels and gems,
filled with artificial gardens, and decorated with divine garments.
Adorned on all sides by the form of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa,
in the center was a beautiful throne resplendent with jewels, gold, and other precious materials.
And they place there comfortable mattresses;
having installed therein an image of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, they arrange them in its midst.
They bathe them with streams of milk and bathe them with water;
they repeatedly rub fragrant sandalwood oil upon them. (17)
Having bathed him, they present divine garments in the morning;
they wear ornaments and assume a graceful, amorous demeanor.
They worship again and again with leaves, flowers, fruits, and water;
they offer incense, lamps, and fragrances in the presence of Kṛṣṇa.
They massage his feet, they take the nectar of his feet,
and those devoted women smell the fragrance born of Kṛṣṇa’s grace.
They behold that form of Hari, they touch the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa,
and they taste whatever fruits and other offerings have been given during the worship.
They listen to the hymn of praise for the Blessed One sung by one another, and they speak of the virtues and conduct of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. (22)
They undertake the work of Hari and circumambulate Him;
likewise, they assume playful gestures, amorous expressions, and mental bliss.
They perform reflection, determination, and the sense of ownership born of union with Kṛṣṇa;
before him are vessels of sweet food and nectar, as well as vessels of water. (24)
They presented golden plates filled with food offerings;
they fed Him with full devotion and further delighted Hari.
They cause water to be offered for drinking and they take delight before Hari; they play musical instruments and joyfully perform the ārātrika ceremony. (26)
They bow down to Hari and praise his virtues;
they describe his deeds and recount his stories. (27)
They meditate on Him whose heart is dark blue and offer their hearts to Hari;
they satisfy Nārāyaṇa by offering handfuls of flowers.
They praise the Supreme Self, remember and utter the names of Hari, constantly perform service, cultivate friendship, and offer their very selves. (29)
Thus they perform these divine rites consisting of devotion;
even at midday, having worshipped him, Śrī herself offers them fruits.
The celestial maidens carry from the wish-fulfilling trees even the most excellent, supreme, delightful, flavorful, sweet, and non-sour [fruits]. (3.1)
The daughter of the tree, Śrī, also offers ever-new fruit;
she gathers well-ripened plantains from the plantain trees.
And having gathered the finest mangoes from the mango trees, and having obtained the desired sour fruits that grant the results of one's actions from the *karmada* trees; ||33||
And having gathered from the creepers ripe and succulent karkaṭikās, as well as well-ripened kaliṅgas which bring about coolness; (34)
Then, having brought ripe wood-apples from those trees, and having also gathered sweet dates from the date-palm trees; 35.
Having brought from Kaṭīṅguda the fruits of the Kaṭīṅgunda tree—large iṅguda fruits indeed, with cooked, oily juices—[he gave them]. (36)
Śrī brings and offers them, and Nārāyaṇa himself eats—dates that are very sweet and grapes that are most delicious. (37)
Dates, dates-pods, and the like, palm fruits, and *śrīphala* fruits; earthy fruits that are very sweet and smooth-textured fruits. ||38||
Kṣīrikā fruits, tawny-colored jackfruits, and large ones;
various kinds of garlic, and indeed jars of ghee. (39)
There were ripe śiṅgava fruits, as well as jambū and rāvaṇa fruits; they were like nectar, most delicious, and the ṭiṭīma fruits possessed a sweet, excellent flavor. ||40||
Pomegranates, stalks of sugarcane, fresh jujubes, tamarinds, madhuka fruits, almonds, and many-seeded nuts. ||41||
And *rāmaphala* fruits, sweet *sītāphala* fruits, various trees, as well as *jambīra* citrons and flowering plants.
Having brought cirbhaṭas along with people bearing fruit, ṭimṭimas, and other fresh-colored fruits, Śrī gave them [to him]. (43)
To Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the embodiment of Śrī Puruṣottama; indeed, the Blessed One has offered these with devotion and supreme faith. (44)
But the maiden Māṇikyā, possessing divine splendor, for the sake of the Blessed One, brings together jewels and herself bears Acyuta. ||45||
Likewise, garlands of jewels, strings of pearls, pearl bracelets, diamonds, rubies, and emeralds; ||46||
And also sapphire gems, kaustubhas, as well as bhīṣmaka stones, cat's-eyes, topazes, karketakas, and gold-colored gems. ||47||
And likewise emeralds, topazes, rubies, crystals, corals, rubies, and citraka-gems. ||48||
Taking gomedas, mahānīlas, and kūpyas, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa gave them those [gems] consisting of precious jewels. 49.
Having donned the ornaments, he became exceedingly delighted;
then indeed Lakṣmī, the daughter of the Ocean of Milk, who is ever-disposed toward the virtuous, [appeared]. (50)
He caused them to eat and indeed caused them to drink that essence of milk:
milk-rice, milk-porridge, and rice cooked in milk.
The milk-heap, the churning of milk, the milk-vortex, the milk-offering,
the decoction of milk, the lumps of milk, and the auspicious milk-mountain.
He gave curd, clarified butter, buttermilk, fresh butter, and milk-porridge; he provided rice with milk, milk mixed [with other ingredients], and various drinks of milk.
Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa indeed ate and drank those various things;
she also gave him diverse jewels produced from the milk-ocean.
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, filled with devotion, accepted those things which Śrī Māṇikyā Lakṣmī had offered with heartfelt sincerity. (55)
He partook of fruits, jewels, and milk-rice; he wore and ate that which was filled with devotion.
Seeing his excellence, his most precious gems, and his fortune ever intent on service, Hari was pleased. (56)
And in the evening, those daughters, intent on propitiation, performed worship just as before;
with great devotion, they always offered the lustration ceremony, food, and other offerings. (57)
On the fourteenth day of the intercalary month, at midday, following the worship,
the sound of drums was indeed heard by them for Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa.
May they perform worship constantly; may they perform my propitiation;
may they offer something to me and attain my abode. (59)
I am the Person known as Puruṣottama, the Lord of the abode of Brahman; I am the presiding deity of the intercalary month. I speak it, and indeed I bestow it.
Those who reside in Goloka and those who reside in Vaikuṇṭha, as well as whoever else—both men and women—perform this vow on the fourteenth day of the intercalary month; ||61||
I, the Blessed One, shall fulfill their mental desire;
I will grant them the supreme abode, the dwelling place beyond the imperishable.
People shall worship me with fruits, jewels, and milk-rice;
they shall attain the supreme abode where I, the Supreme Person, reside.
To others who dwell in my abodes, I grant the highest station;
let my devotees, full of devotion, attain the supreme state.
Neither Vaikuṇṭha nor Goloka is like this;
indeed, there exists nothing else whatsoever that is equal to my abode.
There is no one equal to me, nor indeed anyone superior; there is nothing comparable to Brahmā.
There is no other happiness equal to my own happiness; let the noble ones taste it by giving even a very small gift. (66)

May they become my female servants and masters of devotion; may they eternally enjoy the measure of bliss obtained from my form and revel in me through the performance of the excellent vow on the fourteenth day.
"May the daughters of Manu, having propitiated me, become deities in heaven;
and may the goddesses, having propitiated me, likewise become ṛṣis."
"May the wives of the Ṛṣis, having propitiated me, become indeed the Īśānīs;
and may the Īśānīs, having propitiated me, become the Īśvarīs. (69)
"Having propitiated me, let the goddesses become Nārāyaṇīs;
and having propitiated me, let the Nārāyaṇīs joyfully become gopīs. (70)
And having propitiated me, the Supreme Person, may they all become "Puruṣottamīs," eternally liberated indeed.
Having propitiated me, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person,
let those who seek my vow attain my supreme, imperishable abode.
Whoever performs this vow at Śrī Puruṣottama on the fourteenth day of the intercalary month has indeed acquired everything that belongs to me. (73)
I speak, I speak, I speak again: let them come with me;
let them indeed dwell with me in my imperishable abode.
"I am pleased by your roar; I say it again and again:
on the fourteenth day of the intercalary month, come to my abode through the observance of this vow. (75)
Having heard the drum of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa in Vaikuṇṭha,
they went there with joy and haste to where the sound was being made.
Śrī, Hṛṣṭā, Māṇikyā, and Lakṣmī, delighted within their hearts,
bowed again and again and spoke to that drum of Hari’s.
We dwell here in the great bliss of Vaikuṇṭha, the abode of Nārāyaṇa; therefore, if the Lord grants us even greater supreme good fortune, [we shall accept it]. (78)
"We are maidens; we always perform the worship of that Hari.
Today, according to the determination regarding the intercalary month, we shall observe the vow of the fourteenth day. (79)
When will Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord of the syllables, appear? When will the Supreme, the Ancient One, the Puruṣottama, lead us away? (80)
Having heard that, Dundubhi then said to them: "Today indeed the Lord will come at night after the worship; you must keep a vigil."
Praise Janārdana, the Supreme Self who dwells within the heart;
may your desires bear fruit and come to fulfillment. (82)
Having spoken thus, Dundubhi, honored with unbroken grains and flowers, departed;
and at midnight, the maidens worshipped Śrī Kṛṣṇa as he was flowing with semen.
While they were keeping watch there, Śrī performed a beautiful dance;
Māṇikyā played musical instruments there in accompaniment with rhythmic beats. 84.
Lakṣmī made music by singing, and the three of them sang together with melodious voices, accompanied by the sounds of small bells, anklets, and bracelets.

I bow to the Supreme Lord, the manifest Lord of Bliss, who is Truth, the imperishable Brahman, both supreme and non-supreme, the Lord of this world and the Lord of the next world, eternal knowledge, infinite and boundless, possessing manifold forms, the Lord of the lotus; who is peaceful, as lovely as the sun, free from sin and sorrow, the great bliss of the bliss of Brahman. (86)

In that abode, I bow to the Supreme Lord, whose feet are worshipped by the hosts of liberated attendants of the Lord of the Imperishable Brahman; who shines with the nectar-abode of consciousness as the sole moon of nectar for the liberated; whose soles are bowed to by Śrīvatsa, Brahmā, and Śiva; who is the bliss of his friends; and who is the supreme bliss of the Lord of Manifestations. (87)

I bow to the Supreme Lord, the manifestation of supreme bliss, who is the divine, partless, and infinite one; whose form dwells in the midst of the circle of lords of sages; who is the manifest form and the supreme form, to be known through the sections of the Vedas and Agamas; who is the divine abode, of unborn nature, beginningless, and the treasury of divine qualities. 88.

I bow to the Supreme Lord, the Sovereign of Manifestations, the Supreme Bliss; who possesses a gentle luster, wears a garland of consciousness as his earrings and a crown, and is clothed in fine yellow garments; who is the omniscient Hari-Kṛṣṇa endowed with immeasurable power, the bestower of inconceivable bliss; whose fame is honored by the Vedas and Agamas, and who proclaims the Dharma according to the Vedic doctrine. (89)

I bow to the Blessed One, the supreme Lord and best of gods, who illuminates the world and its beyond, whose splendor dwells in the unworldly realms, who is ineffable, from whom the birth and so forth of this universe proceed, who is the refuge for the shelterless, the beloved of the lowly, Kṛṣṇa, whose very form is the essence of compassion, who is merciful toward the distressed, and the sovereign bliss of the manifest Lord. (90)

I bow to the Supreme Lord, the bliss of the manifesting Ishvara, whose form is radiant like refined gold, lightning, jewels, the sun, and the moon; who is the essence of existence, of profound color, inconceivable, unborn, seated within the heart, and the source of the three worlds; whose eyes are like the petals of a dark blue lotus, whose face is smiling, and who is the joy of all. 9.1.
I bow to the Supreme Lord, the dark-complexioned, all-pervading, supreme person, the source of bliss, who illuminates the entire multitude of beings with the splendor arising from his own lotus feet;
to the true Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Sovereign, the Lord of the Mistress of Māyā, the foremost among the liberated, the Supreme Lord, the Lord of manifestations, the Supreme Bliss. (92)
Śrī, the daughter of the wish-fulfilling tree, constantly meditates upon her beloved self; Māṇikya, the daughter of divine splendor, prays for you as her own master;

and even Lakṣmī, the daughter of the divine ocean of milk, desires you as her sinless husband, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama) abiding in the imperishable realm—you are that very one who fulfills the purpose of worldly existence.
Take our hands and never let them go;
as long as you remain in the imperishable abode, so long shall we be your wives. (94)
O Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, O compassionate refuge, act quickly!
Accept from our hands the garlands of choice offered all at once. (95)
Having thus offered praise, those three ceased their chanting; at that very moment, the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Master, manifested himself.
He who is the cause of the manifestation of all things, the cause of all causes, the Lord of the lords of all lords, the supreme Brahman, the illustrious Puruṣottama. ||97||
In the sky of consciousness, he drives a celestial vehicle called a *vimāna*, drawn by white elephants, extending for ten million *yojanas* and filled with liberated souls. (98)
Having consoled the three [goddesses] in Vaikuṇṭha, he offered them the celestial trees, divine prosperity,
and the Ocean of Milk, which were presented by them according to the prescribed rites.
Requested by his ancestors, O Kṛṣṇa, he accepted the three maidens;
however, he said, "O Keśava, act in such a way that there shall be no separation from us. (100)
Then Hari took hold of their hands;
Śrī, Lakṣmī, and Māṇikyā shone forth, equal to Kṛṣṇa.
The best of men, having caused two forms of each of them to be made, and having well-guarded the three shadow-forms of them under the supervision of his father, [placed them in the water]. || 102 ||
Having assumed three divine forms suitable for Puruṣottama—forms worthy of dwelling in the imperishable abode (Akṣaradhāma) and suited to be His consorts—[He appeared]. 103.
Having caused the three of them to ascend the celestial chariot, Hari himself, the Supreme Person, went to his own divine abode of imperishable syllables, accompanied by his wife.
And thus, by means of the vow on the fourteenth day of the intercalary month,
those three— Śrī, Lakṣmī, and Māṇikyā— became the eternal wives of Hari.
In this eternal abode, what indeed is difficult to attain?
Such is the fruit for both the listener and the speaker; of this there is no doubt. (106)

Thus ends the three hundred and sixth chapter, titled "The Description of Lakṣmī—the Daughter of the Divine Ocean of Milk—and Māṇikyā—the Daughter of the Kalpavṛkṣa-tree—Attaining the Status of Consort to the Supreme Brahman, Puruṣottama Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, in the Imperishable Abode through the Vow on the Fourteenth Day of the Extra Month, by Hearing the Drum in Vaikuṇṭha," within the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, in the first section concerning the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga, specifically the majesty of the month of Puruṣottama.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī, to the auspicious story of the two daughters of Bhakti, the wife of Dharma,
who were born on a middle lunar day during an intercalary month— a most excellent and purifying account.
In the beginning, during the Kṛta Yuga, two daughters of devotion appeared in the mind,
both named Preyasī and Śreyasī.
Wherever those two parents were, there they both constantly served them; indeed, having abandoned them, they were unable to sustain their own lives. || 3 ||
Constantly devoted to the service of their father and dedicated to their own duties,
they would always bathe in the morning and bow at the feet of their parents.
For the purpose of performing the rites of bathing and so forth for their parents, they gave water and other necessities;
and having bathed them, they gave garments for them to wear.
They worshipped with sandalwood, unbroken rice grains, jasmine flowers, saffron, and other offerings;
as well as most delicious and refined food offerings, fruits, betel leaf, and water.

Having offered themselves, both performed the massaging of their parents' bodies and other such services; they did everything else that was pleasing to their mother and father, setting aside all other concerns.
She attends to the bedding and coverlets, as well as the cleaning of the alms-bowls;
she performs the sweeping of the house, the washing of clothes, and the cooking of food.
Fetching water, milking the wish-fulfilling cows (kāmadhenus), purifying the grains, and likewise bringing flowers and other materials for worship.
The chanting of the mantra of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the worship of the gods, the satiation of the ancestors, the sacrifice to all beings, and the honoring of guests. || 10 ||

Generosity, knowledge, self-realization, and even the spiritual wisdom of Brahman—all these, as well as all household duties and constant service to one's parents, [are accomplished through this]. || 1 1 ||
According to their mutual desire, they performed other rites as well day and night;
consequently, they both became recipients of blessings and were greatly beloved.
Just as her name was, so did virtues take up residence there;
according to her strength and according to her power, Sundarī offered herself with her whole being.
Disregarding her own body, she always served her beloved with devotion, offering all her possessions and enjoyments, even though it was difficult day and night.
For she was exceedingly dear and the object of her parents' greatest affection;
because of that, she became known as "Preyasī" (the Beloved) and "Bhukti" (the Enjoyment). || 15 ||
She is always intent on bringing about the welfare of her parents, others, and the multitude of distressed maidens, repeatedly dispelling their sufferings. (16)
Because she perfectly brings about a bliss equal to liberation through her virtuous deeds,
that [city] attained even the renown of being "Superior Liberation" (Śreyasī-mukti).
By a drop of grace from Dharma and Bhakti, their two daughters, Preyasī and Śreyasī,
were given the meaningful and divine names Bhukti and Mukti respectively.
For those whose father is Dharma himself and whose mother is the divine Bhakti, what wonder is there in their virtuous qualities? They are a supreme and celestial treasure.
Whom does service to the two parents, who are themselves pure, not endow with the highest virtue?
By him who has satisfied his parents, Mādhava himself is satisfied. (20)
All the gods were satisfied, and the entire world was gratified;
for if a daughter were to grant satisfaction to her childless parents, [then all would be well]. (21)
She is indeed declared to be equal to a son, for by her,
through her own wisdom, her aged parents were satisfied and thereby delivered.
That daughter, who is like a son, is entitled to a share of the inheritance;
for although she is a girl in body, she is a son in her heart and in her very self. (23)
According to the scriptures, she must always be protected by him; through her, heaven for both of them is certain.
Indeed, the water, food, and gifts offered by her reach the ancestors.
For one who indeed has no sons, his daughter shall perform the rites:
fame, charity, recitation, fire-offerings, Vedic study, and libations to the ancestors.
The daughter should perform all the prescribed rites and wear the sacred thread;
she should remain in celibacy as long as she serves her parents. (26)
Once a son has been born, or even if one has been taken [in adoption], she shall later, with the father’s permission, complete her period of celibacy according to the rules and be married. (27)
When one is established in the practice of celibacy (*brahmacarya*), even if impurity such as menstruation occurs,
there is no fault because of the superior power of that ascetic celibacy.
Impurity must be observed for four days;
however, there is no senility, nor any other defect, nor any sin incurred by doing so. (29)
By the fire of celibacy, everything pertaining to the body is reduced to ashes;
there has never been, nor will there ever be, a dharma equal to celibacy.

Whether she be a maiden or one joined in marriage, whether she be without a husband or possessed of a husband, whether she be without a spiritual partner or with one— such a person purifies the vow of celibacy.
Wherever there is devotion to Brahman and the vow of Brahman within the life of celibacy (brahmacarya),
whatever is indeed other than Brahman there is utterly reduced to ashes by that destruction.

The destruction of seed, the destruction of passion, the destruction of the fertile season, and so forth, are defects [in other contexts]; however, in the case of celibacy (*brahmacarya*), these are ornaments, for such [restraint] brings about liberation.
In this way, those two maidens devotedly performed service for their parents,
remaining constantly established in celibacy within that auspicious house of devotion to Dharma.
In the morning, while you were indeed coming to bathe in the celestial river (Svarṇadī) in Satyaloka,
you heard from those two [sages] about Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa.
In this supreme month of Māgha, Puruṣottama—the best of men, the source of all abodes, and the origin of all incarnations—bestows [his grace]. || 36 ||
To the performer of the vow on the middle lunar day, I grant the imperishable abode, prosperity,
my own presence, my very form, and my sovereignty.
I grant my equanimity, my sovereignty, and my world;
I grant my yoga, my power, and my divine nature.
I indeed bestow my lap, my own form, and even my own renown;
likewise, I grant me equal worshipfulness and preeminence.
I bestow my own state, my divinity, and my splendor;
likewise, my divine throne and my all-pervasiveness, just like my own. ||40||
And during the Madhyāvrata, I grant the state of being identical with me—that is, identity itself.
Here, in this half-month, I am full; this vow bestows the fruit of nourishment.
I shall grant the eternal, true fruit; let them accept it and acquire it!
This month of Puruṣottama is my most excellent month. (42)
The merit generated by that single day surpasses all other merits;
for while others are impermanent, this merit is eternal.
I am indeed the eternal deity, and the month is also mine, eternal;
my vow is eternal, so may you receive this eternal merit.
By him who has gratified his mother and gratified his father with devotion, may they receive eternal fruit through the grace of their mother and father. 45.
Having made whatever arrangements they desire, let them perform the vow of the middling [disciples];
I shall fulfill their intentions, whether they be appropriate or otherwise. (46)
Having caused the drum to be sounded in this manner, he maintained silence for a moment and then went forth,
taking the leaves, flowers, and fruits offered by the maiden.
The two maidens, having made their resolve for the vow on the day of the moon's midpoint,
went home and duly worshipped the Lord.
Having had a beautiful golden image of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa fashioned, they performed the invocation ceremony with the sixteen articles of worship. ||49||
Worship performed in due order is appropriate; first with milk and other substances, and then, having bathed [the deity] with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta), they caused it to be done. ||50||
Then they both bathed with water from sacred fords (tīrtha) and performed the ritual sprinkling;
thereafter, they washed their limbs with a cloth and put on [clean] garments. ||51||
Then they adorned themselves with ornaments, sandalwood paste, and collyrium,
and further embellished themselves with flower garlands and other such items.
They adorned Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa with the finest unguents and perfumed him with sandalwood paste and other fragrant substances.
They offered saffron, unbroken rice grains, tulasī leaves, and other items, as well as floral crests and ornaments, to him who was in the form of Puruṣottama.
They offered incense, lamps, excellent food offerings, sweetmeats such as milk-rice (pāyasa),
and fruit along with betel-leaf and lime.

They respectfully performed circumambulation, prostrated like a staff, offered an apology for any faults, presented the waving of lights (ārātrika), offered praise, and made an offering of handfuls of flowers.
Having offered the *arghya* and made the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*) for the attainment of the Supreme Person,
they both addressed him with repeated heartfelt prayers.
The state of maidenhood is indeed always appropriate in the abode of Brahman;
liberation there is indeed appropriate, adorned with divine states and the like.
May celibacy, which is the form of Brahman, and Brahman himself as the Supreme Lord, and Hari Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, be the protectors of us both. (59)
He is indeed the protector, the impeller, the supporter, the ordainer, and the sustainer;
he is the innate Lord, the Lord of the lords of all lords. ||60||
Kṛṣṇa is the Lord of the syllables, the Brahman-Lord, the Supreme Person; He is our Protector and Sustainer. Apart from Him, there is no other protector for us two.
O Lord of Compassion, Lord of Action, Lord of Effort, Bestower of Fruit!
O Lord of both Body and Self, lead me to the Imperishable, the Lord of All! 62.
O Your own maidservant, O Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa residing within my heart, O Inner Controller, O giver of the merit of vows, O You who are dear to the heart! 63.
O dweller in the heart, O knower of the heart, O knower of our inner feelings, fill our inner being! O Lord Kṛṣṇa, taking our hands, lead us quickly to the Imperishable. 64.
When, having praised him thus, they offered their own wounds as an oblation to his form,
at that moment the compassionate and beautiful one manifested there.
The youth Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Hari, possessed a divine form;
that person stood upon the back of an elephant, his every limb endowed with a celestial appearance.
The ends of whose hair are as brilliant as ten million flashes of lightning,
while from the roots they possess a lovely, wavy luster that is glossy and black.
His hair is full of wonder, beautified by its wavy style;
moreover, it is auspicious, being drawn back from behind toward the middle and the ends of his ears. 68.
And his forehead-slab is adorned with an upward-pointing line like the moon;
it is auspicious, possessing the beauty of the tips of the bow-like eyebrows, and it removes pride. (69)
On the forehead, the unbroken line of the *sadrekha* indicates the path to Brahman;
reaching the vicinity of the ears, it awakens one to both worlds. (70)
Both ears, adorned with the beauty of two ear-rings, are enchanting;
the two eyes, resembling beautiful red lotuses, are long with lovely lashes. (71)
There are beautiful lines, exceedingly subtle like lightning, extending to the tips of the ears, slightly curved, and filled with emotion that captivates the lover. (72)
"Come, come!"—this is indeed the expression of that which resides in the heart;
for the pair of eyes and cheeks, when deeply red and elevated, indicate a smile. (73)
His nose was beautiful, shaped like a sesame flower; his lips were deep red like ripe *bimba* fruit. (74)
A subtle, beautiful, and not too prominent line of beard shone upon him;
likewise, Hari’s neck was like a conch shell, his chest was well-developed, and his shoulders were broad and muscular. (75)
His two arms, like the coils of a serpent, serve as a resting place for rows of moon-like nails;
they are resplendent with the [auspicious] signs of the banner, the bow, the great fish, the arrow, and the svastika. (76)
The two hands of Hari, joined in añjali, are marked with the lines of the trident, the discus, and the ocean;
both hands consist of rows of hair and possess white and red colors.
His chest bore the Śrīvatsa mark, the Kaustubha gem, and lines of beauty like necklaces; his abdomen was graced by the three folds, and at his navel was the auspicious seat of Brahmā.
The waist is slender and well-concealed, filled with existence, consciousness, and bliss;
the beautiful thighs, resembling the trunks of elephants, are adorned with a line of hair. (79)
His knees are rounded, his shanks are well-developed yet slender, and he has three ankle-bones on each foot, which are prominent in the middle and bring about renown. (80)
O King, with sixteen lines marked by digits, his body was filled with splendor, nourished and equal in all its sixty-four parts, possessing the luster of the jewels on his fingernails. 81.
Both of those maidens, Preyasī and Śreyasī, beheld the supremely wonderful and beautiful form of Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa.
Having reached Śrī Puruṣottama there, they both rejoiced;
they both placed flower garlands around the neck of Hari. (83)
Both of them remained in his presence, their hearts moved by devotion; then Hari said to him, "By my vow and by your sincere disposition, O Lord... (84)
I lead you both to my own abode, the imperishable, which is perfectly full of bliss;
and by means of the state of identity with me, I lead you both into my very body.
Having spoken thus, the Blessed One vanished from that place at that very moment; for both of them became deeply distressed by his departure.
At midday, as well as in the evening and at night, they both performed such worship according to the prescribed rite and kept a vigil for Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa.
They performed divine dancing and singing at midnight;
meanwhile, the Great Lord quickly returned during the night.
White, pervaded by his own moonlight, Hari himself shone at night just as he had appeared, bringing about the welfare of all.
Knowing that Śrī Puruṣottama had arrived at their home for the festival, Dharma and Bhakti bowed to him, realizing that it was Śrī Hari who had come. ||90||
Having obtained Hari, the Supreme Person, as their beloved, the two daughters issued the command to take them to their own abode. ||9 1 ||
When one has accomplished all that was to be done and is established in the supremely perfected, resplendent, and imperishable abode,
both enjoyment and liberation are indeed renowned in that divine realm.
And for the sake of serving both Dharma and Bhakti, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa assumed two forms and offered them even in the house of his parents.
Where there is righteousness and devotion, there is both worldly enjoyment and liberation; these two exist in the world, and they also exist in the divine abode.
They both attained all eternal desires together with Brahmā;
thus indeed did they reach the abode of the Supreme Lord Śrī.
And whoever here is possessed of righteousness and devotion toward the Supreme Lord,
having attained both worldly enjoyment and liberation, rejoices together with Brahmā.
Having attained both the beloved and the supreme, he rejoices in the abode of the Imperishable;
O dear one, both the listener and the speaker of this obtain the full fruit of their vow.

Thus ends the three hundred and seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Attainment of Śrī Puruṣottama in the Imperishable Abode through the Vow on the Middle Tithi of the Month by Dharmā and Bhakti, the Mind-born Daughters of Preyasī and Śreyasī, and their Renown as Possessing Enjoyment and Liberation," within the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, in the first section concerning the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga, specifically the majesty of the month of Puruṣottama.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī, to how Vairājñī attained the state of Vairāja through her vow, she who is indeed the mother of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa. || 1 ||
The primordial person has as his son the Pradhāna-puruṣa;
he indeed has a son named Hiraṇyagarbha, who is Mahāviṣṇu.
From that, Virāj was born, the father of Vairāja and the creator;
his lifespan was indeed one hundred years according to the calculation of those years.
When it becomes full, it then undergoes destruction;
thereafter, another Vairāja arises and attains sovereignty over the world.
Thus, in this gradual process of creation, there is an infinite number of Vairājas,
day after day, through the continuous flow of succession during the day of Mahāviṣṇu.
Indeed, for each individual Vairāja Īśvara, there is a destruction within a single year of Mahāviṣṇu, occurring thirty-five and sixty [times].
For the Vairājas, there are exactly thirty-six thousand and five hundred years in their successive lifespans.
O beloved, I know all that pertains to the Vairājas;
now hear the account of this current Vairāja.
In the sovereign empire of Mahāviṣṇu, at the level of the creation of Īśvarī,
beyond the eight enclosures (aṣṭāvaraṇa), there indeed exists the Virāṭ Puruṣa prior to this [creation].
At the final moment of the final day of his own final year,
while the final piercing was occurring, at the very moment of the dissolution of the universe, he passed away.
There was a sovereign named Sahasrākṣa, a turner of the wheel;
that devoted Sahasrākṣa [ruled] over the earth and in Pātāla.
He always travels by means of a celestial chariot; he hears through the thread of the sky; he perceives by means of a transparent substance; and he touches by means of the swift wind.
In an instant, he performs the worldly affairs of all people;
for one endowed with all means of accomplishment, nothing remains to be gone to. (13)
While he remained in one house, his subjects situated in the four directions conducted their affairs as if they were right before him, just as they would know the weight on a touchstone.
The thousand-eyed Indra himself goes and comes at the proper time to the assembly of Brahmā in Satyaloka, which is filled with great beings.
It was likewise [honored] by the guardians of the directions, by the Manus, by the Sun and the Moon,
by the sages, by the great gods, and by universal monarchs.
There, at the first location, he did not obtain his own seat;
thus, impelled by the fault of such partiality within his heart, he [proceeded]. (17)

Having summoned those who possessed the knowledge of Brahman, he questioned them regarding spiritual prosperity: "How might one attain that supreme state which is even higher than the position of Brahmā? (18)
The Brahmins requested him: "Perform the most excellent sacrifices—the Agniṣṭoma, the Vājapeya, the Rājasūya, and the Vaiṣṇava. (19)

The Mahāraudra, the human sacrifice (naramedha), the horse sacrifice (vājimedha), the Vṛṣakratu, the Sautrāmaṇī, the Suteṣṭi, the fire-oblation (agnihotra), and the recitation of prayers (japa) and so forth. || 20 ||
Perform these sacrifices of great undertaking for a hundred years;
by that merit, O King, you shall attain the supreme station of Parameṣṭhin.
Your kingdom will certainly endure; therefore, perform those sacrifices.
Upon the completion of a hundred [years], you shall attain the station of Indra, and upon a thousand, the realm of the Sun.

For ten thousand years there is a steady reign; for a hundred thousand years is the station of Brahmā; and when ten million sacrifices are completed, one attains the state of the hundred-faced Brahmā.
When the second half of the sacrifice is completed, the station of Vairāja is attained;
yet neither such longevity nor such an opportunity exists for anyone here in this world-egg (golaka).
Therefore, O King, you should enjoy what has been given by him and remain peaceful;
for the end of the demoness of craving is not attained through enjoyment.
Having fully experienced all that is obtained and enjoyed right here,
and having utterly exhausted the great defects of passion and hatred, bring about what is beneficial.
Thinking, "There is someone greater than I in fortune, intellect, or even in social standing," one will never attain happiness anywhere. (27)
"I am the Great Self, filled with the bliss of Hari"—thinking thus, there shall indeed be no suffering born from the defects of thirst and the like;
nor should one even consider it a sorrow upon seeing the greater suffering of others. (28)

That happiness which is obtained through what one has earned by oneself is considered to be the giver of peace. But he who develops a sense of sufficiency regarding things that have come to him by chance or through effort, shall always be happy in this world. (29–30)
Indeed, you possess a firm empire over the three worlds, unassailable by any teacher;
if peace is not attained through that, what greater [peace] could there be?
For one who perceives "this is mine" and "that is another," there is nowhere any happiness.

However, O King, throughout the entire world of māyā— whether in the primordial nature (prakṛti), its transformations (vikṛti), or in effects (kārya)— there exists everywhere and in every way a gradation of degrees;
for nowhere has supreme peace been attained by anyone.
No one shall attain peace if there be a lord of primordial nature (prakṛti), or even a lord of the primary matter (pradhāna); what further talk can there be of others here, O King? (34)
"Therefore, O King, attain peace; do not increase your craving, O Lord. Having thus instructed him, the Brahmins, who see the further shore, desisted. (35)
But the thousand-eyed Indra, without even cutting off those ears,
caused him to perform many most magnificent sacrifices according to the rules every year.
By these means, he indeed attained the merit acquired by a hundred Brahmās;
then, in the final year of his life, during the intercalary month (adhimāsa) in the dark fortnight, ||37||
On the morning of the first day of the lunar fortnight, O King, he heard the drum of Hari,
as the thousand-eyed Indra was engaged in sacrifices.
In the month of Puruṣottama, when the moon had entered the asterism Śravaṇa, during the second intercalary month, on the first day of the lunar fortnight (pratipad).
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord of All, Śrī Puruṣottama, shall grant whatever is desired by anyone, even that which is unattainable in ten million kalpas. (40)
"That which cannot be obtained even through ten million sacrifices or ten million gifts, I bestow here;
in this vow, the king should give charity according to his capacity, and my worship should be performed with whatever offerings are available. (41)
Food should be given to me with appropriate grains and flavorful juices;
(42) a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) should be bestowed upon me with wealth according to one's faith.
One should perform service for others for the sake of pleasing Puruṣottama. (43)
If the Emperor, the sovereign of the fourteen worlds, were to worship me, Kṛṣṇa, according to his wealth with the most excellent of offerings;
and if, having personally performed his morning bath, he were to bathe me with water containing the five jewels; [44]
And one should perform the cleansing of the teeth with water containing fragrant heartwood.
One should offer fragrant unguent and a fresh tooth-stick;
one should perform the cleansing of the tongue and other rites with mouthfuls of fragrant water. || 46 ||

The king should cause my purification and other rites to be performed with the finest essences of flower juices and fragrant waters; he should cause the cleansing of my hands and so forth to be carried out. 47.
Then, one should effect the purification of the limbs with very fragrant clay smeared with sandalwood, and subsequently bathe [the image] with scented water and pure water.
Then one should bathe [the deity] with milk, curd, honey, sugar, and nectars, as well as with water accompanied by the single-syllable mantra.
The king should have him massaged with the finest fragrant oils,
bathe him with waters from sacred fords, and wipe away the water with garments.
Then, one should adorn me with very fine and extremely costly excellent gold, silver, and moon-disc ornaments, as well as soft, variegated, and exceedingly delicate garments.
With golden crowns worthy of a royal throne, bracelets and other ornaments, golden rings, chains and the like, earrings, necklaces, and crest-jewels; ||5 2||
With more than ten million precious gems, pearls, and woven ornaments, as well as topazes,
corals, lapis lazuli, and sun-crystals.
With moonstones, emeralds, rubies, and likewise with crystals; with diamonds, emeralds, pearls, and excellent rubies.
With sapphire flower-rows, with karketana and bhīṣmaka gems, with pulaka, rudhira, gold, and silver ornaments as well. ||55||
One should worship the Supreme Lord with ornaments and garlands of jewels produced from the ocean, from mines, from fire, and likewise from the sky. 56.
And with woolen cloths of the highest quality, as well as others made of cotton, silk, bark, gold, resin, and indeed those fashioned from tree-bark. ||57||
One should adorn Kṛṣṇa with garments and with fragrant oils;
one should also rub him with collyrium, fresh butter, and fragrant substances for massaging.
One should cause the black [deity] to be perfumed with musk, sandalwood, and so forth;
one should worship him with camphor mixed with saffron filaments, using forehead marks (tilaka) and other offerings.
With saffron, unbroken grains of rice, and flowers— namely golden campaka, kunda,
pārijāta, land-lotuses, water-lilies, and tulasī leaves— ||60||
One should worship the Lord with kalpa-tree flowers and blossoms from golden creepers;
one should cause Him to prosper with golden unbroken rice grains and offer garlands of necklaces.
One should color with pigments the palms of the hands, the soles of the feet, the cheeks, the temples reaching to the ears, the arms, the shanks, the nails, and the lips of Hari.
His feet possess the luster of sandals bound with gold, gems, and jewels;
his hands are provided with leather guards, staffs, clusters of flowers, and chains.
One should beautify it with a yellow *tilaka* and cause a red moon to be fashioned;
one should also provide incense, lamps, and food, one hundred and eight times.
One should offer what is sour, sweet, salty, pungent, bitter, and astringent—whatever is pleasant to the taste and desired—as well as that which is delicious and fragrant. ||65||
Eatables, soft foods, foods to be sucked, foods to be licked, and even foods to be sipped;
grains, vegetables, pulses, cooked rice, and excellent fruits—[all these were provided]. (66)
The king should cause to be given milk-rice prepared with gold, endowed with excellent flavors, rich in nectar-like essence, sweet, and refined.
The king should offer to Hari mouth-perfumes, powders, betel, other chewing substances, and other stimulating items. (68)
The king should quickly offer to Hari various cooling drinks, as well as diverse intoxicating beverages enriched with powdered flavors.

And songs were performed by the queens, accompanied by the sounds of cymbals and other instruments, along with dances filled with the suggested aesthetic flavors (*rasa*) of gestures (*hāva*), emotional states (*bhāva*), and the like. (70)
The king should have [the rite] performed by his female companions and cause it to increase through many meditative visualizations,
using parched grain, sandalwood powder, unbroken rice, and golden grains.

One should honor the deity again and again with precious gems and other offerings; one should cause cries of victory to be proclaimed and perform the lustration ceremony (nīrājana) at dawn and at night.
With hundreds and thousands of wicks, camphor, and other substances,
he reverently performed seven circumambulations from the waist up and likewise seven from the head down.
Then one should move through seven coils, each having seven wheels,
and then through seven waves extending upwards and downwards.
One should rotate the coils on the two feet toward Hari in succession;
then, with a cloth, one should rotate the three coils toward Hari.
Then, one should cause the [deity] to descend from the swing with water from the conch;
one should perform the ārārtika offering three times with that water. ||76||
Then one should offer incense to the Supreme Lord three times, while sounding the bell and playing other musical instruments as well. (77)
One should sound the dundubhi, jhallarī, ghaṇṭā, and paṭaha drums loudly;
thereafter, one should perform praise, prostration, and a prayer while lying flat like a staff (daṇḍavat). ||78||
Having performed circumambulation and other rites, he should then offer a handful of flowers;
thus the sovereign should worship in the morning, at midday, and at night.
Having adorned his excellent army and having placed Hari upon a celestial chariot, an elephant, or a carriage,
he should parade him through the capital, gardens, and other such places.
The people should honor Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the supreme among men;
then, having brought him back to the royal palace, they should offer him water and other services.
The king should provide rest through such means as massaging the feet and so forth,
and for the sake of pleasing the Blessed One, he should indeed bestow abundant gifts.
The gift of elephants, the gift of horses, the gift of camels and mares, the gift of bulls and goats, and the gift of cows and peacocks. ||83||
The gift of a parrot, the gift of a maina bird, as well as the gift of male and female servants and the gift of daughters to men; ||84||
One should also give gifts of vehicles, mounts, and animals;
one should cause excellent items such as blankets, garments, and ornaments to be given.
He saw dwellings, cities, fields, and likewise mountains;
lakes, mines, quarries, and forest regions as well. ||86||
One should give gifts of food and clothing to the twice-born and to the destitute;
likewise, one should bestow trees, creepers, fields, and gardens.
One should give rivers and streams, as well as dug-out reservoirs; one bestows heaven, great splendor, austerity, the world of truth, and the depths of the nether regions. ||88||
One should cause [the recipient] to receive a country, a region, a district, a kingdom, or an island;
if the giver is a leader of the universe (Brahmāṇḍanetā), the receiver should likewise be so. (89)

If one has received [the gift] for a thousand years and, having resolved it, offers it to Hari, [then] the Lord is the sustainer of the universe, the nourisher of the universe, and the protector of the universe. 90.
Hari, hungry for meditation, certainly grasps it—of this there is no doubt;
he would bestow the crown of sovereignty, as well as a queen and sons. (9.1)
One should give everything to Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Soul who bestows happiness;
indeed, one should offer treasuries, armies, and kingdoms to Śrī Keśava.
One should give according to one's faith to a qualified recipient who possesses desire;
one should give to a worthy vessel, and one should also give abundantly to women.
He should provide a livelihood for young women, widows, and virtuous wives; he should give food to chaste women, female yogis, and beggars. (94)
He should satisfy the gods and humans of the three worlds with their shares of the sacrifice, and he should gratify all living beings of the lineage of Kaśyapa with food and water. 95.
The king may give all of this, or he may give even one;
provided he does not practice stinginess regarding his wealth, and gives with faith. (96)
The gift of a bronze vessel-casket and the gift of a golden vessel-casket, joined with eight enclosures and containing fourteen petals within. (97)
One should offer a casket filled with gold and jewels, as well as other caskets;
Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa grants the fruit of that entirely according to one's desire.

If one gives during this additional month, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama) will indeed grant eternal rewards that bestow great satisfaction; whether with desire or without desire, I shall grant them. 99.
Let them perform acts of charity, bestow wealth, and cast it into the worthy vessel with the realization of the Blessed One;
Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa alone is the giver, and I too grant the kingdom of Vairāja.
Thus does the drum speak when the month of Śrī Puruṣottama arrives;
the thousand-eyed Indra indeed hears that bestower of prosperity on the first lunar day.
At dawn, that pure king, having heard about the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa from Dundubhi and having bowed down to him, worshipped him. || 102 ||
Just as it was proclaimed by Dundubhi and according to the king's own faith,
so did the king perform everything— the worship and the ritual dismissal.
Then, in the assembly of the world of Brahmā, Satyaloka, he summoned that twice-born man and gave a gift in the morning to that Brahmin who was devoted to his wife.
O you of Brahmic form, best of the twice-born, you alone are the Supreme Person; O soul presiding over the intercalary month, you are the embodied bestower of fruits.
"Having heard the sound of the drum, I shall indeed observe a vow today; for the sake of attaining the state of Vairāja, accept this gift so that it may be meaningful. (106)
"I am the king of the fourteen worlds, and I myself grant [this],
O twice-born one, in the presence of the witness that is the water of the celestial river, within the assembly of Brahmā."
"I grant fourteen worlds for the attainment of the fruit;
they have been given and accepted," the best of the twice-born replied.
Then, in the form of one devoted to his wife, the Blessed One, Puruṣottama,
suddenly manifested, possessing a splendor like that of ten million suns.
Laughing, Puruṣottama said to that thousand-eyed one:
"O King, a gift has been obtained by me in every respect through the form of a twice-born."
The fruit granted by me to you is the eternal station of Vairāja;
at the end of your life, you shall attain that sovereign state of Vairāja.
Having thus granted him grace and revealed his form to the king,
he suddenly vanished while touching the king’s head.
The king performed the vow and the entire worship with faith;
he gave the gift of the Brahmāṇḍa, wherein nothing whatsoever remained.
He himself became a servant and a slave to that brahmin;
at the end of the year, the thousand-eyed Indra attained perfection through his meditative absorption.
One perceives before oneself the Vairāja station which was created by one's own [merit]; for indeed, that is seen when the previous Vairāja state has passed away and is near at hand. || 1.15 ||
Thus, by that high-souled king who lived in this manner,
the royal body was eventually cast off through the sequence of time and the power of destiny.
Leaving behind this physical body, which was like that of the thousand-eyed Indra,
he departed by the divine path to that place created by Īśa where it exists.
He, the thousand-eyed one, attained the sovereign state of Vairāja,
who is today the lotus-navelled Lord, the father of Brahmā.
Thus, by virtue of his observance of the vow on that day, he attained the universal sovereignty of Vairāja,
as well as the status of Hiranyagarbha and other lordships in abundance.
There, he who was Nārāyaṇa became that consecrated king;
from whose lotus Brahmā arose, and from whose forehead the Lord of Śivā [Śiva] appeared.
He from whose heart Viṣṇu indeed [arose], and from whose belly this entire world [emerged]—
he is truly this king Sahasrākṣa by the power of his vow.
Through true devotion to Puruṣottama, Nārāyaṇa was born as the Virāṭ;
thus, on the first day (pratipad) of the middle of the intercalary month.
O beloved Padmaja, the fruit resulting from the observance of vows, worship, and charity has been told to you; when Śrī Hari is pleased therein, what indeed will he not bestow?
O Lakṣmī, the one who causes this to be heard and even the one who composes its recitation shall obtain such a fruit; I declare this, O Puruṣottama.
One who is an atheist, lacking faith, a speaker of falsehood, a defiler,
and a reviler of me, shall obtain neither grace nor fruit.

Thus ends the three hundred and eighth chapter, titled "The Description of how, in the primordial creation, after King Sahasrākṣa—the sovereign of the entire earth—had performed thousands of sacrifices, he attained the station of Vairāja-Nārāyaṇa through the vows, gifts, and other rites on the first day of the bright fortnight of the month of Puruṣottama," in the section concerning the greatness of the month of Puruṣottama within the first book, the *Kṛtayuga-santāna*, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī, to this divine and captivating narrative of what occurred in the past: prior to this present Brahmā, there was another Brahmā a hundred years earlier. (1)
At that time, in the final moment within the sphere of Brahmā,
the king named Sarvahuta on earth reached the state of being about to enter his end.
He was a devotee of the Blessed One, intent upon my worship;
he had surrendered all his possessions for my sake and dedicated his mind to me for my sake. (3)
She wore my necklace, my garland, and my auspicious forehead mark;
she partook of my food, which purifies the self through my grace.
He undertook a vow for the four-month period, characterized by great generosity throughout the seven continents, the various regions, and the lands of the ocean islands.
"Wherever my kingdom may be, in every place there, my food must indeed be given away, and water must certainly be drunk by me. (6)
"Until they are satisfied, the groups of monks must eat from my own [portion];
likewise, the Brahmins and the Kṣatriya sages must eat from mine. (7)
Likewise, my food should be eaten by Vaiśyas, sages, and Śūdras who are full of devotion, as well as by celibate students and forest-dwellers in every way.
By ascetics, virtuous men, those who have renounced the world, and likewise by chaste women;
by the destitute, those resembling guests, performers of sacrifice, and worshippers of the gods.
Those seeking food, the miserly, servants, and those deprived of a livelihood—only my food should be eaten by them, and only my water should be drunk. (10)
"My garments are to be worn by me alone; they must not be taken by anyone else.
For that purpose, I have stationed [guards] at every location throughout the kingdom at every moment. (11)
Food-donations, garments, and canopies were established everywhere;
service-stations were set up, and attendants were stationed at every location.
One who is hungry shall be a vessel for food, one who is thirsty a vessel for water, and one who is naked a vessel for clothing; by him, my gift shall be joyfully accepted. (13)
May he whose heart is miserly and who has craving in his mind also take my food and water for the sake of destroying that craving and other such afflictions. (14)
Thus was it proclaimed by him, written upon the wall and wooden panels:
"During my four-month retreat, food, fruit, water, and likewise clothing [shall be provided]. (15)
"Abundant and worthy of being accepted, yet not to be grasped by other [unworthy] Dharma-bhikṣus"—
thus did it occur to that king, who was like a sacrificial fire into which all offerings were poured.
Whatever is considered meritorious in the Agnihotra sacrifice and other sacrifices, as well as the offering of articles for the worship of the gods—of that indeed [he is the master]. (17)
The expenditure for students in the granting of knowledge is like that for cattle in grass;
and for dogs and other domestic animals and birds, it is like a handful of grain.
Water, clothing, and likewise other excellent articles were provided as required; thus, for all guests, there was that which brings satisfaction, just like a universal sacrifice (sarvahuta).
In villages, hamlets, and inhabited places; in fields, cowherd settlements, and on riverbanks;
in forests, wildernesses, and mountains; and on islands, in the ocean, and in desolate battlefields. ||20||
In the foothills, in the cities, in the royal retreats, and in the sacrificial grounds—
everywhere indeed, for King Sarvahuta, there were excellent sacrificial sessions and magnificent acts of charity.
At the junctions of the carriage-roads between villages, at the meeting points of forest paths,
and at the landing-stages for crossing rivers and streams, sacrificial sessions were established by that king.
At the borders, in the regions of deep ravines, on the roads of chariots, in the far reaches of the quarters,
at sacred fords, and at places frequented by those on pilgrimage— there were the sacrificial offerings of King Hutāśana.
The name of that one who has offered all oblations is proclaimed in every direction by the gods at morning, evening, and midday.
His fame is indeed sung of in truth, in austerity, among his own people, in the great heaven, on earth, and also in the netherworlds.
The gods, the sages, the Daityas, and other embodied beings as well,
having assumed forms such as swans and others, went indeed to witness the universal sacrifice.
They attained supreme wonder upon seeing the king, radiant with merit, adorned by a countenance resplendent with an exceedingly brilliant halo.
From afar, all the gods shone with exceeding splendor;
however, having gone near him, they became devoid of luster.
Thus, that king, whose majesty was merit, who made the purpose of all sacrifices meaningful, who resembled fire, and who was a devotee who humbled the pride of the gods, became [renowned]. (29)
Honored by all the gods and seated upon half of Indra’s throne,
though worshipped even by the guardians of the quarters, he did not experience even the slightest astonishment.
The wife of that very man, who was devoid of passion, was devoted to her husband;
she was endowed with the quality of magnanimity and was known by the name Gaurtambharā.
Even more endowed with supreme beauty than the goddesses, she was exceedingly beautiful in her physical form and attire;
she could assume any form at will, enjoyed all pleasures, and was supremely virtuous in acting according to her own desire.
She stands behind the goddesses in the assembly of the god of gods;
there, for a moment, she becomes bashful and lowers her face. (33)
She said to her own master: "I shall sit behind;
as before, however, remain on the excellent seat—do that. (34)
O Lord, O King, act in such a way that Indrāṇī, Vāruṇī, Sauryā, Cāndrī, and the wives of other gods and asuras shall bow down to me. (35)
The king said to his virtuous queen: "O beloved, you are human;
yet even there, among the host of gods, our residence is most exceedingly great. (36)
Do not harbor desire for the human realm, O auspicious lady, for that [state] cannot be attained there;
nevertheless, through an abundance of merit, it may perhaps be realized. (37)
I shall make an effort to offer praise in the presence of Nārāyaṇa;
yet even when such union is attained, thirst will not indeed be extinguished.
The queen constantly reminds the king of his word at the proper time, and the king, for his part, awaits the arrival of the opportune moment for its fulfillment. (39)
Once, on the morning of the second day of the dark fortnight of the intercalary month, he had bathed and was indeed still engaged in the worship of the deity. (40)
The learned Queen Goṛtambharā also heard the delightful Dundubhi drum proclaiming the words of Hari, as did Sarvahuta. (41)
Both remained fixed in their minds upon that word with steadfastness;
they heard the heart-stirring proclamation of the drum.
I am the month Śrī Puruṣottama, the bestower of desired objects upon those people who observe the vow on the second day of the intercalary month. ||43||
Those who, having practiced eating once a day, or eating only at night, or subsisting on fruits, or drinking only water, or even subsisting on air, shall perform this vow; ||44||
To them I shall give sons, wives, wealth, houses, and so forth;
as well as vehicles, mounts, elephants, and the like, along with water, fields, lands, and other such things. (45)
A fragment, an island, and the ocean; a terrestrial kingdom and the circle of the earth;
heaven, the world of men, the world of heat, and the world of truth; and that which belongs to Indra, the Sun, and the Moon. 46.
I shall grant you sovereignty over Sāmrājya, Atala, Pātālaka, and Rasātala,
as well as the supreme lordship over the fourteen worlds.
The domain of Varuṇa, that of Agni, that of Īśa, and likewise that of Yama which is purifying, as well as that of Kubera and Nairṛta— these are the great stations of the guardians of the quarters.
I shall grant the status of a world-protector, as well as the position of Vāsava, the circle of planets,
the state of Naidheya, Raudra, Māruta, and the vault of heaven.
The eightfold supernatural powers (siddhis) and the quality of creating the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa) are given as service;
likewise, the capacity for protection and preservation is granted by me to the one who observes my vow.
I am the deity of the intercalary month, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person.
Even for a very slight hardship undergone for my sake, I shall grant you infinite fruit.
That which I do not give in another month, I give here in abundance;
here I am a giver out of compassion, and indeed a giver by my own will.
To him who truly bears my word upon his head, I grant a gift,
or a reward, as a token of my favor.
An exchange is not the proper principle here; rather, my principle here is compassion.
Out of compassion, I myself, as the Master, bestow everything without exception.
"I bestow ten millionfold, I bestow infinitely;
therefore, let them receive from that Supreme Person exactly as they have intended. (55)
Thus did Śuśruṣatī and Goṛtambharā, the daughter of Sarvahuta, listen;
having bowed to Dundubhi, they then worshipped him with flowers. (56)
But Dundubhi having gone elsewhere, the couple reflected upon the Lord;
they pondered, "Where else will we obtain our desired object? (57)
Then Sarvahuta said to Queen Gaurtambharā:
"O Goddess, it has been heard that through the vow of the second [lunar day], the desired goal is attained. (58)
Your mind is capable of remaining in the most exalted position of worship among all the celestial women dwelling on the fourteen levels. (59)
"For the sake of attaining that, a vow must be performed by us two so that it may bear fruit.
Dundubhi said to him: "Even in a small [vow], the fruit is indeed abundant."
"I shall become Brahmā; you become my companion.
You shall be Brahmāṇī, my wife, and indeed the mother of the celestial women."
That being so, your purpose here shall be fully accomplished;
the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa will grant you the fruit of your vow.
Having thus formed their resolve, they performed the vow with devotion;
having bathed in the morning and meditated upon Hari, they had a golden image fashioned.
Having invoked the supreme deity Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Puruṣottama, into the image there, and having offered water for sipping, a seat, and water for the feet; ||64||
And those two gave him water for sipping from the water of the sacred ford,
as well as milk, thick curd, ghee, and honey.
Then, having bathed them with sugar,
they caused them to be washed with pure, fragrant water mixed with sandalwood.
They cleansed Hari with garments and adorned him with golden robes, ornaments, and the finest jewels and gems. (67)
With necklaces, sandalwood scents, liquid extracts, and likewise heart-essences;
with collyriums, the best of oils, flowers, saffron, and rice grains. ||68||
They both worshipped Kṛṣṇa with crowns, bracelets, and other ornaments, as well as with necklaces of excellent gems and jewels, parasols, chowries, and staffs. ||69||
With incense, lamps, excellent food offerings, fruits, betel leaves, and aromatic powders,
the two caused Śrī Hari, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), to attain satisfaction.
Having offered water along with musical instruments, the two performed the lustration ceremony (nīrājana);
they then respectfully performed circumambulations, hymns of praise, and prostrations.
O Keśava, they both prayed to the Lord with this vow:
"Be gracious, O Soul of the Universe; accept this water-offering (arghya) along with the fruit and other gifts. (72)
Thinking thus, they both offered a handful of flowers along with gold for the sake of the fruit; they then performed worship and rendered service.
Likewise, at midday as well, both performed the worship and other rites;
having worshipped the Lord of Gods in the evening, they performed the *ārātrika* ceremony at night.
They kept a vigil, holding a festival of instrumental music, dance, and songs;
they gave gifts to Kṛṣṇa and presented him with a golden throne.
Adorned with umbrellas, chowries, canes, and other ornaments, it was exceedingly brilliant;
it shone with decorations consisting of strings of jewels, gems, and fine pearls.
And they also gave a dwelling-place consisting of fourteen stories, adorned with golden water-jars, vessels, and various elegant furnishings. (77)
Wherever there is a house for the sacred fire, that is a home of the essence of merit, adorned by beds, coverlets, food, and other such things, as well as by its very site. (78)
There was a hall for the libations to the ancestors, where there was a noble house for gifts,
and also a treasury filled with jewels, gems, and other treasures.
And the house, consisting of both sentient and insentient beings, was filled with vehicles and carriages, and was provided with male and female servants, groves, gardens, rivers, and streams. (80)
There was a house on the ground, which served as a rest-house, as well as a house for amorous pleasure and likewise a house for meals. ||81||
Likewise, there was a bathing chamber and a well-guarded subterranean vault of great excellence;
and there was a house containing the trees of the Kalpa and a stable for cows.
Where all these and other such palaces exist,
that great mansion stands, beautifully adorned and surrounded by a wall.
The two of them indeed offered it as an act of dedication to Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa;
at that very moment, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), arrived there.
He spoke to them: "I am pleased with your gift and your vow;
showing compassion, I grant this—choose a boon. (85)
There the couple said: "O Lord, grant us the supreme state of Brahmā, and thereafter, your own imperishable and eternal abode of liberation. (86)
"So be it," Hari said, and he spoke thus to Gaurtambharā:
"In the future, at the sacred site of Puṣkara on earth, there shall indeed be a king of the Kṣatriya caste. (87)
The son of Virāṭa, named Gāyatra, will indeed become the king of the Ābhīras and cowherds who dwell in the Puṣkara forest. (88)
His wife shall be the queen named Ṛṣī, the daughter of Puṣkara;
from those two shall be born a beautiful daughter, a maiden named after the Ṛṣis. (89)
O future Gopī, you shall become this very Gomatī, Go-Ṛtambharā, and Gāyatrī, performing service to Gokula there. (90)
This King Sarvahuta shall become Brahmā there;
and in the first age, he will go to Puṣkara for the sake of sacrifice.
Together with the gods, sages, seers, ancestors, and others, as well as with eighty-four lakhs of human beings dwelling on that level, the Creator of the Universe [remained].
Today he will perform the primordial sacrifice for the sake of setting the three worlds in motion; for when the fires have been kindled and the time for initiation has arrived— (93)
Summoned by the Adhvaryu priest, Sāvitrī, who was long-winded in her deliberations, prepared herself but did not arrive at the sacrificial ground at that time. ||94||
Brahmā, having summoned Śakra, will say:
"O Śakra, quickly bring another wife for my sake. (95)
"Act quickly so that the sacrifice proceeds without being deficient in time; bring a woman here to serve as a wife. (96)
Thus addressed, Śakra spoke to the daughter of Gāyatrī-Rāja:
"He will indeed take you away, for you have come to behold the sacrificial ground."
That creator of the universe will take as his wife, by the Gāndharva rite of marriage, the beautiful and youthful maiden Gāyatrī, the daughter of the Ṛṣis.
Then he will commence the priestly office with Brahmins who have mastered the Vedas;
that sacrifice shall indeed take place at Puṣkara for a thousand days.
From that time forward, you shall be Gāyatrī, the consort of Brahmā;
you shall be the Mother of the World, the Mother of the Vedas, and the Mother of Creation. || 100 ||
O Ṛtambharā, you shall become worthy of all worship, worthy of all honor, and one whose prayers are recited by the twice-born; you shall be a bestower of Brahman and a consort of Brahman.
