Having established a boundary as a barrier and hurled his wheel of great power,
he brought about the destruction of thousands of billions of Dānavas.
Then the gods and humans indeed attained happiness in that place;
thus was that sacred field named Lohārgala created by me. (85)
Thus, I have established the auspicious holy site of Lohārgala-kuṇḍa;
there, a white horse should indeed be given as a gift, for it bestows heaven.
Now, there is the Pañcasaras Kuṇḍa, a sacred ford that grants access to the world of the Gandharvas;
here four streams fall down, white as conch shells and bestowing liberation.
Then there is the Nārada-kuṇḍa, a sacred bathing place with five streams;
and then the Vasiṣṭha-kuṇḍa, a sacred bathing place with three streams. ||88||
The holy ford of Pañcakuṇḍa, endowed with five streams, bestows great merit;
as does the Saptarṣikuṇḍa ford, where seven streams descend. ||89||
There is the Śarabhaṅga-kuṇḍa Tīrtha, joined by the Śarabhaṅgā River;
and the Agnisaras-named Kuṇḍa Tīrtha, which bestows the abode of Fire.
The Bṛhaspatikuṇḍa tīrtha has one stream flowing from the snow;
the Vaiśvānarakuṇḍa tīrtha has one stream flowing from the snow. ||9 1 ||
At the Kārttikeyakuṇḍa tīrtha, fifteen excellent streams fall from the Himavat mountain; by bathing there, they bestow merit.
The sacred field known as Umākuṇḍa is where Gaurī went to take birth;
having bathed there, one should indeed behold Gaurī, and he rejoices in the world of Gaurī. (93)
Indeed, at the pool of Maheśvara where Umā was wedded, one who bathes there and is devoted to Rudra goes to the world of Rudra. 94.
And there is the famous Brahmakuṇḍa, from which the Vedas arose;
and from Himālaya fall the four streams of the Vedas. ||95||
In the east it is white, in the north golden, in the west blue-colored, and in the south it has the luster of an indragopa insect; these are the four streams of the Vedas. (96)
Having bathed there, one attains the world of Brahmā; of this there is no doubt.
Such is the sacred field of Lohārgala, measuring twenty-five yojanas.
By me the divine Himalaya was made the source of sacred fords, from which flow rivers that purify and grant liberation to men. 8.
The gods dwell there, and the sages dwell there as well;
O daughter of the ocean, I dwell there for the sake of the welfare of the worlds.
Those people who have performed bathing, giving, and religious duties at each of those sacred fords certainly attain heaven and liberation, always by my grace.

Thus ends the three hundred and forty-second chapter, titled “The Description of the Holy Tirthas, beginning with Rurukṣetra, Ṛṣīkega, Niṣkramaṇa, Pañcapada, Brahmakṣetra, Koṭivaṭa, Viṣṇusaras, Svāmivarāhakṣetra, Pañcāsama, Bhṛgukuṇḍa, Maṇikuṇḍa, Lohārgala, the Five Lakes, and the Kuṇḍas of Nārada, Vasiṣṭha, the Seven Sages, Śarabhaṅga, Agni, Bṛhaspati, Vaiśvānara, Kārttikeya, Umā, Maheśvara, Brahmā, and others,” in the first section on the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga in the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Lakṣmī said:
O eternal Sun of primordial knowledge, witness of all,
you alone are the creator of all worlds and always the performer of sacred rites.
Through your yoga, even insentient earth and water become conscious and truly deliver embodied beings; thus, you alone are the supreme sacred ford (tīrtha).
In this world, upon the acquisition of a body by living beings, the attainment of liberation is considered the great gain;
without liberation, all those who have acquired a body are merely following the path to death.
Vṛndāvana, Māthura, the eternal Śālagrāma,
Tulasī, Kṣetrapati, and so forth— these ancient [sacred sites] have been described by you.
Tell me, O Lord, how many manifestations have been obtained by you there?
And tell me, O Lord, how many more will be obtained, and on what part of the earth?
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: O Lakṣmī, indeed my manifestations are innumerable,
occurring among humans, gods, animals, beasts, and birds.
They exist in abundance among aquatic creatures, forest-dwellers, sages, virtuous people, seers, the good, and chaste women.
O Lotus-born One, in every four ages I manifest upon the earth in the regions of Vṛndāvana, in the lands of Mathurā, and on the banks of the Yamunā.
I wander and I dwell like the bringer of destruction to the Daityas;
there are one hundred and five Nārāyaṇas who recline upon the waters.
There are thirty forms of Kamaṭha, twenty forms of Matsya,
one hundred and eight Gopālas, and Buddhas exist by the thousands.
There were thirty Paraśurāmas and one hundred and one Rāmas;
O my beloved, there have been other incarnations as well, occurring according to the requirements of their tasks.
Indeed, many cosmic eggs and many Daityas and Dānavas have arisen either together with you or entirely on their own. (12)
Indeed, the gods and ascetics are also innumerable, yet they are possessed of desires;
[I am here] for the destruction of the suffering of the afflicted and for the attainment of wealth by those who seek it.
To fulfill the desires of those who possess longing, I manifest in various places:
in some instances as a partial incarnation, in others as a complete one, and in others through the form of divine possession.
In some places, in some way, he appears as a partial incarnation (kalā), in other places in the form of divine power (vibhūti);
likewise, he appears in the form of a holy man, in the form of a king, and in the form of a true guru.
I indeed manifest in the form of Vyāsa and in the form of the wise;
I alone am Viṣṇu, dwelling in the midst of the circle of the liberated.
He took birth many times in Vṛndāvana and Mathurā;
for Mathurā-kṣetra is the foremost of all sacred sites (tīrthas). || 17 ||
In age after age, I am born again and again on the banks of the Yamunā in the form of Kṛṣṇa, fulfilling the millions of desires of my male and female servants.
Drawn by the desire, longing, and devotion of infinite women of creation, I manifest myself in the form of a king, the destroyer of the pride of ten million desires. (19)
Vasu is my father and the Goddess is my mother; Sukarṣaṇa is my brother.
Whether others exist or do not exist, I dwell together with these.
But in the first Dvāpara age, O beloved, I appeared as a twin with Saṃkarṣaṇa, born of Vasudeva and Devakī.
At that time, there were indeed asuras born of the lineage of Kālanemi there;
I, Kṛṣṇa, the husband of the daughter of the Earth, slew them all.
At that time, you were the daughter of the Wind-god named Kamalā, my beloved;
and in the first Dvāpara age, I was Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Kamalā.
He was the destroyer of the descendants of Kālanaimeya in the city of Mathurā;
from that time forth, the sacred field of Mathurā became supremely purifying. (24)
O beloved, my soles remain pure at all times;
beyond that, my manifestations are thousands in number.
O lotus-eyed one, I do not count their end, whether here or elsewhere.
And there will be incarnations; men shall proclaim them. ||26||
And the Vyāsas will describe them as appropriate for the sake of liberation.
Listen, O beloved, to that sacred and most excellent Mathurā-kṣetra. 27.
Neither in heaven nor in the netherworld, nor at any sacred ford, is there a place equal to Mathurā;
that birthplace of mine is always delightful and entirely divine. (28)
O beloved, by dwelling in this place, humans as well as other living beings attain liberation in heaven, for this ground of mine is like Goloka.
The fruit that is eternally obtained at Prayāga on the full moon of Māgha in the waters of Yamunā,
and the fruit of a thousand years in Kāśī, is indeed obtained here in a single day.
Indeed, the fruit that is obtained at Puṣkara on the full moon of Kārtika is attained here in a mere moment.
Those deluded by illusion wander elsewhere after abandoning Mathurā;
yet even by merely hearing of Mathurā, the multitudes of their sins are dissolved.
Whatever holy fords, sacred fields, lakes,
rivers, streams, cities, forests, and groves exist upon the earth,
they all come to Mathurā when Janārdana has fallen asleep in the month of Āṣāḍha.

Through a śrāddha performed in the district of Mathurā, the ancestors remain satisfied for a yuga; those people who dwell in Mathurā go to my own abode at the time of death, especially at Kubjāmraka and Saukarava, which is the place of my birth. (34)
For those who dwell [in this way], liberation is certain even without Sāṃkhya or Yoga.
Men who give food and clothing are liberated; of this there is no doubt.
O lady of excellent limbs, I shall become [thus] when the Dvāpara Yuga has arrived.
I am Kṛṣṇa, the destroyer of Daityas, born in the lineage of Yayāti;
there, the Yamunā, the beloved daughter of Vaivasvata, flows beautifully,
and having reached the Gaṅgā at Prayāga, she proceeds as the Triveṇī.
And having received the Sarasvatī, she became renowned as the remover of sins. || 38 ||
O my beloved, Yamī shall be a hundred times more excellent than the Gaṅgā in the Mathurā region; furthermore, other sacred fords (tīrthas) shall come to exist there.
By bathing in these and drinking their water, liberation is attained without a doubt;
one who dies in the sacred field of Mathurā becomes four-armed.
The holy ford named Viśrānti bestows the attainment of rest;
it is the most excellent and greatly meritorious, granting Goloka to men through bathing there. ||4.1||
O Lakṣmī, by the mere sight of the Viśrānti-tīrtha, one obtains all that is gained from bathing, giving, meditation, fire-offerings, and austerity at all sacred fords. 42.
But neither by sacrifices, nor by austerity, nor by meditation, nor by restraints does one obtain that fruit which a bathed person obtains at Viśrāntighaṭṭaka; likewise,
from beholding it at the three times of day and from performing two circumambulations.
By performing the fivefold salutation (*namaskāra-pañcaka*), one is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu.
I have established my eternal rest there at the landing-place (*ghaṭṭa*) of the Yamunā; here resides perpetual peace, just as it does in the abode of Goloka.

Now, there is another supreme sacred site belonging to me, Prayāga, which exists there; it is difficult for even the gods to attain, secret, and the liberator from the entire cycle of worldly existence. ||46||
One who bathes there attains my world and shares in the merit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice;
if he possesses desire, he becomes like Mahendra, and from that state, he goes to the supreme goal.
Furthermore, there is another holy site, Kanakhala, which bestows heaven through bathing;
and there is another, Tinduka, which grants me the abode of Goloka. ||48||
In the country of Pañcāla, there was the city of Kāmpilya, whose inhabitants were righteous;
there lived a barber named Tinduka.
In time, the family of that very barber fell into ruin;
thereafter he arrived in Mathurā and lived constantly on the bank of the Yamunā.
Indeed, for the sake of restoring his family, he performed śrāddha ceremonies and other rites.
Constantly bathing in the Yamunā, he met his death in due course;
having then obtained birth as a brāhmaṇa in Mathurā,
he became a supreme Vaiṣṇava and went to the abode of Goloka.
Thus, that twice-born man named Tinduka, remembering his former births,
informed everyone and made that sacred site famous before passing away.
Next is another supreme solar tirtha, which destroys all sins.
She was indeed propitiated by Bali with the desire for wealth and sovereignty.
With arms raised and abstaining from food, he performed supreme austerity.
The Blessed Lord Sūryanārāyaṇa himself became pleased with him;
having approached, he said to Bali, "What is the purpose of your penance?"
Bali said to Sūrya, the lord of the world and the eye of the three realms:
"I am destitute; I possess no kingdom, and it is for the sake of wealth that I have performed this austerity.
Thereupon, Sūrya gave him a *cintāmaṇi* gem from his own crown.
Having obtained that wish-fulfilling gem, he indeed went to Pātāla;
Sūrya, having bathed in the waters of Yamī, went to the golden orb.
Thus this excellent holy ford (tīrtha) came into being, the destroyer of sin and suffering;
by bathing there, one attains heaven and then liberation, and shall become four-armed.
On a Sunday, during a solar transit (saṃkrānti), at a lunar or solar eclipse,
or on an auspicious lunar day, one who bathes at Sūryatīrtha obtains the fruit of a Rājasūya sacrifice.
Now, here is Dhruvatīrtha, where in ancient times Dhruva performed austerities;
by bathing there one attains sovereignty, and by dying there, one reaches the station of Dhruva.
Through faith, the ancestors cross over here and attain liberation;
there, to the south of Dhruva, is the Tīrtha known as Tīrtharājaka.
By bathing there, O Lakṣmī, one shall indeed attain my Goloka.
Now, O Lakṣmī, to the south of that is the supreme Ṛṣitīrtha;
having bathed there, one goes to the world of the sages and, upon the departure of life, to Goloka.
Further to the south of that is my supreme Mokṣatīrtha.
Whereby bathing brings liberation and one attains my Goloka, right there is Koṭitīrtha, which is difficult even for the gods to obtain.
By bathing there, as well as by giving gifts, chanting, performing fire-sacrifices, and eating [the remnants], [one attains the same]. || 65 ||
Through both libations and fasting, one is glorified in the world of Brahmā.
By him who frequented Koṭitīrtha, his ancestors were delivered;
likewise, seven times seven generations of his lineage were delivered.
Now, indeed, there is the Vāyutīrtha, the supreme savior of the ancestors;
those who offer funeral cakes (piṇḍas) certainly deliver the ancestors in every way.
Indeed, the fruit of offering the funeral rice-ball (piṇḍa) at Gayā is obtained here;
especially in the month of Jyeṣṭha, one's ancestors cross over [to liberation] through the performance of Śrāddha. ||69||
These sacred fords have indeed been described as bestowing both worldly enjoyment and liberation;
for bathing, giving, recitation, and burnt offerings performed there yield a thousandfold merit.
Through the mere remembrance, salutation, or sight of these holy fords (tīrthas),
and by drinking even a single drop of their water, eternal liberation is attained.
Now, herein lies the preeminent among holy fords, a collection of divine descents (avatāras).
All the incarnations of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, gathered together at the moment of his birth.
Having arrived and stayed for a moment on that auspicious bank of the Yamunā near their birthplace, they found that the sacred site remained hidden. (73)
By bathing there, by drinking the water, or even by sprinkling it upon oneself, it utterly destroys all sins and bestows the worlds of Goloka, Vaikuṇṭha, and others. (74)
In that place, liberation from death shall certainly occur; of this there is no doubt.
Even by fasting for a single day, one shall obtain the fruit of ten million sacrifices. ||75||
Even those embodied beings—be they even animals, insects, or the like—who are touched by the particles of dust from Mathurā, shall attain liberation. (76)
Indeed, even in another land, one who utters its name becomes a partaker of enjoyment;
so what need be said of where the Supreme Brahman shines in person?
Wealth, dwellings, land, wives, sons, daughters, and all such prosperities [are attained there].
Authority over fields and gardens, sovereignty, existence as a king, and lordship over people; || 78 ||
Gold, silver, great fortune, prosperity, wealth, palaces, and so forth,
indeed come to be for a devotee here through the grace of Hari, by even a single drop of his compassion.
Just as it is a savior, a sustainer, a protector, and a guardian,
so too is the supreme Mathurā-tīrtha the bestower of heaven and the giver of liberation.

Thus ends the three hundred and forty-third chapter, titled "The Demonstration of the Infinity of the Lord’s Incarnations, the Incarnation of Kṛṣṇa in the First Dvāpara Age, and the Tīrthas of Viśrānti, Prayāga, Kanakhala, Tinduka, Sūrya, Dhruva, the Royal Ṛṣis’ Liberation, Koṭi, Vāyu, and Others," within the *Māhātmya* of Mathurā-kṣetra, in the first section concerning the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī, to the account of the supreme and great Śivakuṇḍa in Mathurā;
that sacred ford was created by Śiva, and there Hara himself performed austerities for a long time.
Then Kṛṣṇa, the descendant of Mādhava, having arrived there, said to Śiva:
"O Śambhu, why indeed does he perform such a most dreadful penance?
Śambhu replied: "O great king, the gods have been excessively tormented by the Daityas."
"You ought to descend here for the destruction of the Asuras.
"So be it," Hari replied. Then, having bathed in the Yamunā and completed his ascetic penance, Hara departed from there for Kailāsa itself.
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa also went indeed to Goloka;
he was born as Kṛṣṇa himself at the junction of the first Dvāpara age.
This holy ford is Śivakuṇḍa, which caused Kṛṣṇa to arrive;
it bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation, and by bathing here, one attains Vaikuṇṭha.
To the north of Śivakuṇḍa is the Saṃyamana Tīrtha, which bestows great merit;
by bathing there, one attains fortune, good luck, and beauty.
In this way, both heaven and the supreme liberation are attained; there is no doubt about this.
Whatever ancient events occurred at the great holy site of Saṃyamana [are told].
Listen, Lakṣmī, to this most wonderful account that destroys all sins:
a Niṣāda dwelling in the Naimiṣa forest was once of a contented mind. (9)
Once, a man of evil conduct arrived at Mathurā;
he used to bathe daily in the Yamunā by swimming across with his arms.
It comes to the bank and likewise goes away again;
thus, one who has bathed on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight also crosses over.
Desiring to cross, that Niṣāda plunged into the waters of the Yamunā;
he then crossed the Yamunā toward the holy ford of Saṃyamaṇa.
O auspicious lady, as soon as he arrived at the banks of Saṃyamana,
that exhausted man sank down and, being submerged, drank the water.
Unable [to endure it], that great sinner was instantly deprived of his life;
and by the power of the sacred ford, the basket of his sins was destroyed.
Great merit was produced by him, and by that he was born as the lord of the earth,
a king who was the sovereign of the Saurāṣṭra region in the land of Saurāṣṭra.
That archer, a Kṣatriya king named Yakṣmadhanus, ruled over the empire of Bhadrāpattana. || 16 ||
Relying upon the duty of a Kṣatriya, he protected the earth;
indeed, he was a servant of the Siddhas who dwell on Mount Raivata.
He constantly travels with joy by vehicle to the mountain for the purpose of seeing [the deity],
to the auspicious shore of the Aśvapaṭṭa lake in the east.
Having gone to the hermitage of Patnīvratā, he beheld that great sage;
he beheld the Lord Gopālakṛṣṇa and the goddess Kaṃbharālakṣmī.
He also beheld Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa constantly;
by His power, this king became a devotee of Kṛṣṇa and a Vaiṣṇava.
A great and powerful one was born, for whose protection a neck-garland was given, which, being of the nature of armor, protects the king in every way. (21)
Because he protected the king even in battle, making him always victorious, he obtained the kingdom of the Gaurjaras and the Marus for this reason. (22)
Having learned that he was a supreme devotee of Viṣṇu, the King of Kāśī sent him by means of an aerial vehicle for the very purpose of a pilgrimage to Kāśī.
Having honored the victorious and illustrious one, his own daughter named Pīvarī was bestowed upon him; taking her, he departed for his city.
Having arrived at Bhadrāpattana, he married the auspicious Pīvarī;
she was made his beloved, the foremost among his hundreds of principal wives.
And he delighted her in beautiful gardens and forests,
in lovely palaces, and on the sandy banks of rivers.
As he protected his subjects and likewise bestowed gifts,
time passed for that king, who came to be accompanied by sons and grandsons.
And as he remained attached to worldly enjoyments, ten thousand years indeed passed;
he had five hundred very beautiful sons and daughters.
All the maidens were married by him in every way according to the prescribed rites;
he bestowed the great kingdom upon the eldest, and indeed the cities upon the middle ones.
The land was assigned for the livelihood of the youngest sons;
thus, having attained happiness for himself, he withdrew from the affairs of state.
Then, having arranged for the livelihood of the queens, he once slept upon a bed with Pīvarī;
while asleep, he conversed like one awake in a dream.
"Alas, alas! Oh, oh! Let us go; what indeed is the use of life here?
Having remembered that land of Mathurā, and having remembered the holy site of Saṃyama. (32)
Then Pīvarī said, "O King, why do you speak thus?
Having heard the words of his beloved, the king spoke to her in reply.
One who is intoxicated, asleep, or heedless speaks incoherently;
O beloved, you should not take the word of one under the influence of sleep to heart. (34)
Pīvarī said: "O Lord, I have heard this again and again;
because it has been heard many times, it must indeed arise from a firm latent impression (saṃskāra). (35)
"O Great King, you appear to me to be one who remembers his past births; tell me that. O sinless King, speak to me of what occurred in your previous existence."
Tell me today, O King, if I am dear to you;
I shall give up my life if you will not protect me.
Having heard the words of his beloved, the lord of men replied:
"If it must certainly be said, then let us go to the city of Mathurā."
"In the light, however, our death will surely come; there is no doubt.
Having gone there, I shall indeed relate the account of my previous birth. (39)
O fair-eyed one, bestow abundant gifts upon the brahmins,
having established your sons and your grandsons, and having seen each of them settled in their respective positions.
Having bestowed villages, treasuries, jewels, and even his sons, the king honored the people residing in the city. ||41||
Having entrusted his sons, as well as his householders and dear kinsmen, to protect the kingdom inherited from his father and grandfather in due order; 42.
Having instructed his wife in the meaning of virtue and appointed her to her protection,
he then spoke to his friends, allies, servants, female slaves, and attendants.
That kingdom which has been acquired is indeed a bondage in every respect;
therefore, for the sake of my own liberation, I shall go to the city of Mathurā.
There is no other supreme happiness than contentment and renunciation;
there is no eye equal to knowledge, and there is no strength equal to the eye. (45)
There is no suffering equal to passion, and there is no happiness greater than renunciation—for him who indulges in all desires, and for him who abandons them entirely. (46)
Generally, the renunciation of all desires is considered superior;
therefore, I must depart for the sacred site of the city of Mathurā. 47.
Having thus informed all the people and appointed his sons to guard them,
he arrived at the city of Mathurā, endowed with an army according to his requirements.
By him was seen a delightful city, and it was beheld by Pīvarī;
it was holy, auspicious, a destroyer of sins, and endowed with sacred fords that grant liberation. 49.
O Lakṣmī, there is a beautiful place named Vṛndāvana, the unsurpassed abode of Viṣṇu;
by seeing which, a person indeed becomes one who has fulfilled his life's purpose.
On the eleventh day of the bright fortnight of the month of Śrāvaṇa, one who has bathed in Yamī is liberated;
likewise, Saumya Madhuvana is my unsurpassed abode. (51)
Having seen that second forest, one indeed becomes one who has accomplished their purpose;
the third is the excellent Caitra forest, named Kunda-vana.
Having bathed on the eleventh lunar day of the dark fortnight of the month of Bhādrapada, one is liberated;
this is my fourth auspicious grove, which grants the abode of my own self. 53.
One who bathes in the pool of Vimala is indeed liberated from sin;
he who gives up his life there goes to my world.
The fifth is Bakulavana, my own sacred site for a monastery;
having gone there and likewise bathed, one proceeds to the world of Vahni. (55)
On the opposite bank of the Yamunā lies my sixth sacred grove, Bhadravana;
having gone there and likewise bathed, one proceeds to the world of the Nāgas. (56)
My seventh forest there is made of khadira wood and resembles a sacrifice;
by seeing this purifying place, a person shall go to my world. 57.
And my eighth [forest] is Mahāvana, endowed with all kinds of trees;
having gone there, a person is glorified in the world of Indra. ||58||
The ninth forest, however, is Lohajaṅghavana, the best of forests; for a person who goes there, it destroys even great sins. 59.
The tenth forest, named Bilvavana, is honored by the gods;
having gone there, a person is glorified in the world of Brahmā.
The eleventh is Bhāṇḍīra, which indeed bestows yoga upon yogis;
there stands the tree known as the Bhāṇḍīra-vaṭa.
Wherever my marriage with Rādhā takes place, by the mere sight of it, people do not conceive. ||62||
Having seen Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa there, one is not subject to rebirth;
O beloved, the grove of Tulasī alone is the twelve forests here.
To me, Vṛndāvana—the place of my marriage—is the bestower of liberation for trees with black bark;
it is truly a forest of green trees for me. (64)
Having gone there, having plucked leaves and petals, and having seen a cluster of Tulasī, one should remember me in the waters of the Yamunā. (65)
Having bathed and attained liberation, he is honored by me in Goloka;
O beloved, those people who behold Vṛndā, Tulasī, and Govinda [attain the same].
They do not go to the city of Yama; they go instead to Goloka itself. Those with desires go to heaven, and from there, indeed, to my supreme abode.
Having approached Mathurā, that great sacred site of such a nature, the two of them attained joy and performed the rites of the holy place with devotion.
Having eaten and caused her husband to eat, Pīvarī then asked him about the account of his dream, including that which had been previously spoken in secret.
"O Great King, tell me that which was previously spoken by the king of men regarding Mathurā, concerning what he said he would say, and whatever was kept secret."
The king also spoke to his own wife regarding the story of their previous birth:
"Listen, O wife, I was a Niṣāda who dwelt in the Naimiṣa forest. (7.1)
Having come here and died at the Saṃyamana tīrtha within the water, he was born as a powerful king in Saurāṣṭra by virtue of that merit. ||72||
Through the prowess of Kṛṣṇa, known as Pannīvratāka, who was born from the soil of Amaruka, sovereignty was indeed obtained; you too have been obtained from the King of Kāśī.
"Remembering my past lives, I always remember this sacred site while lying upon your bed; sometimes, when overcome by sleep, I even speak of it aloud. (74)
"Alas, alas! Oh, oh! Let us go; what indeed is the use of life here?"—thus, O lady, has this account of my former existence been told to you. (75)
Having heard this, the queen, who remembered her former births, spoke of her own history:
"I am indeed named Pīvarī, a resident on the banks of the Gaṅgā. (76)
Having come to see this city on the twelfth lunar day of the month of Kārttika, she boarded a boat and, while traveling here, fell into the waters of the Yamunā. (77)
Immediately deprived of my life-breaths, O King, I became the daughter of the King of Kāśī;
though married by you, that memory did not leave me.
By the power of this sacred ford, you have become the wife of a king;
my death occurred at the Dhārāpatanaka Tīrtha. (79)
O King, as we perform great meritorious deeds, the holy site of liberation has been seen once again in Mathurā; the end of our two lifespans has now arrived.
"Right this very day, many gifts must be given by my own hand.
Having said this, she bathed at the bank of the Yamunā and gave those gifts. (8.1)
The king also performed meritorious deeds, such as giving gifts, feeding Brahmins and others, and bestowing the gift of cows, gold, sesame seeds, and wealth. ||8 2||
He joyfully gave gifts of land to Brahmin maidens, as well as gifts of sacred threads, garments, and food. (8.3)
After they had all performed their duties, the king and queen both remained together;
then, the attendants of Goloka arrived at the bank of the Yamunā.
Accompanied by their celestial chariot, they assumed four-armed forms with divine bodies and led the king of consumption (yakṣmarāja) to the abode of Hari. 85.
Thus, having reached Mathurā and bathed at the Yamunā-tīrtha, they beheld me according to their observances and met their death right there.
Having abandoned all worldly existence, they have gone to my very same world.
This great wonder that occurred has been told to you, O Lakṣmī. (87)
Having cast off the body at the tirtha known as Dhārāpātana, a person attains the heavenly realm and Goloka; of this there is no doubt. (88)
Having reached Yamuneśvara and surrendered one's own life,
one attains the world of Viṣṇu, assuming a divine form with four arms.

Thus ends the three hundred and forty-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of the Śivakuṇḍa Tīrtha, the Saṃyamana Tīrtha, the Attainment of the Kingdom of Saurāṣṭra by the deceased Niṣāda, the Marriage of the Daughter of the King of Kāśī, the Death of the Two of Them—Who Retained Memory of Their Past Lives—in Mathurā, and the Majesty of Yamuneśvara," in the first section concerning the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga within the *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī, I shall likewise describe another sacred ford (tīrtha) to you;
it is the supreme Nāga-tīrtha, from which the serpent was banished.
Having bathed here, those who die go to heaven and are not born again;
furthermore, there is the Ghaṇṭābharaṇaka Tīrtha, which is indeed supremely purifying.
Having bathed there, one goes to the world of the Sun; of this there is no doubt. Furthermore, there exists another sacred ford (tīrtha) of Brahmā within the waters of the Yamunā.
Having bathed there and drunk the water, one is glorified in the world of Brahmā.
Now, there is another sacred Soma-tīrtha in the purifying waters of the Yamunā.
There, the Moon-god, seeing me, then worshipped me with devotion;
one who performs an ablution there is glorified in the world of Soma.
Now, there is another supreme sacred site, the Sarasvatī-prapātana;
O Lakṣmī, a man who bathes there becomes an ascetic (yati), even if he was previously of low caste.
In the southern region of Mathurā, a person who has fasted for three nights and performs the vow is liberated from the sin of killing a Brahmin merely by bathing.
Now, there is the purifying holy site named Daśāśvamedha on the Yamunā;
that place, located in the western part of Mathurā, is exceedingly sacred.
Those who bathe there with self-restraint will not find heaven difficult to attain;
for it was there that Brahmā created the Mānasa-tīrtha in ancient times.
Having bathed there, which is honored by the sages, people indeed go to heaven.
Now follows the Vighnarājatīrtha, which is meritorious, auspicious, and a destroyer of sins.
On the eighth, the fourteenth, and especially on the fourth lunar day,
the Lord of Obstacles does not afflict one who has bathed in that most excellent of sacred fords.
The son of Pārvatī constantly ensures that there is no obstacle for him in all undertakings of learning, as well as in the performance of sacrifices and acts of charity.
Furthermore, there is another sacred site, Koṭitīrtha; by bathing there, one obtains the merit of ten million cows.
Upon casting off one's life there, one goes to the world of Soma and then to my own world.
Beyond this lies the sacred field of Śiva, measuring half a krośa;
the god Hara, stationed there, eternally protects Mathurā.
Having bathed there and drunk the water, one obtains the fruit of Mathurā;
furthermore, if one gives up their life-breaths here, they go to my world. || 15 ||
Now, there is another auspicious ford, always the best among all fords;
I dwell there eternally out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds. (16)
Upon seeing me and bathing there, men become partakers of liberation,
especially during the solstices, the equinoxes, the Viṣṇupadī days, and during solar eclipses.
Having bathed and obtained fruit of infinite merit, one is liberated from all sins;
that person attains the fruit arising from the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices.
O Sudhanā, having bathed at this holy ford, one partakes in the merit of bathing at Prayāga;
O beloved, hear what occurred here in the first Dvāpara age.
Indeed, by name he is called Sudhana, and he is always devoted to me;
he is possessed of abundance in wealth, grain, sons, wife, cattle, houses, and so forth.
Characterized by moral conduct, contentment, honoring the virtuous, compassion, charity, and so forth, that devotee of mine lived indeed together with his wife and children. (21)
The days, months, and likewise the years pass for him through constant devotion to me alone and through service to the virtuous and the faithful.
He performs his household duties with whatever wealth he has obtained;
he never practices deception regarding measures or weights. (23)
He performs my supreme worship constantly at the three times of day,
with the invocation and with the five nectars, milk and the rest, as well as water.
By means of bathing, ornaments, various garments, and excellent unguents, as well as flowers, lamps, incense, sandalwood, nectar, and choice fruits; || 25 ||
With food offerings of most delicious dishes, with water, betel leaves, and spices, and likewise with daily waving of lights (ārātrika), hymns of praise, and songs of glorification; || 26 ||
He always worshipped me with circumambulations and prostrations like a staff;
likewise, he observed the fast on the eleventh day and kept a vigil.
Having reached the bank of the Kālindī near my own form, he constantly performs his ablutions three times a day with sincere devotion. (28)
He would dance during the first quarter of the night and then go to his own home;
he performed this daily, especially on the eleventh lunar day (Ekādaśī).
Having bathed at night on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight of Kārttika, he went to the bank of the Yamunā to reach the temple for the purpose of keeping a vigil; just then,
he was seized by a certain approaching Brahma-rākṣasa.
Black-complexioned, with a massive body and hair standing erect, he was exceedingly terrifying.
He said, "I am a Rākṣasa here, wandering about for the sake of food.
I dwell in the distant forest; I shall devour you, so do not grieve. (31-32)
"I have been hungry for a long time; I shall indeed find satisfaction for a long while.
Having seen, heard, and reflected upon this, the merchant then spoke with fortitude. (33)
“I am Sudhana; I shall give you a great feast—be gracious to me!
Wait for a moment from me today, and I will give you an abundance.
You shall eat my body, mixed with much delicious food.”
"Only after performing the service for the God shall I give all of that to you.
On the day of Hari, I perform the vigil for the God of gods;
indeed, it is my perpetual vow that I keep vigil before Hari."
Having kept vigil there until dawn in your presence, tell me where [you will be], and I shall come there; he shall be under my control.
"You shall devour me at your pleasure once I have kept my vigil,
provided you grant me permission to perform that vow which, for the satisfaction of Viṣṇu,
bestows all desires, is meritorious, and grants liberation. (38)
"Do not break my vow; have mercy so that it may turn out well.
Having heard Sudhana's words, the hungry Brahmarākṣasa said to Sudhana:
"You speak falsely, for you are but a merchant."
"One who has been released from the jaws of death does not indeed return to death again.
Having been liberated from my noose, how could you return once more?
Hearing the words of the Rākṣasa, the merchant, the most excellent of devotees, replied:

The entire world has truth as its root; everything is established in truth. All living beings have existence (sat) as their root. If you have hunger, and that hunger is real, then I am your food of truth; for if hunger were unreal, how could there be anything to be eaten? || 42-43 ||
Hunger and thirst were indeed created by Brahmā for the sake of the work of Brahman;
if I have been created for that purpose, your success shall be achieved, and not otherwise.
If I, as a merchant, have not been corrupted by past actions, then the inner self dwells within my heart just as it does in yours. (45)
"I am devoted, I am one whose nature is truth, and I speak by means of truth.
Listen, O Rākṣasa, to my agreement by which I may return:
having kept a vigil at night and performed a dance before Hari. (46)
"I shall come again, O Rakshasa; falsehood does not abide in me. (47)
Brahman is acquired through truth; dharma is protected by truth;
a daughter is given away through truth; for the gods on earth (brahmins) are indeed speakers of truth. 48.
Kings have crossed over [all difficulties] through truth; the earth is sustained by truth;
and heaven and liberation are obtained through the vow of truth, O Rākṣasa. (89)
By truth the sun shines; by truth the moon waxes;
by truth time moves on; by truth rain is born. (1.345.50)
"I live by truth; I have never committed an untruth.
May that truth of mine perish indeed if I do not return again. (5.1)
If I do not come before you, may I be tainted by the sin of that person who forcibly enjoys a woman through the impulse of lust.
If, after having performed such acts as the gifting of land, I were to take it back again, I would be defiled by that sin and would not return here again. (5.3)
Having enjoyed a woman or a man for one's own sake alone, one should then abandon them;
one should not act for the sake of another either, for that sin shall not be mine at the time of my return.
If I should abandon a virtuous and devoted wife who is innocent of any fault, may I be tainted by that sin, should you not return to me again. (55)
If I do not come before you, may I be tainted by the sin of whoever creates a breach in the row of those eating in a single line.
If that sin which belongs to one who breaks a vow does not come upon me, nor the sin of harming others, before you, O Nāga; [then may my vow be fulfilled].
O Rākṣasa, may that sin which belongs to one who reviles the twice-born, the virtuous wife, the holy man, and the gods be mine, if I do not return again. 5.8.

Whatever sin is incurred by one who commits treachery against a guru, a friend, or a well-wisher—that very same sin would be mine, O Rākṣasa, if I were not to come before you; I speak this truth to you. (59)
May the sins committed by me at sacred fords not come back again;
[may they befall] the slayer of a Brahmin, the drinker of liquor, the thief, the breaker of vows, and the rogue.
May I attain that same destination as one who betrays trust, one who commits an act of violence, or one who kills a child, if I do not return to you again.
Whatever sin there may be in the confinement or the killing of innocent beings,
let that sin be mine here if I do not return again;
after this life, may I undergo birth as a Rākṣasa for that sin.
"If I were to abandon the truth and not return, I would be a deceiver.
Hearing these words of the merchant, that Rākṣasa was pleased;
he inspired confidence in the one who had fallen into danger and said to him, "Go, and come back again."
The merchant quickly returned to my house and honored me;
having performed a dance before me, he joyfully kept a vigil. At dawn, he again repeatedly uttered "Obeisance to Nārāyaṇa."
Speaking thus, he went repeatedly prostrate like a staff upon the bank of the Yamunā.
As the devotee who performs his ablutions in the Kālindī proceeded along the path of the Rākṣasa,
I, becoming full of compassion, stood there blocking his way.
Beholding Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person, who bears a divine form and possesses four arms, the devotee Sudhana spoke to me.
Oṃ, salutations to you, the Blessed One, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa;
to the bestower of liberation upon devotees here, and to the giver of divine vision. (69)
O Lakṣmī, when I asked him, "Where is the merchant going so quickly?
Sudhana replied, "I am going into the presence of the Rākṣasa. Upon hearing this, I tried to dissuade him, saying, "You must not go, you must certainly not go! (1.345.7)
"While living, dharma is abandoned; when dead, what means for liberation is there?
Nevertheless, having heard this and bowed to me, he went to the presence of the Rākṣasa and said: "O Rākṣasa, eat me as you wish; do not delay! (71–72)
"Whether according to the prescribed rule or as it pleases you, truth must always be protected by me; eat, O Rākṣasa, without delay.
And the Rākṣasa, perceiving this marvel directed toward him, [reflected].
Becoming pleased, the merchant said, "You have won."
"By you, the dharma of true vows has been protected; through that, I have attained satisfaction. My hunger has vanished and eternal contentment has arisen.
Oh, how could I commit an act of treachery here against one who is so devoted to truth?"
But grant me indeed the merit of my vigil. || 76 ||
"By the power of truth and merit, may I attain liberation.
Having heard those words, Sudhana then spoke to the rākṣasa: || 77 ||
Do you know, O Rākṣasa, what kind of merit indeed belongs to the vigil?
The merit of staying awake for even one ghaṭikā bestows the station of Mahendra;
for those who stay awake for two ghaṭikās, it grants the supreme station of Brahmā.
For one who remains awake at midnight, there is indeed the supreme station of Vairāja; for one who remains awake during the *ūnarātra* (the waning night), there is the station of Vaikuṇṭha itself;
and for one who remains awake until dawn, there shall be liberation that bestows the world of Brahmā.
Indeed, by remaining awake for even half a ghaṭikā, a universal sovereignty is surely attained;
and for one who dances while awake, Goloka is certainly attained. ||81||
Therefore, I shall not give the fruit of one who has fully awakened;
give half of it, or half of that, or even half of half of that to me.
"Do not harbor greed, O lord of devotees; grant me liberation as well! Though thus entreated, Sudhana, being himself desirous of liberation, did not indeed give [it]. (83)
And again the Brahma-rākṣasa entreated Sudhana:
"O best of merchants, give me the merit of a single dance. Sudhana asked him: "Tell me, what was your former birth?"
"Afterwards, I shall relate the entire account, including the fruit of the single falsehood. (85)
"Do you not know me? the Rākṣasa said to the merchant;
"I am the Brahmin Agnidatta, living near your house. (86)
That very person who was your friend in former times is indeed I myself; having been a Brāhmaṇa learned in the Vedas, I have attained the state of a Rākṣasa due to my own past actions.
"I have begun constructing a fine two-storied house for you, just like your own.
For that purpose, I have always been taking bricks belonging to others at night. (88)
I committed the sin of theft, yet my house was not filled;
afflicted by fever, I remained within the palace, possessed by longing. (89)
Due to the sin of theft, even a Brahmin has fallen into the state of a Brahma-rākṣasa;
such as I am, O best of merchants, consider me indeed to be your friend.
O Friend, having shown compassion upon my arrival, please do me this favor:
grant me the merit of a single dance, by which I may attain a favorable rebirth. (9.1)
"O devotee, may you become one whose nature is liberation; this I entreat you repeatedly.
Having heard this, the merchant, his heart moistened with compassion, spoke to the Rākṣasa.
"Excellent! O Rākṣasa, I have granted you the fruit of one dance.
Having said this, as he was about to place the water into the hand of the Rākṣasa—
Then the body of that Rākṣasa indeed fell upon the earth,
while his soul became four-armed, like an attendant of Śrī Hari.
Having become thus, he shone at the head of the merchants as one sixteen years of age;
Viṣṇu, adorned by his divine attendants, arrived to lead him away.
Seeing Hari, Sudhana fell to the ground at his feet and said there to his Lord: "O Blessed One, we have been delivered by you."
Just as you are the bestower of liberation from even a mere fragment of the Rākṣasa’s dance, O Mādhava, so too become the giver of liberation to me. 97.
Then Janārdana, the God of gods, spoke sweetly to him:
"Come, O lord of devotees; let even this best of brahmins come to me."
O Sudhana, let your family quickly reunite with me upon my vehicle;
having ascended this supreme celestial chariot, let them indeed go to my world.
Having spoken thus, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa caused them all to ascend the celestial chariot and departed for the eternal abode of Vaikuṇṭha.
This is that very Tīrtha known as Sudhana, where this wonder occurred;
for those who perform their ablutions there on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight of Kārtika, [this marvel takes place]. (101)
From giving gifts, one obtains the fruit of the Rājasūya sacrifice, and heaven shall be the fruit;
he who performs the ritual release of a bull on the full moon day shall deliver his lineages.
"The performer of the śrāddha rite shall deliver his ancestors here at this sacred ford (tīrtha).
Thus, O Lakṣmī, I have related to you the liberation of Sudhana."

Thus ends the three hundred and forty-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Nāga-tīrtha, Ghaṇṭābharaṇaka-tīrtha, Soma-tīrtha, Sarasvatī-tīrtha, Daśāśvamedha-tīrtha, Rāja-vighnarāja, Koṭi-śiva-kṣetra, and Sudhana-tīrtha within the Greatness of Mathurā-kṣetra, along with the Liberation of the Brahmarākṣasa through the Merit of the Dance Offered by Sudhana," in the first section on the Lineage of the Kṛta-yuga in the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī, to another sacred ford within the Mathurā region;
it is the Vatsakrīḍanaka Tīrtha, constructed from red stone.
By bathing there, a human being shall indeed go to the world of Vāyu;
however, upon the relinquishing of life, supreme liberation shall occur—of this there is no doubt.
Then there is the supreme Bhāṇḍīraka Tīrtha, which bestows the status of husband and wife;
it is there in the forest region that Rādhā was indeed married by Kṛṣṇa.
In that region of Bhāṇḍīraka, which was filled with sāl, tāla, and arjuna trees, as well as tamāla, iṅguda, pīluka, karīra, and raktapuṣpa trees.
Having bathed there, he is liberated from sin and goes to the world of the Moon;
upon the relinquishing of his life-breaths, however, he attains Goloka—of this there is no doubt.
Vṛndāvana is my sacred pilgrimage site, where the cows, cowherds,
and gopīs shall always sport with me in various wonderful pastimes.
Having bathed in the pool at Vṛndāvana— a place difficult for all to attain, situated in a forest of many shrubs and creepers— he was welcomed in heaven by hosts of celestial nymphs.
Served by Gandharvas, he rejoices there for many years;
if he gives up his life there, he certainly rejoices in Vaikuṇṭha.
Furthermore, one who bathes at that place in Vṛndāvana where the demon Keśin was struck down undoubtedly obtains a hundredfold merit.
Beyond that is the Hariviśrāma Tīrtha, which bestows a hundredfold merit;
by offering funeral cakes (piṇḍa) there, one obtains a fruit equal to that of Gayā.
Bathing, giving gifts, and performing oblations here yield the fruit of the Vahniṣṭoma sacrifice;
furthermore, this supreme holy site of the twelve suns is considered the most excellent.
In the waters of the Kālindī, Kṛṣṇa danced upon the head of the serpent Kālīya for the sake of subduing him; there, ten blazing suns appeared.
"Lakṣmī was established by me alone at that time and informed for the sake of a boon. Then the Ādityas said, 'If a boon is to be granted to us...'"
At this sacred ford of ours, liberation shall come to people through bathing;
it is situated to the north of Harideva and to the south of Kālīya.
"Those who have died in the middle [of the journey], their liberation shall be in the abode of Goloka"—this was requested by them, and "So be it," I granted. (15)
Now, on the opposite bank of the Yamunā is the pilgrimage site of Malayārjuna;
there a cart has overturned, and a pool is found there.

In that regard, by means of bathing and fasting on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Jyeṣṭha, one becomes a partaker of infinite fruit through bathing, giving gifts, and beholding [the deity]. (17)
By worshipping Acyuta, one attains the supreme goal;
Kṛṣṇa himself comes to lead away the person who has observed the fast. 18.
Moreover, one born in our family, having bathed in the waters of the Kālindī and fasted, shall worship Govinda in Mathurā. (19)
Blessed is he who shall offer the funeral pinda-offering in the Yamunā on this twelfth day of the month of Jyeṣṭha; for there will be no further satisfaction [for our ancestors]. (1.346.20)
Thus do the ancestors who have gone to the other world always sing:
"Now here is a blessed holy site, the forest known as Bahula. (21)
Having bathed on the twelfth lunar day (dvādaśī), one proceeds to the abode of Rudra;
but having bathed on the tenth day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, one shall attain my own state.
Now, on the opposite bank, the Bhāṇḍahrada tīrtha is well known;
there, every day, the Ādityas are seen as beautiful birds.
Whatever person performs a bath at that holy site in the Arkakuṇḍa, being liberated from all sins, he goes to the world of the Sun. ||24||
Now, there is here a pure well named Saptasāmudra;
one who bathes there becomes free from desire and goes to his own desired world. (25)
There, at the departure of the vital breaths, he attains my abode;
furthermore, there is the supremely auspicious sacred field named Vīrasthala. 26.
And having bathed there at the nearby waters adorned with lotuses and water-lilies, one attains the world of heroes and, in the end, goes to my abode. ||27||
Likewise, the sacred field of Kuśasthala is meritorious and supremely purifying;
having bathed there, one goes to the world of Brahmā, and upon death, one attains Goloka.
There, at the Puṣpasthala Tīrtha, is the unsurpassed sacred field of Śiva;
by bathing there, a person goes to the world of Śiva. ||29||
Then, the Gopīśvara image, which destroys great sins and bestows liberation, was installed by Mātali at the Gopīśa Tīrtha.
Indeed, thousands of gopīs had gathered there for the sake of sporting with Kṛṣṇa;
then Kṛṣṇa assumed a thousand forms. ||3 1||
The Lord, the bestower of happiness, sported as He desired with each and every cowherd girl;
then Mātali arrived there and installed him as the lord of the cowherd girls.
Having brought seven jars overflowing with gems and medicinal herbs, he performed the consecration of the God who was wearing the dress of a cowherd.
The gopīs sang and danced, crying out "Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!
There, he established a well using seven jars.
There is a sacred ford named Sāmudrika which bestows the abode of Goloka; by one who offers water and funeral cakes there during a śrāddha ceremony, [the ancestors] are satisfied in every way. (35)
By him, seventy-seven generations of ancestors are delivered; this is true for the ancestors of one who performs the Śrāddha on a New Moon day falling on a Monday. (26)
His ancestors indeed remain satisfied for a hundred times ten million years, as do those of the god Govinda and likewise of Gopīśvara. (37)
A person who dies in the middle goes to the same world as Mahendra; likewise, by dying in the middle of Bahularudra and Govinda, one attains that same state.
Likewise, between the Creator and the Lord of the Gopīs, he shall uplift a hundred generations of the family of one who performs the offering of funeral cakes and the ritual bathing. (39)
There is Vasutīrtha to the south of Mathurā, as well as Phālgunaka;
having bathed and drunk there, one is glorified in my world.
There, at the Phālgunaka Tīrtha, is the site of Vṛṣabhāñjana;
having performed his ablutions there, he rejoices together with the gods.
Now, there is the place named Tālavana, situated to the west of Mathurā;
one who performs ablutions in the pool there, or makes offerings, shall obtain their heart's desire. 42.

O Lakṣmī, there is a sacred ford (tīrtha) called Saṃpīṭhaka located at the site of Kṛṣṇa’s birth; one who bathes there on the seventh lunar day falling on a Monday partakes in the merit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice. (43)
Having observed the vow, she should worship me; she shall indeed become possessed of sons.
My domain, centered at Mathurā, extends for twenty yojanas.
Having bathed anywhere there, one is liberated from terrible sins;
during the rainy season, one should remain in whatever place may be conducive to happiness.
While I am ever asleep, the holy fords and sacred shrines throughout the seven continents shall come to Mathurā.
And seeing me upon rising from sleep, they become vessels for liberation;
having performed their ablutions in the Yamunā, they behold Keśava. (587)
Being freed from all sins, he attains my world;
at every step he obtains the fruit of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices. ||48||
By whomsoever Keśava has been circumambulated in Mathurā, by him the earth with its seven continents has been circumambulated. (49)
Likewise, one should offer a ghee lamp and a garment to Kṛṣṇa in his temple;
[the temple] shall be five yojanas in width and five and a half yojanas in length.
A person obtains a celestial mansion filled with rows of lamps,
enriched with all objects of desire, and frequented by hosts of apsarases.
It is delightful, bestowing all desires, and resplendent with every splendor;
even the Siddhas, Cāraṇas, and Gandharvas who have gone to heaven long for it.
If indeed merit had been performed, such a house as this might have been obtained;
yet in the end, liberation would have been attained through the power of Mathurā. ||53||
Indra protects the eastern Mathurā, while Yama protects the southern;
the Lord of Waters (Varuṇa) protects the western, and Kubera likewise protects the northern.
My devotee Śaṅkara, the husband of Pārvatī, protects the center;
or whatever person builds a house or a temple in Mathurā. || 95 ||
He should be known as four-armed and liberated while living, without a doubt.
In Mathurā, there is a great pool named Vimalodaka. (56)
In the winter it should be warm, and in the summer it should be cool;
it does not increase during the rains, nor does it diminish in the summer. (57)
But this is a great wonder for me regarding that supreme pool in my field of Mathurā—among the pits and the rivers. (58)
One should bathe in a well, a lake, a natural pool, a flowing stream, or at a confluence;
wherever one may bathe, by that act one shall attain the supreme goal.
On the ninth day of the month of Kārttika, the king among my devotees,
having performed a circumambulation, proceeds with the bull that strides across the earth.
Neither by gifts, nor by austerities, nor by sacrifices is there such a fruit as that which comes from circumambulating the earth through the service of sacred fords. 61.
In measuring the circumference of the earth correctly,
the measurement is sixty thousand crores and six hundred crores of yojanas.
There, the holy fords and the gods were indeed enumerated by Pavana,
as well as by Brahmā, Lomaśa, Nārada, and Dhruva.
By the Brahmin Patnāvratas, by Garuḍa, and by Hanumān—
by these and many other gods, the earth was protected in various ways with respectful offerings and defenses.
It was traversed by all the powerful ones along the outer boundary line of the maṇḍala,
as well as by certain masters of yoga, such as Mārkaṇḍeya and others.
Whatever fruit may be obtained from wandering through the sacred fords of the seven continents, even more than that is attained by circumambulating Mathurā. (66)
Just as the sequence of the ritual procedure was performed in Mathurā,
I shall now correctly describe the method of the successive order and the fruit of circumambulation.

Whatever merit exists among all the gods, whatever fruit exists in all sacred fords, whatever merit exists in all acts of giving, and whatever fruit exists in sacrifices and works of public utility; || 68 ||
O Lakṣmī, that fruit is obtained by circumambulating Mathurā;
for there reside Brahmā and other millions of deities, together with divine sages and seers. (69)
On the ninth day of the bright fortnight of Kārtika, they began their journey toward Mathurā;
having reached Mathurā on the eighth day, they bathed at Viśrāntitīrtha.
Having performed the worship of the ancestors, the gods, and the sages, as well as the worship of Yamunā, and having beheld Viśrānti, Dīrgha-Viṣṇu, and Keśava; 71.
Having undertaken a fast, or otherwise consuming only a small amount of pure food,
one should be devoted to celibacy and diligently maintain silence.
Having taken sesame seeds, unbroken rice, kuśa grass, and cooked food, one should offer a lamp at the place of rest;
on the morning of the ninth day, one should commence the pilgrimage from this spot.
At the Brāhma-muhūrta, before the sun [rises], one should bathe at Dakṣiṇakoṭika;
having washed one's feet and performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana), one should propitiate Hanumān.
O bestower of all auspiciousness, the achiever of success, and the witness of the fruit;
be the grantor of success for my pilgrimage through this circumambulation. (71)
Having thus informed Hanumān, the lord of the hosts, according to the prescribed rites,
he then worshipped him before him with offerings of lamps, flowers, and other gifts.
One should worship Padmanābha and Dīrghaviṣṇu, the bestower of happiness, as well as the goddess Vasumatī and the other, Aparājitā. (77)
Having bowed to the one stationed in the armory, he should then proceed further ahead to Kaṃsavāsanikā,
as well as to Auprasenī and Carcikā.
There the young bride, having bowed to the destroyer of the Dānavas and the bestower of victory,
then bowed to the Mothers who are worshipped by the gods.
Having seen the goddesses of the house and the goddesses of the site (vāstu), and having obtained their permission, he should go out;
reaching the southern extremity, he should bathe and offer libations to the ancestors.
Having prostrated before the Lord Kṛṣṇa, one should go to the virtuous Ikṣuvāsā,
where the holy ford was indeed established by Kṛṣṇa with his childhood playthings.
From there, O Vatsaputra, one should go to Arkasthala, and then to Vīrasthala, Kuśasthala, Puṇyasthala, and Mahāsthala. ||82||
Through the observation of the five sites, one rejoices together with Brahman;
having beheld the face of the perfected Śiva, one should gaze upon Hayamukti.
Since the horse has attained liberation here along with its companion,
the prince should remain there and not undertake a journey.
Having visited Mallikā, one should go to Kadambakhaṇḍa;
having seen the Yoginī Carcikā, one should then proceed to Mātṛkā.
Both the Aspṛśyā and the Aspṛśā are indeed protectors of children;
having gone from there to the Varṣakhāta pool, one should offer libations to the ancestors. ||86||
One should go to Kṣetrapāla, Śiva, and Bhūteśvara and worship them;
then one should go to Kṛṣṇakrīḍā, Setubandha, and Balihrada.
Thence one should go to the place called Kukkutakrīḍā, which bestows [favorable] rebirth;
there, one should worship the collection of pillars with beautiful peaks and circumambulate it. 88.
He is liberated from all sins and shall go to the world of Viṣṇu;
[he goes] to the place where Vasudeva and Devakī lay together in solitude.
Having gone to the abode of Nārāyaṇa, one should enter and circumambulate it,
having bowed to Vighnavināyaka, as well as to Kubjikā and Vāmanā.
The two Brahmin women, Kṛṣṇadāsīs, having bowed down, proceeded to Garteśvara;
upon seeing Mahāvidyeśvarī, the fruit of success in their pilgrimage was attained. ||9 1 ||
One should go to and worship Prabhāmallī, the Great Mistress of Vidyās;
likewise, one should worship Siddheśvarī and Saṅketeśvarī. ||92||
In front of which Hari made an appointment for the purpose of destroying the Daityas;
having performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana) at the pool, one should proceed to Gokarṇeśvara. ||93||
Having seen the river Sarasvatī, one should go to Vighnarāja;
likewise, having seen and touched the Gaṅgā, one should proceed to Rudramahālaya.
One should worship that Kṣetrapa, the lord of the assembly of the Uttarakoṭi Gaṇas, at the place where the game of dice was played with Kṛṣṇa. ||95||
Thence one should go to the great holy site called Rudramahālaya, which is pure within the waters of the Yamunā; there one should bathe and offer libations to the ancestors. 96.
From there, one should go to Gārgyatīrtha and to Somaka Bhadreśvara;
by worshipping Someśvara, a person obtains the full fruit of the pilgrimage. ||97||
And at the confluence of the Sarasvatī, having gratified the gods, sages, ancestors, and humans according to the rules and having made offerings, one shall attain union with Kṛṣṇa. ||98||
Having gone to Ghaṇṭābharaṇaka, as well as to Garuḍa and Keśava;
having gone to Dhārālopanaka, Vaikuṇṭha, and Khaṇḍavelaka.
Mandākinī-saṃyamana, Cāsikuṇḍa, Gopaka,
Muktikeśvara, and the site of Vailakṣa-Garuḍa.
Having gone everywhere and offered oblations to the ancestors and the gods, one should satisfy them and pray: "May my pilgrimage to Mathurā be fruitful. (10.1)
Having thus addressed Śiva, the Lord of the gods and protector of the field, and having bathed in the place named Viśrānti and performed the libations for the ancestors; || 102 ||
Having rested and circumambulated, and likewise having bowed to the Guru and Hari,
one should then go to Sumaṅgalā and seek her favor for the successful completion of the journey.
Thinking, "May this pilgrimage of mine become fruitful through your grace," one should go to Pippalādeśvara and circumambulate it while reciting the Upāli hymn.
Then the pilgrim should establish one auspicious [liṅga] in his own name;
he shall obtain the fruit of the pilgrimage by worshipping and likewise prostrating before it. 105.
Likewise, one should go to the nāga Karkoṭaka and to the goddess Caṇḍikā;
then, having meditated upon Vajrānana, one should [meditate] upon Sūrya, the Lord of the Family (kuleśvara). 106.

Having seen [the deity] right there and having given a gift, one should conclude the pilgrimage; by performing the rite of return for one's family, indeed, residence in the world of the Sun shall come to pass. 107.
One who performs circumambulation is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu;
one who performs circumambulation of me is glorified in Goloka. || 108 ||
Those who slay Brahmins, those who drink liquor, thieves, those who have broken their vows, those who violate women by force, and those who steal wealth and fields—[these are purified by this]. (109)
Indeed, those who are harmful, givers of suffering, revilers, rogues,
and deceivers become truly sinless after performing the pilgrimage to Mathurā.
Any person who comes from another land and performs a circumambulation from afar—by the mere sight of him, other men become purified. || 1 1 1 ||
Even those living far away, having drunk but a single drop of the Yamunā’s water, are liberated from all sins and go to the supreme goal. || 112 ||
Those who make Mathurā their residence, those who frequent the sacred sites of Madhurā, and those who behold the forests of Madhurā become partakers of liberation. 113.
Madhuvana, Tālavana, and Kundavana as the third;
Kāmyakavana, Bahuvana, and likewise Bhadravana.
The Khādira forest, the Lohārgala forest,
the Bilva forest, the Bhāṇḍīra forest, and Vṛndāvana as the twelfth.
Those who behold these do not go to the realm of Yama;
indeed, those who undertake forest journeys go to the world of Indra.
And those devotees of mine,
whether men or women, who perform a pilgrimage for my sake, go to me alone, the eternal one, in Goloka.

Thus, in the first section, concerning the lineage of the Kṛta Yuga, within the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, this is the description of the Vatsakrīḍanaka, Bhāṇḍīraka, Vṛndāvana, Hari-viśrāma, Sūryatīrtha, Malaya-arjuna, Bahula-bhāṇḍahrada, Arkakuṇḍa, Vimala-kūpa, Vīrasthala, Kuśasthala, Puṣpasthala, Gopīśvara, the seven Sāmudrika sites, Vasu-phālgunaka, Vṛṣabha-añjanaka, Tālavana, Sampīṭhaka, and Vimalodaka-kuṇḍa; as well as the procedure for the circumambulation of Mathurā.

The three hundred and forty-sixth chapter, titled "The Demonstration of the Forests and the Sequential Description of the Holy Places Therein, Including Their Beginnings, Resting Points, and Conclusions. || 346 ||
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Now I shall tell you something else; O Mahālakṣmī, listen to that which occurred at Cakratīrtha situated to the north of Mathurā.
In Jambūdvīpa, a Brahmin residing in the great city of Gṛhodaya, who was well-versed in the Vedas, took his daughter and his son with him.
He went to Śālagrāma, that great sacred field, specifically for the purpose of pilgrimage;
he made his dwelling there, bathing and worshipping the deities at the holy sites.
While he was in the sight of the deities, a certain perfected being (siddha) in human form, a resident of the village named Kalāpa, appeared before his eyes.
The Siddha constantly comes and goes for the purpose of seeing him,
and he also finds rest in the leaf-hut of the Brahmin.
He described the great splendors of Kalāpa village;
having heard this, the Brahmin then conceived the intention to go there. || 6 ||
He said, "My friend has indeed been accomplished today;
O friend, lead me to Kalāpa, for I wish to see your supernatural powers."
The Siddha said: "O best of Brahmins, you shall have no passage there;
O twice-born one, your body will perish from the cold winds."
Nevertheless, the Brahmin said, "Lead me by means of your yoga.
Thus entreated, the Siddha took the maiden, the son, and Mitraka by the hand and flew up into the sky by the power of his yoga.
The Siddha placed three Brahmins in his own hermitage at Kalāpa.
Then, as time passed, the brahmin became afflicted by illness;
and the son carried his father, who was fit for death, to the bank of the Gaṅgā.
The daughter also attended to her father with wholesome foods.
Once, she prepared a meal in the leaf-hut for the sake of her father.
At that time, a certain Brahmin also arrived at the house for the purpose of begging alms.
He was asked by that Bhadrā: "Where have you come from here?"
He said, "I am a Brahmin from Kānyakubja who has attained perfection;
I wander happily here at this great holy site, Kalāpa."
Having been informed by the maiden, he, possessing a perfected body, was approached by her father;
after due deliberation, that maiden was given by the father to the perfected brāhmaṇa.
For although this son-in-law was already accomplished, he lived in his father-in-law’s house;
in the course of time, having reached a moment of leisure, he questioned his father-in-law.
"What is this disease, and when will its destruction occur?
I shall perform service in such a way that the destruction of the disease may come to pass. (17)
Having heard the words of his son-in-law, the father-in-law attained peace of mind and said to him:
"If you know through your supernatural power, then speak."
Having meditated upon his father-in-law, the accomplished son-in-law said to him, "O twice-born one,
while residing here in Kalāpa, you have eaten the food of a Śūdra."
"It was offered by him unknowingly, and it was consumed by me also unknowingly;
because of that fault, O twice-born one, this disease persists in my body. (1.347.20)
Food exists at his feet, but above the knees it is not found;
for one deprived of the food of a Śūdra, O Brāhmaṇa, death will surely come.
Having heard the words of his son-in-law, the brahmin reproached himself severely;
afflicted by grief and emaciated, that best of the twice-born desired to die.
Then at dawn, those three—the son-in-law, the daughter, and the son—went out from the house for the sake of their business; and in that very moment, [the following occurred].
Having found an opportunity when there was no one else around and having reflected upon death,
he rose from the bank of the Gaṅgā, looking toward all the directions.
Seeing a stone nearby, the twice-born man, distressed by the pain, took it to the house of Parṇakṛt and crushed those two feet with it.
Then, having renounced his life-breaths, he went to the highest heaven;
and the son-in-law, the daughter's son, and the [other] son, having accomplished their task, returned home.
Seeing that old man dead, they wept excessively,
as did those killed by snakes or horns, and those slain by fanged beasts.
Even for one who has committed suicide, there is no fitness for the ritual consecration;
consider again how there could be a cremation for such a person. (28)
Relying on the injunction, "One should prescribe an expiation, but one should not perform the water-libation rites," they then carried out the cremation and other funeral ceremonies.
They performed the expiatory rite accordingly and went to the village of Kalāpaka;
there, having bowed down to a perfected being (siddha) who was a friend of the deceased brahmin residing there, they [proceeded].
Having experienced death and other such states for a moment, they performed their lamentation;
then this Siddha, residing within the bundle of grass, spoke to his son-in-law, the twice-born man.
"The murder of a Brahmin has indeed occurred for you; therefore, perform an expiation.
Having heard these words of the aged Siddha, the son-in-law spoke this speech: ||32||
"O venerable one, I have never at any time committed the killing of a Brahmin.
By what fault, then, is this fruit of Brahmin-slaughter upon me? Tell me. (33)
Having heard the words of his son-in-law, the aged Siddha said to him:
"By you, it has been demonstrated that there is food belonging to a Śūdra at his feet. (34)
Likewise, it was shown by that Brahmin that death occurs upon the exhaustion of food;
and in that same manner, he crushed his own two feet.
"Then death was brought about there; thus you became the one who bears the fault.
And so, O best of the twice-born, the means for his slaughter was pointed out by you. (36)
O brahmin-sage, because of that fault—due to sharing the same bed, eating together, and likewise conversing—you shall incur the fruit of killing a Brahmin. (37)
Sin transfers to a person through close association;
therefore, purification must be performed, and let there be no dwelling for me in his house.
"O brāhmaṇa, abandon Kalpagrāma and go to Mathurā;
know that your purification will not occur elsewhere, so depart! (39)
Having heard those words of the elder, the three of them went to Mathurā,
along with his wife and his brother-in-law, who was the son-in-law possessed of perfected sciences.
Having been brought toward Mathurā by flying through the path of the sky,
they respectfully took up residence outside the city for the Brahmins.
At that time, at the sacrifice of King Kuśika in Mathurā,
two thousand brahmins were eating pure food every day.
Then those three eat the remnants of the *brahmayajña* performed there;
having reached Cakratīrtha, they always perform their ritual ablutions. (43)
The wife fed her husband—who had come for alms after the sacrifice—with the remnants of the offering and ate herself; in this manner, half a year passed by.
Then the Brahmins, performers of sacrifices, respectfully asked the Siddha who had arrived for alms: "O twice-born one, where do you reside? (45)
"Tell me truthfully, where do you stay and where do you take your meals?
The Siddha then related his own beneficial account.
Having taken alms here together with my wife and brother-in-law,
and having bathed at this Cakratīrtha, I shall divide [the food].
"I shall indeed take food here for the sake of removing the sin of killing a Brahmin.
Hearing that, all the Brahmins said, "O twice-born one, you are indeed purified. (48)
"By the power of Cakratīrtha, you are entirely liberated from sin;
and by the words of the brāhmaṇas as well, O twice-born one, you have indeed become pure once again. (49)
Thus, there was purification for those who had been wronged, as well as for those who had performed rites at Cakratīrtha,
for those who had performed expiatory rites, and likewise for those who had partaken of the Lord’s grace.
Having attained perfection, he rejoiced along with his wife and brother-in-law;
then, having arrived at Cakratīrtha, he settled down to eat the alms-food.
With a joyful heart, the wife spoke these words to her husband:
"O best of Brahmins, take your meal; I perceive that the sin of slaughter has departed from you. (52)
O best of the twice-born, by the power of Cakratīrtha, the sin of killing a cow has been destroyed;
therefore, you must certainly reside here in Mathurā forever.
Having resolved thus, those three remained there in Mathurā forever;
completely abandoning Kalāpa, Mathurā bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation. ||54||
Furthermore, that holy site is Bhadreśvara, frequented by the Siddhas;
indeed, Cakratīrtha bestows merit a hundred times more than Kalāpa.
By fasting for a day and night, the sin of killing a Brahmin is destroyed; what need has he for a bundle of ritual implements, or even for the face of Vārāṇasī? (56)
If Mathurā is attained and Cakratīrtha is visited, even a worm or an insect is born as four-armed [Viṣṇu]. (57)
O beloved, those three brahmins, having met their end in time,
attained my divine Goloka, where they became eternal four-armed beings.
Listen further as I shall proclaim another power born of the Vaikuṇṭha-tīrtha:
the people residing in Mithilā went to Mathurā for the sake of visiting the sacred ford. (59)
Having reached Vaikuṇṭha-tīrtha, they remained there;
among them was a certain brāhmaṇa who was greatly tormented by the sin of killing a brāhmaṇa.
Indeed, a stream of blood flowing from his hand was seen visibly, yet it did not diminish even after he had bathed in many sacred fords.
But by bathing in the Vaikuṇṭha-tīrtha, it has been dissolved;
one should not feel wonder here, for that is indeed the fruit of Vaikuṇṭha.
Having bathed here, one becomes free from sin and goes to Vaikuṇṭha.
O Lakṣmī, I shall further describe another [tirtha] born of the Gandharvakuṇḍa.
The greatness [of this place] is such that one who performs the ritual bath rejoices together with the Gandharvas.
The Mathurā region is a lotus measuring twenty yojanas. ||64||
In the pericarp, I am Kṛṣṇa, the eternal bestower of liberation upon the deceased;
and in the west, I dwell as Hari, the upholder of Govardhana.
Govinda is in the north, and Devaviśrama is resting in the east;
I am Varāha in the south, possessing a massive body and exceeding Keśava in size.
In the Kṛta Yuga, I was gratified by King Māndhātṛ;
indeed, being pleased with him, I bestowed my own image upon him.
By the Blessed One Kapila, a beautiful and auspicious image of Vārāhī was fashioned mentally; it was radiant, divine in form, and lovely. 68.
Even Indra constantly meditated upon her after obtaining the Saukarī form from Kapilā, and he worshipped her with great reverence in his own abode.
Rāvaṇa also went to heaven to conquer Śakra;
having defeated Śakra, he entered his palace there, which was shaped like a boar.
The divine form indeed bound Rāvaṇa with many rays;
and Rāvaṇa offered praise: "O Mādhava, you ought to protect me. (71)
"Grant your grace in every way to me, who am filled with devotion.
Then the blessed Lord Hari, being pleased, released Rāvaṇa.
Rāvaṇa also then desired to take that form back to Laṅkā;
when he was unable to lift it, he was struck with great astonishment.
Nemi said to him, "My intention is to take you to Laṅkā. Vārāha replied, "O Rākṣasa, you are indeed not a Vaiṣṇava. (74)
"I will not come from there; however, if you are a Vaiṣṇava, then take me with you!
Rāvaṇa, having become a Vaiṣṇava, led me to that city. (75)
Rāvaṇa was brought to destruction by Rāma, but that image was brought to his own city and worshipped for many years. (76)
By him, his own brother Śeṣasvarūpa was employed for the destruction of the Rākṣasas;
having arrived in Mathurā, he [proceeded] against the Rākṣasas.
And there he destroyed that image of Vārāhī;
for the sake of protection, he brought it and established it according to the ritual injunctions.
Blessed is this land of Mathurā, and blessed are the people dwelling therein, by whom [He] has always been bathed, seen, touched, meditated upon, and contemplated. (79)
And this Varāha, when worshipped, will grant liberation in every way;
by offering funeral cakes (piṇḍas) in the presence of Varāha, one's ancestors are indeed liberated.
The fruit of the Gayā-śrāddha indeed comes to pass, as does the fruit born of Puṣkara;
likewise, by beholding the White Boar (Śvetavarāha), one shall behold final rest.
And having beheld Govinda, the upholder of Govardhana, one should then look upon him; thus, O Lakṣmī, has his majesty been described to you. 82.
Whoever should hear this, or read it, or likewise cause it to be read—such a person shall obtain the merit described herein and attain liberation. (83)

Thus ends the three hundred and forty-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Destruction of the Sin of Brahmin-Slaughter for a Brāhmaṇa Residing in Kalāpagrāma at Cakratīrtha and His Liberation; the Destruction of the Sin of Brahmin-Slaughter for a Brāhmaṇa from Mithilā at Vaikuṇṭhatīrtha; and the Successive Establishment of the Boar Incarnation, Created by the Lord Kapila from his Mind, in Mathurā," in the first section on the lineage of the Kṛta Yuga within the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, concerning the majesty of the sacred field of Mathurā.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī, to the account of the highly meritorious place known as Govardhana;
it is situated two yojanas to the west of Mathurā.
This sacred field bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation upon embodied beings through the act of visiting it;
here, the heart of men is indeed made free from sin by bathing.
The *aindra* [tīrtha] is in the east; the *priya* [tīrtha] is situated in the south at the Yamatīrtha;
the *vāruṇa* tīrtha is in the west, and the *kaubera* is indeed in the north.
One who performs ablutions at each respective sacred ford (tīrtha) is glorified in that corresponding world;
one who remembers me at the time of casting off life goes to my world.
Having reached the site of the heap of grain, one should circumambulate it;
such a person goes to the supreme world, which is enriched with wealth, grain, and other blessings.
Having bathed in the Mānasa-Gaṅgā, having beheld Hari on Govardhana,
and having circumambulated Annakūṭa, one is not born again.

Having gone to the site of Govardhana on a Monday coinciding with the new moon, one should satisfy the ancestors; then the satisfaction resulting from the offering of funeral cakes at Gayā shall occur.
Having circumambulated Govardhana and beheld Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa,
one undoubtedly attains the merit of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices.
On the eleventh day of the bright fortnight of the month of Bhādrapada, one should observe a fast;
having bathed in the Mānasa-Gaṅgā, one should behold the Sun at the hour of Brahmā.
Having bowed to Govardhana and having bowed to Hari standing upon its peak,
she should descend and, while observing a fast, perform the circumambulation of the mountain.
One should go to the Puṇḍarīka site and perform a bath in the Kuṇḍa;
one should worship the ancestors and the gods, and offer full adoration to Puṇḍarīka.
One who performs such rites goes to the abode of Hari;
thereafter, one should bathe in the Apsaras Kuṇḍa and offer libations to the ancestors.
